requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
**VerificationStatus** enumeration (Section 11.7): whether an identified
sender has proven who they are.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| UNVERIFIED | Identified, not proven: no verification in force |
| PENDING | A verification request is open for the identity |
| VERIFIED | Proven by the integrator's method; in force until it expires |
| EXPIRED | Was verified; its time ran out |
| REVOKED | Ended by the integrator before its time |

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, add_member: a new member, a member not ACTIVE, and a member already ACTIVE. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Joining and leaving:** a deliberate join is the operation `add_member`. It
creates the participant ACTIVE, or reactivates an existing record that is not
ACTIVE (a re-join keeps `joined_at`), then fires `ON_PARTICIPANT_JOINED` with
a `PARTICIPANT_JOINED` event as its payload; on a member already ACTIVE it
only records a newly reached channel, with no event.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, add_member: the identification of a new member and of a re-join, with or without an identity_id. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
With an `identity_id` the
participant is IDENTIFIED; a new member without one is PENDING, and a re-join
without one keeps the identification and the identity the record had.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, remove_member: a member's leave or ban, and an unknown participant. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Leaving is `remove_member`: it
sets the participant's status to LEFT, or to BANNED when asked, keeping the
record, then fires `ON_PARTICIPANT_LEFT` with a `PARTICIPANT_LEFT` event as
its payload; an unknown participant is an error.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, add_member and remove_member: ON_PARTICIPANT_JOINED and ON_PARTICIPANT_LEFT, their execution and their payload's data. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Both hooks are ASYNC; their
payload is a system event whose data carries `participant_id` and, on a join,
`identity_id`, on a leave, the new `status`.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, add_member and remove_member: their system event stored only by an implementation that writes lifecycle records (RK-5.1-015). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation that writes
lifecycle records (§5.1) stores that event; one that does not stores nothing.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, rename_member: the update operation that changes display_name and fires ON_PARTICIPANT_UPDATED. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Renaming (normative):** a member's presentation can change while they are
present — their display name above all. Implementations SHOULD provide an
update operation (`rename_member`) that changes `display_name` in place and
fires `ON_PARTICIPANT_UPDATED` with a `PARTICIPANT_UPDATED` event as its
payload (stored as a lifecycle record only by an implementation that writes
them, §5.1), so an interface reflecting the room learns of the change the same
way it learned of the join.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, rename_member, where an implementation offers it (RK-5.5-019): id and identity_id. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`id` and `identity_id` are not presentation and
MUST NOT be changed through it: they are what attribution, correlation
(Section 12.10.2) and moderation stand on.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, rename_member, where an implementation offers it (RK-5.5-019): a rename that changes nothing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A rename that changes nothing is a
no-op — no write, no event.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, rename_member, where an implementation offers it (RK-5.5-019): the PARTICIPANT_UPDATED record's text and data. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The record's text quotes the new name as
Python's `repr` writes a string: every character `str.isprintable` refuses (a
control, format, separator other than the space, private-use or unassigned
character) is escaped, a tab, a newline and a carriage return as `\t`, `\n`
and `\r`, any other `\xNN` below U+0100, `\uNNNN` below U+10000,
`\UNNNNNNNN` past it (`'Bob\xa0Smith'`, `'\u202e'`), so a name cannot hide or
reverse what a reader of the record sees; its data keeps the name as given.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, resolve_participant (Appendix B.3): the participant set IDENTIFIED as an identity the store holds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Resolving:** an advisor's identification of a participant
(`resolve_participant`, Appendix B.3) sets it IDENTIFIED as an identity the
store holds: its `identity_id`, `resolved_by` (`manual` when the caller names
no one) and `resolved_at` set, its candidates dropped, the identity's
display name taken when the identity has one.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, resolve_participant: the binding of the participant's primary channel, unless it is someone else's conversation (§5.7, §10.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The binding of the
participant's primary channel names the identity from then on, unless it is
someone else's conversation: it names another correspondent (the framework's
own name included, §10.4), or names none and routing reads its recipient
(§5.7) as another address or as a value that is not a recipient. On a channel
not registered nothing reads that recipient, and a binding naming no
participant and not declared `group` is read as someone else's. The
participant's own are their id, the identity they had and the one they get,
and the address whose own record they are (§11.2); a `group` binding names no
correspondent, and one delivering to no one is no one's. The advisor
identifies a person and does not choose whom the room
answers: a binding left so keeps its correspondent, and a message from the
participant is admitted through it no more than before (§10.4).

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, resolve_participant: ON_PARTICIPANT_IDENTIFIED and its payload. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Either way
`ON_PARTICIPANT_IDENTIFIED` fires with a `PARTICIPANT_IDENTIFIED` event as its
payload, whose data carries `participant_id` and `identity_id` (stored as a
lifecycle record only by an implementation that writes them, §5.1).

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, resolve_participant: a participant the room does not have, an identity the store does not hold or of another organization (§17.2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
participant the room does not have, an identity the store does not hold or
one of another organization than the caller acts for (§17.2), is an error,
and nothing is written.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, ensure_participant creating a record. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A host's get-or-create (`ensure_participant`) that
creates a record writes no `PARTICIPANT_JOINED` record and fires no hook:
it is bookkeeping, as recording a channel is.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant: one record per room and participant id, shared by every channel the participant is reached through. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**One record, several channels (normative):** a Participant is one record
per (`room_id`, `id`). Section 4.4 says a participant is connected via one
or more channels, and this is the record all of them share — the same
person reached by SMS and then by email is one participant, not two.
`channel_id` is their *primary* channel; `connected_via` is every channel
the room has reached them through, the primary included.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a store's add of a participant under an id the room has (§14.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A store refuses to
add a participant under an id the room has (participant exists, §14.3) and
keeps the record it holds; a record is rewritten by `update_participant`.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, an event's participant_id: the channels it names a participant on. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Who a sender is (normative):** an event's `participant_id` names a
Participant only on a channel that participant was reached through
(`connected_via`): an id one transport gives says nothing of another's.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant: how a channel is reached, and what an identity's id and a sender's address name on it (Section 11). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
channel is reached by a deliberate join (a member added, a session joined),
and by the identity pipeline, which records the channel it resolved a sender
on (Section 11); an identity's id names its person on a channel one of their
records was reached through; and a sender's address names, on its channel,
the record of their own the identity pipeline left them pending under there
(Section 11.2).

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a sender whose id names no participant on its channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A sender whose id names nobody on its channel is
no participant of the room: it carries no participant's name, role,
authority, identification nor verification.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant: every reading of who a sender is (Sections 6.4, 10.3, 11.6, 11.7.3, 21.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every reading of who a sender is
follows this one rule: the label a transcript gives them (Section 6.4), the
role a tool policy's override is chosen by (Section 21.1), the authority and
the authorship an edit or a delete is checked against (Section 10.3), the
identification that spares resolution (Section 11.6) and the verification a
message is labelled with (Section 11.7.3). Linking one person's channels is
the host's deliberate join or the identity pipeline's resolution, never two
transports' ids that happen to be equal.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a lazy materialisation's get-or-create of a sender: an existing record. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A **lazy materialisation** — the get-or-create that materialises a sender
  the first time they speak — MUST NOT re-home an existing record: the
  `channel_id` it is given applies to a record being created, and to no
  other.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a sender the identity pipeline leaves pending (Section 11.2): the record it is sent under. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Nor does the identity pipeline create a record under the id a
  sender's channel gave: a sender it leaves pending (Section 11.2) stays on
  the room's record of that id when one was reached through the channel (a
  member the host added), and otherwise gets a record of their own, one per
  sender and channel; the event is sent under that record's id, so their
  next message finds it and a later resolution of it (resolving, above) is
  theirs.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, ensure_participant: a deliberate reach of the channel it names. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A host's own
  get-or-create (`ensure_participant`) is a deliberate reach, as a join is: the
  host vouches for the sender, and the channel it names is recorded.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a deliberate join: the primary channel it may set, and the one it replaces. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
  **deliberate join** MAY set `channel_id` to the channel joined through,
  which is what "primary channel used to join" means; the channel it
  replaces MUST remain in `connected_via`.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a lazy materialisation or a deliberate join: connected_via. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- Either way, the channel named by the caller MUST be added to
  `connected_via` when absent from it, and implementations MUST persist
  `connected_via`. A channel reached once and never recorded is a channel
  the room cannot afterwards say it reached.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a participant reached through a channel that is not its primary one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- Being reached through a channel that is not the primary one is legitimate
  and MUST NOT fail.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a participant reached through a channel that is not its primary one: the warning. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It is, however, invisible in the record handed back,
  whose `channel_id` still names another channel: implementations SHOULD
  log it at warning level **naming both channels**, because a caller that
  goes on to keep per-channel state on that record — a lifecycle, a
  presence, a status — is driving another channel's record without having
  been told. That silence is what lets one channel's departure erase
  another channel's membership.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, a channel that observes presence on a record it does not home: the record's status. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `status` follows the primary channel's lifecycle. A channel that observes
  presence on a record it does not home — a conference seeing a member
  connect and disconnect — MUST NOT write that record's `status`: an arrival
  there is not a join, a departure there is not a leave, and a room member
  who hangs up on its call is still a member of the room. What such a channel
  owes the record is the bookkeeping above (`connected_via`); what it owes
  everyone else is its own events and hooks, which report the arrival and the
  departure whether or not the status moved.

requirements.applies: §5.5 Participant, recording a channel in connected_via. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- Recording a channel is bookkeeping, not presentation: it writes no
  `PARTICIPANT_UPDATED` record and does not fire `ON_PARTICIPANT_UPDATED`.

requirements.applies: §5.6 Identity: its fields. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
Identity
├── id: string                              # Unique identifier
├── organization_id: string | null          # Multi-tenant scope
├── display_name: string | null             # Human-readable name
├── email: string | null                    # The person's email address
├── phone: string | null                    # The person's phone number
├── channel_addresses: map<ChannelType, list<string>>
│       # Cross-channel addresses, e.g., {SMS: ["+15551234"], EMAIL: ["john@example.com"]}
├── external_id: string | null              # CRM or external system reference
├── external_ids: map<string, string>       # Other systems' references, by system
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Integrator-defined data
```

requirements.applies: §5.6 Identity, an address another identity of the organization holds, on a creation or a link_address (§14.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An address belongs to one identity per organization and channel type, so a
resolution never chooses: creating an identity, or linking an address
(`link_address`, §14.1), with an address another identity of the organization
holds MUST be refused, and moving an address is an explicit unlink
(`unlink_address`, §14.1) followed by a link, never a silent re-home of
someone's conversations.

requirements.applies: §5.6 Identity, identity resolution for an organization, or for none (§17.2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Identity resolution is scoped to the organization it
names (§17.2); for none, it resolves the identities of no organization only,
never an organization's.

requirements.applies: §5.6 Identity, link_address (§14.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`link_address` links to an identity of the
organization it names, and refuses an unknown identity or another
organization's; linking an address the identity already holds changes nothing.

requirements.applies: §5.6 Identity, unlink_address (§14.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`unlink_address` removes an address from the identity it names, in the
organization it names, under the same refusals; an address the identity does
not hold changes nothing.

requirements.applies: §5.6 Identity, unlink_address: what it changes and what it leaves. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An unlink changes which identity a later message
resolves to, never a stored conversation: the rooms, bindings and participants
that named the address stay as they are.

requirements.applies: §5.6 Identity, a sender's address resolved in its channel's form (§5.7). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Addresses compare as stored: the
framework resolves a sender's address in its channel's form (§5.7), so a host
links addresses in that form (E.164 on a channel addressed by phone number).

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding: the binding a channel's attach creates, and its fields. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When a channel is attached to a Room, a ChannelBinding is created:

```
ChannelBinding
├── channel_id: string                      # Which channel
├── room_id: string                         # Which room
├── channel_type: ChannelType               # Channel type enum
├── category: ChannelCategory               # TRANSPORT or INTELLIGENCE
├── direction: ChannelDirection             # INBOUND, OUTBOUND, BIDIRECTIONAL
├── access: Access                          # Permission level
├── muted: bool                             # Temporarily silenced (suppress response events)
├── output_muted: bool                      # Speech output muted: events still arrive,
│                                           # a speech-to-speech provider's audio is not
│                                           # forwarded, injected text is not spoken
├── visibility: string                      # Write visibility rule
├── participant_id: string | null           # The binding's correspondent (§10.4): the
│                                           # sender a room was created for, or the
│                                           # first one routed to it; on a chat
│                                           # channel, the chat
├── group: bool                             # Several senders share this binding's
│                                           # conversation (§10.4); default false
├── last_read_index: int | null             # Read horizon for unread tracking
├── attached_at: datetime                   # When attached
├── capabilities: ChannelCapabilities       # What this channel supports
├── rate_limit: RateLimit | null            # Per-channel rate limiting
├── retry_policy: RetryPolicy | null        # Per-channel retry configuration
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Binding-specific data (recipient_id, persona, etc.)
```

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, an attach that names no category. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A binding's category is the channel's own unless the attachment names one:
an intelligence channel attached without a category takes part as an
intelligence channel, a transport as a transport.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a binding not declared group: its correspondent (§10.1 step 2, §10.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A binding carries one correspondent's conversation unless it is declared
`group`. The framework records on it the sender a room was created for, or the
first sender routed to it (`participant_id`, §10.1 step 2), and the default
router admits no one else through it (§10.4).

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a transport channel whose replies go to the address the correspondent writes from: the recipient the framework writes when it records the sender. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
On a transport channel whose
replies go to the address the correspondent writes from (a phone number, an
email address: SMS, MMS, RCS, WhatsApp, email, Messenger), the binding's
recipient and its correspondent are one address. When the framework records
the sender, or finds a binding naming the sender (by their address, their
identity, or a participant they are) with no value under the recipient key, it
writes the address the message came from as the binding's recipient, under the
channel's recipient key (below); a recipient the binding already has
is kept, and so is a value that is not a recipient (below).

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a binding the integrator gives a recipient and no correspondent (§10.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Conversely, a binding the integrator gives a recipient and no correspondent
names that recipient as its correspondent: the room is that person's
conversation, and the router admits no one else through it (§10.4).

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, an attach and an update of a binding's metadata: the addresses written and the correspondent named. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An attach
and an update of a binding's metadata write the addresses the integrator gives
in the channel's form and name the correspondent so; a `group` binding's
recipient names no one, and a channel the implementation no longer holds writes
nothing.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a transport that delivers to a chat or a conversation: routing, the correspondent recorded, admission and replies by the chat. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
On a
transport that delivers to a chat or a conversation (Telegram, Teams,
Discord), the chat a message was posted in is its conversation: a private chat
is its user's, a group chat the group's, shared by all its members. The
framework routes the message, records the binding's correspondent and admits a
sender by the chat, and a room opened for the message replies there; the
message's author stays its sender.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a room the integrator opens for a chat. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The chat a binding delivers to names its
conversation as a phone number names its correspondent: a room the integrator
opens for a chat admits no one else. A user who writes to the bot privately
and in a group holds two conversations, and a room found by the sender would
answer one in the other.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel that carries both private chats and groups: a message's conversation. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel that carries both private chats and groups
(WhatsApp Personal) takes a group message's group as its conversation and a
private message's sender.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a transport that delivers to a URL: the recipient. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
On a transport that delivers to a URL (an HTTP
webhook), nothing of the message is written as the recipient.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, addresses by channel type: the recipient and chat keys a channel's declaration names, and the defaults. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Addresses by channel type.** A channel's type decides how its addresses
are written and compared. Its declaration names the binding metadata key its
recipient is written under and, on a channel that answers chats, the
metadata key its inbound messages carry their chat under; a declaration MAY
name other keys, or none. The defaults:

| Type | Address | Recipient key | Chat key |
|---|---|---|---|
| SMS, MMS, RCS, WHATSAPP | Phone number, E.164 (below) | `phone_number` | — |
| WHATSAPP_PERSONAL | Phone number, E.164 | `phone_number` | `group_jid`, a group message's group |
| VOICE | Phone number, E.164 | — | — |
| EMAIL | Email address (below) | `email_address` | — |
| MESSENGER | As written | `facebook_user_id` | — |
| TELEGRAM | Its chat, as written | `telegram_chat_id` | `chat_id` |
| TEAMS | Its chat, as written | `teams_conversation_id` | `conversation_id` |
| WEBHOOK | As written | — (it posts to its configured URL) | — |
| Any other type | As written | — | — |

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel with no recipient key (§10.2 step 3d). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel with no recipient key delivers to a destination of its own (a
WebSocket's connections, a webhook's URL, a voice or video session) and needs
no recipient (§10.2 step 3d).

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a value under a recipient key: a recipient, no value, or a value that is not a recipient, at every read. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A recipient is a value under the key that is a
string, neither empty nor blank, or an integer, for a chat id written as one
(Telegram's). The key absent, null and a blank string are no value: the
binding has no recipient. Any other value (a boolean, a float, a whole one
included (`42.0`), an array, an object) is not a recipient, and is not no
value either: it is a value no one is reached at, and a float has no single
written form, so it cannot be compared as an address. A store whose JSON form
cannot tell a whole float from an integer (Postgres `jsonb` reads `1e16` back
as `10000000000000000`) reads such a value as an integer. Every read of a
recipient takes this rule.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, routing's read of a binding's recipient: the channel's answer, else the key, a value that is not a recipient first; step 1 and the store's lookup read the key as stored (RK-5.7-018). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Routing reads a binding's recipient as its channel
answers it (`recipient_address`, which may read elsewhere than the key), and
where the channel answers none, as the key holds it, in the channel's form: a
channel that declares a recipient key and keeps the default answer delivers to
that value all the same, so its binding is no more open to a stranger than one
whose channel answers. A value under the key that is not a recipient is read
first, whatever the channel answers.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, an attach and an update of a binding's metadata: the recipient read as routing reads it (RK-5.7-016). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An attach and an update of a binding's
metadata read the recipient the same way.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, step 1 of the default routing strategy and the store's lookup it rests on (§10.4, §14.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Step 1 alone, and the store's lookup
it rests on (§14.1), read the key as stored: a binding whose channel reads its
recipient elsewhere is found through the correspondent its attach names, or at
step 3 as the one room bound to the channel.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a delivery to a binding with no recipient or a value that is not one (§10.2 step 3d). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A delivery is refused for no value
and for a value that is not a recipient alike (§10.2 step 3d).

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, routing's read of no value and of a value that is not a recipient (§10.1 step 2, §10.4); a binding naming its correspondent, and a group binding, excepted. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Routing reads no value as no
correspondent, and a value that is not a recipient as the address of someone
other than the sender, whoever writes (§10.1 step 2, §10.4): no sender is
found through it at step 1; on a binding naming no participant and not
`group`, step 3 admits no one through it, and the room is no longer a routed
message's under the lock whatever strategy chose it; the record of a routed
sender never writes over it, on a binding naming the sender too. A binding
naming its correspondent still routes them there, and routing does not read a
`group` binding's recipient.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, routing reading a value that is not a recipient: the warning. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation SHOULD log a warning naming the
binding when routing reads such a value, with the value's type and never the
value, which may be a person's address.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, routing and the record of a sender: a recipient and a chat compared in their written form. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Routing and the record of a sender
compare a recipient, and a chat, in its written form: the integer `12345` and
the string `"12345"` are one address.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, the addresses the framework records, a chat id included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The framework writes the addresses it
records as strings, a chat id included.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a message on a channel that answers chats, carrying its chat under the chat key (§10.1 step 2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A chat message is its chat's, whatever
its sender, an empty or blank one included: it is
routed by the chat its chat key carries, and a room opened for it binds the channel naming the chat
as correspondent and recipient (§10.1 step 2).

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a chat key holding no value or a value that is not a recipient. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The chat under a chat key
takes the recipient's rule, no value and a value that is not a recipient
alike: either is no chat, and a message that carries only such a value does
not carry its chat.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel that carries private chats and groups: a message with and without its group under the key. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
On a channel
that carries private chats and groups, a message that carries its group under
the key is its group's, any other its sender's.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel whose replies go to a chat only: a message that does not carry its chat (§10.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
On a channel whose replies go
to a chat only, a message that does not carry its chat has no address: it
records no one, and a room routing opens for it names no recipient and no
sender (§10.4), so its deliveries are refused `no_recipient` until the
integrator names one. Its author is the message's sender either way.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel addressed by phone number: the inbound sender, a binding's correspondent and recipient, and a participant's id given on it, in E.164. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel addressed by phone number compares and stores numbers in one form,
E.164 (`+15550000001`). The inbound sender, a binding's correspondent and
recipient, and a participant's id given on that channel are written in that
form before they are compared or recorded; the message's raw payload keeps
the provider's own spelling.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel addressed by phone number: URI schemes, separators and the (0) trunk prefix, and what is a number. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A number is written as follows:

- A URI scheme (`whatsapp:`, `tel:`) and the separators people type (spaces,
  `-`, `.`, `(`, `)`) are dropped, and so is the trunk prefix written `(0)`
  after a country code: `+33 (0)6 12 34 56 78` is `+33612345678`. What is
  left is a number when it is digits, after a `+` or not; anything else (an
  email address, a group's id) is kept as written.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel addressed by phone number: a number written with + or 00. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A number written with `+`, or with the international prefix `00`, is
  international: `+` and its digits.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel addressed by phone number that declares a country code: digits written without + or 00. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- Digits without either, on a channel with a country code declared: a
  number that starts with the code and has more than 10 digits already
  carries it (`15550000001` is `+15550000001` for the code 1); any other
  takes the code in place of its trunk prefix `0`, or before its digits
  (`0612345678` is `+33612345678` for the code 33). Six digits or fewer are
  a short code, kept as written.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel addressed by phone number that declares no country code: digits written without + or 00 (§10.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- Digits without either, on a channel that declares no country code, are
  kept as written. The digits alone cannot tell `13800138000`, a national
  number in China, from `+1 380 013 8000`, and a router MUST NOT guess
  (§10.4): a missed match opens a new room, while a wrong merge discloses
  one person's conversation to another.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a channel addressed by phone number: a result of more than 15 digits or starting with 0. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A result of more than 15 digits, or one whose first digit is `0`, which no
  country code is, is kept as written.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, the country code a channel declares, as the channel is configured or a number is written with it; the example after it, one person written three ways, illustrates RK-5.7-029 to RK-5.7-031. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The country code a channel declares is one to three digits, the first not
`0`, written with or without its `+` (`1`, `+33`). An implementation MUST
refuse another as the channel is configured, or as a number is written with
it: a code that is none would leave every national number as written, and
the mistake unseen.

So, on a channel declaring the country code 1, `whatsapp:+15550000001`,
`15550000001` and `+1 (555) 000-0001` are one person.

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, an email channel's addresses. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An email channel
compares and stores an address lower-case and without a display name
(`Alice <Alice@Example.com>` is `alice@example.com`).

requirements.applies: §5.7 ChannelBinding, a binding declared group by the integrator. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A binding declared `group` holds
a conversation of several senders, such as a group chat on a channel dedicated
to its room: every sender writing on it belongs to the room, and none is
recorded on it, as correspondent or as recipient. The declaration is the integrator's to make, because nothing
the store holds tells a group channel from a number shared by many
correspondents.

requirements.applies: §5.8 ChannelCapabilities; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
Each channel declares what it supports:

```
ChannelCapabilities
├── media_types: list<ChannelMediaType>     # What content categories are supported
├── max_length: int | null                  # Maximum text length, in Unicode code
│                                           # points (null = unlimited, §6.6)
│
│   # Text features:
├── supports_rich_text: bool
├── supports_buttons: bool
├── max_buttons: int | null
├── supports_cards: bool
├── supports_quick_replies: bool
├── supports_templates: bool
│
│   # Media features:
├── supports_media: bool
├── supported_media_types: list<string>     # MIME types
├── max_media_size_bytes: int | null
│
│   # Audio/Video features:
├── supports_audio: bool
├── max_audio_duration_seconds: int | null  # Longest audio taken, in seconds
├── supported_audio_formats: list<string>   # Empty takes every format
├── supports_video: bool
├── max_video_duration_seconds: int | null  # Longest video taken, in seconds
├── supported_video_formats: list<string>   # Empty takes every format
│
│   # Delivery features:
├── supports_threading: bool
├── supports_typing: bool
├── supports_read_receipts: bool
├── supports_reactions: bool
├── supports_edit: bool
├── supports_delete: bool
│
│   # Extensible:
└── custom: map<string, any>
```

requirements.applies: §5.8 ChannelCapabilities, ChannelMediaType enumeration. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ChannelMediaType** enumeration:

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| TEXT | Plain text messages |
| RICH | Formatted text with buttons, cards, quick replies |
| MEDIA | Images, documents, files |
| AUDIO | Audio messages, voice notes |
| VIDEO | Video messages |
| LOCATION | Geographic coordinates |
| TEMPLATE | Pre-approved message templates |

requirements.applies: §5.8 ChannelCapabilities, media_types: what a channel receives unchanged, transcoded, or as text (Section 6.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`media_types` decides what the channel receives: a content of a category it
names is delivered unchanged (a file, within the limits below), one of a
category it does not name is transcoded, and text is the fallback every
channel takes, whatever it declares (Section 6.6).

requirements.applies: §5.8 ChannelCapabilities, supports_edit and supports_delete: an edit or a delete delivered natively (Section 10.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Of the `supports_*`
flags, only `supports_edit` and `supports_delete` take part in transcoding:
they decide whether an edit or a delete is delivered natively (Section
10.3).

requirements.applies: §5.8 ChannelCapabilities, the supports_* flags other than supports_edit and supports_delete. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The others describe the channel and do not decide transcoding: a
channel whose `media_types` names RICH receives a rich content unchanged
whatever `supports_rich_text` says, and one whose `media_types` does not
name RICH receives its text form even when `supports_rich_text` is true.

requirements.applies: §5.8 ChannelCapabilities, a channel whose media_types names MEDIA: a file outside its supported_media_types or over its max_media_size_bytes (Section 6.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel whose `media_types` names MEDIA receives a file only when it takes
that file: a MediaContent whose `mime_type` is absent from a non-empty
`supported_media_types`, or whose known size (`size_bytes`) is over
`max_media_size_bytes`, is delivered as its text form (Section 6.6), as for
a channel that does not name MEDIA.

requirements.applies: §5.8 ChannelCapabilities, an empty supported_media_types, a null max_media_size_bytes and a file of unknown size. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An empty `supported_media_types` takes
every type, and a null `max_media_size_bytes`, or a file of unknown size,
any size. A provider's refusal of a file it cannot carry would lose the
whole message; its text form keeps it.

requirements.applies: §5.9 Three Levels of Channel Metadata; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
Channel-specific information lives at three levels. Implementations MUST maintain
all three and MUST NOT conflate them:

| Level | Where | Scope | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Channel Instance** | Channel.info | Global, static | `{provider: "acme", from_number: "+15551234"}` |
| **Channel Binding** | ChannelBinding.metadata | Per-room | `{persona: "formal", language: "fr"}` |
| **Event Source** | RoomEvent.channel_data | Per-event | `SMSChannelData{from_number: "+15559876", segments: 1}` |

requirements.applies: §5.10 Task; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
```
Task
├── id: string                              # Unique identifier
├── room_id: string                         # Originating room
├── title: string                           # Human-readable title
├── description: string | null              # Detailed description
├── assigned_to: string | null              # Who is responsible
├── status: TaskStatus = PENDING            # Current state
├── created_at: datetime                    # When created (default: now)
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Integrator-defined data
```

requirements.applies: §5.10 Task; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text: **TaskStatus** enumeration: PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED

requirements.applies: §5.11 Observation; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
```
Observation
├── id: string                              # Unique identifier
├── room_id: string                         # Originating room
├── channel_id: string                      # Which channel produced this
├── content: string                         # The observation, as text
├── category: string | null                 # Category (e.g., "sentiment", "compliance_violation")
├── confidence: float = 1.0                 # From 0.0 to 1.0
├── created_at: datetime                    # When created (default: now)
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Integrator-defined data
```

requirements.applies: §5.12 Inbound Message: its fields. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The normalized representation of a message arriving from outside the framework:

```
InboundMessage
├── channel_id: string                      # Which registered channel
├── sender_id: string                       # Sender identifier (phone number, email, user ID)
├── content: EventContent                   # Parsed content
├── event_type: EventType = MESSAGE         # SYSTEM for a voice session start;
│                                           # INSTRUCTION (Section 10.1.1)
├── external_id: string | null              # Provider-side reference
├── thread_id: string | null                # Provider-native thread reference,
│                                           # passed through to the provider
├── parent_event_id: string | null          # In-app thread: the event this replies to;
│                                           # the pipeline stores its thread's root
│                                           # (§10.1 step 8)
├── idempotency_key: string | null          # Duplicate prevention
├── raw_payload: map<string, any>           # Original provider payload
├── provider_message_id: string | null      # Provider's message ID
├── metadata: map<string, any>              # Extra data
├── session: VoiceSession | null            # Voice session to connect after processing
├── visibility: string = "all"              # Event visibility (Section 7.3), intersected
│                                           # with the source binding's at commit;
│                                           # "transport" reaches no intelligence channel;
│                                           # never "internal", the framework's
├── addressed_to: list<string> | null       # Intelligence channels asked to act
│                                           # (Section 19.3); null = any eligible
├── response_visibility: string | null      # Where its cascade's answers may go: each
│                                           # is narrowed to it, never widened
│                                           # (Section 8.5); null alone = unrestricted;
│                                           # never "" nor "internal"
├── chain_depth: int = 0                    # The chain the message continues (Section 8.3)
├── standalone: bool = false                # INSTRUCTION only: the turn reads nothing
│                                           # of the room (Section 10.1.1)
└── delivery_key: string | null             # The caller's name for the message's delivery
                                            # while in flight, for its cancellation
                                            # (Section 10.1); never stored
```

requirements.applies: §5.12 Inbound Message: the room a caller names (Section 10.1), and the message's channel type. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The room, when the caller knows it, is passed to `process_inbound()` (Section
10.1), not carried by the message; the channel type is the registered
channel's.

requirements.text:
**The response scope.** A message's `response_visibility` scopes its cascade
(Section 8.5), and that cascade only. Work that leaves the cascade is a new
cascade, which the scope does not follow: a background delegation's hand-back
(Section 23.3), a tool's own direct injection (Section 10.5), a child room's
answer to the channels it shares with the room (Section 23.3). An integrator
that wants such work scoped passes a `response_visibility` itself.

connects the voice session to the channel after successful hook processing. This
allows voice calls and text messages to flow through the same entry point, same
hooks, and same pipeline. See Section 10.1 for the additional step.

requirements.applies: §6.3 reference capabilities table, the Telegram row: the media types and key features an implementation's Telegram channel declares. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Telegram | TEXT, RICH, MEDIA, AUDIO, VIDEO, LOCATION | Buttons, inline keyboards, edit, delete |
|

requirements.applies: §6.3 reference capabilities table, media rows (media features voice, realtime, video and conference): Audio/Video, Realtime Audio/Video, Video and Conference. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Audio/Video | AUDIO, VIDEO | Combined voice + video, STT/TTS + vision |
| Realtime Audio/Video | AUDIO, VIDEO | Speech-to-speech + video, tool calling |
| Video | VIDEO | Video-only, vision provider integration |
| Conference | AUDIO | Multi-party SFU, per-track STT, AI bot participant |
|

requirements.applies: §6.3 reference capabilities table, the Webhook row: the media types and key features an implementation's webhook channel declares. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Webhook | TEXT, RICH | Generic HTTP POST |

requirements.applies: §6.3: each channel declares its maximum text length in its capabilities (max_length, Section 5.8), enforced as Section 6.6 says; each platform's figure belongs to the implementation's documentation. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each channel declares its maximum text length in its capabilities
(`max_length`, Section 5.8), enforced as Section 6.6 says; the figure each
platform allows belongs to the implementation's documentation.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Intelligence channels: the on_event() entry every intelligence channel implements. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Intelligence channels process events and produce responses or insights. They
MUST implement `on_event()`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Intelligence channels: their output, routed through the normal event pipeline and delivered to no external system by the channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
They do NOT deliver to external systems — the
framework routes their output through the normal event pipeline.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Intelligence channels: each call of on_event() as a turn run through the turn backend by a turn executor (§10.6), in the owner's process or another. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each call of
an intelligence channel's `on_event()` is a turn, run through the turn backend
by a turn executor (Section 10.6), which may live in another process than the
room's owner.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel: the outline of what on_event() does, and the anatomy of a turn, a table naming the contract that carries each step; each step is carried by its own contract, below, in Sections 6.7, 7.5, 9, 19.3, 20, 21, 24 and Appendix A.9. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**AI Channel:**

An AI channel wraps an AI Provider (see Section 6.7). When `on_event()` is called:

1. Build conversation history from room timeline.
2. Determine target transport channel's capabilities and media types.
3. Construct AI context with capabilities, system instructions, and room metadata.
4. Run the turn's tool loop over the provider's structured stream (**One loop,
   streamed or not**, below).
5. Return ChannelOutput with a response stream (Appendix A.9).

**Anatomy of an AI turn.** Each step of a turn has its own contract; no stage
abstraction sits on top of them:

| Step | Carried by |
|---|---|
| Whether the channel answers at all | Addressing and the agent-response policy (Section 19.3); `BEFORE_AI_CONTEXT_BUILD` would block here (Planned, Section 9.2) |
| The conversation history | The memory provider (Section 20), over the channel's view of the room (Section 7.5 rule 8) |
| The tools the turn may call | The tool registry, tool policy and skill gating (Sections 21 and 24) |
| The system prompt | The channel's and the binding's instructions, the instructions of the MCP servers the host names (Section 21.2), the skills' preambles (Section 24) |
| The gate before generation | `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` (Section 9.2) |
| Generation and tool calls | The provider's structured stream and the one tool loop (below, Section 6.7); `BEFORE_TOOL_USE`, `ON_TOOL_CALL`, `AFTER_TOOL_ROUND` (Section 9.3) |
| What goes out | `BEFORE_BROADCAST` on each stored segment of a streamed response (Section 9.5) |
| Observing the turn | `ON_AI_RESPONSE` (Section 9.2) |

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel: a streamed segment once delivered, which no check of the whole answer takes back. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A check of the whole answer before anything is sent is only possible on a
turn that is not streamed: a streamed segment, once delivered, is not taken
back.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel: an event originating from the channel itself. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: The AI channel MUST skip events originating from itself to prevent infinite loops.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel: the event types that open a turn (MESSAGE, INSTRUCTION), and an event of any other type, whatever strategy takes the agent's turns (§19.7). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It takes a turn on a MESSAGE or an INSTRUCTION only. An event of any other
type (a SYSTEM notice, a REACTION, a PARTICIPANT_JOINED, a tool-call row)
opens no turn, whatever strategy takes the agent's turns (Section 19.7): it
is submitted to no speak policy, is not handed to a running turn, and goes to
the agent's memory as any event the channel is given, a tool-call row aside.
An application that wants an agent to react to a notice sends it an
instruction (Section 10.1.1).

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel: an edit or a delete (§10.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An edit or a delete opens no turn either
(Section 10.3).

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, capability-aware generation: the target transport channel's capabilities, handed to the model at generation time. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Capability-aware generation:** The framework MUST provide the target transport
channel's capabilities to the AI at generation time, NOT post-process the output.
This allows the AI to tailor its response (e.g., short text for SMS, rich for Email).

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, answer text events (TEXT_DELTA) where an implementation offers them: off by default, published only when the host turns them on. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Answer text events:** `AIChannel` MAY project the text of its answer onto
the realtime bus as `TEXT_DELTA` while it is written, and does so only when
the host turns it on: it is off by default. It serves the code that delegated
a task (§23.3), whose agent's text, collected for its result, reaches no
transport: the live pipe to transports (§10.2) reaches only bound ones.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, answer text events turned on: the coalescing window and each event's fields. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Turned
on, the channel publishes the text coalesced on a window (a time and a size),
each event carrying `text`, `round` (the model round the text belongs to) and
`channel_id`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, answer text events turned on: a round's buffered text against that round's tool-call events and its end. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A round's buffered text MUST be published before that round's
tool-call events and at its end, so an observer reads text and calls in the
order they came; joined in order, a turn's `TEXT_DELTA` texts are its answer's
text, every round's, where a delegated task's result holds the last segment
only.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, answer text events turned on: the turns whose TEXT_DELTA the owner publishes, a delegated task's trace only, which BEFORE_BROADCAST does not judge. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`BEFORE_BROADCAST` (§9.5) judges the message a room stores, never this
stream. The owner MUST therefore publish a turn's `TEXT_DELTA` only when the
turn's reader commits its rows as a delegated task's trace, without crossing
`BEFORE_BROADCAST` (§23.3 step 5).

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, answer text events turned on: every other turn's TEXT_DELTA, one published after its turn, and an executor outside a turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It drops every other turn's (an answer in a
room, in a child room a transport is shared into, or to another channel's
message in a child room) and one published after its turn; an executor
publishes none outside a turn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, answer text events turned on: when the reader says its turn is a delegated trace, and what a subscriber then reads (§10.6.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The reader says so before its first read, so
before any of the turn's text is produced (§10.6.4). A subscriber thus reads
no answer text a hook judges, only the trace's; a delegation cut short may
store less of it than was published, the text its executor read ahead of the
reader (§10.6.4).

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, answer text events turned on: their audience (§8.4) and their persistence. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Like every ephemeral of a turn, it also reaches no one the
answer would not reach (§8.4), and it is never persisted: the trace's stored
messages remain the answer.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel, answer text events turned off. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Turned off, the channel publishes no `TEXT_DELTA`,
and its window has no effect.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call composition events: a provider whose structured stream exposes tool-call argument fragments. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Tool-call composition events:** A provider whose structured stream exposes
tool-call argument fragments MAY yield `StreamToolCallDelta` before the complete
`StreamToolCall`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call composition events: the TOOL_CALL_DELTA frames AIChannel projects (a SHOULD) and the argument content they never carry. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`AIChannel` SHOULD project those fragments onto the realtime bus
as `TOOL_CALL_DELTA`, carrying the call id, name and cumulative argument character
count, but MUST NOT carry the argument content.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call composition events: a composition attempt that published a non-terminal frame. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each composition attempt that
published a non-terminal frame MUST publish one terminal frame with an empty
`tool_calls` list before that attempt ends.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call composition events: the terminal frame (RK-6.4-063) on each way an attempt ends, retry and fallback included, and the counts across attempts. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
This includes successful completion,
cancellation, provider failure, retry and fallback: a retry closes the abandoned
attempt before the replacement attempt starts, so cumulative counts MUST NOT span
two attempts.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call composition events: what is executed and persisted, and composition events. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The complete `StreamToolCall` remains the unit of execution and
persistence; composition events are ephemeral and MUST NOT be persisted.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call events of an AI channel: the status the ephemeral TOOL_CALL_END carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The ephemeral `TOOL_CALL_END` MUST carry each call's `status`, `completed` or
`failed`, as the stored `TOOL_CALL_END` does: a call refused, failed, blocked,
served by nothing or cancelled ends `failed`, so a live surface does not read
the outcome out of the result preview.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call events of an AI channel: the outcome the stored TOOL_CALL_END carries (§9.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The stored `TOOL_CALL_END` also carries
the call's `outcome`, the way it ended as the channel determined it (Section
9.3): `served`, `refused`, `failed`, `blocked`, `unserved` or `cancelled`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call events: a reader that rebuilds earlier turns' tool calls from the store, an AI channel's history among them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
reader that rebuilds what earlier turns did from the store, as an AI
channel's history does with its earlier tool calls (Section 6.4), reads that
outcome rather than inferring it from the body: it keeps the calls the live
tool memory keeps (served, failed, blocked; never a refusal, a call nothing
served or one cancelled).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call events: a stored TOOL_CALL_END with no outcome, read back from the store. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A row stored without it is read by its `status`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool-call events: the ephemeral tool-call events of a call that has an intent (A call's intent, below, names TOOL_CALL_START and TOOL_CALL_END). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Both ephemeral events carry a call's `intent` beside its id when it has one
(A call's intent, below).

requirements.applies: §6.4 One end per started call: every call whose TOOL_CALL_START a channel published on the realtime bus gets one TOOL_CALL_END there, whatever the turn backend (Section 10.6.1), its reader stopping or its turn cut included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**One end per started call:** Every call whose `TOOL_CALL_START` a channel
published on the realtime bus MUST get one `TOOL_CALL_END` there, whatever
the turn backend (§10.6.1), its reader stopping or its turn cut included: a
channel that publishes a call's end once its reader took the call's end
marker publishes it all the same when the stream is closed first.

requirements.applies: §6.4 One end per started call: each ephemeral end reads as the stored TOOL_CALL_END does (its status). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each end
reads as the stored `TOOL_CALL_END` does (above).

requirements.applies: §6.4 One end per started call: a reader that stopped (Section 12.2 step 13s) took the ends it was handed, and each call ends as it did. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A reader that stopped
(§12.2 step 13s) took the ends it was handed, and each call ends as it did.

requirements.applies: §6.4 One end per started call: how a cut turn's owner closes each call (Section 10.6.4), failed unless its end was read or rode its start, a call cut while it ran, while a handler decided it or as its round's first end was handed out, and an executor of another process. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A cut turn's owner closes each call as its end reached it (§10.6.4): as it
ended when its reader read that end or the end rode its start, `failed`
otherwise. A call is thus `failed` when the cut came while it ran or while
an external tool handler decided it (§9.3), and when the cut came as the
first end of its round was handed out, an item the owner then drops (the
round's other ends rode their starts before it): on an executor of another
process the cut may arrive after the tool answered, and that end reads
`failed` all the same.

requirements.applies: §6.4 One end per started call: an AIChannel's ephemeral end of a call so failed carries the result {"error": "Tool call aborted"} when the channel publishes its calls' text (Section 8.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An `AIChannel`'s ephemeral end of such a call carries
the result `{"error": "Tool call aborted"}` when the channel publishes its
calls' text (§8.4).

requirements.applies: §6.4 One end per started call: a turn whose owner is lost (Section 10.6.8) publishes nothing more. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn whose owner is lost
(§10.6.8) publishes nothing more: no owner is left to publish it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a provider whose reasoning comes in blocks, each with its own signature, and what it hands the loop. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**What a provider hands the loop of its reasoning (normative).** A provider
whose reasoning comes in blocks, each with its own signature, hands
the loop every block as it received it, each `StreamThinkingDelta` naming its
`block`: an `AIThinkingPart` carries the block's `thinking` and `signature`,
or, for a block the vendor redacted, its opaque `redacted` data.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: the tool loop's replay of a round's signed blocks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Such a vendor
wants the blocks back as it sent them (it refuses a round whose blocks changed
in number, and a block without its signature), so the tool loop replays a
round's blocks one by one, in the order and at the place they came in relative
to the round's calls and stretches of text.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a block cut before its signature, or without one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A block the response cut before
its signature is not replayed, nor is a block without one at all: that is
another vendor's reasoning, a round a provider a router hands a generation
to (below) receives from the provider before it, which the vendor refuses and
the round does without.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a vendor that refuses, in the current turn, a call without its own signature, and an earlier turn's round. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A vendor that refuses, in the current turn, a call
without its own signature receives such a round of
that turn, none of whose calls carries one, as text: what it said, each call,
then each result with the images it carries, the one form it takes for calls
it did not make. An earlier turn's round, which it does not check, keeps its
form.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a provider whose reasoning has no blocks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider whose reasoning has no blocks hands
one block per round, replayed first.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a caller of generate() and a turn under a response schema, which cannot know where blocks came. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Two readers cannot know where blocks
came, and replay them first, then the text, then the calls: a caller of
`generate()`, since a response does not say where its blocks came, and a turn
under a response schema, whose text is held until it is checked.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: where a provider renders a replayed round's reasoning. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider MUST render a replayed round's reasoning where its vendor reads it,
and nowhere else: in the field the vendor reads it in, on the rounds and the
answers it reads it on.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a vendor that refuses a tool-calling round of the turn in progress without its reasoning field. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A vendor that refuses a round of the turn in progress
that called tools without its reasoning field (save, for one, a round whose
call ids it issued itself a moment ago) receives that field on every round
that called tools, and an answer's reasoning in it too: a round with no
reasoning, as every round of an earlier turn is, carries the field empty, or a
single space where an empty one reads as missing (a gateway's code may read it
so).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a vendor that reads its reasoning back without refusing a round that lacks it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A vendor that reads its reasoning back without refusing a round that
lacks it receives the field on a round or an answer that reasoned, and nothing
on one that did not.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a provider for generic Chat Completions servers whose configuration names the field a server reads (thinking_field), the integrator's choice. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The configuration of a provider for generic Chat
Completions servers MAY name the field a server reads (`thinking_field`), for a
server whose documentation asks for its reasoning back: a round or an answer
that reasoned then carries it there, and one that did not carries nothing.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a provider for generic Chat Completions servers whose configuration names no field. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider cannot tell whether a server takes the field, and strict
servers refuse one they do not know, so nothing is sent unless it is named; a
provider that already sends reasoning where its vendor reads it takes no such
option.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a Chat Completions request to a server no provider or configuration renders reasoning for. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A Chat Completions request to any other server
carries no reasoning, in no form: a `<think>` block in a message's text is read
as words the model said, and a server's prompt cache does not survive it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a round or an answer whose reasoning the request does not carry and that said nothing else. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
round that only reasoned and called goes back with no text, and an answer that
only reasoned with an empty one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: a round whose reasoning the request does not carry, as hooks and stream readers read it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only the request loses it: the round keeps its
reasoning for what reads a round (a `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` hook, a reader of the
stream), and the reasoning block that opens a model's output is still read out
of its text (Section 6.7).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: the rendering the provider an integrator builds gives, behind a custom base URL too. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The vendor's rendering is the integrator's choice, made by the provider it
builds, and it holds behind a custom base URL: a vendor's weights served by a
generic server get their reasoning back through that vendor's provider, given
that server's URL, or through a generic provider whose configuration names the
field, and none through a generic provider that does not.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Reasoning: how long a round's reasoning goes back, whatever the provider. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Whatever the provider, the reasoning goes back for as long as its turn lasts,
and a later turn reads none.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: a call a provider hands the loop, streamed or not. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**What a provider hands the loop for a call (normative).** Every provider,
streamed or not, hands the loop the same thing for the same call.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: a call's id within its response, minted by the provider when the server issues none or the same one twice. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each call of
a response carries an id no other call of that response carries: a provider
whose server issues none, or the same one twice, MUST mint one, since results,
eviction and cancellation all find a call by its id.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: two calls, a re-emission and an identical later copy. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Two calls stay two calls,
whatever stream index or arguments they share; a call the provider receives
twice (a re-emission carrying what the first lacked) stays one, and only a
call the wire cannot tell from such a re-emission (an identical call
in a later chunk, one copy or both without an id) is folded into the first,
which keeps what either copy carries (its id, its thought signature).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: a call's arguments as the loop receives them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call's
arguments reach the loop as a mapping and never as an error: no arguments
(nothing, or JSON `null`) are `{}`, and arguments that do not parse to an
object (invalid JSON, an array, a fragment) are kept whole under `raw`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: the stop reasons that mark a response cut short, read alike by every provider. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
response is cut short when it ran out of room (`length`: the output cap, or
the context window filling up mid-answer), when a content filter or a refusal
stopped it (`content_filter`, `refusal`), when its generation failed
(`error`), or when it ended on no stop reason (none given, or a word its
provider does not know): every provider reads its vendor's words into these
stop reasons (Section 6.7), so none runs a call another provider refuses.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: the calls of a response cut short that are not its last. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only the last call of a response
can be cut: a call another call followed was closed by it, and runs when its
arguments read, the response cut over its successor or not.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: the last call of a response cut short, and the argument text that shows it whole. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Under a response
cut short, only argument text that arrived and reads shows the last call's
arguments whole: a call with no argument text yet, or known only through a parse
of what arrived (a vendor SDK reads a fragment leniently), does not read either.
Nothing under a cut is no evidence of no arguments (a vendor may send no stop
for the block it cuts, often before its first argument chunk).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: a call marked partial, which no tool loop runs (an AI channel's or a reasoning backend's; the sentence also binds a realtime channel, Section 12.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Such a call
is marked partial, whatever the provider and whatever stop reason the response
gave, and a tool loop, the AI channel's or a reasoning backend's,
MUST NOT run it, nor may a realtime channel, whose provider hands such
arguments as the model's text rather than a mapping (Section 12.4): no tool
does anything useful with `raw`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls, realtime (media feature realtime): a realtime provider whose wire tells a cut, and one whose wire does not. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A realtime provider applies the same rule
where its wire tells a cut: a call whose item the response cut (an item whose
status says it is incomplete, whether the output cap or a cancel ended the
response) runs only when its argument text arrived and
reads, and is otherwise handed on marked cut, so the model reads that its
call was cut off; such a provider hands a call on once its item says whether
it was cut (a wire may say that a call's arguments are done before it gives
the item's status). A provider whose wire carries no sign of a cut reads none.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: what the model reads of a call that did not run, cut or unreadable. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The model reads that nothing
ran, and why: its call was cut when the response was cut short, so it can
call again, with less if the response ran out of room; its arguments could
not be read otherwise, so it can call again with valid ones.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: a response the provider ended because it could not parse or would not take the model's call, within the bound of an empty round. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A response the provider ended
because it could not parse the model's call, or would not take it (a call to
a tool the request did not enable), carries
no call at all: the tool loop MUST tell
the model that its call did not run and why (its call could not be read, or
the tool is not in the request: calling it again would end the same way),
within the bound it gives an empty
round, on any round and whatever text the round said, and a turn whose bound
runs out ends cut short (`empty_response`), never `completed`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Provider calls: a round that ran out of room before any answer after a tool round. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A round that ran
out of room before any answer after a tool round ends the turn `truncated`
and is not tried again, since the same room runs out again: the output cap
and the context window alike, read by the same rule as a response schema's
`truncated` (Section 6.7).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents: the option an implementation may offer to ask the model for a sentence with each call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A call's intent (normative).** An AI channel MAY ask its model to write,
with each call, one short sentence for the person saying what the call does,
so that a surface can show the agent's work ("Je recherche les fichiers texte
du projet.") rather than a tool's name and raw arguments.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents where an implementation offers them: the agent's option (tool_call_intents), off by default, and an agent with it off. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The option is the
agent's (`tool_call_intents`), off by default; off, nothing below applies and
schemas, arguments, events and rows are the same as without it. On:

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: the property each tool schema of a request is shown with. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **What the model is shown.** Each tool schema a request declares carries
  one optional string property more, `_roomkit_intent`, which asks for that
  sentence in the language of the conversation.
