requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: the request's copy of a schema and the tool's own schema. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It is added to the request's
  copy only: the tools' own schemas, which a call's arguments are checked
  against, a hook reads and a turn reports as declared, stay as their tools
  declared them.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: a schema that already declares _roomkit_intent, or is no object schema. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A schema that already declares `_roomkit_intent`, or is no
  object schema, is shown as it is, and the implementation logs it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on, with tool_call_intents_required on: the shown schema's required list. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
With the
  agent's `tool_call_intents_required` on (off by default), the property is
  listed in the shown schema's `required` too, for a model that leaves
  optional properties out; a schema whose `required` is no list is shown as
  it is.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on, with tool_call_intents_required on: a call that comes without the property. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The requirement asks the model and refuses no call: a call that
  comes without the property runs, with no intent.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on, with tool_call_intents_only: the tools whose schemas carry the property. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The agent's
  `tool_call_intents_only`, a list of tool names (absent by default, which
  asks every tool), limits the property to the tools it names: the others'
  schemas are shown as their tools declared them, and a host renders those
  calls from their arguments.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on, with tool_call_intents_only: a call to a tool the list does not name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The list limits what is shown, not what is read:
  a call to any tool is treated as below.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: where the loop takes the property out of a served call's arguments. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Where it is taken.** At the one point a complete call enters the loop,
  before its start row, its `TOOL_CALL_START` and its gate, the property is
  removed from the arguments of a call the loop serves, whatever its value,
  and its value becomes the call's `intent`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: a tool whose own schema declares the property, and a call marked partial. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool whose own schema declares
  the property keeps it as its argument and its call has no intent; a call
  whose arguments do not read (marked partial) is left as it is.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: the arguments the handler, BEFORE_TOOL_USE, the policy and the schema check see. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
So the
  handler, `BEFORE_TOOL_USE`, the policy and the schema check see the tool's
  arguments only, and a closed schema (`additionalProperties: false`) does
  not refuse the call over the property.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: roomkit_intent, the property written without its leading underscore. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A model that drops the property's
  leading underscore writes `roomkit_intent`: it is taken the same way, and
  removed with the property when both come, the property's value being the
  intent, unless the tool's own schema declares `roomkit_intent`, which then
  stays its argument.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: the value that makes an intent, and its normalization. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **What it becomes.** Only a string is an intent. Each control character
  (general category Cc) becomes a space, the bidirectional formatting
  characters (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069) are
  removed, each run of white space (Unicode White_Space) becomes one space,
  and the text is trimmed, cut at 200 characters (Unicode scalar values) and
  trimmed again. Absent, null, not a string or empty after this, the call has
  no intent.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: what an intent never does to its call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An intent never fails a call, never changes its outcome, and is
  never interpreted as markup or code.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: where an intent rides, and a call without one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Where it rides.** On the call, on every report of it (`BEFORE_TOOL_USE`,
  `ON_TOOL_CALL`, a refusal, a cut call, Section 9.3), on the ephemeral
  `TOOL_CALL_START` and `TOOL_CALL_END` beside each call's id, on both stored
  rows (`ToolCallContent.intent`, Section 5.3) and on a turn's stream items
  across processes (Section 10.6.4); each carries it only when the call has
  one: a payload, a row or a frame of a call without one has no `intent`
  key, and a reader takes a row with no `intent` key as a call without one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: calls under one id in one round. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Calls under one id in one round keep their own (Section 12.4).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents: what the model reads back of a call's intent, with the option on and off. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **What the model reads back.** A replay shows the model its call with its
  intent, as normalized, back in `_roomkit_intent` among its arguments (a
  value that made no intent is not replayed), in the turn's next rounds and
  in later turns (The tools of earlier turns, below) while the option is
  on; off, a later turn replays the arguments alone.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: a BEFORE_TOOL_USE rewrite and the model's history. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
  `BEFORE_TOOL_USE` rewrite never reaches the model's history, as without it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: what an intent grants, what an approval shows of the call, and the call's states and outcomes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **What it is not.** Display text the model wrote: it grants nothing, it is
  not what an approval shows of the call (its arguments are), and it says
  nothing of what the call did; states and outcomes stay the engine's.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents on: a hook and a call's intent. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook
  cannot change it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents: the calls they do not apply to, an external agent's (ACP) and a provider-served call's (the sentence also names a realtime session's own calls, Section 12.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Where it does not apply.** A realtime session's own calls (Section
  12.4), an external agent's calls (Section 6.4, ACP) and the calls a
  provider serves itself carry no intent: their schemas are not the
  channel's to show.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Call intents, realtime (media feature realtime): an agent with the option that a realtime session delegates to (Section 12.4.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An agent with the option that a realtime session
  delegates to takes the property out of its calls' arguments in its own
  loop, but its calls are reported through the session's door, whose
  reports carry no intent (Section 12.4.1).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Continuation policy, the integrator's choice: what the policy is given and answers. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**An answer that did not act.** An AI channel MAY carry a continuation policy:
given the text a round ended on, the instruction that makes the model go on, or
nothing when the answer stands (a host's recognizer of an announced action, "I
will check that", say).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Continuation policy: the rounds the loop consults it on. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The loop consults it only for a round that ended
naturally, with text and without a call: not cut short (Section 6.4 above), not
a call it could not parse, not a refusal, and with a tool declared, since going
on means acting.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Continuation policy: the stop reasons that count as a natural stop, read alike by every provider. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A round that ended `stop` stopped naturally, whatever its
provider's own word for it (Section 6.7), and no other: a truncation, a filter,
a refusal or a stream that ended without saying why is never one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Continuation policy: its bound, shared with an empty round's, and the loop's guards. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The policy shares the bound of an empty round, and the loop keeps
its guards: no continuation after a cancellation or a force-stop, nor past the
turn's deadline or budget.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Continuation policy: what a continuation hands the next round, and the round's segment already sent. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A continuation hands the next round the text as the
assistant's message, then the instruction as the user's; the text already
reached the room as the round's segment and is neither repeated nor withdrawn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel: a round the loop tries again (an empty one, one whose call could not be parsed, one the policy continues) and its segment. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Any round the loop tries again (an empty one, one whose call could not be
parsed, one the policy continues) ends its segment there, as a call's start
does, so the next round's text never runs on from it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AI channel: a streamed response segment whose text is blank, empty or whitespace only. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A segment whose text is
blank, empty or whitespace only (a reasoning model's line break before its
call), says nothing: no row is stored, no channel is delivered it, a channel
that buffers the stream reads it as no text, and `ON_AI_RESPONSE`'s segments
leave it out; the stream's reader still reads its deltas, and the record it
would have carried goes to the turn's last message, else its last row.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Continuation policy: a turn whose policy still asks once the bound has run out. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn
whose policy still asks once the bound has run out ends `unfinished`, never
`completed`: the loop reaches its end (its end marker, `ON_AI_RESPONSE`), and
running out of the bound never raises out of the loop.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy, the integrator's choice: the events the channel would answer, each decided speak, offer or silent. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Whether the agent speaks.** An AI channel MAY carry a speak policy, which
decides on every event the channel would answer whether the agent speaks now,
offers to, or stays silent: an agent in a conversation with several people, or
listening to one who thinks aloud, does not answer every turn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: an instruction (§10.1.1), a delegated task's hand-back among them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An instruction
(Section 10.1.1), a delegated task's hand-back (Section 23.3) among them, is not
submitted to it: the application asked for that turn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: when the channel consults it in a turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The channel consults the
policy once per event, after building the turn's context and before
`BEFORE_AI_GENERATION`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: the recent events a policy reads, and an event withheld from the channel at delivery (§7.5 rule 8). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The recent events a policy reads are those the channel
may know, as its context has them (Section 7.5 rule 8): a policy may hand them
to a classifier outside, and an event withheld from the channel at delivery
MUST NOT reach it that way.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: the SpeakPolicy interface, the SpeakTurn it decides and the SpeakDecision it returns. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
SpeakPolicy (interface)
├── decide(turn: SpeakTurn) → SpeakDecision
└── forget_room(room_id: string)        # Optional: drop what it keeps of a room the channel joins or leaves

SpeakTurn
├── event: RoomEvent                    # The event the turn would answer (its trigger)
├── recent: list<RoomEvent>             # The conversation the turn reads, `event` excluded, oldest first, the agent's answers included:
│                                       #   what came before `event`, and in a discussion what came after it up to the turn's start (§19.7.5)
├── people: list<string>                # Who takes part besides the agent, named as its context names them
├── channel_id: string                  # The agent's channel: its own answers in `recent` come from it
├── speakers: map<string, string>       # Who said `event` and each of `recent`, by event id, where the room names them
├── thought: Thought | null = null      # What the agent has in mind, when the channel has a thinker (below)
└── cut: CutReply | null = null         # The agent's answer cut off just before the event, when it has not spoken since (below)

SpeakDecision
├── mode: "speak" | "offer" | "silent"
├── reason: string = ""                 # Why, in a few words, for logs and hooks
├── judgments: map<string, float> = {}  # What the policy weighed, by name, each in [0, 1] or its own scale
├── notes: list<string> = []            # Blocks the turn's notes carry when the agent speaks or offers
└── final: bool = false                 # A silence the agent's thought will not change (below); only on `silent`
```

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: a speak decision. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `speak` runs the turn as without a policy; the decision's notes join the
  turn's notes (below) before `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION`, which sees them.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: an offer decision. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `offer` runs the turn with one more block: offer, in one short sentence, what
  the agent could add, without giving it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: a silent decision and the turn it does not run. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `silent` runs no turn: no generation, `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` does not fire,
  nothing is delivered and no answer names the event (Section 8.5).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: the event of a silent decision, as the room stores it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The event
  is stored as any event is: the conversation is the agent's memory whether it
  spoke or not.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: the bound on the wait for a decision. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: The channel bounds the wait for a decision (2 s by default).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: a policy that fails or does not decide in time. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A policy that
fails or does not decide in time does not silence the agent: the channel logs
it and runs the turn as without a policy, and the decision it reports is
`speak` with the reason `fallback`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: ON_SPEAK_DECISION and what it carries for every decision. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every decision fires `ON_SPEAK_DECISION`
with the event, the channel and the decision, how long the policy took to
decide (the bound, when it did not decide in time), whether it was asked
again once the agent thought, the thought it was decided with and whether the
decision is late (below), so that what an agent left unanswered, why, and what
deciding cost can be followed and measured without wrapping the policy.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: a channel without a policy, and a policy that always speaks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
channel without a policy answers every message and instruction but an edit
or a delete, which opens no turn and is submitted to no policy (Section
10.3), and decides nothing; a policy that always speaks reports each
decision, a baseline to measure another against.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: a turn the channel's strategy takes in a room (§19.7), and a discussion's turn in answer to a message (§19.7.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn the
channel's strategy takes in a room (Section 19.7) is not submitted to it
either, save a turn a discussion gives in answer to a message (Section
19.7.5): that one is the agent's own answer to the room, and is submitted to
it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: the agent's identity, which the policy holds from when it is made. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The agent's identity is the policy's own: a policy that judges whether
the agent was addressed is told its name when it is made.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: the decision the SYNC hooks of ON_SPEAK_DECISION leave, MODIFY and BLOCK. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The channel acts on the decision its `ON_SPEAK_DECISION` hooks leave, as on
any SYNC trigger's payload (Section 9.3). Its SYNC hooks run in order before
the channel acts: a MODIFY replaces the decision with the one its payload
carries, and a BLOCK leaves the agent silent, with the reason `blocked by
<hook>` (`hook_error:<hook>` for the failure of a fail-closed hook).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: what the channel reads off a MODIFY's payload. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only the
decision is read off a MODIFY's payload: the event decided on, the room and
the channel stay the channel's.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: the ASYNC hooks of ON_SPEAK_DECISION. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its ASYNC hooks then observe the decision that
stands.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: what an application takes in code of a decision, an offer become a raised hand and a silence and the notes of the turn it later gives the agent; only the application keeps it, the channel acting on the decision its hooks leave (RK-6.4-145). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An application so takes in code an action the decision calls for,
rather than leaving it to the model: an offer becomes a raised hand and a
silence, and once the agent is given the floor its turn's notes say what it
raised its hand for.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: a hook of ON_SPEAK_DECISION that fails, and a room whose hook context cannot be built. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The trigger is fail-open: a hook that fails changes
nothing, and a room whose hook context cannot be built keeps the policy's
decision, unless a hook registered there fails closed, which leaves the agent
silent as that hook's own failure would.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: a silence a hook leaves, and the thinker. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A silence a hook leaves is thought
about as any other (rule 1 below).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: the people a SpeakTurn names. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The people are those who take part besides the agent (*Who takes part*,
below), or, when more, the distinct speakers named in the recent events: one
microphone is one participant but may carry several diarized voices.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Speak policy: how a speaker is named in a SpeakTurn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
speaker is named as the turn's context names speakers: the name the sender's
transport stamped on the event, else the participant's display name.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy, where RoomKit provides it (Section 6.8): its one call and its composition, in order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.

§6.4 Classifier speak policy: what its questions count as a speaker who has not finished, which is the wording of the questions it asks a model, shown by a review of that wording or by a live model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A speaker has not finished when the turn ends cut off or says they are not
done: a hesitation inside a turn whose last sentence is complete, or saying
one does not know, is no unfinished turn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: what its questions count as addressing the agent, which is the wording of the questions it asks a model, shown by a review of that wording or by a live model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn about the agent said to
someone else, or asking someone else to tell or explain something to it, does
not address it: that person speaks next.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: what its questions count as a request for quiet, which is the wording of the questions it asks a model, shown by a review of that wording or by a live model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Asking the agent whether it is ready
to listen expects an answer, and is no request for quiet.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: the judgments reported with its decision. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Each judgment is reported with the decision.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: its questions and its composition, replaceable. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its questions can be replaced by
name, and its composition by an implementation of its own.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy told the languages the agent answers in. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Told the languages
the agent answers in, it also judges the language the speaker speaks, over
their recent turns, so that one misheard word does not switch it, and its
decision's notes say which language to answer in.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: a classifier that fails. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A classifier that fails
falls back as any policy does: the agent speaks, unless the room listens
(below).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: a request to stay quiet as a state of the room, kept per room in memory, and the channel's forget_room on a room it joins or leaves. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Staying quiet when asked.** A request to stay quiet or only listen from now
on is a state of the room, not a judgment remade on every turn: re-judged from
the recent turns, it faded as they passed, and was lost once it left them. The
classifier policy keeps it per room, in memory as the thought is (rule 6
below): the channel has the policy forget a room it joins or leaves
(`forget_room`), so a room that reuses an id inherits no request.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: the turn that sets the listening state. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It is set
when a turn asks the agent to stay quiet or only listen until told otherwise:
that turn is silent, and final.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: what the classifier reads and is asked while a request to stay quiet stands. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The classifier reads the request with every
turn, with who made it and bounded as any text from outside, so that each
judgment is made knowing it, and is asked, instead of that request, whether
the turn puts a question or a request to the agent itself and whether it lets
the agent talk again.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy while the room listens: a turn not put to the agent. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
While the room listens:

- the agent is silent, and the decision is final (below), unless what it
  has in mind answers or corrects the turn as surely as the policy's
  proactivity asks of an open room (below), the speaker has finished, neither
  postpones it nor asks for quiet, and no question put to someone else waits
  for them: the agent then offers, asking for the floor without taking it
  (an application may show it as a raised hand), and the room goes on
  listening;

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy while the room listens: a question or a request put to the agent and addressing it directly. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a question or a request put to the agent and addressing it directly (its
  name, or "you") is answered, and the room goes on listening: answering one
  question does not lift a request to stay quiet; a speaker who has not
  finished, postpones it or asks for quiet is not answered;

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy while the room listens: a turn that lets the agent talk again. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a turn that lets the agent talk again ends the state, and is decided as
  without it;

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy while the room listens: a turn the policy cannot judge. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a turn the policy cannot judge (no text, a classifier that fails) is silent:
  falling back to speaking would break the request.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy: a turn whose classifier call another turn's change of state overlaps. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn is decided as it was judged: when another turn of the room starts or
ends the state during the classifier call, the answers to the questions asked
decide it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy while the room listens: a conversation with one person. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A conversation with one person does not make every request the
agent's while the room listens: a question said aside and one put to the agent
read alike without the address.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy while the room listens: a cut answer. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A cut answer is not resumed.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy while the room listens: the judgment each decision reports. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each decision
made while the room listens reports it among its judgments (`listening`).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Answer-only speak policy, where RoomKit provides it: an event whose speaker it does not answer, or whom the room does not name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
RoomKit also provides a policy that answers only some people, around any
other: an agent that listens to everyone in the room (a television, a
meeting it assists one person in) but answers only them. An event whose
speaker, as `speakers` names them, is not one of them is decided `silent`
with the reason `only listened to`, final, without asking the policy it wraps, and
so is an event whose speaker the room does not name.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Answer-only speak policy: the people it passes on to the policy it wraps. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The people it passes on
are only those it answers, the speaker among them even when no participant
record names them so (a microphone's record and the voice its transport
stamps), so that a voice only listened to never makes a conversation with one
person a group one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Answer-only speak policy: an event it leaves silent, as the room stores it and the thinker reads it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event so left silent is stored, and thought about, as
any other: the agent hears it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Answer-only speak policy: how a speaker is matched. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A speaker is matched by the name the room gives
them, kept to a name's characters as the room keeps it and ignoring case: this
chooses whom the agent answers, it is not an access control.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, the integrator's choice on a channel that has a speak policy: what a thinker is. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**What the agent thinks.** An AI channel that has a speak policy MAY also
carry a thinker: what the agent thinks while it listens, its answer, when it is
silent, to "what are you thinking about?".

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker: what a thought is and what it is about, which is what a model writes under the thinker's instructions, shown by a review of those instructions or by a live model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The thought is neither memory (the
room's history is, Section 20) nor a summary: what the agent makes of what is
said, what it would say if given the turn, and whether that cannot wait. It is
about what the agent hears: what is being talked about, what the speaker is
doing (asking, telling, thinking aloud, talking to someone else, reading
something), and what the agent makes of it, the people named; never about the
agent itself (what it said or did, whether it should speak, how it is seen).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker: what a thought holds of what the agent would say, which is what a model writes under the thinker's instructions, shown by a review of those instructions or by a live model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
What it would say holds only what it would say to the people about what is
being discussed: never a rule for itself, nor what it does not know.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker: a thought when the topic changes, which is what a model writes under the thinker's instructions, shown by a review of those instructions or by a live model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When the
topic changes, the thought starts again from the new one, keeping of the
previous only what still concerns it: a thought rewritten from itself on every
call drifts into its own concerns.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker: the Thought it returns and the Thinker interface. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
Thought
├── text: string = ""                   # What the agent thinks, in the first person
├── want_to_say: list<string> = []      # What it would say if given the turn, most important first, three at most
└── urgent: bool = false                # What it wants to say cannot wait

Thinker (interface)
└── think(previous: Thought, context: AIContext) → Thought
```

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 1: the events it runs on. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
1. The thinker runs only on events the policy left silent: a turn the agent
   answers waits for no thought.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 1: the context the channel builds for it and passes through BEFORE_AI_GENERATION with the purpose thought. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The channel builds the event's context as for
   an answer (the agent's own prompt, the conversation it may know), every
   speaker named, the one person of a one-to-one conversation included (an
   answer's context leaves that conversation unlabelled), passes it
   through `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` with the purpose `thought`, and hands what the
   hooks left to the thinker with the previous thought.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 1: a BEFORE_AI_GENERATION hook that blocks the thought. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook that blocks it
   keeps the previous thought.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 1: the context a thinker reaches a model with. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A thinker MUST NOT reach a model with a context
   that hook did not see: whatever an application keeps from a model there
   (consent, redaction, a budget) holds for the thought too.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 2: thinker calls per room, and events that arrive during a call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
2. One thinker call runs at a time per room. Events that arrive during a call
   are thought about in the next one, from the latest context; none is queued.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 3: the bound on the wait for a thought. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: 3. The channel waits for that thought up to a bound (1.5 s by default).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 3: a thought that comes back in time with something to say. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When
   it comes back in time with something to say, the policy is asked again on
   the same event, with the thought: the agent may raise its hand on a turn it
   first listened to. Each decision fires `ON_SPEAK_DECISION`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 3: a decision the policy marks final. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A decision the
   policy marks final is a silence no thought changes now (a room that
   listens, a voice only listened to): the thinker thinks, and the channel
   does not wait for it, so the next turn is not held back.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 3: a thought that comes back after its event was decided, while no later event was given to the thinker. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A thought that comes back after its event was decided (past the bound, or
   on a final decision) with something to say, while no later event was given
   to the thinker, is decided late: the policy is asked again on that event
   with it, and the decision fires `ON_SPEAK_DECISION` marked late.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 3: a late decision and the turn it does not run. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
No turn
   runs on a late decision, whatever it says: the event's turn is over, and
   the conversation may have moved on. Its hooks act on it (raise a hand, or
   deliver an instruction for the agent to speak, Section 10.1.1).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 3: a thought a later event reads. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A later
   event reads the thought itself, and no late decision is owed to the
   earlier one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 4: the thought when the agent speaks or offers on an event submitted to the policy. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
4. When the agent speaks or offers on an event submitted to the policy, the
   turn's notes carry its thought, and what it wanted to say is then empty: it
   is said, or offered.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 4: a thinker call running meanwhile, or on a context taken while one of the agent's turns ran. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A thinker call running meanwhile does not bring it
   back, nor does one on a context taken while one of the agent's turns ran
   in the room: what it would say is that answer, not in its context yet.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 4: an instruction and the thought. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
   instruction carries no thought and empties nothing.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 4: the thought in the turn's notes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The thought is
   a model's reading of what people said, so whatever they said can reach it:
   the notes MUST carry it quoted (as any text from outside, below), bounded,
   and named as information to weigh, not as the runtime's instructions.
   Asked what it is thinking, the agent answers with it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 5: a thinker that fails, or the end of its wait. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: 5. A thinker that fails, or the end of its wait, keeps the previous thought.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, rule 6: where the thought lives, a restart, and a room the channel is attached to or detached from. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
6. The thought is the channel's, per room, in memory: it is not stored, and a
   restart starts from an empty thought, as does a room the channel is
   attached to or detached from, so that a room reusing an id never inherits
   another conversation's thought.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker: ON_THOUGHT and what it carries for a new thought. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every new thought fires `ON_THOUGHT` with the room, the channel and the thought,
the one it replaces, and how long the thinker call that brought it took; a
thought emptied because the agent spoke (rule 4) came from no call and carries
no duration.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker: a call that fails or brings back the same thought. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A call that fails or brings back the same thought fires nothing.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker: the thought a speak policy reads. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A policy reads it in `SpeakTurn.thought`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy with a thinker: what it also judges of the thought. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The classifier policy then also
judges whether what the agent wants to say answers a question or a need still
open at the turn (asked in it, or before it and answered by no one since, the
agent included), or corrects or warns about what the turn says, and whether a
question put to someone other than the agent still waits for that person's
first try (they have not answered it, said they do not know, nor given up).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy with a thinker: speaking or offering on the thought, and its proactivity. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only wondered about and knowing the answer, the agent speaks rather than
offers; not addressed, it offers when that judgment reaches the policy's
proactivity (0.5 by default, lower is more eager), half of it when the thought
is urgent, never on urgency alone.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy with a thinker: a question that waits for someone else, and a question put to everyone. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Unless the thought is urgent, a question
that waits for someone else is theirs to answer first: wondered about, the
agent offers rather than speaks, and not addressed, it stays silent. A
question put to everyone waits for no one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Thinker, where RoomKit provides one: the thinker on an AI provider that answers under a JSON schema, and a mock. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
RoomKit provides a thinker on any AI provider that answers under a JSON schema
(Section 6.7), whose instructions the application can replace, and a mock.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer, voice (media feature voice): the record a barge-in (§12.3.13) leaves in the room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A cut answer.** When the agent's answer is cut off by a barge-in (Section
12.3.13), the room holds a record of it that names the answer.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer: the CutReply the AI channel reads of the record. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The AI channel
uses it twice:

```
CutReply
├── text: string                        # What the agent was saying: the text handed to speech when it was cut
├── played_ms: int                      # How much of it played before the cut
└── at: datetime                        # When it was cut
```

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer: the mark after a cut answer in the context of the agent's next turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- In the context the agent's next turn reads, that answer is followed by a
  mark that says when it was cut and quotes how far the person heard it
  (`[The person cut you off during this answer, 5.7 s in: they heard it up to
  “…” and not the rest.]`), rather than reading as an answer heard whole.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer: the AI channel's estimate of how far the person heard. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
  quote is the AI channel's estimate, and it SHOULD end early rather than
  late: a model told the person heard words they did not goes on past them.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer, where RoomKit estimates the quote: the words taken with no word timed by the TTS, and too little played. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
With no word timed by the TTS, RoomKit takes the words by their letters at
  the share of the answer's audio that played, less two words, or at 11
  letters a second when that share is unknown; with too little played to
  quote, the mark says the person heard little or none of it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer: the quoted words in the mark. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The words are
  the agent's, which a participant may have led it to say: they MUST be
  given as a quote (below, "Text from outside in a model's context"), a copy
  of a runtime mark in them replaced; a long quote keeps its end, where the
  person stopped hearing.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer: the turn's notes while the history window holds a cut answer. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
While the history window holds a cut answer, the
  turn's notes say how one reads, and
  that an answer of the agent's without the mark was heard to its end:
  without it, a model asked whether it was cut off answers for the last cut
  it reads, however many whole answers followed it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer: SpeakTurn.cut. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A speak policy reads it in `SpeakTurn.cut` when the event came after the cut
  and the agent has not answered since.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy with a cut answer: what it also judges. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The classifier policy then also judges
  whether the turn leaves the agent free to go on (an acknowledgement, a
  thanks, a short reaction, talking over it by accident) or wants the turn (a
  question, a request, a correction, asking it to stop).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Classifier speak policy with a cut answer: a turn that leaves the agent free to go on. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Free to go on, and
  not asked for quiet nor talking over an unfinished speaker, the agent speaks
  with the reason `resume after cut`, its notes asking it to go on from where it
  was cut without repeating what was heard.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer, voice (media feature voice): what the record keeps, and where the quote is estimated. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The record does not guess which part of the answer was heard: it keeps the
text handed to speech, how long it played, and the share of its audio when
that is known. The quote above is estimated where the model reads it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer: the records that count, written by a voice channel of the room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only a record a voice channel of the room wrote counts: `internal`, with no
participant, its source a channel bound to the room as voice, and
`interrupted` exactly `true`. Event metadata is anyone's to write, and a
record taken at its word would put a sender's text in the agent's mouth as
its own.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Cut answer: a malformed record. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A record whose `answer_responds_to` is neither a string nor absent is
skipped, and a `played_ms` that is not a non-negative number reads as 0: a
malformed record never fails the turns of the room it stays in.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Generation hooks: BEFORE_AI_GENERATION fires once per turn (purpose answer) and once per thinker call (purpose thought). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**What the generation hooks see:** `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` fires once per turn
(purpose `answer`), and once per thinker call (purpose `thought`, above, with
the context the thinker would read, its tools never called), so a hook tells
the agent's turn from its thinking.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Generation hooks: a turn's BEFORE_AI_GENERATION event, its context, its trigger and its tools, the toolset the tool policy and skill gating leave. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
For a turn it fires
with the context the turn starts from and the event the turn answers (`trigger`,
Section 8.5), and its `tools` are the turn's toolset
as the tool policy and skill gating leave it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Generation hooks: the tools a turn's hook is shown without Tool Search. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Without Tool Search that is the
first round's declaration, the tool that reads back a large result aside
(below).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Generation hooks: the tools a turn's hook is shown under Tool Search, and what the first round declares of them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Under Tool Search it is the whole catalogue the
turn may reach, before Tool Search collapses it: the first round declares the
pinned floor, the tools orchestration injected (Section 21.1), the tools the
hook added and the discovery tools, all taken from what the hook left, and a
tool `find_tools` reveals enters the declaration of the *next* round. A hook
that sees only the first round's declaration cannot withdraw a deferred tool,
which `find_tools` would then reveal.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Generation hooks: the toolset the hook leaves is the turn's, a tool it removes and a tool it adds or edits. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The toolset the hook leaves is the turn's: a tool it removes MUST NOT be
declared at any later round of the turn, MUST NOT be named by `find_tools` or
`list_tools` nor recovered at call time, and a call naming it MUST be refused,
a tool the channel provides itself included; a tool it adds or edits stays as
the hook left it, subject to the tool policy and skill gating, and a tool it
adds is declared at every round of the turn, never deferred by Tool Search.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Generation hooks: a tool the hook adds served by the channel's handler, a call to a tool it edited checked against its schema, and a tool the channel serves itself. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool it adds is served by the channel's tool handler, and a call to a tool
it edited is checked against the schema it left (Section 21.1); a tool the
channel serves itself keeps its own definition, the hook able to withdraw it,
never to redefine it nor to add a tool under its name.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Generation hooks under Tool Search: a hook that withdraws a tool from the first round only has withdrawn nothing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
hook that withdraws a tool from the first round only has withdrawn nothing.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Generation hooks under Tool Search: a tool the hook adds is never named by find_tools. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A tool the hook adds is never named by `find_tools`, being declared already.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Toolset: a call names a tool the round declared, or one Tool Search recovers at call time. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Once the turn's toolset is resolved, a call MUST name a tool the round
declared, an empty declaration included, or one Tool Search recovers from the
turn's catalogue at call time: a round that declares nothing admits no other
call.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Toolset: a tool of the channel's own that the turn does not offer, refused as an undeclared tool on every path. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The channel's own tools are no exception: one the turn does not offer
(`find_tools` while Tool Search hides nothing, `run_skill_script` with no
executor) is refused as any undeclared tool is, on every path (Section 12.4).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Skill activation: it counts only once its activate_skill call is served. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Likewise a skill activation (Section 24.4) counts only
once its `activate_skill` call is served: an ON_TOOL_CALL BLOCK or a failure
activates nothing, whatever the model read.

requirements.applies: §6.4 find_tools reveal: a blocked or failed call, and a search that finds nothing, reveal nothing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
So does a `find_tools` reveal, on
every path: a BLOCK or a failure reveals nothing, not for the next round nor
for a later turn, and a search that finds nothing reveals nothing, the reveal
window left as it was.

requirements.applies: §6.4 find_tools reveal: a served call reveals its matches whatever an ON_TOOL_CALL hook replaced its result with. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A served call reveals its matches whatever an
ON_TOOL_CALL hook replaced its result with, as a served activation opens its
gates.

requirements.applies: §6.4 find_tools reveal, realtime (media feature realtime): when a realtime session declares what a served find_tools call revealed, and a reconfiguration while the call was judged. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A realtime session declares what a served `find_tools` call revealed
once its result went out, its call id belonging to the connection a
reconfiguration can replace, and declares nothing of it when a
reconfiguration gave the session another catalogue while the call was judged:
its matches were found in the catalogue that left.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Skill activation hint: the tools an activation's hint names are revealed as find_tools matches are (a realtime session's included), and an activation whose answer carries no hint reveals nothing and is refused. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
So for the tools an
activation's hint names. An activation whose answer carries no hint (it
finds no skill and no tool matches the name, or the skill exists but is
unavailable) reveals nothing and is refused, as a reference or a script asked of a skill
the registry does not offer is.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool Search: a tool recovered at call time joins the reveal window once it answered the call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool Tool Search recovers at call time joins the
reveal window only once the tool answered the call (served, failed, or its
result withheld by an ON_TOOL_CALL hook), as the room's tool memory keeps any
tool used.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Toolset: a tool the model called and that answered stays declared for the rest of the turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool the model called and that answered MUST remain declared for
the rest of the turn, even after a later `find_tools` replaces the search
window.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Toolset: a tool whose call was refused solely for invalid arguments is declared for the turn's next rounds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool admitted by the catalogue, tool policy and skill gates whose
call was refused solely because the model's arguments were invalid MUST also
be declared for the turn's next rounds, so the provider can parse a corrected
call against its schema.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Toolset: the declaration of a tool called with invalid arguments never enters the room's memory of tools used. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
This declaration is not an executed call and MUST NOT
enter the room's memory of tools used.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Toolset: other refusals, and a call nothing served, reveal nothing and leave the round's other reveals. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Other refusals (an access gate,
BEFORE_TOOL_USE, the handler's refusal), or a call nothing served, reveal
nothing and leave every other reveal of the round as it was.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Retention, realtime (media feature realtime): a reconfigurable realtime session retains a called tool for its current catalogue, publishes a needed schema after the call's result, and a call from an earlier catalogue reveals nothing into its replacement. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The same rule applies to a reconfigurable realtime session: retain a called
tool for its current catalogue, publish a needed schema only after delivering
the call's result, and discard retained names when the session ends or its
catalogue is replaced. A call from an earlier catalogue MUST NOT reveal tools
into its replacement.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Retention: search matches not called follow the search window, and retention widens no access and activates no skill. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Search matches that have not been called still follow
the search window; retention does not widen access or activate a skill.

requirements.applies: §6.4 declared_tools: ON_AI_RESPONSE carries the union of the turn's declarations, each tool with its definition and the reason it was visible. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`ON_AI_RESPONSE` MUST therefore carry the turn's whole declaration as
`declared_tools`: the union, over every generation round of the turn, of the
tools the channel handed the provider, each with the name, description and
parameters as declared and the reason it was visible (`always` when Tool Search
did not gate it, `pinned`, `sticky` or `revealed` when it did, the earliest
reason winning).

requirements.applies: §6.4 declared_tools: keyed by name in first-declaration order, one entry per name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The union is keyed by name in first-declaration order, one
entry per name: the reveal window slides from one `find_tools` to the next, and
a per-round rewrite would lose a tool revealed earlier in the same turn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 declared_tools: a turn without Tool Search reports its single declaration, the declaration RoomKit made. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn
that runs without Tool Search MUST report its single declaration through the
same field, so a host has one reading whatever the turn's mode. The field
reports the declaration RoomKit made, not the provider's wire form of it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 declared_tools: empty for an intelligence channel whose toolset is not RoomKit's to declare (an external ACP agent). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
intelligence channel whose toolset is not RoomKit's to declare (an external ACP
agent, below) leaves it empty.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Declaration from round to round: within a turn the declaration changes only where a tool must appear, in the toolset's order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The declaration from round to round.** A provider that caches requests
reads each one as a prefix, in the order tools, system prompt, messages, and a
declaration that gains, loses or reorders a tool invalidates everything cached
after the tools, the history included: the next round is billed as if nothing
were cached. Within a turn the declaration SHOULD therefore change only where
a tool must appear, one `find_tools` reveals or one a skill activation opens
(Section 24.4), and its order is the toolset's, the same from one turn to the
next.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Declaration from round to round: the tool that reads back a large result, declared from the first round after the others, and when the generation hook sees it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The tool that reads back a large result (Section 21.5) is declared from
the first round of any turn that declares a tool, after the others, so the
declaration does not change when a result is stored; the generation hook sees
it once the room holds a stored result, and may withdraw it then.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard, forced round: it keeps the round's declaration, runs none of its calls, and the turn ends force_stopped. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A round the
implementation forces to
answer, when an anti-loop guard stops a model that keeps repeating a refused
call, keeps the round's declaration and tells the model that no further call
will run: none of that round's calls runs, and the turn ends `force_stopped`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard: the third identical call of a turn refused before it runs, in words that say so, its outcome a refusal. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The anti-loop guard.** A small model can re-issue one call round after round and
burn the whole turn without answering. Within one turn, an implementation counts
each call by its tool's name and its arguments, whatever the order of their keys,
and refuses the third call with the same arguments before it runs, in words that
say so, the outcome a refusal (Section 9.3).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard: find_tools and list_tools refused at their second identical call, and those names under the channel's tool_search off. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool the channel keeps for itself
that reads what cannot change within the turn (`find_tools`, `list_tools`) is
refused at its second, whether or not a search hides anything; under the channel's
own `tool_search` off, those names are any tool's.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard: a call past its gate counted on the arguments it would run with. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call past its gate is counted
on the arguments it would run with, once repaired and once `BEFORE_TOOL_USE` left
them.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard: a call its gate refuses counted on the model's arguments, and the guard's words in place of the gate's past the limit. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call its gate refuses is counted on the arguments the model wrote, and past
the limit the model reads the guard's words in place of the gate's.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard: a model that re-issues a refused call three times past the limit is force-stopped. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A model that
re-issues a refused call three times past the limit is force-stopped, the forced
round above.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard: a served call of a changes_state tool starts the turn's counts again. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool whose definition declares that its calls change what later
calls read (`changes_state`, false by default: a file edited, a row written)
starts the turn's counts again once a call of it is served, the counts of identical
answers below included, all but that call's own: a test rerun after each edit is
no repeat, and the same edit made a third time is still refused when no other
change came between (two changes made in turn start each other's counts again,
and only the round limit, the loop's time bound or a budget ends them).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard: a changes_state call that failed, was refused or was blocked starts nothing again. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call of it that
failed, was refused or was blocked starts nothing again.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Anti-loop guard: what the guard's words tell the model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The guard's words tell the
model to stop repeating the call; they do not ask it to answer now, which is the
forced round's to ask.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Settled answer: from the third identical answer of one tool in a turn, a note on what the model reads and on the call's row. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A model that varies its arguments never reaches that limit, so the guard also tells
it, and never refuses: from the third time one tool answers a call past its gate
with the same text in a turn, what the model reads of it, and the call's row with
it, carries a note saying the answer is settled, with how many times it came.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Settled answer: what the note compares, what the tool's observers read, and what is never noted. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The note
compares what the call answered, a failure's words too; the tool's observers read
its answer without the note, what a gate refused is never noted, nor is the guard's
own refusal, and a result of parts a model that sees reads is not compared.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AFTER_TOOL_ROUND: after which rounds it fires, and when. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Between two rounds.** `AFTER_TOOL_ROUND` fires after each round in which the
channel ran at least one call, once that round's results are in and before the
next round is built: not after a round cancelled before its calls ran, nor after
one whose calls were all served outside the channel.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AFTER_TOOL_ROUND: what its event carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its event carries the
round's index, its calls, the results the channel produced and the ones the
provider served, each in the order of the calls, and the names of the turn's
toolset as `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` is shown it: what the tool policy and skill
gating let the turn reach, Tool Search's whole catalogue included, nothing
withdrawn. A hook reads the round whole and names what it withdraws: the
calls of one round run concurrently, and a rule about them (one success among
failures, say) is a rule about the round.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AFTER_TOOL_ROUND: a hook's withdrawals, with every guarantee of a generation hook's, and the messages it adds after the round's results. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook MAY withdraw tools for the
rest of the turn, any name whether the event lists it or not, with every
guarantee of a withdrawal by `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` above (never declared
again, never named by `find_tools` or `list_tools` nor recovered, a call naming
it refused, a tool the channel provides itself included, never handed to an
external handler), and MAY add messages the next round reads after the round's
results. A withdrawal changes the declaration of the next round, the one
exception this hook makes to the declaration staying the same, and costs what a
changed declaration costs.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AFTER_TOOL_ROUND: a hook acts on its event in place, and a MODIFY that returns no event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook acts on the event it receives, in place: the
event a MODIFY returns is not read, but a MODIFY that returns none is an
unusable result (Section 9.3).

requirements.applies: §6.4 AFTER_TOOL_ROUND, where an implementation's hooks receive a copy of their own: the event a MODIFY returns is read. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation whose hooks receive a copy of
their own rather than the event reads instead the withdrawals and messages of
the event a MODIFY returns, to the same effect.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AFTER_TOOL_ROUND: a BLOCK, and a hook that raises, times out or returns an unusable result. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A BLOCK stops the hooks after it, as on any
SYNC trigger, and changes nothing of the round, which has run; a hook that
raises, times out or returns an unusable result is skipped, or, registered
fail-closed, stops the hooks after it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 AFTER_TOOL_ROUND belongs to a registered AI channel's tool loop: a reasoning backend's agent and an external agent do not fire it (the sentence also names a realtime session). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The hook belongs to a registered AI
channel's tool loop: a realtime session does not fire it, nor does a
reasoning backend's agent (not a registered channel), nor an external agent
that runs its own loop (Section 6.4, ACP).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: an AI channel's history carries its earlier turns' tool rounds at their place, as the turn sent them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The tools of earlier turns (normative).** An AI channel's history MUST carry
the rounds of tool calls its own earlier turns made, each at its place in the
conversation (after the turn's input, before its answer), the way the turn
itself sent it: the assistant's message holding the text the model wrote with
its calls, then the calls, then their results, as the tool messages the
provider's API carries. A recall of them riding the turn's input instead
reads to a model as something the participant asked, and models answer it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: a replayed call's arguments, as the model wrote them, under the model's id. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
round replays what the model was given, as it was given:

- the arguments it wrote, never a BEFORE_TOOL_USE rewrite of them, with its
  intent back among them while the agent asks for one (A call's intent,
  above), under the id the model gave the call;

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: a replayed call's result, as the model read it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- the result it read, whole: an ON_TOOL_CALL rewrite, or an oversized
  result's placeholder while the room still stores what it points to
  (Section 21.5); once it no longer does, the result's size alone.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: every call its turn ended is replayed, never a call cancelled before it answered nor a refused call under an invalid name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every call its turn ended is replayed, whatever its outcome or tool: a
refusal, a call nothing served, a discovery or housekeeping call of the
channel's own included; never a call cancelled before it answered, whose
result no model read, nor a refused call under a name outside
`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}`, which only a model's invented call carries and which
a vendor would refuse in every later request.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: the channel's own only, read from its stored rows. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
They are the channel's own only, read from its stored
rows (`TOOL_CALL_START`'s arguments and intent, `TOOL_CALL_END`'s result and
outcome), so they outlive the executor.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: an end row pairs with its turn's start row by id, first in, first out. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
end row pairs with the start row of its turn and id, first in, first out within
a round of that turn, so that two calls under one id each read their own result;
a call an earlier round left without its end stays without one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: a turn with no store, or an unreadable one, goes without them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn
with no store to read, or whose store cannot be read, goes without them rather
than failing.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: a round older than the history window is not replayed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A round older than the history window is not replayed: a history never opens
on the assistant's calls.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: a discussion's turn reads after its event the rounds of the turns that followed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A discussion's turn, which reads its event at its
place (Section 19.7.5), reads after it the rounds of the turns that followed.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: a later turn's first request opens with what the previous turn's last request sent, but for what the room does not keep. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Nothing shortens a round from one turn to the next: a later turn's first
request opens with what the previous turn's last request sent, then its
answer, so that a provider that caches a prompt's prefix keeps the history
(The prompt from turn to turn, below), but for what that request carried and
the room does not keep: the notes that rode its input, a round's reasoning
(Section 6.7).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: what bounds the replayed rounds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The history window, the memory's budget, which charges each
round to the event it reads with (Section 20), and a compaction, once a
provider refuses the context as too long (above), are what bound the rounds.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tools of earlier turns: an id the provider gave two calls is replayed as given. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An id the provider gave two calls, in one turn or two, is replayed as given:
the provider took it so.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Instructions of earlier turns: replayed at their place. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The instructions its earlier turns read
are replayed the same way, at their place (Section 10.1.1, The instruction a
turn read).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Instructions of earlier turns: a standalone turn replays none, and the turn's footprint counts them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A standalone turn replays none (Section 10.1.1), and the turn's
footprint counts them (Section 20).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Prompt from turn to turn: the system prompt stays the same from one turn to the next. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The prompt from turn to turn.** For the same reason, the system prompt SHOULD
stay the same from one turn to the next: a system prompt that changes
invalidates everything cached after it, the whole history included.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Turn notes: what changes between turns travels with the turn's input as notes, each passage set apart as data (the sentence also names what a vision provider last saw). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
What changes
between turns as the conversation works travels with the turn's input instead,
as notes: the room's plan, the room's background tasks and how far each got
(Section 23.4), how speakers are named when the history window holds
several (which speakers it holds changes as it slides), who takes part
when two people or more do (below; who is present changes as people come
and go), how a cut answer
reads while the window holds one (above, "A cut answer"), what a vision
provider last saw (Section 12.8.7), and what a memory provider retrieved for this turn
alone (Section 20.2), each passage set apart as data.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Turn notes: their place, after the turn's input in the same message, after the last user message, or a message of their own. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The notes follow the
turn's input (the participant's words, or the application's instruction) in the
same message, marked as the channel's, asking for nothing; when the
conversation does not end on such a
message (an input that reads as nothing is left out), they follow its last
message when it is a user's, and are a message of their own otherwise. They
come after the input, so what changes comes last and a provider that caches
a prefix keeps the input in it;
they are not a message of their own when the input is one, since a model whose
chat format requires alternating roles would refuse two in a row.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool images: for a model that sees, the two latest images the channel's tool calls returned follow the notes in the turn's input, under a header. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
For a model
that sees, the latest images the channel's own tool calls in the room returned
(two, newest last) follow the notes in the same message, each after the call
that returned it, under a header that sets them apart as data a tool returned,
never instructions; the notes then take a text part of their own, which a
hook's block joins. A replayed result says what an image showed in its tool's
words, never what it looks like, and a follow-up about a picture needs the
picture.
They ride the turn's input, never an assistant's message, where several
providers refuse an image.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool images: only an inline PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP data URI of 2,000,000 characters at most, from a live result, is kept. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only an image every vision provider takes is kept:
inline (a data URI, never a link, which may expire or be out of the vendor's
reach), PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, its data URI 2,000,000 characters at most, its
scheme and type read in any case, from a live result (never
history rebuilt from the store).

requirements.applies: §6.4 Tool images: after a turn whose content the provider refused, none of the room's tool images is replayed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn that replayed them and whose content
the provider refused replays none of the room's images after it: one the
provider refused would fail every later turn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Content refused: the provider errors that count as a refusal of the content. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The content is refused when the
turn's first request fails, before anything of it streamed, on a provider
error that is not retryable and is no authentication, payment, permission,
missing model or rate limit (HTTP 401, 402, 403, 404 or 429): a later round, or
a stream already under way, shows the images were taken.

requirements.applies: §6.4 Content refused: refusals a provider makes before any request, for something other than the content, are none, and its error says so. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
These refusals a
provider makes before any request, for something other than the content the
request carries, are no refusal of the content, and its error says so: a
response schema the model does not take or outside the portable subset
(Section 6.7), a model or tools its endpoint does not serve, a tool name the
vendor refuses or a tool it cannot declare.
