requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn's budget: the turn's cost is the sum of its responses' costs. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The turn's cost is the sum of its
responses' costs, never the cost of their summed usage.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn's budget: the check at each round boundary, and a turn that reached a budget or failed to answer past it ends budget_exceeded. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The loop checks them at each round boundary, on the usage the provider
reported for the generations so far: a turn that has reached a budget ends
there, `budget_exceeded`, running none of the calls its last generation asked
for and asking for no further generation, a retry of an empty answer included; a
final round that failed to answer past its budget ends `budget_exceeded` too.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn's budget: a budget that is not a positive number, or a cost budget with no known price, is a configuration error, and when it is reported. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
budget that is not a positive number, or a cost budget for a model with no known
price, is a configuration error, reported when the channel is built for a
channel budget and by the turn that reads it otherwise; a channel with a router
checks the price on the provider it names for each turn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn's budget: every generation of a turn is priced at the rate of the provider the turn started on, one a router hands over included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every generation of a
turn is priced at the rate of the provider the turn started on, one a router
hands to another provider included.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn that did not complete: ON_AI_RESPONSE reports a turn whose loop reached its end, cancelled between rounds or error for an interruption after a round. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A turn that did not complete.** `ON_AI_RESPONSE` reports a turn whose loop
reached its end, with the reason it ended for: `cancelled` for a cancellation
between rounds, `error` for a turn the provider interrupted after a round (a
turn constrained to a schema aside, Appendix A.9).

requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn that did not complete: what the hook carries, and the provider's error surfacing through the response stream once the hook has fired. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The hook carries what its rounds used, then the provider's error surfaces as
when the loop raises (ON_ERROR fires), through the turn's response stream once
the hook has fired.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn that did not complete: a turn whose loop did not reach its end (it raised, or its response stream was closed) fires no ON_AI_RESPONSE. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn whose loop did not reach its end MUST NOT fire it:
one that raised (the provider's interruption after a round aside), or one
whose response stream was
closed before the loop's end (a barge-in, a transport that stopped reading, a
consumer that refused the answer, a task cancelled from outside). Its
response never reached the end the hook reports, and a closed stream is never
reported as `completed`; what its rounds delivered stays in the room.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn that did not complete, where telemetry is configured: the llm.generate span of a turn whose loop did not reach its end. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its
`llm.generate` span MUST end `cancelled` or `error`, never `ok`, and never
stay open, and it carries what the rounds used, since no hook reports the
turn.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A turn that did not complete, where telemetry is configured: the span of a turn that reached its end cancelled or error. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The span of a turn that reached its end `cancelled` (a steering
`Cancel`) or `error` ends with that status too, never `ok`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: the keys a turn that reached its end records in its last MESSAGE's metadata. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The turn's record.** A turn that reached its end records it on its last
MESSAGE: `loop_end_reason` (the reason above), `ai_usage`
(what its rounds used) and, when its channel says so, `ai_last_usage` (what
its last generation used, null when that generation failed),
`ai_usage_complete` (whether every generation reported its input and output
counters at its end: one cut before it never did), `ai_model` and
`ai_provider` (what its last generation ran on, a
provider a router handed a generation to when it served it) in the message's
metadata.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: ON_AI_RESPONSE carries usage_complete beside its usage. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`ON_AI_RESPONSE` carries that completeness beside its usage
(`usage_complete`).

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: executor_id for a turn that ran on an executor other than the room owner's own (Section 10.6), none on the owner's own. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn that ran
on an executor other than the room owner's own (§10.6), whatever its end, also
records `executor_id` there, the id that executor took the turn under; a turn on
the owner's own executor records none.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: the message that carries it, the turn's final text or the last message the turn wrote. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
That message is the one of
the turn's final text or, when the turn has none (a cancellation between
rounds, an interruption), the last message the turn wrote.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: a turn that wrote no message records it on its last row, the end of its last call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn that wrote no
message at all (a first turn cut while its call runs) records it on its last
row, the end of its last call, with the same keys in that row's metadata.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: a response without tools records it, and a provider that streams text alone records no usage. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
response without tools records it too; a provider that streams text alone
reports no usage, and its record carries none.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: the stored row updated, ON_EVENT_UPDATED over the row as the store holds it, no second delivery, and the row the caller reads. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn learns its end after its
segments are written, so the implementation updates the stored row, and
ON_EVENT_UPDATED fires as for a direct `update_event()` (§10.3), over the row as
the store holds it then, an update since its commit standing; it does not
deliver the row again, and the row its caller reads among its response events
is that one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: a failure to write the update is logged, and the turn's outcome stands. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Writing that update is best effort: a failure is logged, and the
turn's outcome stands.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: the LoopEndMarker the stream hands the channel rendering a streamed turn, as its last item, and its place among the rows and a failure. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A host reads how any turn ended from its reply, and the
channel rendering a streamed turn reads it from its stream: once the loop
reached its end, the stream hands that channel the loop's `LoopEndMarker` (its
reason, its rounds, what they used) as its last item, after the row of the
turn's last text and before the response's failure when it fails, whichever
row carries the record.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: a channel the room stopped letting read the stream, and one that renders text alone. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel the room stopped letting read the stream is
handed none; one that renders text alone skips it, as it skips a piece of
reasoning.

requirements.applies: §6.4 The turn's record: what it says of its generations rides that row alone; the caller reads the end and usage under turns. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
What a turn's record says of its generations rides that row alone: its
caller reads the end and the usage under `turns`, and no more of it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 What a generation used: the UsageMarker the loop yields after each generation that returned, in its order among the text and the rows. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**What a generation used.** After each generation that returned, the loop
yields what it used, its model and its provider (`UsageMarker`), in its order
among the text and the rows, as it does a piece of reasoning, so a streaming
channel can show what a long turn uses as it goes (Section 6.1).

requirements.applies: §6.4 What a generation used: a UsageMarker is never stored. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It is never
stored.

requirements.applies: §6.4 What a generation used: a generation that reported no counters tells an empty usage. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A generation that reported no counters tells an empty usage.

requirements.applies: §6.4 What a generation used: a partial UsageMarker for usage told before a generation's end, replaced by the generation's own, and a reader that sums usage skips it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
provider that tells what a generation used before its end (the input counters
it tells as its stream starts, Section 6.7) has the loop yield it at once, as a
`UsageMarker` marked `partial`, which the generation's own replaces: a reader
that sums usage MUST skip a partial one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 What a generation used: a generation whose end reports no usage counts what it told before its end, once, into the turn's usage, budget and span, its record incomplete. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A generation whose end reports no
usage (one a `Cancel` or a cut stopped, one that failed, one whose done event
carries no counters) counts what it told before its end, once, into the turn's
usage, its budget and its span, and its record reads incomplete.

requirements.applies: §6.4 What a generation used: the record of a turn its reader stopped, or cut from outside, once it began (Section 12.2 step 13s), its end cancelled. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn its
reader stopped, or cut from outside, once
it began (Section 12.2 step 13s) records what its generations told as a turn
that reached its end does, its end `cancelled`: `ai_usage` sums what they told,
a generation in flight counting what it told before its end, as the reader read
it, absent when no counter was told, `ai_last_usage`, `ai_model` and
`ai_provider` are what the last of them told, and `ai_usage_complete` is false
when one told no counters or one is in flight.

requirements.applies: §6.4 What a generation used: when a generation counts as in flight once the reader stopped, and a call that ends then asks no model again. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A generation counts as in flight from the end
of the calls that followed the last one told, as the reader read it, or from a
segment break, until it tells; a call that ends once the reader stopped asks no
model again.

requirements.applies: §6.4 What a generation used: a stream cut before anything told what it used records only its end, with executor_id when it ran apart. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A stream cut before anything told what it used records only its end,
with `executor_id` when it ran apart: an
ACP agent's or a text-only channel's reports no usage at all, and a first
generation in flight cannot be told from them.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other: the option an implementation may offer to take a room's turns one at a time (serialize_room_turns). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A room's turns one after the other.** An AI channel MAY take a room's turns
one at a time (`serialize_room_turns`, declared as `serializes_room_turns`,
Section 10.6.2).

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: the order the owner keeps, and a turn starts only once the turn before it has written what it said. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its turns in a room then run in the order they were asked,
which the room's owner keeps: a turn takes its place when its delivery set
executes (Section 10.2), in the room's delivery order, and MUST NOT start
before the turn before it has written what it said, the text a cut turn keeps
included, so that it reads that answer.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: a waiting turn waits outside the room's delivery lane. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A waiting turn MUST wait outside the
room's delivery lane, through which the turn before it delivers its answer.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: the room a turn that waited reads, without a message committed after it was asked, with a change accepted meanwhile. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn that waited reads the room as it is when it starts, less the events
committed after it was asked that the channel did not write: a message
committed after it MUST NOT be in the history it is handed, since that message
waits a turn of its own and a turn that read it unanswered could do its task
too, and a change accepted meanwhile (an edit, a deletion, Section 10.3)
applies.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: a waiting turn whose delivery is cancelled never starts, and a running turn cut lets the next start once it wrote what it keeps (the reference implementation's timing included). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A waiting turn whose delivery is cancelled (Section 10.1, *Explicit
delivery cancellation*) never starts, and a running turn cut lets the next one
start once it has written what it keeps: a streaming target working on past
the cut holds its caller, not the room's line (Section 12.2 step 13s). The
reference implementation stores what the turn keeps once the target's
`finally` returned, so the line waits for that `finally`, and one that never
returns is the target's defect there.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: a turn whose channel was detached while it waited does not start. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn whose channel was detached from
the room while it waited does not start.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: a muted channel takes no place (Section 7.2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A muted channel takes no place: it
reacts to each event as it comes,
its answer not delivered (Section 7.2).

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: a message the running turn sends into its own room that asks the same channel is answered after that turn, and the call does not wait for it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A message the running turn sends into
its own room (a tool's call, Section 10.1) that asks the same channel is
answered after that turn: the call, awaited or deferred, returns without
waiting for that answer, since waiting would wait on the turn that made it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: a strategy that takes the channel's turns (Section 19.7) orders its generations itself. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
strategy that takes the channel's turns in the room (Section 19.7) orders its
generations itself, and they do not wait.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns one after the other, with serialize_room_turns on: the order is the owner's process's; two processes each handed a delivery run side by side. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The order is the owner's process's:
two processes each handed a delivery of the room run their turns side by side,
as an ACP agent channel's prompts are serialized by its process.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A room's turns, with serialize_room_turns off: the channel's turns in a room run side by side, each on the room as it stood when it was asked. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Without it,
the channel's turns in a room run side by side, each on the room as it stood
when it was asked.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, where an implementation offers steering (steer_room_turns) and a channel steers its room turns: it hands the room's next message to the running turn and takes the room's turns one at a time. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A message for the running turn.** An AI channel MAY hand a running turn the
room's next message rather than give that message a turn of its own
(`steer_room_turns`, declared as `steers_room_turns`, Section 10.6.2); it then
takes the room's turns one at a time as above.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn: serializes_room_turns defaults to steers_room_turns, a declaration that steers is taken as serialized, and registering a live channel that steers without serializing fails. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
So does any channel that steers
its room turns: a channel's `serializes_room_turns` defaults to its
`steers_room_turns`, the owner holding a channel by a declaration that steers
them takes them as serialized, and registering a live channel that says it
steers them but does not serialize them MUST fail, its steering otherwise
dead.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: a message from the author of the message the running turn answers, no other turn waiting, is committed, delivered and steered into that turn as an InjectMessage, and no turn of its own starts. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A message that comes while the channel's turn runs in the room, when no
other turn of the channel waits in the
room and the message is from the author of the message that turn answers, is
committed and delivered as any message (Section 10.1), and the room's
owner steers it into that turn (Section 21.3) as an `InjectMessage` of the text
its content reads as (Section 6.6), under its speaker's label when the turn's
history labels the room's speakers, as above: the turn
reads it at its next stop, and no turn of its own starts.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: who the author is (the room source and the name it signs with). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The author is the
room source that wrote the message (a participant, a sender on its channel, or
a channel: Section 10.1, step 12) under the name it is signed with, so one
sender id that carries several people is not one author, and neither are two
senders who sign one name.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: a turn runs in its author's name, its tools, tool hooks and tool policy reading them (Sections 21.1, 21.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn runs in its
author's name: its tools and its tool hooks read them as its actor (Section
21.4), and its channel's tool policy is resolved for their role (Section
21.1).

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: a message from anyone else is not handed to that turn and waits a turn of its own. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A message from anyone else MUST NOT be handed to that turn, where
their request would be served under that name and that role (RMK-1840): it
waits a turn of its own, after the running one, as above.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: the owner reads the author on the request of the one turn the channel runs in the room, and a channel running no turn or several there. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner reads the author on the request of the one turn the channel runs in
the room, and steers that turn by its id; when the channel runs no turn or
several there, the message waits a turn of its own.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: a turn cut before its next stop never reads the message, which the room's next turn reads. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn cut before that
stop never reads it: the message stays in the room, and the room's next turn
reads it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: whether the turn can take it is decided at delivery, and a turn being cut takes it until its loop has ended. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Whether the turn can take the message is decided at its delivery, not
at its commit, and a turn being cut takes it until its loop has ended.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: a turn that cannot take it, or a message that reads as no text, leaves it waiting a turn of its own. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When the
turn cannot (its loop is not reachable yet, or reads its queue no more, as once
a cut turn has ended) or the message reads as no text, the message waits a turn
of its own, as above.

requirements.applies: §6.4 A message for the running turn, with steering on: an edit, a delete or an event that opens no turn is no message for the running turn, and a message after it waits a turn of its own too. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
edit or a delete (Section 10.3), and an event of a type that opens no turn
(a notice, a reaction, a participant's arrival: above), is no message for
the running turn: it waits its place as such a message does, and no turn
answers it; while it waits, a message that comes after it waits a turn of
its own too.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel (the integration's scope, RoomKit as the ACP client): its channel type, category and direction. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ACP Agent Channel:**

An ACP agent channel connects a Room to an external
[Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com/) agent. In this
integration RoomKit is the ACP **client** and the coding agent is the ACP
**server**. Exposing a RoomKit-built agent as an ACP server is a separate
integration surface and is outside this channel's contract.

An ACP agent channel:

1. MUST use `ChannelType.AI`, category `INTELLIGENCE`, and direction
   `BIDIRECTIONAL`;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 2: one connection per channel instance, a distinct session per Room opened once, callers at the same time sharing it, a host call from inside a turn not waiting for it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
2. MUST initialize one ACP connection per channel instance and create a distinct
   ACP session for each Room, opened once: callers that ask for it at the same
   time (a first prompt, a rebuild, a host setting a session value) find the
   session the first of them opened, and a host call made from inside a turn
   MUST NOT wait for that turn to end to get it;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 3: prompts serialized within a session, different Rooms' sessions concurrent. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
3. MUST serialize prompts within an ACP session while allowing different Room
   sessions to operate concurrently;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 4: Room message content converted to ACP prompt content, agent message chunks mapped to the streaming output path. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
4. MUST convert Room message content into ACP prompt content and map ACP agent
   message chunks back to the normal RoomKit streaming output path;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 5: tool-call lifecycle updates mapped to tool-call stream markers, plan updates to realtime events. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
5. MUST map ACP tool-call lifecycle updates to RoomKit tool-call stream markers
   and MUST map ACP plan updates to RoomKit realtime events.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 5: each session update and permission request handled under the Room turn prompting that session (Section 10.6.5), outside any turn when none prompts it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each session
   update and permission request MUST be handled under the Room turn prompting
   that session (its publications, hooks and host, §10.6.5), whichever Room's
   turn opened the connection, and outside any turn when none prompts it;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 6: events from the channel itself and persisted tool-call activity events prompt nothing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
6. MUST skip events originating from itself and persisted tool-call activity
   events, preventing duplicate prompts and agent loops;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 7: cancellation of an active Room turn, and sessions and transport released when the channel closes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
7. MUST support cancellation of an active Room turn and MUST release ACP
   sessions and transport resources when the channel closes.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 7: a turn cancelled while it is active before prompting (the agent starting, its session opening, set up or rebuilt) ends without prompting, marked interrupted, a session opened for it alone closed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn is active
   from the moment it holds its Room, while the agent is started and its
   session is opened, set up or rebuilt: cancelled then, it MUST end without
   prompting, its response metadata marked `interrupted`, and a session
   opened for it alone (a standalone turn's) MUST be closed.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 7: a steering Cancel for the turn (Section 10.6.8) is that cancellation. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A steering
   `Cancel` for the turn (§10.6.8) is that cancellation;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 8: generated text and tool activity go through the standard persistence, visibility, chain-depth and re-broadcast behaviour. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
8. MUST NOT bypass the standard RoomKit persistence, visibility, chain-depth,
   or re-broadcast behavior for generated text and tool activity; and

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 9: ON_AI_RESPONSE on a completed Room turn, with its text, tool call count, duration and loop_end_reason (the agent's stop reason, completed for end_turn). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
9. MUST fire `ON_AI_RESPONSE` when a Room turn completes, carrying the text the
   turn produced, the number of tool calls it made, its duration, and how it
   ended as its `loop_end_reason`: the stop reason the agent returned,
   `completed` for `end_turn`.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 9: a turn that ended in an error, or whose response stream closed before its terminal update, fires no ON_AI_RESPONSE. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn
   that ended in an error, or whose response stream was closed before its
   terminal update, MUST NOT fire it: no response was delivered to the Room.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 9: token counters the agent reports are relayed unaltered. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Token counters the agent reports MUST be relayed unaltered. ACP annotates
   them as running session figures while agents are observed to report them per
   prompt; a client cannot distinguish the two from a single reading, and
   reinterpreting them silently corrupts an accounting figure.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 9: the option an implementation may offer to carry the session's context occupancy and running cost under distinct keys. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
   implementation MAY carry the session's context occupancy and running cost
   alongside them under distinct keys; and

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 10: an unclean prompt outcome on the response metadata (acp.stop_reason, acp.interrupted), and a clean end_turn with neither. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
10. MUST expose an unclean prompt outcome on the turn's response-metadata record:
    a returned ACP stop reason other than `end_turn` is written as
    `response_metadata["acp"]["stop_reason"]`, while a prompt that exits before
    returning a response is written as
    `response_metadata["acp"]["interrupted"] = true`. A clean `end_turn` writes
    neither marker.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, item 10: the same final record reaches the caller through InboundResult.response_metadata, a turn with no final MESSAGE included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The same final record MUST reach the caller through
    `InboundResult.response_metadata`, including when the turn produced no final
    MESSAGE event.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel: the stable protocol version is the default. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: The stable ACP protocol version MUST be the default.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel: experimental protocol versions only behind an explicit opt-in, never silently replacing the stable default. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Experimental protocol
versions MAY be supported only behind explicit opt-in and MUST NOT silently
replace the stable default.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel: the protocol version negotiated during initialization, and a clear failure when no version is compatible. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The channel MUST negotiate the protocol version
during initialization and MUST fail clearly when no compatible version exists.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, the stdio transport: the configured command launched as an argument vector, without a shell. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The reference transport is ACP over stdio. A stdio implementation MUST launch
the configured command as an argument vector without a shell.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, where an implementation offers an alternate ACP transport: it keeps the lifecycle and permission requirements. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Alternate ACP
transports MAY be implemented when standardized, but MUST preserve the lifecycle
and permission requirements above.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel: sessions are process-local by default, local to the turn executor that hosts the channel (Section 10.6.7). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
ACP sessions are process-local by default: local to the turn executor that
hosts the channel, to which the room's turns are placed while it holds the
session (§10.6.7).

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP agent channel, where an implementation offers persistent session resumption: resumed session identifiers are scoped to the Room and the agent endpoint. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation MAY add persistent
session resumption, but MUST scope resumed session identifiers to the associated
Room and agent endpoint.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP session setup: the channel's mcp_servers given to each session in session/new, a list or a function of the Room called at each opening. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Session setup.** What a session is opened with is the integrator's, per
Room. The channel's `mcp_servers` (default none) are the MCP servers given to
each session in `session/new`: a list, the same for every Room, or a function
of the Room identifier, called each time the channel opens a session for that
Room, so that a server can be told which Room it acts for (a stdio server's
environment, a URL).

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP session setup: each session_config value set on every session opened for a Room before it is prompted. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The channel's `session_config` (default none) maps ACP
session configuration option identifiers to values (`mode`, `model`, an
agent's own options). The channel MUST set each of them on every session it
opens for a Room before the session is prompted: the Room's first session, one
opened again after the previous one was invalidated or after a new connection
to the agent, and a standalone turn's session (Section 10.1.1 step 7).

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP session setup: a value the session already announces is not set again. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A value
the session already announces is not set again.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP session setup: a value the host sets on a Room's live session (set_config_option) is set again on the Room's next session, until the host closes the session or detaches the channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A value the host sets on a
Room's session while it lives (`set_config_option`, a channel call through the
kit, §10.6.3) belongs to the Room as well: the channel MUST set it again on
the Room's next session, over `session_config`, until the host closes the
Room's session through a channel call or detaches the channel, either of
which forgets it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP session setup, across executors: the owner stores the host's value with the Room, so another executor's session is set to it too (Sections 10.6.2, 10.6.7). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner stores it with the Room (§10.6.2), so the session
another executor opens once the executor that held the Room is lost is set
to it too.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP session setup: only a channel call writes a Room's value; a mode the agent switches to itself stays its live session's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only a channel call writes it, so the Room's next session is set
only to values the host set through the kit; a mode the agent switches to
itself is its live session's, not the Room's.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP session setup: a value the host sets while the Room has no open session replaces the Room's earlier value on the session that call opens. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A value the host sets while the Room has no open session is set on the
session that call opens in place of the Room's earlier value for that
option, so a value the agent has come to refuse is replaced by setting
another one.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP session setup: a value the agent refuses; the session is not prompted, it is released, and the turn or the opening call fails naming the option. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An agent's mode decides what it asks the client before acting, and an agent
that acts unasked never reaches the external tool handler: a session left on
another value than the one set up is not degraded but ungated. So when the
agent refuses a value, the channel MUST NOT prompt that session, MUST release
it, and MUST fail the turn, or the call that was opening the session, with an
error naming the option.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP detaching: the channel closes the Room's session and forgets the host's values, so a later attachment opens a new session. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Detaching.** Detaching the channel from a Room drops the Room's state
(§10.6.3): the channel MUST close the Room's session and forget the values
the host set on it, so a later attachment opens a new session, caught up on
the Room (§19.3.2).

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP detaching: a detach does not wait for the agent; the session is closed once the Room's running turn has ended. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A detach MUST NOT wait for the agent: the session is
closed off it, once the Room's turn still running has ended, a standalone
turn's included.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP detaching: a turn that started before the detach and has not prompted ends without prompting, marked interrupted, and a session it opened is closed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn that started before the detach and has not prompted
yet MUST end without prompting, marked `interrupted`, and a session it
opened for the detached Room MUST be closed.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP detaching: a host call running across the detach closes a session it opened and keeps no value, and the owner stores no call result for the detached Room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A host call running across the
detach (a value being set while the session opens, or while a turn holds the
Room) MUST close a session it opened and keep no value for the Room, and the
owner stores no call result for a Room the channel is no longer attached to.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP permissions: filesystem and terminal capabilities advertised as unavailable unless the integrator supplies them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
ACP agents can request permission to execute tools and can request client-side
filesystem or terminal operations. An ACP agent channel:

- MUST advertise filesystem and terminal capabilities as unavailable unless the
  integrator explicitly supplies conforming implementations;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP permissions: a permission request is denied or cancelled when no external tool handler is configured. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- MUST deny or cancel permission requests when no external tool handler is
  configured;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP permissions: what the channel passes to the configured external tool handler. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- MUST pass tool name, input, call identifier, ACP session identifier, and Room
  identifier to the configured external tool handler;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP permissions: only a permission option the agent offered is selected. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: - MUST select only a permission option offered by the ACP agent;

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP permissions: on session/cancel, each pending permission request of the session answered cancelled after the notification, and the handler's decision abandoned. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- when it cancels a session's prompt (`session/cancel`), MUST answer each
  permission request of that session still pending with ACP's `cancelled`
  outcome, after the notification, and MUST abandon the external tool
  handler's decision on it, which never reaches the agent: unlike the cut of
  §9.3, which leaves a decision still pending to the handler to withdraw.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP permissions: a call whose permission the agent asked, pending at the turn's end or answered cancelled, is reported once, cancelled (Section 9.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call whose permission the agent asked is closed with its turn whether or
  not the agent announced it: one whose request is still pending when the
  turn ends, or was answered `cancelled`, is reported once, cancelled
  (§9.3); and

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP permissions and progress: tool and plan progress exposed through the realtime backend, transient progress not persisted. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- SHOULD expose tool and plan progress through the realtime backend without
  persisting transient progress updates.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP identity, where an implementation offers one and the integrator gives it: a name, a role and a description that a discussion's notes, a dispatch policy and a host's view present the agent by (Section 19.7.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Identity and instructions.** An ACP agent channel MAY carry an identity as
an Agent does (Section 19.1): a `name`, a `role` and a `description`, which a
discussion's notes, a dispatch policy and a host's view present it by
(Section 19.7.5).

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP instructions: the integrator's standing instructions sent in the first prompt of each session opened for a Room, as the runtime's block, and not again while the session keeps them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its `instructions` (default null) are the integrator's
standing direction for the agent (a persona, how the room works), since the
agent's own system prompt is not RoomKit's to set. The channel sends them in
the first prompt of each session it opens for a Room, a session opened again
after its transport died included, as the runtime's block ahead of the
catch-up and the request, never as a participant's words, and not again
while the session keeps them.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP in a discussion: an ACP agent channel takes a discussion's turns as an AI channel does (Section 19.7.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**In a discussion.** An ACP agent channel takes a discussion's turns as an AI
channel does (Section 19.7.5).

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP in a discussion: the turn's notes ride its prompt as the runtime's block, and every copy of the notes' header in the prompt's other text is replaced. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The turn's notes (rule 14) ride its prompt as
the runtime's own block, under the notes' header, and every copy of that
header in the prompt's other text (the catch-up, the request, a host's
block) is replaced as Section 6.4 replaces it in a turn's input, so a
participant cannot pass their words off as the runtime's notes.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP in a discussion: the turn sends what the agent has not read yet, up to its start, and the event it answers as its request. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its session
keeps its own history, so the turn sends what the agent has not read yet,
up to the turn's start, and the event the turn answers as its request; the
notes say which event that is and who asked for it.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP in a discussion: a hold that cuts the turn (rule 12) is a steering Cancel, its session's opening included, wherever the turn runs. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hold that cuts its
turn (rule 12) is a steering `Cancel` (§10.6.8), which cancels it (item 7),
its session's opening included, wherever the turn runs.

requirements.applies: §6.4 ACP in a discussion: its answer streams like any agent's, so a silent one is held back and blocked (rule 13). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its
answer streams like any agent's, so a silent one is held back and blocked as
rule 13 says.

requirements.applies: §6.5 Source providers, where an implementation offers them (persistent connections that push inbound events, unlike webhook channels, folded in): the SourceProvider interface, id, status, start(emit), stop() and healthcheck(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Source providers maintain **persistent connections** that push inbound events to
the framework. This is distinct from webhook-based channels where the framework
receives HTTP callbacks.

```
SourceProvider (interface)
├── id: string                              # Source identifier
├── status: SourceStatus                    # STOPPED, CONNECTING, CONNECTED, RECONNECTING, ERROR
│
├── start(emit: function(InboundMessage)) → void
│       # Connect and begin listening. Call `emit` for each inbound message.
│
├── stop() → void
│       # Disconnect and release resources
│
└── healthcheck() → SourceHealth
        # Report connection health
```

requirements.applies: §6.5 Source providers, where an implementation offers them: the SourceStatus enumeration (the table of example sources, informative, folded in). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**SourceStatus** enumeration: STOPPED, CONNECTING, CONNECTED, RECONNECTING, ERROR

Examples of source providers:

| Source | Description |
|---|---|
| WhatsApp Personal | Persistent WhatsApp Web multidevice connection |
| WebSocket | Client connection to an external WebSocket server |
| SSE | Server-Sent Events stream from an HTTP endpoint |

requirements.applies: §6.5 Source providers, where an implementation offers them: a source attached to the framework calls emit for each inbound message. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Sources are attached to the framework and MUST call the `emit` callback for
each inbound message.

requirements.applies: §6.5 Source providers, where an implementation offers them: the framework routes each emitted message through the standard inbound pipeline (Section 10.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The framework routes emitted messages through the standard
inbound pipeline (Section 10.1).

requirements.applies: §6.6 Content transcoding on broadcast: each target's media_types (Section 5.8) decides; a content of a category it names is delivered unchanged, one of a category it does not name is replaced by its text form per the table, and so is a file whose type or size the target does not take. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When an event is broadcast to channels with different capabilities, the framework
MUST transcode content to match each target channel's supported media types.
The target's `media_types` (Section 5.8) decides: a content of a category it
names is delivered unchanged, and one of a category it does not name is
replaced by its text form, as the table below gives it; so is a file whose
type or size the target does not take (Section 5.8).

requirements.applies: §6.6 Content transcoding: text is the fallback every channel takes whatever its media_types declares, a text unchanged and a rich text as its text form (the sentence's example is a voice channel that declares AUDIO alone). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Text is the fallback
every channel takes, whatever its `media_types` declares: a voice channel
that declares AUDIO alone receives a text unchanged and a rich text as its
text form.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules (the table's header), the TextContent row: a text reaches any target unchanged. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Default transcoding rules:**

| Source Content | Target | Transcoded To |
|---|---|---|
| TextContent | any | Unchanged |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the RichContent row: a target without RICH receives a TextContent of the plain_text, else the body unchanged. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
RichContent | no RICH | TextContent (plain_text, else body unchanged) |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the MediaContent row: a target without MEDIA, or that does not take the file's type or size, receives the media's label, a URL only when it is an http or https link, else the media type, never a data URI or a reference. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
MediaContent | no MEDIA, or a type or a size the target does not take (Section 5.8) | TextContent ("[Media: {caption or filename or url}]"): the URL only when it is a link (`http`, `https`), else the media type; never a data URI or a reference |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the AudioContent row: a target without AUDIO receives the transcript, or the voice-message label, a URL only when it is a link, else the media type. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
AudioContent | no AUDIO | TextContent (the transcript, or "[Voice message: {url}]"): the URL only when it is a link, else the media type |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the VideoContent row: a target without VIDEO receives the video label, a URL only when it is a link, else the media type. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
VideoContent | no VIDEO | TextContent ("[Video: {url}]"): the URL only when it is a link, else the media type |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the LocationContent row: a target without LOCATION receives the location label, with its label or address when it has one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
LocationContent | no LOCATION | TextContent ("[Location: {label or address} ({latitude}, {longitude})]", or "[Location: ({latitude}, {longitude})]" with neither, e.g. "[Location: (45.5, -73.6)]") |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the CompositeContent row: a composite is transcoded part by part, each part by its own row. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
CompositeContent | any | Each part by its own row (below) |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the TemplateContent row: a target without TEMPLATE receives the template's body, or its template label. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
TemplateContent | no TEMPLATE | TextContent (use body or "[Template: {template_id}]") |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the EditContent row: a target without edit support receives the correction text. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
EditContent | no edit support | TextContent ("Correction: {new text}") |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the DeleteContent row: a target without delete support receives the deletion text or a SystemContent. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
DeleteContent | no delete support | TextContent ("[Message deleted]") or SystemContent |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the SystemContent row: a system content reaches any target unchanged. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
SystemContent | any | Unchanged |
|

requirements.applies: §6.6 Default transcoding rules, the ToolCallContent row: a tool call content reaches any target unchanged. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: ToolCallContent | any | Unchanged |

requirements.applies: §6.6 Composite transcoding: no part is dropped; a part the target cannot carry becomes its text form. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A composite is transcoded part by part, each part by its own row, and no part
is dropped: a part the target cannot carry becomes its text form.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Composite transcoding: a composite whose every part ends up a TextContent becomes one TextContent, its text form (the parts' texts joined in order by a newline, an empty one skipped). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When every
part ends up as a `TextContent`, the composite becomes one `TextContent`, its
text form (below): the parts' texts joined in order by a newline, an empty
one skipped, so that a channel that declares TEXT alone receives one message.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Composite transcoding: any other composite keeps its transcoded parts, in order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Otherwise the composite keeps its transcoded parts, in order.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Text form: every content's one text, the text of the TextContent its row transcodes to, or for the rows delivered unchanged a TextContent's or SystemContent's body and the tool-call label of a ToolCallContent. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Text form.** Every content has a text form, the one text it reads as: for a
row above that transcodes to a TextContent, the text of that TextContent; for
the rows delivered unchanged, a TextContent's body, a SystemContent's body,
and `[Tool call: {tool_name}]` for a ToolCallContent.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Text form of a composite: its parts' text forms in order, joined by a newline, an empty one skipped. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A composite reads as
its parts' text forms in order, joined by a newline, a part whose text form
is empty skipped.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Text form of an EditContent (the correction of its new content's text form) and of a DeleteContent (the deletion text), whatever a reader supports. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An EditContent reads as "Correction: {the text form of its
new content}" and a DeleteContent as "[Message deleted]", whatever a reader
supports.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Text form: a number (a location's latitude and longitude) written as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same IEEE 754 binary64 value, at least one digit after the point, never an exponent (so that every implementation writes the same text, folded in). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A number in a text form (a location's latitude and longitude) is
written in decimal, as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same IEEE
754 binary64 value, with at least one digit after the point and never an
exponent: 45 is `45.0`, 5e-05 is `0.00005`, and -73.6 is `-73.6`, so a
location at latitude 45, longitude -73.6 reads "[Location: (45.0, -73.6)]".
Every implementation then writes
the same text, and an instruction's fingerprint over it agrees (§10.1.1
step 6).

requirements.applies: §6.6 Text form: every reader of a content as text takes its text form, save the mentions §6.4 gives an author image and an empty event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every reader of a content as text takes its text form, save the
mentions §6.4 gives an author image and an empty event: an instruction's
fingerprint (§10.1.1 step 6), a turn's history and input read as text (§6.4),
a reader outside a channel (below), a part a target cannot carry and a
composite flattened to one text (above).

requirements.applies: §6.6 Edits and deletes: a target whose capabilities support edits or deletes natively receives the EDIT or DELETE event without transcoding. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When the target channel supports edits or deletes natively (i.e.,
`capabilities.supports_edit` or `capabilities.supports_delete` is true), the
framework MUST deliver the EDIT or DELETE event without transcoding.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Edits and deletes: a target that does not support the operation receives its fallback representation. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When the
target channel does NOT support the operation, the framework MUST transcode to
the fallback representation shown above.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Text form outside a channel: a reader that takes a room's message as text outside a channel (a delegated task's brief, a speak classifier, a discussion's dispatch and its turns' notes, a scoring query, a memory's summary, an ACP agent's catch-up) reads its text form. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A reader that takes a room's message as text outside a channel (a delegated
task's brief, a speak classifier, a discussion's dispatch and the notes of
its turns, a scoring query, a memory's summary, an ACP agent's catch-up)
reads its text form: its text, each media as its label above, a composite's
parts in order.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Text form outside a channel: a reader of names (a discussion's addressing) or of a search query (a memory's retrieval) reads the author's words alone, a media's caption included, never a file name or a type. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One that reads names in it (a discussion's addressing) or a
search query in it (a memory's retrieval) reads the author's words alone, a
media's caption included, never a file name or a type: an agent named in a
file name is not addressed.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Max length enforcement: after transcoding, a target that declares max_length has its TextContent truncated to it: a text, a composite that became one text, or each text part of a composite that keeps its parts. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Max length enforcement:** After transcoding, if the target channel declares a
`max_length`, the framework MUST truncate TextContent to that limit: a text,
a composite that became one text, or each text part of a composite that
keeps its parts.

requirements.applies: §6.6 Max length enforcement: the limit counts Unicode code points, and a cut never splits a code point. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The limit counts Unicode code points, as an instruction's
length does (Section 10.1.1), and a cut MUST NOT split a code point (a UTF-8
sequence, a UTF-16 surrogate pair).

requirements.applies: §6.6 Max length enforcement: a cut text ends with three ASCII full stops, counted within the limit. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A cut text ends with `...`, three ASCII
full stops counted within the limit, so that the reader sees the cut: with a
limit of 8, "Thank you for calling" becomes "Thank...".

requirements.applies: §6.6 Max length enforcement: a limit below 4 code points cuts without the marker. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A limit below 4 code
points cuts without the marker: with a limit of 3, the same text becomes
"Tha".

requirements.applies: §6.6 Max length enforcement: the marker is never U+2026 (HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The marker is not U+2026 (HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS): outside the GSM 7-bit
alphabet, that character would turn an SMS into UCS-2.

requirements.applies: §6.6: a custom transcoding strategy an integrator provides. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Implementations SHOULD allow integrators to provide a custom transcoding strategy.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Provider abstraction (channel type and provider separate concepts for every channel, AI included, folded in): the AIProvider interface's name and model_name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Channel type and Provider are separate concepts. This applies to ALL channels,
including AI.

**AI Provider interface:**

```
AIProvider (interface)
├── name: string                            # Provider name (e.g., "acme")
├── model_name: string                      # Model identifier (e.g., "acme-large-2")
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: supports_vision, false by default, whether image parts reach the model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── supports_vision: bool (default false)   # Whether image parts reach the model
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: supports_streaming, false by default, whether generate_stream is implemented. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── supports_streaming: bool (default false) # Whether generate_stream is implemented
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: supports_structured_streaming, false by default, whether generate_structured_stream streams natively, else wrapping generate. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── supports_structured_streaming: bool (default false)
│       # Whether generate_structured_stream streams natively (else it wraps generate)
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: supports_response_schema and supports_response_schema_with_tools, false by default (their rules in the paragraphs below), context_window and generate(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── supports_response_schema: bool (default false)
│       # Whether generate honours AIContext.response_schema (see below)
├── supports_response_schema_with_tools: bool (default false)
│       # Whether a schema may ride a turn that also carries tools
├── context_window: int | null              # Input window of the active model, when known
│
├── generate(context: AIContext) → AIResponse
│       # Answer the conversation the context carries
│
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: generate_stream(), text deltas as they arrive, which requires supports_streaming; it streams a turn without tools when the provider streams text alone (Section 6.4, One loop). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── generate_stream(context: AIContext) → async_iterator<string>
│       # Yield text deltas as they arrive (requires supports_streaming = true)
│       # Streams a turn without tools when the provider streams text alone
│       # (Section 6.4, One loop)
│
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: generate_structured_stream(), thinking deltas, text deltas and tool calls, then one done event; a usage event before it tells what the generation used so far, which the done event's usage replaces and a generation cut before its end counts (§6.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── generate_structured_stream(context: AIContext) → async_iterator<StreamEvent>
│       # Yield thinking deltas, text deltas and tool calls, then one done event;
│       # a usage event before it tells what the generation used so far (the
│       # input counters told as the stream starts), which the done event's
│       # usage replaces and a generation cut before its end counts (§6.4)
│
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: available_models(), the curated offline catalogue, which MAY be empty. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── available_models() → list<ModelInfo>
│       # Curated offline catalogue (MAY be empty)
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: list_models(), the live catalogue, by default available_models(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── list_models() → list<ModelInfo>
│       # Live catalogue; default: available_models() (see Model listings below)
│
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIProvider: close(), which releases connections. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
└── close() → void
        # Release connections

```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIMessage: role, content (a text or a list of content parts) and metadata. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
AIMessage
├── role: string                            # "user", "assistant", "system", "tool"
├── content: string | list<AIContentPart>   # Text, image, tool call, tool result, thinking parts
└── metadata: map<string, any>

```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIContentPart, told apart by type: AITextPart, AIImagePart and AIToolCallPart and their fields. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
AIContentPart                               # One of these, told apart by type
├── AITextPart
│   ├── type: string = "text"
│   └── text: string
├── AIImagePart
│   ├── type: string = "image"
│   ├── url: string
│   └── mime_type: string | null
├── AIToolCallPart
│   ├── type: string = "tool_call"
│   ├── id: string
│   ├── name: string
│   ├── arguments: map<string, any>
│   └── metadata: map<string, any>
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIToolResultPart: tool_call_id, name, result and is_error, a failure or a refusal carried, never inferred. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── AIToolResultPart
│   ├── type: string = "tool_result"
│   ├── tool_call_id: string
│   ├── name: string
│   ├── result: string | list<AITextPart | AIImagePart>
│   ├── is_error: bool (default false)      # A failure or a refusal, carried, never inferred
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIToolResultPart: structured_content and outcome, never rendered to providers, and references, the tools the result makes callable (Section 6.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
│   ├── structured_content: map<string, any> | null  # MCP structuredContent; never rendered to providers
│   ├── outcome: string | null              # served, refused, failed, blocked, unserved or cancelled; never rendered to providers
│   └── references: list<string>            # Tools the result makes callable (Section 6.4)
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIThinkingPart: thinking, signature and redacted (a redacted block's opaque data, its thinking then empty). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
└── AIThinkingPart
    ├── type: string = "thinking"
    ├── thinking: string
    ├── signature: string | null
    └── redacted: string | null             # A redacted block's opaque data; thinking is then empty

```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIContext: messages, system_prompt, temperature (0.7 by default), max_tokens (null defers to the provider's cap), thinking_budget, enable_thinking, reasoning_effort, tools and response_schema. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
AIContext
├── messages: list<AIMessage>               # The conversation to answer
├── system_prompt: string | null
├── temperature: float                      # Default 0.7
├── max_tokens: int | null                  # null defers to the provider's configured cap
├── thinking_budget: int | null
├── enable_thinking: bool | null
├── reasoning_effort: string | null
├── tools: list<AITool>                     # Functions the model may call
├── response_schema: map<string, any> | null  # JSON Schema of the answer, see below
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIContext: room, the current room state, and target_capabilities and target_media_types, what every transport that sends shares (§4.2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── room: RoomContext | null                # Current room state
├── target_capabilities: ChannelCapabilities | null  # What every transport that sends shares (§4.2)
├── target_media_types: list<ChannelMediaType>  # The media types every transport that sends shares (§4.2)
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIContext: metadata and response_metadata, the turn's one record. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
├── metadata: map<string, any>
└── response_metadata: ResponseMetadata     # The turn's one record, see below

```

requirements.applies: §6.7 AIResponse: content, thinking, thinking_signature, thinking_parts, finish_reason, usage, tool_calls, tasks, observations and metadata. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
AIResponse
├── content: string                         # Generated text
├── thinking: string | null                 # Reasoning the provider exposed
├── thinking_signature: string | null       # The last block's signature, for a reader of one
├── thinking_parts: list<AIThinkingPart> | null  # The blocks to replay, in order; null for reasoning without blocks
├── finish_reason: "stop" | "tool_calls" | "length" | "content_filter"
│       | "refusal" | "malformed_call" | "unexpected_call" | "error" | null
│       # Why it stopped, in one closed vocabulary that each provider maps
│       # its vendor's words onto, a stream's end as a whole response; null
│       # for no reason the provider knows
├── usage: map<string, int>                 # input_tokens, output_tokens, cache counters
├── tool_calls: list<AIToolCall>            # Calls for the tool loop to run
├── tasks: list<Task>                       # Tasks to create
├── observations: list<Observation>         # Observations to record
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Provider-specific data (model, latency)
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 Model listings: a live listing backfills from the curated catalogue what the vendor's endpoint leaves blank, but not its capabilities, an empty list meaning unknown. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Model listings.** A live listing backfills from the curated catalogue what
the vendor's endpoint leaves blank (display name, context window, vision,
price), but not its `capabilities`: a catalogue's tags MAY be internal routing
flags, and an empty list means "unknown", never "none".

requirements.applies: §6.7 Model listings: a provider whose endpoint reports no model type taking the tags from a catalogue that holds public tags only. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider whose
endpoint reports no model type at all MAY take the tags from its catalogue
when that catalogue holds public tags only.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Model listings: a conversational provider's listing that surfaces speech models tags them transcription or speech, from what the vendor reports, else from the model's name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A conversational
provider's listing that surfaces speech models SHOULD tag them, as the image
catalogue is tagged (Section 25.6): `transcription` for a speech-to-text model,
`speech` for a text-to-speech one, from what the vendor reports or, failing
that, from the model's name.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Model listings: a model that converses in audio is tagged neither transcription nor speech. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A model that converses in audio is neither.

requirements.applies: §6.7 The model that answered: metadata.model names the model the response names, the model asked for only when it names none, and a stream's done event names the same. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The model that answered.** `metadata.model` names the model that answered,
as the response names it (a dated snapshot, a router's pick), and the model
asked for only when the response names none; a stream's done event names the
same, so both modes report it alike.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Usage counters: input_tokens, output_tokens and the cache counters are disjoint (Section 25.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Usage counters.** `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and the cache counters are
disjoint, as in Section 25.5.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Usage counters: a cache counter reported at zero is omitted on a text turn, as one not reported (an image's usage keeps a reported zero, Section 25.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A cache counter the vendor reports at zero is
omitted, as one it does not report: on a text turn the two bill the same, and
every provider reports them alike (an image's usage keeps a reported zero,
Section 25.5).

requirements.applies: §6.7 Usage counters: output_tokens counts every billed output token, the model's thinking included wherever the vendor reports it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`output_tokens` counts every output token the
vendor bills, a model's thinking included, whether the vendor reports that
thinking inside its completion count or beside it.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Usage counters: reasoning_tokens, where a provider reports it, the thinking share of output_tokens, never added to the other counters nor priced again. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`reasoning_tokens`, when a
provider reports it, is the thinking share of `output_tokens`: a detail, never
added to the other counters nor priced a second time.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning written in the text, for a provider that reads the <think> convention (a server MAY write it, folded in): a block read as thinking only where it opens the generation, after nothing but spaces, tabs, line feeds and carriage returns, which stay the answer's text. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Reasoning written in the text (normative).** A Chat Completions server MAY
write a model's reasoning in the answer's text, between `<think>` and
`</think>`, rather than in a field beside it. A provider that reads that
convention reads a block as `thinking` only where it opens the generation: the
text starts with `<think>`, after nothing but spaces (U+0020), tabs (U+0009),
line feeds (U+000A) and carriage returns (U+000D), which stay the answer's
text.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning written in the text: any other character before the tag makes the text the answer whole. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Any other character before the tag, another space or a byte order mark
included, makes the text the answer whole.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning written in the text: the block ends at its first closing tag, everything after it the answer. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The block ends at its first
`</think>`, and everything after it is the answer, a later `<think>` included.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning written in the text: a text that does not open with the tag is an answer, stored, delivered and sent back as written, never cut at its tag. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`The parser reads the <think> tag. Everything after is lost.` is an answer,
stored, delivered and sent back as written, never cut at its tag.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning written in the text: a block the response stopped before closing (the output cap) is reasoning to its end. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A block the
response stopped before closing (the output cap) is reasoning to its end, never
answer.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning written in the text: each round of a tool loop is a generation of its own, its block read as the first round's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every round of a tool loop is a generation of its own, its block read
as the first round's is.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning written in the text: a tag cut across a stream's chunks reads as it does whole, and a response reads the same streamed or not. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tag cut across a stream's chunks reads as it does
whole, and a response reads the same streamed or not.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning written in the text: a reasoning field the server sends beside the text changes none of this, both being the response's reasoning. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A reasoning field the
server sends beside the text changes none of this: both are the response's
reasoning.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings, the turn's (folded in): where a provider's configuration carries one under the same name, the provider prefers the turn's value, false included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Reasoning settings.** `thinking_budget`, `enable_thinking` and
`reasoning_effort` are the turn's. Where a provider's configuration carries one
of them under the same name, the provider MUST prefer the turn's value, `false`
included.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings: a vendor setting of the provider's own yields to the turn on what the turn states and supplies what it leaves unstated. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
