requirements.text:
A vendor setting of the provider's own (a named level, a switch of its
own) yields to the turn on what the turn
states and supplies what it leaves unstated.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings: whether the model reasons, stated by thinking_budget, else enable_thinking, a reasoning_effort of none stating off; how much, stated by reasoning_effort. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Whether the model reasons is
stated by `thinking_budget` (`0` off, above `0` on), else by `enable_thinking`,
and a `reasoning_effort` of `none` states off; how much it reasons is stated by
`reasoning_effort`.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings from several levels (Appendix A.9): an enable_thinking false at one level states off over a thinking_budget at a less specific one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Where the turn's settings come from several levels
(Appendix A.9, per-turn settings), an `enable_thinking: false` set at one level
states off over a `thinking_budget` set at a less specific one.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings, a vendor setting that names levels: a level the model does not take sent as the nearest it takes, left out where the provider cannot know them; a model that cannot stop reasoning sent its lowest level for off. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Where such a vendor setting names levels, a level the model
does not take is sent as the nearest one it takes, and left out where the
provider cannot know the levels the model takes; and a model that cannot stop
reasoning is sent its lowest level where the turn states off.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings: the provider knows the levels and whether the model can stop reasoning from its model catalogue, or the levels from its configuration, never from the model's name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The provider
knows both from what its model catalogue declares of the model, or the levels
from one its configuration already sets, never from the model's name.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings applied on a turn that declares tools as on one that does not, save for the cases RK-6.7-055 to 057 give. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
provider MUST apply them on a turn that declares tools as on one that does not, save for the
cases below.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings, a vendor that restricts what a turn with tools accepts: the value accepted, read from the model catalogue, never guessed from the model's name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Where the vendor restricts what a turn with tools accepts (a vendor
may take function tools only with reasoning off on some models), the provider
sends the value accepted, read from
what its model catalogue declares of the model, never guessed from the model's
name.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings on a turn with tools: the two cases where a provider MAY leave a setting out (a model it cannot know behind its endpoint, without a configuration statement; reasoning it cannot pass back between tool rounds), which it documents, and never otherwise. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider MAY leave a setting out of a turn with tools where it cannot
know the model behind its endpoint (a `base_url`, a deployment name, a proxy's
alias) and its configuration does not state that the server takes the setting
there, or where turning reasoning on would require passing the model's reasoning
back from one tool round to the next in a form it does not produce; it documents
that it does, and MUST NOT leave it out otherwise.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Reasoning settings: a configuration statement covers only what the catalogue does not declare; a provider that knows its vendor's rule refuses the statement. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Such a statement covers only
what the catalogue does not declare: a model the catalogue declares is sent the
value the catalogue says it accepts, and a provider that knows its vendor's rule
refuses the statement in its configuration rather than ignore it.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response metadata, one record per turn: AIContext.response_metadata created with the turn and shared by identity by every extension point of that turn (a memory provider, a BEFORE_AI_GENERATION hook, a tool handler or a BEFORE_TOOL_USE hook through current_response_metadata(), each of which MAY write it). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Response metadata is one record per turn.** `AIContext.response_metadata` is a
dict-like mapping created with the turn and shared by identity by every
extension point of that turn: a memory provider MAY write it while the context
is built, a `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` hook MAY write it through
`event.ai_context.response_metadata`, and a tool handler or a `BEFORE_TOOL_USE`
hook MAY write it through `current_response_metadata()` (the hook runs under
the call's turn, so a host counts the calls a turn started there, before any
runs).

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response metadata: the record a caller reads on InboundResult.response_metadata is the turn's, whether the turn answered, failed or was cut from outside. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The record a caller reads on `InboundResult.response_metadata` is the
same one, whether the turn answered, failed or was cut from outside (a
delivery's cancellation, the kit's close).

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response metadata, the caller's copy alone: turns[channel_id] for each channel that replied to the caller's own event, streamed or not, with its loop_end_reason (an AI channel's; an ACP agent's stop reason) and the ai_usage its record carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The caller's copy alone also
names how each channel that replied to the caller's own event ended, streamed
or not, under `turns[channel_id]`: its `loop_end_reason` (an AI channel's;
an ACP agent's stop reason, `interrupted` when its prompt never returned or
failed after, `completed` once it returned on `end_turn`) and the `ai_usage`
its record carries (an ACP agent's carries none), so a turn that produced no MESSAGE still tells its caller how
it ended and two agents replying to one inbound never overwrite each other's
end.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response metadata: an answer to an answer, and an ACP turn never prompted, have no turns entry. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An answer to an answer is no reply to the caller and has no entry, nor
has an ACP turn never prompted (a transport that read nothing).

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response metadata: turns is the framework's key; a value a turn's hooks or tools write under it reaches neither the caller nor a MESSAGE. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`turns` is the
framework's key: a value a turn's hooks or tools write under it is not
carried to the caller, and never on a MESSAGE.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response metadata, the caller's copy: no reply's loop_end_reason or ai_usage at its top; every other key of the reply's record is the caller's; a buffered reply's end and usage read off its record, else off its last MESSAGE that names one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Nor are a reply's
`loop_end_reason` and `ai_usage` at the top of the caller's copy, which reads
them under `turns` alone; every other key of the reply's record is the
caller's, and a buffered reply's end, with the usage beside it, is read off its
record, else off the last of its MESSAGEs that names one.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response metadata merged into the metadata of every MESSAGE the turn produces, as the record stands when that event is created (how a host attributes a reply, folded in). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The framework MUST merge the record
into the metadata of every MESSAGE event the turn produces, as the record
stands when that event is created — a streamed segment persisted before a tool
round carries what was known then, the final answer carries everything the
turn learned. It is how a host attributes to the reply what the turn read
(cited sources, say) without a post-hoc rewrite of persisted events.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response schema (a caller sets AIContext.response_schema, folded in): a provider whose supports_response_schema is true translates it into its native constrained output. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Response schema.** A caller that needs the answer in a known shape sets
`AIContext.response_schema` to a JSON Schema. A provider whose
`supports_response_schema` is true MUST translate it into its native
constrained output, so that the `content` returned by `generate()` is one JSON
document satisfying the schema.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response schema: the implementation checks the document against the schema before returning it, whatever the server claims (the portable subset is checkable without a library, folded in). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The implementation MUST check the document
against the schema before returning it, whatever the server claims: a proxy may
accept the constraint and route to an upstream that ignores it. The subset below
is small enough to check without a JSON Schema library.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response schema: content stays a string, a typed value being the caller's work. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`content` stays a
string all the same, and turning it into a typed value is the caller's work.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response schema: the schema stays within the portable subset. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The schema MUST stay within the portable subset below, the one every provider
that supports response schemas accepts.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response schema outside the portable subset, refused before any provider call where the language checks as a context is built or a field assigned, else where the channel takes it, before the model is asked, or in the provider before any request for a schema written on a context. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation whose language runs a
check as a context is built or a field assigned MUST refuse a schema outside it
there, before any provider is called; one whose language runs none MUST refuse
it where the channel takes it (its own as the channel is built, a binding's as
the turn reads its settings), before the model is asked, and a schema written on
a context by hand or by a `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` hook in the provider, before
any request.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset (the table's header), the type row: one of object, array, string, number, integer, boolean, as a single string. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
| Keyword | Rule |
|---|---|
| `type` | One of `object`, `array`, `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, as a single string.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset, the type row: the schema's root an object. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The root MUST be `object`. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset, the properties row: required on an object, possibly empty. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`properties` | REQUIRED on an object: a map from names to subschemas, possibly empty. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset, the required row: required on an object, every key of properties once. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`required` | REQUIRED on an object: every key of `properties`, each once. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset, the additionalProperties row: required on an object, and false. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`additionalProperties` | REQUIRED on an object, and `false`. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset, the items row: required on an array, one subschema. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`items` | REQUIRED on an array: one subschema. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset, the enum row: on a string only, a non-empty list of distinct strings. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`enum` | On a string only: a non-empty list of distinct strings. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset, the title and description row: allowed on any subschema, as strings. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: `title`, `description` | Allowed on any subschema, as strings: guidance for the model. |

requirements.applies: §6.7 Portable subset: no other keyword is portable (why, and the agreed empty value of an answer that may be absent, folded in). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
No other keyword is portable. `null` and optional fields, `anyOf`, `$ref`, and
numeric or string bounds each break on at least one provider. An answer that may
be absent is a required field with an agreed empty value (an empty string, an
empty list).

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response schema: a provider never ignores a schema it cannot honour, and never returns text that does not answer it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider MUST NOT ignore a schema it cannot honour, and MUST NOT return text
that does not answer it.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Response schema: generate() and the streaming methods raise a ResponseSchemaError, a ProviderError never retryable, with one of the table's reasons. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`generate()` and the streaming methods raise a
`ResponseSchemaError`, a `ProviderError` that is never retryable, with one of
these reasons:

requirements.applies: §6.7 ResponseSchemaError reasons (the table's header), the unsupported row, raised before any request. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `unsupported` | `supports_response_schema` is false, or the context also carries `tools` and `supports_response_schema_with_tools` is false. Raised before any request is sent. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 ResponseSchemaError reasons, the refusal row. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`refusal` | The model declined to answer: a refusal field, a refusal or safety stop reason, or the prompt itself blocked before any answer. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 ResponseSchemaError reasons, the truncated row. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`truncated` | The answer was cut: the stop reason `length`, its output cap or the context window filling up mid-answer. |
|

requirements.applies: §6.7 ResponseSchemaError reasons, the invalid_json row. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: `invalid_json` | The text is not a JSON document satisfying the schema: a server that accepted the constraint and did not apply it. |

requirements.applies: §6.7 Streaming a constrained answer: generate_stream() and generate_structured_stream() carry the schema as generate() does (their text deltas provisional until the stream ends, folded in). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Streaming a constrained answer.** `generate_stream()` and
`generate_structured_stream()` carry the schema like `generate()`. The text
deltas are the document as it is written: partial JSON, provisional until the
stream ends.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Streaming a constrained answer: the whole document checked before the final done event, the error raised instead of that event when the check fails. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The implementation MUST check the whole document, as `generate()`
does, before it yields the final done event, and MUST raise the error above
instead of that event when the check fails.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Streaming a constrained answer: a consumer does not act on the streamed text before the done event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A consumer MUST NOT act on the
streamed text before the done event, which is what marks it as a document
satisfying the schema.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Tools in the same turn, where supports_response_schema_with_tools is true (folded in): a response that carries tool calls is a step of the tool loop and is not checked; the final answer is. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Tools in the same turn.** A context may carry `tools` and a schema together
where `supports_response_schema_with_tools` is true. The model then either calls
tools or answers in the schema: a response that carries tool calls is a step of
the tool loop and is not checked, and the check applies to the answer that
carries none, the final one.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Tools in the same turn: a provider whose constraint is a decoding grammar leaves supports_response_schema_with_tools false. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider whose constraint is a decoding grammar
(it forces the output into the schema token by token) MUST leave that capability
false: the grammar stops the model from calling a tool, and it writes a
schema-valid answer in its place, invented rather than looked up, which no check
can tell from a true one.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Tools in the same turn: a response that ended on a call the provider would not hand over is a step of the tool loop, not checked, with no document, saying so by its finish reason. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A response that ended on a call the provider would
not hand over (a call it could not parse, or one to a tool the request did
not enable) is a
step of the tool loop as well, which tells the model and asks again (Section
6.4): it is not checked, carries no document, and says so by that finish
reason, which a caller of `generate()` outside the loop reads.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Tools in the same turn: supports_response_schema a provider default the host can override in the provider's configuration. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Support depends on the model and, behind a custom base URL, on the
server, so `supports_response_schema` is a provider default that an
implementation SHOULD let the host override in the provider's configuration.

requirements.applies: §6.7: a consumer that must run on any provider reads supports_response_schema and, where it is false, asks for JSON in the prompt; only the consumer keeps it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
consumer that must run on any provider reads the property, and where it is false
asks for JSON in the prompt and parses the answer itself.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Declaring tools: a provider declares each tool of the context in its vendor's format. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Declaring tools (normative).** A provider declares each tool of the context
in its vendor's format.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Declaring tools: a tool without parameters declared as an object schema with no properties, never an empty map, and a schema whose root has no type declared an object's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool without parameters (an absent or empty schema)
is declared as an object schema with no properties, which every vendor
accepts, never as an empty map, and a schema whose root has no type is
declared an object's, for every vendor: some vendors refuse it
untyped.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Declaring tools, tool names (checked in two places, folded in): a name no vendor accepts (empty, or with a character other than a letter, a digit, _, ., : or -) refused when the tool is defined. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Vendors accept different tool names, so the
names are checked in two places:

- An implementation refuses, when a tool is defined, a name no vendor accepts:
  an empty one, or one with a character other than a letter, a digit, `_`,
  `.`, `:` or `-`.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Declaring tools: a loader of tools defined elsewhere (MCP) skips a tool under such a name with a warning and keeps the others. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A loader of tools defined elsewhere (MCP) skips such a tool
  with a warning and keeps the others.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Declaring tools: each provider checks its vendor's name rule when it declares tools (an AI provider a turn's; the sentence also names a realtime provider's session), raising before the request an error naming the tool and the rule. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- Each provider checks its own vendor's rule when it declares tools, an AI
  provider a turn's, a realtime provider a session's (at connection and at
  every reconfiguration), and for a name its vendor refuses it raises, before
  the request, an error naming the tool and the rule, rather than letting the
  vendor reject the request mid-turn, or a realtime endpoint accept the
  declaration and fail the call later, opaquely.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Declaring tools, realtime (media feature realtime): a realtime endpoint that hands the tools to another model checks that model's vendor's rule. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Where a realtime endpoint
  hands the tools to another model (a hosted reasoning backend, an agent's
  think provider), the rule is that model's vendor's.

requirements.applies: §6.7 Declaring tools: a provider that cannot know its server's rule (behind a custom base URL, a vendor-compatible gateway included) checks none. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider that cannot
  know its server's rule (any server behind a custom base URL, a
  vendor-compatible gateway included) checks none: the server decides.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A tool result on the wire, rendered in the vendor's format: where that format has an error flag, a result whose call was refused, failed, blocked, served by nothing or cancelled carries it, the text the same either way. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A tool result on the wire.** A provider renders each tool result as its
vendor's format carries one. Where that format has an error flag on a result, a
result whose call was
refused, failed, blocked, served by nothing or cancelled carries it; the text
the model reads is the same either way.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A request the model cannot serve: where the provider's model catalogue says the model refuses function tools on the endpoint, or the endpoint does not serve it, the request fails before it is sent with a non-retryable error naming the model; behind a base URL the server decides. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A request the model cannot serve.** Where a provider knows, from its model
catalogue, that the model refuses function tools on the endpoint it calls, or
that the endpoint does not serve the model at all, the request fails before it
is sent, with a non-retryable error naming the model. Behind a base URL the
server decides.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A failed generation: a ProviderError whose retryable flag depends neither on the provider nor on the failure's form. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**What a failed generation reads as (normative).** A provider MUST raise a
failure as a `ProviderError` whose `retryable` flag does not depend on the
provider or on the form the server gave the failure.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A failed generation: its status, the one the server described (the HTTP status, else the status or error type in the error's body). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its status is the one the
server described: the HTTP status of an error response, else the status or
error type written in the error's body, as when a stream already answered 200
carries an error event (an error type that stands for a status, an
overload's, reads as that status).

requirements.applies: §6.7 A failed generation: a status of 408, 409, 429 or any 5xx retryable, any other final. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A status of 408, 409, 429 or any 5xx is retryable; any other
status is final.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A failed generation without a status: a lost connection retryable; an answer that could not be read final, never an empty success. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Without a status, a lost connection (refused, reset or timed
out) is retryable, and an answer that could not be read is final: a body that
is not the provider's format, such as a gateway's HTML page in place of JSON,
including a stream that ends without one event, never reads as an empty
success.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A failed generation: a 200 whose body is an error object reads as the status it names. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A 200 whose body is an error object reads as the status it names.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A failed generation: a status the provider's SDK drops makes the failure final; another failure without a status retryable only when its message names a retryable status, a rate limit or an overload, as whole words. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
provider whose SDK drops a status it does not classify cannot read it, and
its failure is final; any other failure without a status is retryable only
when its message names a retryable status, a rate limit or an overload, as
whole words.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A failed generation, the one exception: a provider whose server reports with no status only a stream it aborted reads that failure as a lost connection. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One exception is kept: a provider whose server reports with no status only a
stream it aborted (its template failed to parse the model's own output) reads
that failure, a generation defect that a new sample may not repeat, as a lost
connection.

requirements.applies: §6.7 A failed generation: the failure's text leads with the provider's name and its status, unless its message already names the provider as a word or names none, keeping the provider's own text. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The failure's text, as a turn's error record, `ON_ERROR`
and a log line read it, leads with the provider's name and the status it
answered, `acme (402): Payment required`, `acme: connection reset`,
unless its message already names the provider as a word, in any case, or it
names no provider; its message keeps the provider's own text.

requirements.applies: §6.7 SMS provider interface, where an implementation offers SMS transports: send(), parse_webhook() and verify_signature(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**SMS Provider interface:**

```
SMSProvider (interface)
├── send(event: RoomEvent, to: string, from: string) → ProviderResult
├── parse_webhook(payload: map) → InboundMessage
└── verify_signature(payload, signature, timestamp) → bool
```

requirements.applies: §6.7 Email provider interface, where an implementation offers email transports: send() and parse_inbound(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Email Provider interface:**

```
EmailProvider (interface)
├── send(event: RoomEvent, to: string, from: string, subject: string | null) → ProviderResult
└── parse_inbound(payload: map) → InboundMessage
```

requirements.applies: §6.7: similar provider interfaces for WhatsApp, Messenger, Teams, RCS, HTTP, voice (STT, TTS, media feature voice) and custom channel types. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Implementations SHOULD define similar provider interfaces for WhatsApp, Messenger,
Teams, RCS, HTTP, Voice (STT, TTS), and any custom channel types.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers (what a classifier is and why a component asks one, folded in): support is optional. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A classifier answers narrow, typed questions about a state (a text, or
structured data such as a turn with the conversation around it) with
probabilities, not generated text. It is how a component asks for judgment where
code needs understanding (was the agent addressed, did the person finish)
without a generation: the component asks its questions together, in one call,
and composes the answers in code, where each one stays visible and measurable.
Support is OPTIONAL.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers them: the Classifier interface (classify(), close()) and the YesNoQuestion, ChoiceQuestion (two options at least) and ScoreQuestion (ordered levels, two at least) questions. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
Classifier (interface)
├── classify(state: string | JSON, questions: map<string, Question>) → Answers
└── close() → void

YesNoQuestion
├── instructions: string                # The question, and what it means
├── yes: string | null = null           # What a yes covers, when that needs saying
└── no: string | null = null            # What a no covers

ChoiceQuestion
├── instructions: string
└── options: map<string, string>        # Each option and what it covers; two at least

ScoreQuestion
├── instructions: string
└── levels: list<string>                # Ordered levels, lowest first, each described; two at least

```

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers them: the YesNoAnswer, ChoiceAnswer and ScoreAnswer answers (a score the expected level) and Answers, every question answered by name. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
YesNoAnswer
└── probability: float                  # Of yes, in [0, 1]

ChoiceAnswer
├── choice: string                      # The most probable option
└── probabilities: map<string, float>   # Every option's

ScoreAnswer
├── score: float                        # The expected level: 0 for the first, a fraction between two
└── probabilities: list<float>          # Each level's, in the levels' order

Answers: map<string, Answer>            # By question name, every question answered
```

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers them: a classifier answers every question asked, or raises ClassifierError for what kept it from answering, its wait bounded. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
§6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers them: the questions' wording sent as the caller wrote it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It sends the questions' wording as the
caller wrote it.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers them: a trained classifier's probabilities are calibrated, a generative model asked for one answer gives the answer it chose probability 1, and an implementation documents how far its probabilities can be trusted. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation says how far its probabilities can be
trusted: a trained classifier's are calibrated; a generative model asked for one
answer gives the answer it chose probability 1, and is documented as such.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers them: close() releases what the classifier opened itself, a provider or client it was handed staying its owner's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`close()` releases what the classifier opened itself; a provider or a client it
was handed stays its owner's.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers them: a classifier whose service reads a text alone sends a structured state as its JSON. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A classifier whose service reads a text alone sends a structured state as its
JSON.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers them: a question the service declines to answer fails the call with ClassifierError. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A question the service declines to answer (a refusal) fails the call with
`ClassifierError`, since a classifier answers every question or none.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers (their consumers, a speak policy and a discussion's dispatch, folded in): the classifiers an implementation provides are listed in its documentation, each with how far its probabilities can be trusted; only the documentation keeps it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A speak
policy built on judgments (Section 6.4) is a classifier's first consumer; a
discussion's dispatch policy (Section 19.7.5) is another. The classifiers an
implementation provides (a scripted mock, a classifier on any AI provider that
answers under a JSON schema, Section 6.7, classifiers on hosted or local
decision models) are listed in its documentation, each with how far its
probabilities can be trusted.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers one on a decision-model server: the model it was given sent with every call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A classifier on a decision-model server, one it starts itself included, sends
the model it was given with every call.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers on a decision-model server: the score computed from the levels' probabilities when the server sends them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A server does not always put the expected level in its `score`
(one may put the likeliest level there), so such a classifier computes the
score from the levels' probabilities when the server sends them, and a score
means the same whichever server answered.

requirements.applies: §6.8 Classifiers, where an implementation offers one that runs a decision model on the integrator's machine: downloaded and started at the first question, stopped by close(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A classifier that runs a decision
model on the integrator's machine downloads and starts it at the first
question, and `close()` stops it.

requirements.applies: §7 Permission Model; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
The permission model consists of three orthogonal primitives. The framework
provides the primitives; the integrator decides when and how to use them.

requirements.applies: §7.1 Access (its header), the READ_WRITE row: what a binding's access controls, and READ_WRITE, which reads and writes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Controls whether a channel can read events, write events, or both within a room.

| Value | Can Read | Can Write | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| READ_WRITE | Yes | Yes | Full participation |
|

requirements.applies: §7.1 Access, the READ_ONLY row: a channel that reads events through on_event() and writes none. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
READ_ONLY | Yes | No | Observe only (events via `on_event()`) |
|

requirements.applies: §7.1 Access, the WRITE_ONLY row: a channel that writes and reads no event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
WRITE_ONLY | No | Yes | Blind sender (unusual, but valid) |
|

requirements.applies: §7.1 Access, the NONE row: a binding that stays in the room and neither reads nor writes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: NONE | No | No | Fully disconnected (binding exists but inactive) |

requirements.applies: §7.2 Muting: the muted flag of a binding, and a muted channel still reading events through on_event(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A boolean flag on the binding. When `muted = true`:

- The channel STILL receives events via `on_event()` (reading is preserved).

requirements.applies: §7.2 Muting, a binding with muted = true: its channel's response stored BLOCKED with source_muted, or source_read_only when its access does not write, after its hooks (§7.5 rule 2); a streamed one may be closed unread instead. The paths RK-7.5-010 leaves out are not refused. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- The channel's response events are not broadcast (writing is blocked):
  each re-enters and its commit pass stores it `BLOCKED` with
  `source_muted` (`source_read_only` when its access does not write either),
  after its hooks (§7.5 rule 2); a streamed one MAY be closed unread instead.

requirements.applies: §7.2 Muting: a mute that lands while the channel's response streams, from the next row it commits (§7.5 rule 2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A mute that lands while the response streams holds from the next row it
  commits: that row and the ones after are stored `BLOCKED`, and the
  streaming target reads nothing more of the stream (§7.5 rule 2).

requirements.applies: §7.2 Muting, a binding with muted = true: the tasks and observations of its channel still collected (§7.5 rule 3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: - Side effects (tasks, observations) are STILL collected.

requirements.applies: §7.2 Muting: mute() and unmute(), the integrator's calls that set and clear a binding's muted flag. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Muting is temporary. The integrator calls `mute()` and `unmute()` as needed.

requirements.applies: §7.2 Muting: a binding's output_muted (§5.7), set by mute_output() and unmute_output(), against a mute. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A binding's `output_muted` (§5.7) is no mute: the integrator sets it with
`mute_output()` and `unmute_output()`, which fire no trigger and write no
lifecycle record, and the channel still receives every event.

requirements.applies: §7.2 A binding change that changes nothing: a detach or a binding update for a channel the room does not bind. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A binding change that changes nothing.** Detaching or updating a channel
the room does not bind fails, with nothing written.

requirements.applies: §7.2 A binding change that changes nothing: a binding update, applied to the binding as stored; one that changes nothing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An update applies to the
binding as stored, carrying over every field it does not name (§7.5 rule 6),
and one that changes nothing writes nothing and fires nothing, so a retried
call duplicates no hook and no record.

requirements.applies: §7.2 A binding change that changes nothing: when ON_CHANNEL_MUTED and ON_CHANNEL_UNMUTED fire on a binding change. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`ON_CHANNEL_MUTED` and
`ON_CHANNEL_UNMUTED` fire when `muted` changes, and only then: muting a
muted channel fires nothing.

requirements.applies: §7.2 A binding change that changes nothing: a binding change of access, visibility or metadata. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A change of access, visibility or metadata
fires no trigger and emits no framework event.

requirements.applies: §7.2 A binding change that changes nothing: a binding change in a room of any status (§5.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A binding changes whatever
the room's status, which governs what the timeline accepts (§5.1).

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility (its header), the all row: a visibility set on the binding and carried by each event (§5.2), and all, which every channel of the room sees. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Controls which channels see events produced by the source channel. Set on the
binding as a string value, and carried by each event (§5.2):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"all"` | All channels in the room see the event |
|

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility, the none row: an event no channel sees, stored in the timeline only. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`"none"` | No channels see the event (stored in timeline only) |
|

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility, the internal row: an event no channel sees, which marks a record the framework wrote (§6.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`"internal"` | No channels see the event, as with `"none"`; marks a record the framework wrote (§6.4) |
|

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility, the transport row: an event only the room's transport channels see. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`"transport"` | Only transport channels see the event |
|

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility, the intelligence row: an event only the room's intelligence channels see. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`"intelligence"` | Only intelligence channels see the event |
|

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility, the list row: an event only the channels a comma-separated list names see. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`"channel_a,channel_b"` | Comma-separated list of specific channel IDs |
|

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility, the single id row: an event only the channel the id names sees. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: `"channel_a"` | Single channel ID |

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility grammar; keywords are all, none, internal, transport and intelligence. The internal value is framework-only under §7.3 Who writes internal; public doors include attach, binding update, inbound visibility/response_visibility and direct injection visibility/response_visibility. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Grammar.** A visibility is one of the five keywords `all`, `none`,
`internal`, `transport` and `intelligence`, or a list of one or more channel
ids separated by commas. A keyword is written exactly as above, in lowercase
(`"All"` is a channel id, not the keyword).

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility grammar; keywords are all, none, internal, transport and intelligence. The internal value is framework-only under §7.3 Who writes internal; public doors include attach, binding update, inbound visibility/response_visibility and direct injection visibility/response_visibility. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The keywords are reserved: a
channel whose id is one of them MUST be refused when it is registered, and so
MUST a channel whose id contains a comma or starts or ends with whitespace, so
that every channel id can be written in a list.

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility grammar; keywords are all, none, internal, transport and intelligence. The internal value is framework-only under §7.3 Who writes internal; public doors include attach, binding update, inbound visibility/response_visibility and direct injection visibility/response_visibility. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Whitespace around the whole
value and around each id is ignored (`" sms , ws "` is `"sms,ws"`).

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility grammar; keywords are all, none, internal, transport and intelligence. The internal value is framework-only under §7.3 Who writes internal; public doors include attach, binding update, inbound visibility/response_visibility and direct injection visibility/response_visibility. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An empty
value and an empty item (`""`, `"sms,,ws"`, `"sms,"`) MUST be refused, a
`response_visibility` at the doors included (an inbound message, §5.12, a
direct injection, §10.5).

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility grammar; keywords are all, none, internal, transport and intelligence. The internal value is framework-only under §7.3 Who writes internal; public doors include attach, binding update, inbound visibility/response_visibility and direct injection visibility/response_visibility. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An empty value that reaches an event any other way
(a hook's modify, a custom store) reads as `none`, so that it restricts rather
than opens.

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility grammar; keywords are all, none, internal, transport and intelligence. The internal value is framework-only under §7.3 Who writes internal; public doors include attach, binding update, inbound visibility/response_visibility and direct injection visibility/response_visibility. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An id listed twice counts once, and a list is written back with
each id once, sorted by code point.

requirements.applies: §7.3 Visibility grammar; keywords are all, none, internal, transport and intelligence. The internal value is framework-only under §7.3 Who writes internal; public doors include attach, binding update, inbound visibility/response_visibility and direct injection visibility/response_visibility. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An id that names no channel bound to the
room is allowed and matches nothing.

requirements.applies: §7.3 Who writes internal: the framework alone writes internal, on the records it writes itself (§6.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Who writes `internal`.** Only the framework writes `internal`, on the
records it writes itself (an interruption record, §6.4): a value that marks
the framework's record is not the integrator's to give.

requirements.applies: §7.3 Who writes internal: internal given at a public door (attach, binding update, inbound message, direct injection), by a hook's modify (§9.4) or by a channel's response (§8.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation
MUST refuse it, before anything is read or written, on an attach and a
binding update, on an inbound message, as its `visibility` and as its
`response_visibility` alike (§5.12), and on a direct injection, its
visibility and its response visibility alike (§10.5); a hook's modify that
writes it, or that changes the visibility of an event that holds it (a
framework record), has the event's visibility put back from the original,
and one that writes it as a response visibility has it read as `none`
(§9.4); a channel's response that carries it is committed with `none`, and
one a channel gives its response as a response visibility reads as `none`
(§8.5).

requirements.applies: §7.3 Who writes internal: a record committed outside the pipeline (§10.5), whatever visibility its caller gives it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A record committed outside the pipeline (§10.5) is stored as its
caller gives it, and reaches no channel.

requirements.applies: §7.3 Who writes internal: the visibility an integrator gives an event to be stored and shown to no channel; the integrator's choice, which no implementation can keep for it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event the integrator wants stored
and shown to no channel takes `none`.

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: the visibility an event carries, all unless the caller sets one, beside its source binding's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**An event's visibility.** An event carries a visibility of its own (an
inbound message's `visibility`, §5.12, `"all"` unless the caller sets one),
and its source binding has one.

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: which channels see an event whose source the room binds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel sees an event whose source is
bound to the room only when both include it.

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: the visibility computed when an event commits, DELIVERED or BLOCKED, and stored as its visibility; the exceptions are RK-7.3-026 to 029. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The framework MUST compute the
visibility that includes exactly those channels when it commits the event,
DELIVERED (§10.1 step 12) or `BLOCKED` in its place (steps 10 and 11, §8.3),
and store it as the event's `visibility`: delivery (§10.2) and every history
rebuilt for a channel (§7.5 rule 8) read that field alone, so a binding
changed or removed later changes no past event.

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: an accepted EDIT or DELETE, narrowed to its target's visibility (§10.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An accepted EDIT or DELETE
is narrowed once more, to its target's visibility (§10.3).

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: a record stored BLOCKED, by a hook's block, a source refusal, the chain-depth limit or the reentry budget (§8.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A record stored
`BLOCKED` takes the visibility its event would have been delivered with, so
that a reader shown it later (a host's view of the room) sees no more of it
than it would have seen of the event: a hook's block and a source refusal,
of an inbound message, a direct injection or a response; the record of an
agent not asked at the chain-depth limit, and a response stored past the
reentry budget (§8.3).

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: an event whose source the room does not bind. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: An event whose source has no binding keeps its own.

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: an event a hook injects (§9.4), blocked or stored past the budget. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event a hook injects is no channel's and keeps its own (§9.4), blocked or
stored past the budget.

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility, the intersection of two visibilities: all with any value. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The intersection of two visibilities is:

- `all` with any value: that value;

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility, the intersection of two visibilities: internal with any value. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `internal` with any value: `internal`, which keeps the mark of a record
  the framework wrote;

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility, the intersection of two visibilities: none with any value but internal. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: - `none` with any value other than `internal`: `none`;

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility, the intersection of two visibilities: two categories. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a category with itself: that category; `transport` with `intelligence`:
  `none`;

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility, the intersection of two visibilities: two lists of channel ids. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: - two lists: the ids both name;

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility, the intersection of two visibilities: a category with a list, read from the room's bindings at commit. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a category with a list: the listed channels of that category, read from
  the room's bindings at commit; a listed id that no binding of the room
  holds is dropped.

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: an intersection of two visibilities that leaves no channel id. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: An intersection that leaves no id is `none`.

requirements.applies: §7.3 An event's visibility: an event a channel was not allowed to see at delivery, in the history the framework rebuilds for that channel (§7.5 rule 8); a channel's own accepted events stay in its context (RK-7.5-032). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
"See" is not "be delivered to". `"none"` reads *stored in timeline only*, and it
means it: an event a channel was not allowed to see at delivery MUST NOT reach
that channel later through history the framework rebuilds for it either. Rule 8
in §7.5 states that half.

requirements.applies: §7.4 Named Patterns; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
These are vocabulary for common configurations, NOT framework concepts. The
framework only knows access, muted, and visibility.

| Pattern | Configuration | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| **Direct** | `access=READ_WRITE, visibility="all"` | AI speaks to everyone in the room |
| **Assistant** | `access=READ_WRITE, visibility="ws_advisor"` | AI whispers only to the advisor |
| **Observer** | `access=READ_ONLY` | Sentiment analyzer watches, produces side effects only |
| **Muted** | `muted=true` | AI temporarily silenced but still tracking |
| **Internal** | `access=READ_WRITE, visibility="none"` | Writes stored in timeline but never broadcast; not the `internal` keyword, which marks a framework record (§7.3) |

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 1 (Reading): which channels receive an event through on_event(); a channel's own events are skipped (rule 5, RK-7.5-021). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Implementations MUST enforce these rules:

1. **Reading:** A channel receives events via `on_event()` if and only if its
   binding has `access` ∈ {READ_WRITE, READ_ONLY} AND the event's visibility
   includes this channel.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2 (Writing): whether a channel's response events are broadcast; the paths rule 2 does not cover are RK-7.5-010, 017 and 018. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
2. **Writing:** A channel's response events are broadcast if and only if its
   binding has `access` ∈ {READ_WRITE, WRITE_ONLY} AND `muted = false`.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: an inbound or directly injected event whose source binding cannot write. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Likewise, an inbound or directly-injected event whose source binding cannot
   write (`access` ∉ {READ_WRITE, WRITE_ONLY} OR `muted = true`) MUST be stored
   with status `BLOCKED` rather than `DELIVERED`, and MUST NOT be broadcast.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: the blocked_by of an event whose source binding cannot write, read-only or muted. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its `blocked_by` is `source_read_only` when the access does not write,
   `NONE` included and whether the binding is muted or not, since the access
   is the lasting cause; it is `source_muted` when the source could write but
   is muted.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: an event whose source has no binding in the room, a detached channel's included; a direct injection naming one raises instead (RK-7.5-007), and the paths RK-7.5-010, 017 and 018 leave out are not refused. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event whose source has no binding in the room, such as a
   channel the integrator detached (rule 7), MUST be stored `BLOCKED` with
   `blocked_by` = `source_unbound` and MUST NOT be broadcast either; the
   channel of an inbound message still parses it (§10.1 step 4), with a
   context that holds no event of the room.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: a direct injection (§10.5) whose source has no binding in the room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A direct injection that names
   such a channel raises instead, with nothing written (§10.5).

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: a response, checked after its BEFORE_BROADCAST hooks on each path that commits one, but the paths RK-7.5-010 leaves out. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A response
   re-enters like any other event (§10.1 step 14) and meets this check after its
   `BEFORE_BROADCAST` hooks (step 11 after step 9), on each path that commits
   a response: a buffered response, a streamed row, a regenerated answer.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: the source binding the check reads, as the event's hooks left it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
   check reads the source's binding as the hooks left it, so a hook that
   mutes the source of the event it reads blocks that event.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: the paths it does not cover (the greeting, a delegation's trace in a child room no transport is shared into, a record committed outside the pipeline) and a child room with a shared transport, which it covers. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The greeting,
   and the trace a delegation writes into a child room no transport is
   shared into (§23.3), and a record an integrator commits outside the
   pipeline (§10.5), are committed by paths of their own and are not
   covered here; a child room with a shared transport commits its agent's
   response as a room does, and is covered.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: the response of a muted or read-only source, stored BLOCKED with what its hooks decided (rule 3); the paths RK-7.5-010 leaves out are not refused. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A muted or
   read-only source's response is therefore stored `BLOCKED` with what its
   hooks decided collected (rule 3), and a hook that blocks it names the
   block.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: a streamed response from a source that cannot write, read-only or muted; the paths RK-7.5-010 leaves out are not refused. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A streamed response from a source that cannot write is piped live
   to no channel: a read-only source's stream is read to its end and each row
   stored `BLOCKED`; a muted source's MAY be closed unread, the reply never
   generated.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: the bindings each row of a streamed response is checked and planned with, a binding changed while it streams included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each row of a streamed response reads the room's bindings at
   its commit, under the room lock, and is checked and planned with them: a
   binding changed while the response streams (its source muted, made
   read-only or detached; a transport made write-only or detached) holds from
   the next row.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: the streaming target once the room no longer lets it read the response. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Once the room no longer lets the streaming target read the
   response (its source can no longer write, the room refuses the row,
   §5.1, the target is no longer one the answer reaches, §12.2 step
   11s, or a message's hooks narrowed its visibility away from the target,
   §7.3), the target is handed nothing more of
   the stream, neither text nor rows, and the rows after are delivered as
   their plans say.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: a streamed tool-call row whose hooks narrowed it away from the streaming target. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool-call row whose hooks narrowed it away from the
   target is not handed to the target, and the stream goes on.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: a source both read-only and muted, and its streamed response. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A source
   both read-only and muted is refused as read-only, so
   its stream is read to its end.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: an event a hook injects (§9.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event a hook injects takes no source
   check: it is the hook's, not a channel's (§9.4).

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 2: an event the framework itself writes through the pipeline, such as a delegation's task description (§23.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Nor does an event the
   framework itself writes through the pipeline, such as a delegation's task
   description (§23.3): it is the framework's, not a channel's.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 3 (Side effects): the tasks and observations of an event, whatever access or mute status, rule 2's refusals included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
3. **Side effects:** Tasks and observations are ALWAYS collected regardless of
   access or mute status — including for events blocked by rule 2.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 4 (Visibility filtering): the channels an event is delivered to. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
4. **Visibility filtering:** When broadcasting an event, the framework MUST
   deliver only to channels that both the event's own visibility and its
   source binding's include: the intersection the event carries from its
   commit (§7.3).

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 5 (Self-skip): a channel's own events. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: 5. **Self-skip:** A channel MUST NOT receive its own events via `on_event()`.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 6: a binding the framework creates from an existing one (sharing a channel into a delegated room, copying a template, re-attaching a detached channel). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
6. **A binding is never widened implicitly.** Wherever the framework creates a
   binding from an existing one — sharing a channel into a delegated room
   (§23.3), copying a template, re-attaching a channel it detached earlier — the
   new binding MUST NOT grant more than the one it derives from. Carrying over
   a binding's category and metadata while letting `access`, `visibility` and
   `muted` fall back to defaults silently promotes a read-only observer into a
   full participant, in a room the integrator never configured.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 6: what widens a binding. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Widening a
   binding is an explicit act: it MUST come from an integrator call that says
   so, never from a default filling a gap.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 7: attaching a channel automatically when a message arrives for a room it is not bound to; what such an attach must not do is RK-7.5-025. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
7. **Attaching a channel is a decision, not a repair.** An implementation MAY
   attach a channel automatically when a message arrives for a room the
   channel is not yet bound to.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 7, where an implementation attaches a channel automatically (RK-7.5-024): a channel detached from the room earlier, and a binding that already exists. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It MUST NOT do so when the channel was
   previously detached from that room, and MUST NOT use such an attach to
   replace a binding that already exists — detaching is how an integrator
   revokes a channel's access, and an automatic re-attach at default
   permissions undoes exactly that.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8: everything rebuilt from the timeline for a channel (memory history, model prompt, per-channel replay), against the visibility withheld at delivery; a channel's own accepted events stay in its context (RK-7.5-032), and host code reads the history whole (RK-7.5-034). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
8. **Reconstructed context obeys the same rule as delivery.** Rule 1 governs
   `on_event()`; this one governs everything the implementation rebuilds from
   the timeline *for* a channel — the history handed to a memory provider, the
   turns assembled into a model prompt, any per-channel replay of what was said.
   A channel MUST NOT obtain there an event visibility withheld from it at
   delivery. Withholding an event at broadcast and returning it one turn later
   as context is not a partial enforcement of visibility; it is none.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8: an event stored BLOCKED, in the context rebuilt for any channel, its own source's included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The same holds for an event delivered to nobody. An event stored `BLOCKED`
   — refused by a hook (§10.1 step 10), written by a source that could not
   write, read-only or muted, or that has no binding in the room (step 11,
   rule 2), stopped by the chain-depth cap or the reentry cap (§8.3) —
   MUST NOT reach any channel's reconstructed context, its own source's
   included: the room
   refused that turn, and a model that reads its own refused answer as
   history continues from a turn nobody received.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8: a BLOCKED record in the timeline reads (§14.1) and in the history rebuilt for hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The record stays in the
   timeline for host code and audit (the point on host code below applies to
   it unchanged), behind an explicit request: a timeline read serves the rows
   the room received by default and the `BLOCKED` rows only when asked
   (§14.1), a read by id is unconditional, and the history rebuilt for hooks
   stays whole.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8: an event deleted by an accepted DELETE (§10.3), in the history rebuilt for a channel and for hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event deleted by an accepted DELETE stays in the history rebuilt for a
   channel, with its content withheld: an empty text in place of what was
   said, and nothing of the provider's original payload; its stored record,
   and the history rebuilt for hooks, keep the content (§10.3).

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8: where the per-reader filter is applied, against a context shared by every channel of a broadcast. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The filter is per reader, so it MUST be applied where the reader is known —
   a single `RoomContext` shared by every channel of a broadcast cannot be
   filtered once for all of them.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8: the filter applied before a component that can transform the history (a summarizing memory provider), and a per-reader view host code can ask for. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation MUST apply it before the
   history reaches a component that can transform it (a summarizing or
   compacting memory provider re-emits hidden content as a summary otherwise),
   and SHOULD expose the per-reader view so host code can ask for it.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8, the first point it does not cover: a channel's own accepted events in its rebuilt context; its refused ones stay out (RK-7.5-027). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Three points the rule does NOT cover:

   - **A channel always sees its own accepted events.** Rule 5 skips a
     channel's own event at delivery because it produced it, not because it
     may not know it. A rule that dropped an agent's own turns from its own
     prompt would erase the assistant pattern of §7.4
     (`visibility="ws_advisor"`) from the inside. Its own *refused* turns are
     the exception stated above: an answer nobody received, a muted channel's
     included, is not history the channel may continue from.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8: a channel with no binding in the room, handed none of its events (rule 2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel with
     no binding in the room is handed none of its events, its own included
     (rule 2).

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8, the second point it does not cover: the history read by host code (hooks, scorers, framework machinery). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Host code reads the timeline whole.** Hooks, scorers and framework
     machinery run in the integrator's process and hold the store already;
     filtering their `recent_events` would forbid nothing and would break
     legitimate readers. Visibility is a rule between the room and its
     channels.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8, the third point: the visibility a rebuilt history reads, the one stored at the event's commit or by a later write of it (§11.7.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Visibility is stamped at commit.** The event's own `visibility` field
     is the whole answer: the intersection stored at its commit (§7.3), or
     what a later write of the event set (a held message's release,
     §11.7.6), never the source's binding as it stands when the history is
     read. Widening or
     narrowing a binding changes what the source's later events reach, not
     what its past ones reached.

requirements.applies: §7.5 Permission Rules, rule 8: an event whose source binding no longer exists, in the history rebuilt for a channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The same holds when the source binding no
     longer exists: an implementation MUST NOT treat an unresolvable source
     as a reason to hide ordinary history, which would empty a room's context
     the moment a transport detaches.

requirements.applies: §8.1: a room event, stored in its room's timeline with an index that increases within the room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Room events are stored in the room's timeline. They have a sequential `index`
that is monotonically increasing within each room.

requirements.applies: §8.1 sequential indexing: the index of a room's first event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Sequential indexing requirements:**

- The `index` MUST start at 0 for the first event in a room.

requirements.applies: §8.1 sequential indexing: the index each event takes, the room's event_count, given out once; a hard delete's gaps (§14.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- Each event MUST take the room's `event_count` as its index, so indexes
  are given out consecutively and never again; a hard delete leaves the
  gaps it makes (§14.3).

requirements.applies: §8.1 sequential indexing: the room's latest_index (§5.1), with and without events. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- The room's `latest_index` (§5.1) is the highest index committed in it, and
  MUST be `null` while the room has no event.

requirements.applies: §8.1 sequential indexing: index assignment within a room, concurrent commits included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- The `index` MUST be assigned atomically per room. A room-level lock (§13.5)
  serializes assignment within a single process; it is **NOT** sufficient when a
  persistent store is shared across processes (e.g. a load-balanced deployment),
  because per-process locks do not coordinate.

requirements.applies: §8.1 sequential indexing: a persistent store shared across processes (e.g. a load-balanced deployment). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Such a store MUST make index
  assignment authoritative at the storage layer: a `UNIQUE(room_id, index)`
  constraint, with the index computed and the event inserted in a **single
  storage transaction**, so concurrent writers serialize on the store rather
  than on an in-process lock.

requirements.applies: §8.1 sequential indexing: a store handed an event whose (room_id, index) it already holds; the list's last item, what the index serves, is informative. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A duplicate `(room_id, index)` MUST be rejected by the store (the constraint
  violation surfaced to the caller), never silently persisted.
- The `index` enables pagination, read horizon tracking, and gap detection;
  a hard delete's gaps are expected (§14.3).

requirements.applies: §8.1 event ids: every event the pipeline commits, whatever id a channel or a hook built it with. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Event ids.** The pipeline MUST give every event it commits its `id`, whatever id
a channel or a hook built the event with.

requirements.applies: §8.1 event ids: when an inbound event, a response, a hook's injected event and a direct injection (§10.5) take their ids, and what identity resolution and hooks read. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An inbound event takes its id at
§10.1 step 4, when the receiving channel builds it, so identity resolution and
hooks read the id it is committed with; a response event, an event a hook
injects and an event injected directly (§10.5) each take a fresh id as their
pass begins. A channel or a hook that reuses an id (the trigger's, a constant,
one from its provider) therefore never makes two events share one, and
`responds_to` and every read or write by id name one event.

requirements.applies: §8.1 event ids: where a channel puts its provider's own identifier for an event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A provider's own
identifier belongs in `source.provider_message_id`.

requirements.applies: §8.1 event ids: a record committed outside the pipeline (§10.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A record committed outside
the pipeline (§10.5) keeps the id its caller gives it.

requirements.applies: §8.2: framework events, published to subscribers and never stored in a room's timeline. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Framework events are global lifecycle notifications published to subscribers.
They are NOT stored in any room timeline.
