  are the handler's; a handler that hands that error on with its decision has
  it reported on the refusal's `error_detail`, as on the channel's own doors.

requirements.applies: §9.3 SYNC hooks: a hook on any trigger whose SYNC hooks run as a chain (Section 9.2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A hook MAY declare itself fail-closed** (`fail_closed = true`), on any
  trigger whose SYNC hooks run as a chain (Section 9.2): a content check on
  `BEFORE_BROADCAST` (PII, moderation) is exactly such a hook, while the
  trigger as a whole stays fail-open so that a broken
  logging hook cannot take every room down.

requirements.applies: §9.3 SYNC hooks: a hook that declared itself fail-closed (fail_closed = true). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every unusable outcome of a
  fail-closed hook MUST block, and the block MUST name the hook and the
  outcome so the sender can be told why: `blocked_by` is the hook name and
  the reason is `hook_timeout:<name>`, `hook_error:<name>` or
  `hook_invalid_result:<name>`.

requirements.applies: §9.3 SYNC hooks: a MODIFY result that carries a payload, a falsy one included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A MODIFY result replaces the payload with the one it carries, including a
  falsy one. Redacting a string to empty is a modification; treating it as
  absent would pass the original to the next hook.

requirements.applies: §9.3 SYNC hooks: a MODIFY result that carries no payload, as one whose payload is of the wrong type. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A MODIFY that carries no
  payload replaces nothing: it is an unusable result, which the trigger's or
  the hook's fail-open or fail-closed rule decides, as it decides a payload
  of the wrong type.

requirements.applies: §9.3 SYNC hooks: the arguments a BEFORE_TOOL_USE chain hands from hook to hook and leaves to the call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The arguments a BEFORE_TOOL_USE chain leaves are the call's.** The call
  runs with those the chain ended with: a MODIFY's payload, or the payload a
  hook edited in place, each read by the next hook.

requirements.applies: §9.3 SYNC hooks: a BEFORE_TOOL_USE hook that returns arguments in its result's metadata. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook may instead
  return arguments under `metadata["arguments"]`, which no later hook reads
  and which has the last word over the chain's, the last such rewrite
  winning.

requirements.applies: §9.3 SYNC hooks: the arguments a BEFORE_TOOL_USE chain leaves, whichever way a hook gave them (§21.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Either way the arguments are validated again before the call
  runs (§21.1); arguments that are not an object refuse it.

requirements.applies: SYNC hook chains; trigger-specific and per-hook exceptions in §9.3 apply.
requirements.text:
An unusable result's tasks and observations are collected, as side
  effects always are (§7.5 rule 3), save a result holding a sixth composite
  level (§5.3), of which nothing is collected; the events it would inject are
  not.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ASYNC hooks: when they run and whether the triggering operation waits for them; the three triggers it awaits follow. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ASYNC hooks:**

- Run concurrently after the triggering operation completes, which does not
  wait for them, but for three, which it awaits, each hook within its own
  timeout:

requirements.applies: §9.3 ASYNC hooks: ON_ROOM_CREATED, on every room creation, the integrator's and §10.1 step 2's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
ON_ROOM_CREATED: every creation, the integrator's and §10.1 step 2's
    alike, returns once its hooks have finished or timed out, so that a hook
    that attaches the room's agent (Appendix B.1) has done so before anything
    is sent into the room.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ASYNC hooks: ON_RECORDING_STARTED, a room's, a voice session's or a conference track's (Section 12.11). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
ON_RECORDING_STARTED, a room's, a voice session's or a conference
    track's: the recording's start is the consent point no media reaches it
    before (Section 12.11), so its hooks have finished before the first frame
    is recorded.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ASYNC hooks: the triggers a voice, speech-to-speech, conference or video session's media stream fires. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The triggers a session's media stream fires (a voice, speech-to-speech,
    conference or video session's: its start, its speech and turn edges,
    partial transcriptions, barge-ins, DTMF, levels, `AFTER_TTS`, vision and
    detection results): the stream awaits them in order, so that each is
    observed before the stream's next trigger, a SYNC one included. A
    partial transcription observed after its final would bring back an
    utterance the final closed.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ASYNC hooks: the framework event (§8.2) that reports the operation an ASYNC trigger follows. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The framework event that reports the operation (§8.2: `event_processed`,
  `ai_response`, `feedback`, `recording_started`, `recording_stopped`) comes
  once the trigger's hooks have ended, the operation not waiting for them.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ASYNC hooks: an ASYNC hook's result. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Cannot block or modify events.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ASYNC hooks: an ASYNC hook that raises. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Exceptions MUST be caught and logged, never propagated.
- Used for observability, logging, side effects.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: an AI channel's tool calls. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Who serves a call.** An AI channel decides it call by call, not turn by
turn.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a call the provider already ran, and a key a model writes in any call's arguments. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call the provider already ran is reported: the provider says so on the
call, with its result and whether it failed, never in its arguments, which are
the model's text: a key a model writes there (`_result`) is an argument like any
other, and its call is judged as any call.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a call an external tool handler is configured to decide, and any other call of an AI channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
call an external tool handler is configured to decide is that handler's; any
other call is the channel's own, through the pre-execution gate, then its
handler, and is a call nothing served when no handler takes it.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a call the provider ran, and a BEFORE_TOOL_USE BLOCK on a call the channel serves, with or without a handler. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call the
provider ran therefore never reaches the channel's handler because the channel
has tools of its own, and a BEFORE_TOOL_USE BLOCK refuses every call the
channel serves, a channel without a handler included.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a call to a tool a BEFORE_AI_GENERATION hook withdrew from the turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool a
BEFORE_AI_GENERATION hook withdrew is gone from the turn: a call to it is the
channel's to refuse, never an external handler's to decide.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a round with calls served outside the channel and calls the channel serves. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A round that mixes
both kinds hands the next round every call it made, each with its result: the
model reads the calls served outside the channel beside its own.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a call the turn cut before its report (its cancellation, a transport that stopped reading), whoever was to serve it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call the
turn cut before its report (the turn's cancellation, a transport that stopped
reading before the call was decided) is reported once, cancelled, to
ON_TOOL_CALL's observers alone, whoever was to serve it: an external handler
hears of it through `on_tool_cancelled`, which reports it so by default, and
never through `on_tool_result`, which reports an outcome. The handler may
never have been asked about the call; a decision of its still pending is its
own to withdraw.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: an AI channel that closes while its turns execute calls. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The channel's close is such a cut: an AI channel that
closes cancels the calls its running turns execute, each reported once,
cancelled, its end row too, asks no further round, and each such turn ends
`cancelled`, as a speech-to-speech channel's close interrupts its calls
(Section 12.4).

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: an external tool handler that raises while it decides a call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A handler that raises while it decides fails the call, as a
tool handler that raises does.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a call whose outcome the model already read, its report interrupted by a cut. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call whose outcome the model already read
(the provider ran it, an external handler decided it, its realtime result
went out) is still owed its report when a cut interrupts that report: it is
reported once, to ON_TOOL_CALL's observers alone, with that outcome.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: where a call's report is claimed, and an ACP call's end once closed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
report is claimed where the observers hear it, past the SYNC chain and once
their context is built, so a report a cut interrupted is still owed and one
the observers heard is never made twice; an ACP call's end, once closed,
reaches its report even when the task carrying it is cut.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a call issued once its session ended. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call issued once
its session ended runs no gate and is reported once, cancelled.

requirements.applies: §9.3 Who serves a call: a call cut after its report, its turn ended before the model read its result. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call cut
after its report keeps its stored end row `cancelled` when the turn ended
before the model read its result: the row says what the turn delivered, the
report what ran.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: where the rules below hold, and a firing that reports a call that ran outside the channel or whose outcome the model already read. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ON_TOOL_CALL, where the call was served:**

These hold where the channel's own tool loop serves the call. An external
handler's firing is a report on a call that ran outside the channel, and so is
a firing on any call whose outcome the model already read (a call the
provider ran itself): its override is discarded, and the display payload an external agent attaches
(ACP's tool content) is that agent's.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: a firing that reports a call whose outcome the agent already read (an external handler's, a call the provider ran). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
No hook can rewrite or withhold what the
agent already read, so its observers see the provider's outcome and the
provider's own failure marker, whatever a SYNC hook returned, a BLOCK included.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: a call the channel's own tool loop served, and its SYNC hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A SYNC hook sees the call's result and its structured copy (the payload a
  tool publishes for UI surfaces beside its result, such as MCP
  `structuredContent`).

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: a SYNC hook on a call the channel's own tool loop served. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It MAY replace the result, and MAY replace or clear
  the structured copy.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: a SYNC hook that replaces a served call's result and not its structured copy. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A result replaced alone keeps the copy: a hook that
  rewrites text, such as PII re-tokenisation, is not withholding the payload.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: a SYNC hook's BLOCK on a call the channel's own tool loop served. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A BLOCK withholds the result: the model reads the block's reason as a
  failed call, and the tool-call event carries the failure marker and no
  structured copy. An event that kept the payload while the text was
  withheld would publish, to every surface that renders it, what the hook
  was there to withhold.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a call that failed or was refused, and its structured copy. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A call that failed or was refused carries no structured copy either.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: several SYNC hooks on one served call, whatever form each replacement takes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
SYNC hooks apply in turn to one outcome: each sees the result and the
  structured copy as the previous hook left them, whichever form its
  replacement took (a MODIFY whose event carries a new result, or the result
  override). The model reads what the last one left. A second hook handed the
  original would undo the first: "redact", then "cite the source", would
  publish what the redaction removed.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: a SYNC hook's MODIFY whose payload is not a tool-call event (§9.3 SYNC hooks). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A MODIFY whose payload is not a tool-call
  event replaces nothing, as the general rule above has it: the chain carries
  on from the outcome the previous hook left, that hook's own override
  included.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: a SYNC hook that clears a served call's result, on every channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A replacement counts whatever its value: a hook that clears a served result
  (replaces it with no value) has the model read that empty value, serialized
  as any other result (JSON `null`), on every channel, never the original.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: its ASYNC observers. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
ASYNC observers run after the SYNC hooks, on the final outcome: the result
  the model reads, as it reads it (a replacement serialized), never one a hook
  replaced.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, a served call: the ASYNC observers of a call a SYNC hook blocked, or whose result a fail-closed hook withheld by failing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A BLOCK does not spare them, nor
  does the failure of a fail-closed hook that withheld the result: they fire
  with the failure marker and the reason the model reads, since every call
  MUST fire ON_TOOL_CALL with its outcome (below).

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: every tool call, whatever its outcome. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ON_TOOL_CALL, where the call was refused or failed:**

- Every tool call MUST fire ON_TOOL_CALL with its outcome, whether it was
  served, refused before execution (undeclared tool, invalid arguments, tool
  policy, skill gating, a BLOCK from BEFORE_TOOL_USE), failed during execution
  (a handler that raised), or reached no servant at all. A trigger that fires
  only for the calls that succeeded cannot support an audit trail: a refused
  agent and an idle one produce the same record, which is none.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: every report of a call, on every door. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every report of a call, on every door, carries the arguments the call ran
  with, or those the gate had when it stopped it (repaired, rewritten by
  BEFORE_TOOL_USE); the model's own only for a call stopped before its
  arguments were read.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a call its turn or its session cut while it ran. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call its turn or its session cut while it ran is
  reported with the arguments it ran with.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: the firing for a call refused before execution, failed during execution or that reached no servant, where the trigger's SYNC hooks serve tools (the AI tool loop, the realtime channel). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Such a firing MUST NOT be able to serve the call. Where the trigger's SYNC
  hooks do serve tools — the AI tool loop, the realtime channel — that means
  dispatching to **the hooks registered ASYNC only**: a refused call reaching a
  servant would let the refusal hide the side effect instead of preventing it,
  and the pre-execution gate of Section 12.4 would hold under some
  configurations and not others.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a firing that reports a call that ran outside the channel (an external tool handler relaying its provider's outcome). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Where the tool already ran outside the channel
  and the firing is a report by construction — an external tool handler
  relaying its provider's outcome — it MAY reach every hook, and any result
  such a hook offers MUST be discarded.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a call that never ran: refused on any door, failed by a handler that raised deciding it, or cancelled. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call that never ran is no such
  report: a refusal on every door (the pre-execution gate's, an external
  handler's, a call the external door refuses itself, a rejected ACP
  permission, a refusal ACP imposes on an approval it cannot apply), a
  handler that raised while it decided, and a cancellation reach the ASYNC
  observers only, marked
  `refused` or `cancelled` beside `is_error`, so an audit tells a refusal from
  a failure and from a cancellation.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: an external tool handler's own refusal, and a handler that raises while it decides. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An external handler hears its own refusal
  through `on_tool_refused`, which reports it so by default, and never through
  `on_tool_result`; a handler that raises while it decides fails the call,
  which the channel reports itself, with what failed (`error_detail`), as it
  reports a call it refused itself.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a handler that raises while it reports a call, on every door that hands a call's report to a handler (an AI channel's external door, ACP). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A handler that raises while it reports a
  call (its outcome, its refusal, its cancellation) is logged and does not
  fail the turn: the channel reports the call itself, once, as it ended,
  unless the handler's report had already reached ON_TOOL_CALL's observers,
  on every door that hands a call's report to a handler (an AI channel's
  external door, ACP); an override that cannot take the arguments the door
  hands it raises the same way.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: an ACP call, with or without an external handler. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An ACP
  call reports the same body with an external handler as without one: a
  cancellation's envelope, a failure's bounded error.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: an ACP call whose permission RoomKit rejected, run anyway by the agent and closed completed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An ACP call whose
  permission RoomKit rejected (it refused the call, or its handler raised
  deciding it) that the agent ran anyway and closed completed is reported as
  it ended, served, its markers those of a served call, and MUST carry a
  marker of its own (`refused_but_ran`) on its report and its end row, so an
  audit sees the rejection the agent went past; that report carries what
  failed in the rejection (`error_detail`) when something did, whether the
  handler or the channel makes it, but for a handler whose override cannot
  take it, which reports the call without it and is logged, as a refusal's
  detail is.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: every tool call's outcome, on its event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The outcome MUST be carried on the event as a discrete marker, not left to
  be inferred from the result body. A refusal's body is a body like any other:
  one implementation's refusals are JSON error envelopes, another's are the
  prose the model is meant to read, and an external provider's are whatever it
  printed. An observer that has to recognise a failure in the text will read a
  refused call as a completed one, and a tool whose own output resembles a
  refusal as a failure.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: the outcomes the channel itself determines, and a refusal a handler returns in its body (Section 15.8.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
That obligation covers every outcome the channel itself determines: a refusal
  by the pre-execution gate, a tool not available in the turn, a guard the
  channel applies to the call (a repeat of the same call with the same
  arguments), a handler that raised, a call nothing served, and the verdict an
  external tool handler received from its provider. A handler
  that instead *returns* a refusal has stated it in its body, where only its
  own convention can be read — Section 15.8.1 governs that reading.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a producer of a tool call's outcome that can state it structurally. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A producer
  that can state the outcome structurally SHOULD do so rather than leave it to
  be recognised.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: the body of a call's outcome, beside its marker. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The body MUST travel verbatim beside that marker: it is what the model is
  told, and its wording answers to that reader alone.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: an oversized body (Section 21.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An oversized body reaches
  the model through the bound of Section 21.5 like any tool result; the event
  carries it as the tool produced it.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a call whose handler raised, on every channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call whose handler raised MUST read the same on every channel: the tool's
  failure, named by the exception's class and nothing more (`{"error": "Tool
  'x' failed (<ExceptionClass>)"}`), with the failure marker. The exception's
  message can hold anything the failing code held (a connection string with
  its password, a path, a record), and neither the model nor its provider's
  logs are a place for it.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: the exception's message, for a call whose handler raised. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The message goes to the log and to ON_TOOL_CALL's
  observers, on the event's `error_detail`, never to the model nor to the
  stored TOOL_CALL_END.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a handler that raises a refusal (ToolRefusedError) or a failure (ToolFailedError) for the model to read its words. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A handler that wants the model to read its words
  says which outcome they carry: a refusal (`ToolRefusedError`, nothing ran)
  or a failure (`ToolFailedError`, the tool ran and could not do it), whose
  text passes as it is, the failure's also as the event's `error_detail`.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: an MCP tool whose result says isError, on every channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
  MCP tool whose result says `isError` ran and failed: it is a failure, never
  a refusal, on every channel.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a tool the channel serves itself (a skill script, a sandbox command), and work a tool hands off whose failure the model reads, when what it runs raises. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A tool the channel
  serves itself (a skill script, a sandbox command) reads the same when what
  it runs raises, and so does any work a tool hands off whose failure the
  model reads (a delegated task, a reasoning backend's tool).

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a call nothing served whose SYNC hooks raised. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call nothing
  served whose hooks raised reads as any call nothing served: the hooks'
  messages go to `error_detail`.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a result override on the firing of a call refused before execution, failed during execution or that reached no servant. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A result override supplied on such a firing MUST be ignored. Nothing ran, so
  there is no result to correct.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a call no handler and no hook served. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call that no handler and no hook served MUST report a failure, not a
  success. Reporting one — `{"status": "ok"}` and its kin — tells the model
  work was done that nobody did, and records a completed call for a tool that
  was never reached.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a declared tool no handler serves, and the SYNC hooks it reaches. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A declared tool that no handler serves reaches the SYNC
  hooks with no result: a hook MAY serve it by supplying one, and that result
  is then the call's.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a declared tool no handler serves and no SYNC hook serves. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
If none does, the call is reported once, as failed; the
  firing that offered it to the hooks was a chance to serve it, not a report.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a SYNC hook that empties a served call's result (an override of null), and the hooks after it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook that empties a served call's result (an override of null) leaves the
  call served, with a null result: the next hook in the chain reads a served
  call whose result is null, never a call nothing served, and does not get to
  serve it.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a SYNC hook's verdict on a call, on every channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every channel applies a verdict through the same reading (a
  block, an override, a bare override, an emptied result).

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a call whose hooks' context cannot be built, on every channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When the context the hooks need cannot be built, the hooks do not run and
  the call keeps the outcome its handler gave it, on every channel: a context
  that fails is not the tool's failure.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL: a call whose observers' context cannot be built: served, refused, failed, cancelled, or run by an external handler. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The ASYNC observers need that context
  and do not run either; the call is still reported once, by the `tool_call`
  framework event for a served call, and as the failure it is for a call
  nothing served. So for a refused, failed or cancelled call whose observers'
  context fails, and for a call an external handler ran: its `tool_call`
  framework event still reports it once.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, an abandoned call: a speech-to-speech model interrupted while a call is outstanding, and its provider (Section 12.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ON_TOOL_CALL, where the model abandoned the call:**

- A speech-to-speech model interrupted while a call is outstanding MAY discard
  it (the provider's own cancellation of the call; a reconnect that orphans every
  call the previous connection issued, blocking or not, since call ids are
  connection-scoped and the new socket never issued them). A provider that
  learns of it MUST tell the channel (`on_tool_call_cancelled`, Section 12.4).
  A provider whose protocol carries no such event fires nothing: its calls
  stay in the conversation and their results are still read.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, an abandoned call: a call the model abandoned whose handler still runs. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The channel MUST interrupt the handler still running for such a call and
  MUST NOT send its result. The model will not read it, and a result sent for
  an id the provider no longer knows is an error the application never asked
  for.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, an abandoned call: a call the model abandoned. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The call MUST fire ON_TOOL_CALL's observers with a discrete *cancelled*
  marker beside the failure marker. An abandoned call is neither a refusal nor
  a failure, and an audit counting refusals must not count it as one; it is
  still not a served call, so a consumer reading the failure marker alone
  reads it correctly as work that did not complete. The firing is
  observational, as above.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, an abandoned call: a cancellation that arrives once the call's result already left. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call the channel no longer holds when the cancellation arrives (its result
  already left) has no outcome left to report: the provider drops the stale
  result and the channel reports nothing.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, an abandoned call: a reconnect the call's own handler caused (it reconfigured its session). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A reconnect the call's own handler caused (it reconfigured its session and
  the provider reconnected to apply it) is not the model abandoning that
  call. The channel MUST NOT interrupt that handler, which still has work to
  do on the new connection (a handoff greets as the new agent next), and MUST
  NOT send its result, since the new socket never issued the id.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, an abandoned call: the call whose own handler caused the reconnect. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The call's
  outcome is reported as it would be otherwise, served when the handler
  returns a result, and never as cancelled.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, an abandoned call: a reconnect caused by a call's handler, a task it started, or work that does not descend from it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The reconnect is the call's own
  when it runs within the handler's execution, the handler itself or a task
  it started while the call was outstanding; a reconfiguration handed to work
  that does not descend from the handler is not, and abandons the call.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_TOOL_CALL, an abandoned call: the other calls orphaned by a reconnect one call's handler caused. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every
  other call the same reconnect orphaned is abandoned as above.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a human-input request, from its creation. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED, where the other party is a human:**

- A human-input request MUST be answerable from the moment it is created.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a human-input request whose notification is still running. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
  notification MUST NOT gate whether an answer can be recorded, and an answer
  arriving while the notification is still running MUST be honoured. The human
  is not inside the implementation's timing: they answer the question they were
  shown, and a notification that fans out slowly, or a hook that spends its
  whole timeout, is not a reason to lose their answer.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: its SYNC hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
These hooks keep every SYNC property that matters to their authors — priority
  order, and a BLOCK that rejects the request.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a SYNC hook's BLOCK on a request already answered. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
What a BLOCK does not do is
  retract an answer already recorded; a request that has been answered is
  settled.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a SYNC hook's MODIFY of a request. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A MODIFY hands the next hook and the ASYNC observers the request
  as it left it, and changes nothing else: the request stays the tool's, and
  `user_input_required` names it as the tool asked it.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: an answer recorded for a human-input request, and the caller that asked for it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Implementations MUST NOT report an answer that was recorded as a failure to
  the caller that asked for it.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a human-input request's outcome once delivered. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An outcome already delivered SHOULD stay
  readable for long enough that a second read, or a caller that lost track of
  the request, reads the outcome rather than an error.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a request object a human-input handler returns, once settled. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A request object returned by a human-input handler MUST keep exposing its
  recorded status, answer and rejection reason after settlement, including
  after it leaves the handler's active set.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: the outcome of a human-input tool call: rejected, unanswered in time, given up by the handler, or another error. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A human-input tool call follows the line between a refusal and a failure:
  a request a human or a BLOCK rejected is a refusal, the model reading why;
  one nobody answered in time is a failure, the tool having run without an
  answer; one the handler gave up on before an answer (its close, a release),
  whether before the call or while it waits, and any other error take the
  generic failure path, the message withheld from the model.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a request whose waiting call is cut, or still open when the turn that opened it ends (§10.6.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A request whose
  waiting call is cut (a turn cancelled, a session ended, a call abandoned),
  or still open when the turn that opened it ends (§10.6.5), is withdrawn as
  a release withdraws it: no answer is taken for it after.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: human-input tools on every channel that serves them and every door of it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Human-input tools have these rules on every channel that serves them (an
  AI channel, a speech-to-speech channel, a conference) and on every door of
  that channel (a speech-to-speech session's provider calls, the calls it
  recovers from speech, a reasoning backend's): the channel declares and
  serves them itself, before the host's handler, which replacing that
  handler leaves alone; their own timeout bounds the call (Section 21.6);
  each request fires ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED and names the channel type of
  the door it was asked on; the requests still open are settled when the
  channel closes, or when what asked them is taken out (a conference's
  speech-to-speech provider unplugged).

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: human-input tools under Tool Search, and a human-input definition given twice or under a name the channel serves itself (Section 21.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Tool Search never hides them, and a
  human-input definition given twice, or under a name the channel serves
  itself, is refused when the handler is given, as a host tool is (Section
  21.1).

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a human-input handler given as a plain tool handler. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A human-input handler given as a plain tool handler is a host
  handler, bound by none of these rules.

requirements.applies: §9.3 ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED: a realtime pipeline's agent (Section 19.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A realtime pipeline's agent never
  carries human-input tools of its own: the session serves the channel's
  (Section 19.5).

requirements.applies: §9.4: what a SYNC hook returns, which only its author keeps, the identity hooks of Section 11.2 aside; how the framework reads a result that is not a HookResult is RK-9.3-005's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Sync hooks MUST return a HookResult, the identity hooks of Section 11.2 aside:

requirements.applies: §9.4: the fields of a HookResult the framework reads, with what each carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
HookResult
├── action: "allow" | "block" | "modify"
├── event: any | null                       # The replacement payload; required on "modify"
├── reason: string | null                   # Why blocked or modified
├── injected_events: list<InjectedEvent>    # Events to inject, whatever the action;
│                                           # committed on BEFORE_BROADCAST (below)
├── tasks: list<Task>                       # Tasks to create (side effects)
├── observations: list<Observation>         # Observations to record (side effects)
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Additional hook metadata
```

requirements.applies: §9.4: the type of a MODIFY result's payload, trigger by trigger. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`event` carries the replacement payload for a "modify" result, and its type is
whatever the trigger passed in. Only BEFORE_BROADCAST and BEFORE_DELIVER
(Section 22.3) pass a RoomEvent: the
TTS trigger receives a string, the bridge triggers receive media frames, and the
tool and generation triggers receive their own event types.

requirements.applies: §9.4: a MODIFY payload, before the framework substitutes it, whose type may not be the one its trigger expects. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Typing this field as
a RoomEvent would make "modify" unusable for every trigger but one, so consumers
MUST check the type they expect before substituting it.

requirements.applies: §9.4: a MODIFY result whose event is null (§9.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A "modify" result MUST
carry its payload: one whose `event` is null is an unusable result (§9.3).

requirements.applies: §9.4: what a MODIFY on BEFORE_BROADCAST may change in the event; the implementation honours it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**A `BEFORE_BROADCAST` replacement.** A MODIFY on BEFORE_BROADCAST replaces
what the event says and whom it asks, never which event it is. The replacement
MAY change the event's `content`, its address (`addressed_to`), its
`visibility`, its thread (`parent_event_id`), its `correlation_id` and its
`metadata`, and its `channel_data`.

requirements.applies: §9.4: the fields and passed checks a MODIFY on BEFORE_BROADCAST cannot change. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Implementations MUST keep the original's
`id`, `room_id`, `type`, `source`, `index`, `chain_depth`, `responds_to`,
`idempotency_key`, `created_at`, `status`, `blocked_by` and
`delivery_results` on it, and with them the checks already passed: the event
an EDIT or a DELETE targets (`target_event_id`), its `edit_source` or
`delete_type` and its kind of content, which keeps a change from hiding in its
new content (checked at §10.1 step 8a, §10.3; an edit's replacement by another
kind of content is its new content), an INSTRUCTION's visibility, address and
`standalone` word (§10.1.1), and the fingerprint the pipeline wrote on a
response to an instruction (`metadata.instruction`, §10.1.1 step 6), or its
absence.

requirements.applies: §9.4: a MODIFY on BEFORE_BROADCAST that changed a field RK-9.4-012 keeps. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A field of these that the hook changed is put back from the original
before the next hook reads the event, and the hook's other changes stand.

requirements.applies: §9.4: the source's write check and the chain-depth limit, after the BEFORE_BROADCAST hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
source's write check (§10.1 step 11) and the chain-depth limit (§8.3) read
these fields after the hooks: no hook can commit an event under another
source, at another index or chain depth, or as the answer to another event.

requirements.applies: §9.4: an event's visibility a MODIFY on BEFORE_BROADCAST changed, and the internal mark (§7.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
visibility the hook changed is still narrowed at commit by the source
binding's visibility (§7.3), and the original's is put back whenever either
visibility is `internal`, which only the framework writes (§7.3): a hook can
neither give an event that mark nor change the visibility of a framework
record that has it.

requirements.applies: §9.4: an event's response_visibility a MODIFY on BEFORE_BROADCAST changed (§5.12); the implementation honours a narrowing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The replacement MAY narrow the event's
`response_visibility` (§5.12), never widen or clear it: the event keeps the
intersection of the original's and the hook's (§7.3), a null on either side
giving the other's, and `internal` from a hook reads as `none`, as it does
from a channel on its response (§8.5).

requirements.applies: §9.4: a response's visibility a MODIFY on BEFORE_BROADCAST changed (§8.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A response's visibility a hook changed
is narrowed to its cascade's scope again once its hooks are over (§8.5).

requirements.applies: §9.4: a router hook that addresses an event (Section 19.4), by its address or its routing metadata, which the rules of a BEFORE_BROADCAST replacement (RK-9.4-011 to 017) leave free. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
router hook that addresses an event (Section 19.4), by its address or its
routing metadata, is unaffected.

requirements.applies: §9.4 HookResult; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
**InjectedEvent:**

```
InjectedEvent
├── event: RoomEvent                        # The event to inject
└── target_channel_ids: list<string> | null # Deliver to specific channels (null = store only)
```

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: the events a BEFORE_BROADCAST chain's results carry, however the event ends; the refusals of RK-9.4-020 aside. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Injected events.** The events every result of an event's `BEFORE_BROADCAST`
chain carries are collected, whatever its action (allow, modify or block),
off the lock and under it (§9.5.1), and MUST be committed whichever way the
event ends: blocked by a hook, blocked by its source's permissions, or delivered
(§10.1 steps 10 to 12). A hook that lets an event through can still notify
someone.

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: an event refused with nothing stored once its hooks have run. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event refused with nothing stored once its hooks have run (its
room closed under them, §10.1 step 9a; a gate before step 9, §9.5.1; an
expired `process_timeout`, §13.6) drops them with it.

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: when an injected event commits, against its cause; one code under the lock injects directly is RK-9.4-024's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An injected event is committed as a pass of the cascade (§8.3), after the
event whose hooks injected it:

- It commits after its cause, in a pass and a locked section of its own,
  once the cause's section has released the room lock: another event may
  commit between the cause and it.

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: the lock and the hooks an injected event's pass takes and runs. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It takes the room lock for its own
  commit and runs the `BEFORE_BROADCAST` chain, every hook under the lock
  (§9.5.1).

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: an injected event its own hooks block, and the events they inject. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook may block it, which stores it `BLOCKED`, and the events
  its own hooks inject are committed the same way.

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: an event code under the lock injects directly (§10.5), against a hook-injected one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event that code under
  the lock injects directly (§10.5) is another path: it commits ahead of the
  cause, within the cause's section (§9.5.1, Reentrance).

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: the reentry budget an injected event draws on (§8.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- It counts against the cascade's reentry budget, which bounds injections of
  injections (§8.3).

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: an injected event's chain depth and source. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- It keeps the `chain_depth` of the event whose hooks injected it, and the
  source the hook gave it.

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: an injected event's visibility, set from its targets. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its visibility names those of its targets the
  room binds, whatever visibility it came with, and is `none` when it names
  none or is stored only: a target the room does not bind would otherwise
  read the event once attached.

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: what narrows an injected event's visibility (§7.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
No source binding narrows it, and the hooks
  of its own chain may narrow it, never widen it: the visibility a modify
  gives it is intersected with the one it had (§7.3).

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: an injected event's idempotency key (§13.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The pipeline clears
  its idempotency key (§13.4).

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: the source check of an injected event (§7.5 rule 2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: - It takes no source check (§7.5 rule 2): it is the hook's, not a channel's.

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: an injected EDIT or DELETE at §10.1 step 8a (§10.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An EDIT or a DELETE it carries is the hook's change whatever source it
  names, and takes step 8a with the system's authority only (§10.3).

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: whom an injected event is delivered to (§10.2 step 3, §7.5 rule 5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- It is delivered to its transport targets only, under the rules of any
  delivery (§10.2 step 3), and never to its own source (§7.5 rule 5).

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: the AFTER_BROADCAST hooks of an injected event's delivery set. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its
  delivery set fires `AFTER_BROADCAST` like any other (§10.1 step 16).

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: an intelligence channel among an injected event's targets. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An injected event asks no agent. An intelligence channel among its targets
is not called: the event's visibility names it, and the agent reads the
event in its history at its next turn.

requirements.applies: §9.4 Injected events: a transport hosting a model among an injected event's targets (§12.4); an integrator who wants an answer injects directly (§10.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A transport hosting a model (a
realtime voice channel, a conference with a realtime model plugged in,
§12.4) is an agent too: it takes the event into the model's context
silently, and asks no answer. An integrator who wants an agent to answer
injects the event directly (§10.5).

requirements.applies: §9.4: an INSTRUCTION among a hook result's injected events (§10.1.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**No injected instruction.** A hook MUST NOT inject an INSTRUCTION
(§10.1.1). One among a result's injected events is dropped with a warning
before any pass: no hook runs on it, and nothing of it is stored or
delivered.

requirements.applies: §9.4: the rest of a hook result whose injected INSTRUCTION is dropped; a hook that wants an agent directed injects directly (§10.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The rest of the result stands, its other injected events, tasks
and observations included. A hook that wants an agent directed injects the
instruction directly (§10.5), which takes it through §10.1.1.

requirements.applies: §9.4: the results whose injected events are committed, BEFORE_BROADCAST's and an identity challenge's (§11.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Which triggers commit injected events.** The injected events of
`BEFORE_BROADCAST` results are committed as above, and so is the event an
identity challenge injects (`inject`, §11.3), which takes the same pass in a
cascade of its own.

requirements.applies: §9.4: the injected events of a result on any SYNC trigger but BEFORE_BROADCAST. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
On every other SYNC trigger (`BEFORE_DELIVER`,
`ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` and the rest) a result's injected events are not
committed: they are dropped with a warning logged, never silently.

requirements.applies: §9.5 Hook Pipeline (BEFORE_BROADCAST); the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
```
Inbound Event
      │
      ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Sync Hooks (ordered by priority)     │
│                                      │
│ [0] Hook A → allow / block / modify  │
│ [1] Hook B → allow / block / modify  │
│ [2] Hook C → allow / block / modify  │
└──────────────┬───────────────────────┘
               │
          blocked? ──yes──→ Store event (status=BLOCKED, blocked_by=hook_name)
               │              Persist tasks and observations
               │              Then commit every result's InjectedEvents (§9.4)
               │
               ▼ (allowed, possibly modified)
         Event Router
         Broadcasts to channels
         Then commits every result's InjectedEvents (§9.4)
               │
               ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Async Hooks (fire and forget)        │
│                                      │
│ [·] Audit Logger                     │
│ [·] Analytics                        │
│ [·] Webhook Notifier                 │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

requirements.applies: §9.5.1: a SYNC BEFORE_BROADCAST hook registered with needs_lock = false, on the inbound pipeline (§10.1 step 5a) and on direct injection (§10.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A check that only reads the event — a PII scan, a moderation call — does not
need the room lock, and running its I/O under the lock makes every other event
of the room wait behind it (§13.5). A SYNC `BEFORE_BROADCAST` hook registered
with `needs_lock = false` runs **before** the room lock is taken, on the
inbound pipeline (§10.1 step 5a) and on direct injection (§10.5):

```
5a. OFF-LOCK CHECK (only when an off-lock hook fires for the event)
    ├── Take the room's admission ticket (arrival order, per process)
    ├── Run the off-lock hooks in priority order, on the pre-lock context
    │   # Each bounded by its own timeout; checks of different events of
    │   # the same room overlap. A block stops them; a hook that produced
    │   # no usable result is reported now (hook_timeout, hook_error)
    ├── Wait for every earlier ticket of the room to be released
    ├── Acquire the room lock (step 6) and continue; step 9 reuses the
    │   off-lock outcome and runs only the hooks that need the lock
    └── Release the ticket once the locked section has decided and
        committed, after the room lock's release (step 13)
```

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Order: events that took a ticket, within one process. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Order.** Events that took a ticket commit in ticket order, so two events
  from one sender keep their arrival order even when the second one's check
  finishes first. The ticket is held in process memory: the guarantee holds
  within one process.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Order: the events that take a ticket. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event takes a ticket only when an off-lock hook
  fires for it, the hook's filters applied: events that match no off-lock
  hook take no ticket and are not ordered against ticketed ones — a system
  notice does not wait for a scan it has nothing to do with.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Order: an event the off-lock hooks blocked. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event the
  off-lock hooks blocked still waits for its turn, so a blocked record keeps
  the ticket order too.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Release: an event's ticket, on every path. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Release.** A ticket MUST be released on every path: committed, blocked by
  a hook or a gate, refused, timed out, failed, or cancelled.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Release: when a ticket is released. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It is released
  after the room lock, once the locked section is over. A ticket left held
  stalls every later ticketed event of the room.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Bound: an event's wait for its ticket's turn, against process_timeout (§13.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Bound.** Waiting for a turn adds nothing to `process_timeout` (§13.6): it
  counts against the same pre-commit budget.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Bound: what bounds an event's wait for its turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The wait is bounded by the
  earlier holders' hook timeouts and locked sections, never by a separate
  setting.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Decision: the off-lock hooks within the event's one chain. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Decision.** The off-lock hooks are the first hooks of the event's one
  chain (§9.1): a block among them stops the chain, and a modify hands its
  payload on.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Decision: where the off-lock hooks' BLOCK or MODIFY applies, after the gates before step 9. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Their BLOCK or MODIFY is applied at step 9, after the status,
  idempotency and EDIT/DELETE gates, which keep their order and still decide
  first; a block there runs none of the hooks that need the lock.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Decision: the side effects of the off-lock and the locked hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The side
  effects (injected events, tasks, observations) of both phases are collected
  together, in hook order.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Decision: an event a gate refuses before step 9, and its off-lock outcome. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event a gate refuses before step 9 drops the
  off-lock outcome, its side effects included, as it runs no locked hook.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Errors: an off-lock hook that produces no usable result (§9.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Errors.** An off-lock hook that produces no usable result (§9.3) is
  reported when it is met, before the lock: `hook_timeout` when it timed
  out, and `hook_error`, whatever the gates decide next.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Context: the context an off-lock hook receives. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Context.** An off-lock hook receives the context built before the lock
  (§10.1 step 3), the room as step 2 left it: what an attach or the record
  of a routed sender wrote there included.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Context: an integrator's hook that reads the room's state rather than the event, which only its author keeps. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its history can be stale by the
  time the event commits; a hook that reads the room's state rather than the
  event MUST keep `needs_lock = true`.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a call into the room by a caller that already stands in the room's admission order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **Reentrance.** A call into the room (an event injected, §10.5, or a
  message that names the room, §10.1) made by a caller that already stands in
  the room's admission order takes no ticket in that room.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: the callers that stand in a room's admission order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The caller stands
  in it while it holds the room lock (a locked hook, code under the lock),
  and in the work an event's admission runs before the lock: an off-lock
  hook's body, a handler the check's report of a `hook_error` or a
  `hook_timeout` awaits (§8.2), and the message's parse (a channel's
  `handle_inbound()`, §10.1 step 4).

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: how long work stands in the admission order, and a task it spawned that outlives it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It stands there only while that work
  runs: a task the work spawned that outlives it stands in no order.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a locked hook's body and the tasks it spawns, in the admission order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
So does
  a locked hook, only while its body runs, though its section holds the lock
  longer: a task the body spawned acts for it while the body runs, awaited or
  not, and once the body has returned its calls are new arrivals, which wait
  for the lock.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a call made by work that stands in the room's admission order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call that work makes
  is adopted by that work: it would otherwise wait for the ticket its own
  caller holds or, made from a parse, open a cascade of its own for every
  message.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: an adopted call's hooks and its commit, against the event whose processing made it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It runs every hook under the lock and commits ahead of the event
  whose processing made it.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: an adopted call in the ticket order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An adopted call has no place in the ticket order
  (Order, above): it is ordered only ahead of the event that adopted it.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: the reentry budget an adopted call draws on, and the events its own hooks inject (§8.3, §9.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Made
  under the lock, it MUST draw on the reentry budget of the cascade whose
  section holds the lock (§8.3), and the events its own hooks inject join
  that section's queue, committed once the section has released the lock
  (§9.4); made in the admission order, it MUST draw on the budget of the
  cascade of the event that work is for, so that a hook or a parse that sends
  into the room on every event stops at the cap.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a call made by code under a room lock the host holds outside any pass (§13.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Code under a room lock the
  host holds outside any pass (a host serialising its own changes, §13.5)
  belongs to no cascade: its call draws on a budget of its own, and the
  events its hooks inject commit once the host has released the lock, after
  the call returns.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: when an adopted call answers, and what. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An adopted call answers at its commit, with its
  completion detached (§10.1 step 18) and no delivery results.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: when a call adopted by an event's admission work answers, against the events its hooks inject. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Made in an
  event's admission work, it answers only once the events its own hooks
  injected, and those their hooks injected, are committed too, each in a
  section of its own (§9.4), with those the hooks of a call nested in any
  of these sections, its own included, injected, which join that
  section's queue: committed, not delivered, their passes waiting for no
  delivery set in the lane.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: an adopted message held for its sender (§10.1 step 5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A message held for its sender (§10.1 step 5)
  answers once its challenge, a cascade of its own with what the
  challenge's section queued, is committed and delivered.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: the first failed release of an adopted call's sections, and which result reports it (§13.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An adopted
  message's result then carries
  the first failed release of their sections as its error when it met none
  before (§13.5), and the event that adopted it does not; an adopted
  injection (§10.5) returns its event, and that failure is the error of the
  event that adopted it.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: the delivery of a call adopted under the lock. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Made under
  the lock, its delivery waits in the lane behind the work that made it, and
  a wait on it there returns unwaited (§10.1 step 18).

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: the delivery of a call adopted by an event's admission work. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Made in an event's
  admission work, its delivery does not wait for that work: it runs at its
  turn in the lane, ahead of the event's, so a wait on it from that work
  returns with its delivery results, its answers and its turns' ends, and
  the event commits and is delivered after it.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: when the caller of an event whose work made an adopted call is answered. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The event's caller is
  answered once the event's own work is over, blocked or delivered, and
  does not wait for an adopted call that work did not wait for: that
  call's answers, and the reading of their streams, are its own.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a wait on the handle of an event that deferred its delivery (§10.1 step 18) and whose work made an adopted call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A wait
  on the handle of an event that deferred its delivery (§10.1 step 18)
  is answered the same way, without waiting for that call, and reads the
  event's own end even once the kit's close has cut that call.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a wait whose delivery calls into the room and needs the ticket the event holds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A wait whose delivery calls
  into the room and needs the ticket that event holds ends at the event's
  `process_timeout` (§13.6): the event is refused with nothing of it
  stored, and the wait ends with the work.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: the delivery's call in such a wait. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The delivery's call, bound by its
  own `process_timeout`, which started later, commits only if it takes the
  released ticket before that expires; otherwise it is refused too.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: an adopted call that committed, when the event's process_timeout passes (§13.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
  adopted call that committed is not the event's work: when the event's
  `process_timeout` passes, in its off-lock check or under the room's lock,
  while that call's answer is still to come or still being read (a
  streaming target that reads on), the call runs on to its end, its answers
  stored and its handle reading them, and the event is refused on time,
  without waiting for it; the event's delivery key then names no delivery,
  and the handle of an event that deferred its delivery waits for nothing.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: an adopted call's own process_timeout (§13.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An adopted call has a `process_timeout` of its own, from its start, as any
  call has (§13.6): not committed when it passes, it is refused
  `process_timeout` and reports it, naming its channel before the room lock
  and its event under it.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: an adopted call its hook's body or its parse waits for, not committed when that code ends. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It also follows the code that waits for its
  answer. A call its hook's body or its parse makes and waits for
  (awaited, deferred until its decision, or nested under the lock), not
  committed yet when that code ends, ends with it, nothing of it stored, and
  nothing reports it but what ended that code: the event's
  `process_timeout`, the hook's own timeout (§9.3), or the event's caller
  gone (§13.6).

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a call made by a task the event's work started and does not wait for. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call made beside the event's work by a task that work
  started and does not wait for (an off-lock hook's, a parse's) outlives
  the work: its own `process_timeout` bounds it, and it ends only with the
  task that waits for it, the event refused at its own deadline meanwhile
  without waiting for it, even while it holds the room's lock.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a call a locked hook's task makes, while the body runs or once it has returned. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call a
  locked hook's task makes while the hook's body runs is nested under the
  hook's section, as any call made under the lock, and holds that section:
  the hook's result is used once the call is decided, however the body
  ended, its own timeout included, so that the call commits ahead of the
  event; a call the task makes once the body has returned is a new
  arrival, as above.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a call nested under a locked hook's section, against the event's process_timeout. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It is bounded by the event's `process_timeout`, as
  the section is: not committed when that passes, it is refused
  `process_timeout` with the event, nothing of either stored and nothing
  reported of it, the hook's own timeout, if it timed out, reported ahead
  of the event's `process_timeout`.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a call nested under a section with no deadline of its own (an injected event's pass). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A section with no deadline of its own
  (an injected event's pass) waits for it up to the call's own
  `process_timeout`, past which the call is refused and reports it.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 Reentrance: a call nested under a locked hook's section once the event's caller is gone (§13.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
  event's caller gone, it goes on, the lock held for it until it is over
  or the event's deadline passes, where, not committed, it is refused
  `process_timeout`, nothing of it stored and nothing reported of it, nor
  the event's `process_timeout`; whether the caller returns at once or
  once the call is over is left to the implementation.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: a call into the room from its deliveries, its turns and the bodies of its ASYNC hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **The room's work outside the lock.** A call into the room from its work
  outside the lock and outside its admission order (a delivery set's
  deliveries and turns: a transport's `deliver()`, an agent's turn, a tool
  handler, a `TurnHost` verb; and the body of an ASYNC hook a cascade fires
  once an event's delivery set has run: §10.1 step 16's `AFTER_BROADCAST`
  hooks, a change's `ON_EVENT_UPDATED` and `ON_EVENT_DELETED` hooks, §10.3;
  and the body of an ASYNC hook observing a SYNC trigger the room's work
  fires once per event, §9.2, an observer of a trigger fired outside any
  cascade having a budget of its own, §8.3) is a new arrival: it takes a
  ticket when an off-lock hook fires for its event, and `process_timeout`
  bounds it (§13.6).

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: the reentry budget a call into its own room draws on while that work runs (§8.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
While that delivery, turn or hook body runs, a call into
  its own room MUST draw on the reentry budget of the cascade that delivers,
  the one whose delivery set runs it or that
  fired the hook, and so does the cascade the call starts, so that a
  transport whose delivery sends into its room, or a hook that posts after
  every event, stops at the cap.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: what a delivery's, a turn's or a hook body's call draws, and the depth of a hook body's (§8.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A delivery's or a turn's call draws one of
  the cascade's passes; a hook body's call draws one of its hook calls, a
  counter kept apart (§8.3) that all the cascade's hooks share, only while
  that body runs, and is at least one deeper than the event the hook runs
  for (§8.3): a hook that posts once per event draws one hook call per event,
  and a task the body starts and does not wait for draws nothing of it once
  the body has returned.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: a call from that work that creates a room (§10.1 step 2, §10.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
So MUST a call it makes that
  creates a room, whether a routed message opens it or the call names a room
  the store does not hold, which step 2 creates with the id (§10.1 step 2,
  §10.4): the room is that cascade's own work, and the call is charged once,
  before the room is created.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: a call from that work into another room that exists. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only a call into another room that exists
  already has a budget of its own.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: a routed message from that work, once step 2 knows its room (§10.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A routed message is charged once its final
  room is known, after step 2 has routed it once more where the first room
  was no longer the message's (§10.4): one that lands in the room the work
  delivers in draws on that work's budget, wherever the router first placed
  it, and one that lands in another room that exists has a budget of its own.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: a call whose room another call creates first. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When step 2 reads a call's room absent and another call creates it first,
  the call stays charged and goes on into that room as into one that
  exists; its cascade has a budget of its own.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: a message already charged that routing places once more. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A message already charged is
  not charged again, wherever routing places it once more.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: the depth of a call made while a turn, a tool call outside a turn, or a hook on a model's words, delegation or speech runs (§8.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call into any
  room made while a turn runs is at least as deep as the response of the
  deepest turn it runs within, one made while a tool call outside a turn
  runs (a realtime or a conference tool call, §12.4) at least as deep as the
  answer that issued it, and one made from a hook on a model's words or
  delegation, or on what a voice agent says, at least as deep as the answer
  it hears, delegated or speaks (§8.3).

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: work a turn, a tool call or a hook's body began, once it is over. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Once the turn, the tool call or the hook's
  body is over, work it began (a task it spawned) calls into a room as a new
  arrival at the depth of its own event, 0 for a message it creates, or the
  depth the call names (a `chain_depth` it passes to continue a chain,
  §10.5); it draws on the budget of the room's delivery it was started
  within while that delivery runs, as any of the delivery's work does, and
  on a budget of its own once the delivery is over.

requirements.applies: §9.5.1 The room's work outside the lock: the depth floor of an ASYNC hook's body and of the handler of a framework event a turn emits (§8.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The body of a hook run
  asynchronously keeps the floor its trigger fired under for as long as it
  runs, and a handler of a framework event a turn emits keeps the turn's
  (§8.3); once it has returned, what it began calls at the depth of its
