Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.

§10.6.2 On the executor, what the executor gives a channel it builds, as the kit gives a channel it registers: the host's media resolver and attached-media reader (§6.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- the host's media resolver and attached-media reader (§6.4), which the host
  gives the executor as it gives the kit;

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 On the executor, what the executor gives a channel it builds, as the kit gives a channel it registers: what its turn reads of the room, and the room's context for its hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- what its turn reads of the room, which comes with the turn (§10.6.5), and
  the room's context for its hooks, which the owner gives (§10.6.6).

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: a channel keeping state per room between two turns on its executor. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Per-room state.** A channel MAY keep state per room between two turns on its
executor.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: the per-room state an AI channel and an ACP agent channel keep. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An AI channel keeps a room's thought and its speak policy's
listening state (§6.4), its plan, the results it evicted and reads back, the
skills it activated, the approvals to run a served skill's code given there
(§24.7), and the tools Tool Search revealed or it used;
an ACP agent channel keeps the room's session.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: whose a channel's per-room state is, and a cache rebuilt when absent; the state the host sets for the room is the room's (RK-10.6.2-039). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
That state is the executor's,
not the room's, and is one of two kinds, which an implementation documents per
state:

- a **cache**, rebuilt from the timeline and the store when absent (the tools
  it used, reseeded from its rows, §6.4);

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: session state, which starts empty when absent, and the session state the room needs (an ACP session, a speak policy's listening state). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **session state**, which starts empty when absent, as after a restart (a
  plan, a thought). Some of it the room needs: an ACP session, whose agent
  holds the conversation, and a speak policy's listening state, a request to
  stay quiet that is a state of the room (§6.4).

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: one build of a channel and the rooms it serves, two turns at once included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One build of a channel serves every room the channel is attached to, two
turns at once included.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: what a turn reads, and what a build keeps per room, across the rooms of one build; a host verb naming another room or organization. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
What a turn reads comes with its request, its own
room's (§10.6.5), and what the channel keeps it keeps per room: nothing the
build keeps for one room reaches another room's turn. A host verb naming
another room or organization is refused (§10.6.5).

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: what the host adds to a build (a memory provider, a tool handler, a skill's executor), and what it sets on the channel itself. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
What the host adds to a
build (a memory provider, a tool handler, a skill's executor) keys what it
keeps by the turn's room in the same way, and what the host sets on the
channel itself (its system prompt, its tool handler) is the channel's in all
its rooms.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: each request's previous_turn: the room's previous turn of the channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each request names the room's previous turn of the channel (`previous_turn`,
§10.6.3): the one the owner sent last, ended or not.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: when the owner records a turn as the room's previous one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner records it as
it sends it, so a turn sent while the previous one runs names it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: which turns a backend marks handed, and so names as previous: one that failed before, one handed, a refusal that applied nothing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A backend
marks a request handed as it gives it to an executor, before any wait on
the executor's answer: a turn that failed before (no executor declares it,
the backend closed, it cannot be serialized, its placement failed) is never
named, while one handed stays named whatever followed (a cancel, a timeout),
since its executor may have begun it; a refusal that applied nothing (a
closing process's) takes the mark back.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: a channel call (§10.6.3) and the previous turn it names and leaves. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel call (§10.6.3) leaves the
room's state as a turn does: it names the previous turn or call too, and the next
turn names it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: an executor holding state for the channel and room that the previous turn or call did not leave, before it runs the turn or the call's verb. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor that holds state for the channel and room not left
by that turn or call MUST discard it before running the turn or the call's
verb: the turns of a room may have run elsewhere since, and a state they made
obsolete (a speak policy told to talk again, a plan revised) MUST NOT come
back.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: how an executor discards a room's state: every state, a cache rebuilt afterwards. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It discards it as the channel lets go of a room it is detached from
(§6.4), every state it keeps for the room included, a cache rebuilt
afterwards.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 Per-room state: an executor that stops keeping its record of which turn left a room's state, and a discard that failed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor that can no longer vouch for the state it holds
treats it as not left by the previous turn: when it stops keeping its record
of which turn left a room's state (a bounded record), it discards that state,
and a discard that failed is attempted again at the room's next turn.
Placement (§10.6.7) keeps a room's turns where its state is.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 State the host sets for the room: per-room state the host sets through a channel call (an ACP session's configuration values), and a channel's result that reports it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**State the host sets for the room.** Some per-room state is set by the host
through a channel call and is needed again on another executor (an ACP
session's configuration values, §6.4). That state is the room's, not the
executor's. A channel's result reports it when the verb changed it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 State the host sets for the room: where the owner stores it, and any other write of that key (a room's creation or metadata update, a TurnHost verb). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner
MUST store it in the room's metadata (§5.1), under a key of the
implementation's own namespace (`roomkit:`), and MUST drop that key, with a
warning, from any other write (a room's creation or metadata update, a
`TurnHost` verb, §5.1).

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 State the host sets for the room: each request and each channel call, before the turn or the verb runs. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It
hands it to the executor with each request, in the room its `RoomContext`
carries, and with each channel call, before the turn or the verb runs.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 State the host sets for the room: a channel holding none for the room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
channel takes it back when it holds none for the room.

requirements.applies: §10.6.2 State the host sets for the room: a detach of the channel from the room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: A detach forgets it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Messages: the five families of messages a backend carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Five families, each message a record in the serialized form of Section 1.4.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Messages: the TurnRequest record and its OwnerTool entries, owner to executor. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The request**, owner → executor:

```
TurnRequest
├── turn_id: string
├── room_id: string
├── channel_id: string
├── event: RoomEvent                    # transcoded, max length applied (§10.2
│                                       # step 3a-b)
├── binding: ChannelBinding             # as the runner gives it (§10.6.1)
├── context: RoomContext
├── strategy_turn: bool                 # a generation a turn runner asks
│                                       # (§10.6.1): the channel answers, past
│                                       # its speak policy and its thinker (§6.4)
├── notes: list<string>                 # the runtime's own blocks for the turn
│                                       # (a discussion's turn notes, §19.7.5
│                                       # rule 14); never read from event metadata
├── in_place: bool                      # a discussion's turn: the event keeps
│                                       # its place in the history (rule 9)
├── owner_tools: list<OwnerTool>        # the tools the owner serves (§10.6.5)
├── room_hooks: list<string>            # the names of the room's hooks on
│                                       # executor triggers (§10.6.6)
├── previous_turn: {turn_id, executor_id} | null
│                                       # the room's previous turn or channel
│                                       # call of the channel (§10.6.2)
├── channel_rows: list<RoomEvent>       # the channel's own rows its turn reads,
│                                       # oldest first (§10.6.5)
└── trace: map<string, string> | null   # trace context of the broadcast span

OwnerTool
├── tool: AITool                        # its declaration (§6.7)
├── waits_by_design: bool               # bounded by its own bound, not the
│                                       # channel's default (§21.6)
└── ends_turn: bool                     # its served call ends the turn, a
                                        # delegation's result tool (§23.3)
```

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Messages: the frames an executor sends the owner on a turn's link, and what each carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Frames**, executor → owner, each carrying the turn id:

| Frame | Carries |
|---|---|
| `accepted` | The executor's id: it took the turn |
| `heartbeat` | Nothing: the turn is still running |
| `output` | `on_event()` returned: the `ChannelOutput` without its stream (`responded`, `response_events`, `response_metadata`, `tasks`, `observations`, `metadata_updates`, its error as an error record), and whether a stream follows |
| `item` | One item of the stream, within what the `pull` messages granted: a text delta (or the text deltas the channel yielded together, joined, with their number), a reasoning delta, a call's start (its id, name, arguments, and its intent when it has one), a call's end (its id, the sequence number of its start's frame, name, arguments, result, status, outcome, duration, error, structured content, `refused_but_ran`, and its intent when it has one), a segment break, what a generation used (usage, model, provider), the loop's end (reason, rounds, usage, the limits it ran under, the last generation's usage, whether every generation reported its counters, model, provider), or the stream's end |
| `tool_args` | The arguments a call runs with once its gate fixed them (a `BEFORE_TOOL_USE` rewrite, §9.3), naming the call's start frame |
| `tool_ended` | A call's end known before the `item` carrying it was read (§10.6.4): the start's frame and the end |
| `record` | The turn's response-metadata record as it stands (§6.7), sent before the `item` it was read with whenever it changed (§10.6.4) |
| `ephemeral` | An ephemeral event of the turn (thinking, tool-call composition, custom), which the owner publishes on its realtime backend |
| `framework_event` | A framework event the turn emitted (§8.2), with its payload, which the owner emits on its own bus |
| `input_request` | A tool asked a human for input: the request's id, tool and prompt, with its room, channel, tool call and the actor of its turn (§10.6.5) |
| `input_closed` | A request settled on the executor other than by an `input_answer`: its id and its outcome (answered, rejected, timed out), from the host's handler, a hook's block, its bound or a release (§9.3) |
| `input_taken` | Whether an `input_answer` settled its request: false when the request was settled first (§10.6.5) |
| `steer_result` | The number of loops a `steer` reached, or none when the channel cannot steer the turn (§10.6.8) |
| `error` | `on_event()` or the stream raised: an error record (§10.6.8) |
| `end` | The turn ended; nothing follows |

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Messages: the control messages the owner sends on a turn's link, and what each carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Control**, owner → executor, on a turn's link:

| Message | Carries |
|---|---|
| `pull` | Grant the reading of the stream's next items: their number, and how many items the owner's reader read, a joined `item` counting its deltas (§10.6.4) |
| `close` | The reader closed the stream (§10.6.4) |
| `cancel` | The reason the owner cancels the turn (§10.6.8) |
| `steer` | A steering directive (§21.3), answered by `steer_result` with the number of loops it reached |
| `input_answer` | The outcome recorded for an `input_request`: answered with its value, or rejected with its reason |
| `heartbeat` | Nothing: the owner still reads the turn (§10.6.8) |

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Messages: every message of a turn's link, both ways: its sequence number, delivered exactly once and in order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Delivery.** Every message of a turn's link, in both directions (frames,
control, calls and their results), carries a sequence number and MUST reach
the other side exactly once and in order.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Messages: a duplicate or a gap in a link's sequence, and a message of a turn that ended or failed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A side MUST drop a duplicate and
fail the turn with `frame_lost` on a gap in the sequence; the owner MUST drop
a message of a turn that ended or failed.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Messages: the calls an executor makes on the owner during a turn, each answered once by its result. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Calls**, executor → owner, each answered once by its result:

| Call | Result | Serves |
|---|---|---|
| `tool_call` | `tool_result` | A call to a tool the owner serves (§10.6.5) |
| `call_cancel` | none | The executor withdraws a `tool_call` or a `host_call` whose turn it cut or whose bound expired (§21.6): the owner cancels its handler |
| `host_call` | `host_result` | A verb of `TurnHost`, or a reader of owner-process state (§10.6.5) |

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: the channel control messages, owner to executor outside any turn, and what each carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Channel control**, owner → executor, outside any turn, about a channel's
per-room state, or its build:

| Message | Carries |
|---|---|
| `room_attached` | The channel was attached to the room: the room's binding of it (§5.7) |
| `room_detached` | The channel was detached from the room: its state for the room is dropped (§6.4) |
| `committed_event` | An event committed in the room that the channel's memory is handed (a discussion's, §19.7.5 rule 3), answered by nothing |
| `channel_released` | The channel's build is stale (its host changed what it is built from): an executor holding a build lets it go, answered by nothing |
| `channel_call` | A per-room verb of the channel, answered by `channel_result` (an ACP session's `set_config_option` or `close_session`, §6.4); an implementation documents each channel's set. It carries its `call_id`, its channel and room, the verb and its arguments, what the room keeps for the channel as the owner stores it (§10.6.2), and `previous_turn`; a later request's `previous_turn` names the call by its `call_id`. Cutting a running turn is never a channel call: it is the turn's `cancel` or `steer` |

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: the room's organization on room_attached, room_detached, committed_event and channel_call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`room_attached`, `room_detached`, `committed_event` and `channel_call` carry
the room's organization (§17.2), null for a room without one; a turn's
request carries it in its context's room.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: which executors room_attached and room_detached reach. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`room_attached` and
`room_detached` reach every executor that may run the channel's turns: the
owner's own executor alone for a channel the owner holds live (§10.6.7);
every executor that declares the channel and serves the room's organization
otherwise.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: how an executor applies room_attached and room_detached, with a build of the channel or none; a backend that cannot carry room_attached is RK-10.6.3-015's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
They
need no result: an executor holding a build of the channel applies them as
the channel's own attach and detach would for a channel the kit holds, and
logs what the channel raises; one holding no build has nothing to apply and
builds none for them, so a channel is built at its first turn, channel call
or committed event on an executor (§10.6.2).

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: an INTELLIGENCE binding whose channel raises on room_attached, a detach whose channel raises, and a backend that cannot carry room_attached. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A binding of category
`INTELLIGENCE` (§5.7) is therefore kept when its channel raises on
`room_attached`, and a detach does not report what
the channel raised; only a backend that cannot carry `room_attached` fails
the attachment, which is then undone.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: the room's previous turn of the channel, and what the room kept for it, after room_detached, sent or not. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
After `room_detached`, the owner names
no previous turn for the channel in the room (`previous_turn` is null), so an
executor that missed the message still discards the room's state at its next
turn (§10.6.2), and the owner forgets what the room kept for the channel,
even when the message could not be sent.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: which executors channel_released reaches. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`channel_released`, the channel's in all its rooms, reaches every executor
that declares the channel, whatever organizations it serves, or the owner's
own alone for a channel the owner holds live.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: an executor that built the channel, on channel_released: the build let go, its running turns, its close and the provider its factory handed it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One that built the channel
lets the build go: the next turn, channel call or committed event of the
channel builds it anew, and the build let go is closed once the turns running
on it, or still getting it, end, which it never cuts for this; its close
leaves open the provider the factory handed it (Section 6.4), which the
factory may hand every build.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: an executor holding no build of the channel, on channel_released. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One that holds
no build builds none for the message.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: channel_released for a channel the owner holds live. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
For a channel the owner holds live it
changes nothing: that channel is the owner's registry's, and its host
replaces it there.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: the kit's release_channel(channel_id). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A host sends it through the kit's
`release_channel(channel_id)`, which fails when the kit holds no channel of
that id.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: which executor a committed_event reaches; one a closed executor refuses is placed again (RK-10.6.3-033). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A `committed_event` reaches one executor: the owner's own for a channel the
owner holds live (§10.6.7), else the one that holds the room's state for the
channel, else one that would take the room's turns (the room's hooks and
organization it carries included, §10.6.6, §10.6.7).

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: the room's state holder and previous turn, after a committed_event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It never makes that executor
the holder: it leaves the room's state as it is and names no
previous turn.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: an executor given a committed_event: the channel's memory, what it raises, and the order against the owner's later requests. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The executor hands the event to the channel (an AI channel's
memory, §20), logs what the channel raises, and applies it before any later
request of the owner for that channel and room.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: a committed_event no executor takes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One no executor takes is
dropped and logged by the owner.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: a channel_call: the channel attached to the room, in the room's organization. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A `channel_call` is made for a channel attached to the room, in the room's
organization (§17.2).

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: which executor a channel_call reaches; one a closed executor refuses is placed again (RK-10.6.3-033). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It reaches one executor: the owner's own for a channel
the owner holds live (§10.6.7), else the one that holds the room's state for
the channel, else one that declares the channel and serves the room's
organization.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: what a channel_result carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its
`channel_result` is that executor's: the verb's result as data or its error
record, what the room keeps for the channel when the verb changed it, and
the executor's id.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: how a backend answers a channel_call. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A backend answers a call on the call's own exchange, so
the result names no call.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: a channel_call no executor takes, and the previous turn the owner names after it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A `channel_call` no executor takes fails with
`no_executor`, at once from a backend that knows every executor (§10.6.7),
else within `accept_timeout`; the owner then names the previous turn it
named before the call.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: the kit's channel_call, and a verb the channel does not have. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A host makes one through the kit's `channel_call`,
naming the channel, the room, the verb and the verb's arguments; a verb the
channel does not have fails with the channel's own error.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: an executor's close and the kit's close: the channels each closes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor closes the channels it built when it
closes; the kit's close closes its own executor's.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Channel control: a committed_event or a channel_call reaching an executor that closed or a process that is closing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A `committed_event` or a `channel_call` that reaches an executor that closed,
or a process that is closing, is refused unapplied, as a request is
(§10.6.7): the owner places it again, never on the executor that refused it,
and one no other executor takes is dropped and logged, or fails, as above.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Outside a turn: the messages an executor sends the owner outside a turn (room_call, room_publication), and what each carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Outside a turn**, executor → owner, through the port to the owner the
backend gives each executor it serves:

| Message | Answer | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| `room_call` | `host_result` | A `TurnHost` verb made after its turn ended (§10.6.5): its `call_id`, the channel and room, the executor's id, the id of the turn the work began in, the verb and its arguments; the turn being over, the verb is a new arrival at its own event's depth (§10.6.5) |
| `room_publication` | — | A realtime publication or a framework event made after its turn ended, as `ephemeral` and `framework_event` carry them, with the channel, room, executor and turn |

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Outside a turn: which executor the owner accepts a room_call or a room_publication from, an owner that restarted included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner accepts one only from the executor of the last turn it sent for
the channel and room (`previous_turn`, §10.6.2), and anything else is
refused, an owner that restarted included, until its next turn.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Outside a turn: the turn a room_call names. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
`room_call` MUST also name that very turn: work an earlier turn began writes
nothing once a later turn was sent.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Outside a turn: the turn a room_publication names, an external agent's update (§6.4) included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A `room_publication` may name an earlier
turn of that executor, which still holds the room's state: an external
agent's update (§6.4) is handled under the turn prompting its session, or
outside any turn when none is.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Outside a turn: how the owner publishes a room_publication it accepts, and the ephemerals §8.4 allows for the turn it names. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It publishes what it accepts as it
publishes a turn's `ephemeral` and `framework_event` frames, for the room
and kinds a turn may publish, and publishes its ephemerals only as §8.4
allows for the turn it names: that turn's trigger, as it was sent, and the
binding as the room holds it then.

requirements.applies: §10.6.3 Outside a turn: a room_publication naming a turn the owner no longer knows, or a channel call, and a later turn's scope. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn the owner no longer knows, or a
channel call, which has no answer, publishes none; a publication never
takes a later turn's scope.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: the ChannelOutput the owner hands its reader, from the output frame. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: The owner hands its reader a `ChannelOutput` built from the `output` frame.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: a turn whose output a stream follows: the items the owner's stream yields, and its consumer and streaming targets. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When a stream follows, its response stream yields the items the `item` frames
carry, so the consumer that stores segments and the streaming targets that
render them (§10.2, Appendix A.9) read it as they read a local stream.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: the reader's pace: when a model round and a tool call run, a reader that stops, a stream closed unread. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The reader sets the pace, as it does locally: a model round and a tool call run
only as the stream is read, a reader that stops leaves no call started after
that point (§12.2), and a stream closed unread makes no provider call (a muted
binding, §7.5).

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: pull messages and how far an executor advances the channel's stream; reading ahead within a grant is RK-10.6.4-007's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner's reads of its stream send
`pull` messages, each granting a number of items: the executor advances the
channel's stream by at most the items granted, and MUST NOT advance past an
item other than a text or reasoning delta or what a generation used (a call's
start, a segment break, a loop's end) until a later `pull` grants it, so a call
or a round starts only once the reader asked for what follows it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: what a later pull is, and a pull that says fewer items read than the executor read. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A later `pull` is one the owner
sent once its reader read that item: each `pull` says how many items the
reader read, and the executor takes one that says fewer than it had read
through that item as granting nothing.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: what an executor reads ahead of the reader within a grant. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Within a grant the executor reads
deltas, and what a generation used, ahead of the reader, so a round is decided
as its generation ends, whatever its reader is still showing.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: text deltas a channel yields without waiting between them, crossing as one item, and the grant they count against. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Text deltas the channel yields without waiting
between them MAY cross as one `item` holding their joined text and their
number, which counts as that many items against the grant: the text is kept,
not where it was cut, so a reader that decides between deltas decides on the
text (a sentence budget reads it a sentence at a time, §12.2 step 12s.e).

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: closing the owner's stream; a close that finds the executor reading ahead is RK-10.6.4-010's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Closing the owner's stream sends `close`, and the executor closes the
channel's stream as a local reader's close would: it is the reader's close,
not a cancellation (§10.6.8).

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: a close that finds the executor reading ahead, and a read only a later pull let start. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A close that finds the executor reading ahead,
past a delta, cuts that read at once, since a local reader's close would have
found the stream waiting at the item it yielded; a read only a later `pull`
let start (a call running past its start) finishes first.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: items read ahead that the owner had not read when its stream was closed or the turn cut. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Items read ahead
that the owner had not read when its stream was closed or the turn cut are
dropped: what the consumer stores is what its readers read (§10.2).

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream, what the consumer reads in frames: the record each stored segment is stored with. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The consumer reads in frames what the channel changes after yielding it:

- each segment is stored with the record of the last `record` frame received
  before the `item` that ended it: a tool handler's write mid-loop reaches the
  segments that follow (§6.7);

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream, what the consumer reads in frames: a call's arguments. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a call's arguments are its `tool_args` frame's when it has one, its start's
  otherwise;

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream, what the consumer reads in frames: a call's end and its start, two calls under one id included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a call's end names its start's frame, so two calls under one id stay two
  calls (§6.4);

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream, what the consumer reads in frames: a call that ended before the stream was closed or the turn cut, and a call no end was sent for. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a call that ended before the stream was closed or the turn cut is closed
  with its own outcome: the executor sends its end once, before the next
  item it sends and so before the turn's `end`, and the owner closes as
  cancelled only a call no end was sent for, a reader that stops between a
  round's end items included.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: when the executor compares the turn's record with the last one it sent: before each item that is no delta, before a failed stream's error, once the stream is closed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The executor compares the record with the last one it sent before each `item`
that is no delta (the stream's end included), before the `error` a failed
stream ends with, and once the stream is closed, so each of those reaches
the owner after every change written before it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.4 The stream: an executor checking only for a write to one of the record's keys before a delta, and when a change inside a value then reaches the owner. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Before a text or reasoning delta it MAY look only for a write to one of the
record's keys, so that a delta costs nothing for the record's size: a change
made inside a value the record already holds then reaches the owner before
the next `item` that is no delta, the one ending the segment stored with it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: which tools the owner serves: those orchestration sets up for a room and those the implementation binds to the kit. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Owner-served tools.** A tool runs where the live objects it needs live. The
tools that read or change the owner's state are served by the owner: the tools
orchestration sets up for a room (handoff, Section 19.6; the strategies' tools,
Section 19.7; a delegation's result tool, Section 23.3) and the tools the
implementation binds to the kit (a delegation's status and cancel tools,
Section 23.4), which a host attaches on the owner, to the channel's
declaration (§10.6.2), never through the executor's factory.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: the request's owner_tools and the order the channel declares them to its model. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner lists
them in the request's
`owner_tools`, and the executor's channel declares them to its model with its
other tools, in the order the request lists them, whether or not a tool waits
by design; the owner lists those it set up for every room the channel serves
in the order it set them up.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: where an owner-served tool's gate, report and handler run. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Their gate (`BEFORE_TOOL_USE`) and their report
(`ON_TOOL_CALL`) run on the executor, as for every call of the turn; only the
handler runs on the owner:

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: the per-call context a tool_call carries (§21.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `tool_call` carries the per-call context the implementation keeps for the
  call (§21.4), at least: its id, its name, the arguments its gate left, the
  turn's room, chain depth, actor and allowed names, who asked for the turn
  (the author label a strategy heads a task with, §19.7), and the id of the
  voice session it serves when it has one.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: the context the owner installs around the handler. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner installs that context
  around the handler, so the handler reads what it reads locally.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: what a tool_result carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `tool_result` carries the handler's answer as §21.4 reads it, its outcome
  (served, refused, failed, served by nothing, §9.3), the failure's class and
  the structured copy.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: a tool_call or a host_call the executor withdraws (its turn cut, or its bound expired, §21.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A `tool_call` or a `host_call` the executor withdraws (its turn cut, or the
  tool or hook that made it cut by its bound, §21.6) sends `call_cancel`, and
  the owner cancels the handler or the verb.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: the calls of a turn the owner cuts or loses. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner also cancels every
  call of a turn it cuts or loses itself.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: a turn's end and the calls it sent, unless the turn is cut. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Unless the turn is cut, the
  executor sends `end` only once each call it sent was answered.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: an executor whose channel already declares a tool under the name of one of the request's owner_tools. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor whose channel already declares a tool under the name of one of
the request's `owner_tools` MUST refuse the turn, with an error naming the
tool: which of the two handlers a call reaches would otherwise depend on the
executor.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: the owner setting up a tool on a channel it holds live whose name the channel already declares; it cannot for a channel held by declaration. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner refuses the same clash when it sets up the tool on a
channel it holds live, and cannot for one it holds by declaration alone.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: a channel whose declaration says its turns do not take the owner's tools, and a delegation's result tool for it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
owner MUST refuse to set up a tool for a channel whose declaration says its
turns do not take the owner's tools; a delegation's result tool is not set up
for it, and its result is its text.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: the tools the implementation installs that hold the channel's state (a plan, the human-input tools). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The tools the implementation installs that hold the channel's state (a plan,
§6.4; the human-input tools, §9.3) run on the executor.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Owner-served tools: the host's own tools. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The host's tools need
the host's live objects (its MCP clients, its sandbox, its database): they run
on the executor.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: how a host tool or hook on the executor reaches a room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**TurnHost.** A host tool or hook on the executor reaches a room only through
`TurnHost`, which it reads with `current_turn_host()` (§21.4).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: where TurnHost is bound and where it is empty, and a verb called after its turn ended; between turns is RK-10.6.5-022's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It is bound to
the turn's room inside a tool call of a turn and inside a hook the executor
fires while the turn runs, and, after the turn, in work the turn began (a task
or an `ASYNC` hook that outlives it) for the verbs below; it is empty anywhere
else, and any other verb called on it after its turn ended is refused.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: between turns, in work a turn began: send_event, post_status, update_room_metadata and add_observation, their budget and depth. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Between
turns (a background thinker's thought, §6.4) it is bound to the room of the
turn the work began in: `send_event`, `post_status`, `update_room_metadata`
and `add_observation` cross as `room_call` (§10.6.3), each a new arrival with
a budget of its own and the depth of its own event, the turn being over
(§9.5.1); a `send_event` made from the body of a hook run asynchronously names at least
the depth that body runs at (§8.3), which the owner keeps.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: between turns: delegate, wait_task and the readers of owner-process state. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`delegate`,
`wait_task` and the readers of owner-process state are
refused there, with an error naming the verb.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: what work a turn began publishes after the turn (realtime publications, framework events). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
What work a turn began publishes
after the turn (realtime publications, framework events) crosses as
`room_publication`: an executor never publishes it on the owner's realtime
backend or bus itself, and never writes the owner's store.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: TurnHost's surface: one host_call per verb, arguments as data. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Its surface is
minimal and enumerated: each verb is one `host_call`, every argument is data
(no callable crosses), and an implementation documents the set.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: the verbs every TurnHost carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It MUST carry:

```
TurnHost
├── send_event(room_id, channel_id, content, ...) → RoomEvent    # §10.5
├── delegate(room_id, agent_id, task, ...) → string              # the task id (§23.3)
├── wait_task(task_id, timeout) → DelegatedTaskResult | null     # §23.2
└── room_context() → RoomContext                                 # as the owner builds it now (§10.6.6)
```

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: the verbs an implementation adds for its own tools and hooks to write. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation adds the verbs its own tools and hooks need to write (a
status post, §19.8; a room-metadata update; an observation, §5.11), each
documented as one `host_call`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: a host declaring verbs of its own on the owner. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A host's own code may need what only the owner's process holds (a person's live
connection, a service the owner runs). An implementation SHOULD let the host
declare verbs of its own on the owner, each served by name as one `host_call`,
its arguments and its result data.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost, where an implementation lets the host declare verbs of its own: what a declared verb runs under, and a name its own verbs or another declared verb hold, or no host declared. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner runs a declared verb under what
the turn gave the call (its room, the actor of its turn, the requester, its
chain depth, the tool call it is made from), which the accessors a tool handler
reads answer for it (§21.4), and MUST refuse a name its own verbs or another
declared verb hold, and a verb no host declared.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost, where an implementation lets the host declare verbs of its own: a declared verb the host declared to be served between turns. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A declared verb needs its
turn unless the host declared it to be served between turns: work the turn
began then still sends it after the turn, as a `room_call`, and the owner runs
it for the turn's room and channel, with no actor nor tool call, as work that
starts fresh (§8.3).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost, where an implementation lets the host declare verbs of its own: between turns, a declared verb not declared to be served then. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner MUST refuse, between turns, a declared verb not
declared so.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: a verb naming another room or organization than its turn's room's, and an argument the verb does not take. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A `TurnHost` acts for its turn's room, in that room's organization: the owner
MUST refuse a verb that names another room or another organization than the
room's, and an argument the verb does not take.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: a status post made through it (§19.8). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A status post it makes names
the turn's room (§19.8).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: the depth of an event it sends and of a task it delegates, while the turn runs and once it is over. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An event it sends while the turn runs is at least as
deep as the turn's response (§8.3), and a task it delegates inherits the
turn's depth (§23.3), so a chain of turns writing through it stops at the
chain-depth limit as a local one does; an event that work the turn began sends
once the turn is over has the depth of its own event (§9.5.1).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: wait_task, for a task of the turn's room and for any other. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`wait_task`
answers for a task a `TurnHost` of the turn's room delegated, and answers null
for any other, as it does past its timeout.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 TurnHost: a room-metadata update through it, and the implementation's own namespace (§5.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A room-metadata update through it
MUST NOT write a key of the implementation's own namespace (§5.1: a detach's
revocation, §7.5; what the room keeps for a channel, §10.6.2).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 What a turn reads of its room: an executor other than the owner's own. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: An executor other than the owner's own needs no store.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 What a turn reads of its room: what a request carries for its turn to read: its context, and channel_rows for a channel run on an executor other than the owner's own. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
What a turn reads of its room comes with the
request: its context, and, for a channel run on an executor other than the
owner's own, `channel_rows`, which the owner reads for the turn: the channel's
own tool-call rows and the instructions it read, each once, those its history
replays and its latest calls, which rebuild
its tool memory and the skills it activated (§6.4, §24.4).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 What a turn reads of its room: a deleted row (§7.5 rule 8), and a store that fails to read channel_rows. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A deleted row is
withheld (§7.5 rule 8), and a store that fails costs the turn those rows, not
the turn.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 What a turn reads of its room: every write a turn makes to its room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Every write goes through `TurnHost`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 What a turn reads of its room: the reentrancy the owner applies to a call from a turn, and a call that would wait on the room's own delivery. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each call carries the room and the turn it is made from, and the
owner applies to it the reentrancy of its own task waiting on that turn when
the call arrives (the delivery-set target awaiting `output`, or the reader
awaiting an `item`): a call that would wait on the room's own delivery from a
task that delivery needs returns with its completion detached (§10.1 step 18),
as it does locally, rather than wait on the delivery set that runs the turn.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 What a turn reads of its room: a host running a kit beside an executor of another process; only the host can keep it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation cannot keep a host's code from committing through another
kit it holds: a host that runs a kit beside an executor of another process
MUST NOT let that executor's turns reach a room through it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner: whose the turn's response-metadata record is, and what a handler the owner runs for the turn learns of it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The turn's record on the owner.** The turn's response-metadata record
(§6.7) is the executor's, and a handler the owner runs for the turn learns
facts of the turn as a local one does: a document its tool read, a value its
tool protected.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner: the record a tool_call or a host_call made while the turn runs carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A `tool_call` and a `host_call` made while the turn runs carry
the record as the call leaves the executor, in the form a `record` message
carries it (§10.6.4).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner: the record the owner runs a handler or a declared verb on, as current_response_metadata() answers it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner runs the handler, or the declared verb, on a
record holding that copy, which `current_response_metadata()` answers there
(§21.4).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner: the handler's own copy, and the changes its tool_result or host_result carries, whether it answered, refused or failed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The handler works on a copy of its own, nothing of it shared with
the record the call carried, and its `tool_result` or `host_result` carries
what it changed, measured against what the call carried: each key it set to
another value, and each key the call carried that it removed, whether the
handler answered, refused or failed.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner, the changes a call's result brings back: a key removed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.

§10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner, the changes a call's result brings back: a key whose new value is a mapping, where the call carried a mapping or nothing and the turn's record holds one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a key whose new value is a mapping, where the call carried a mapping or
  nothing and the turn's record holds a mapping, takes the handler's change
  entry by entry: the entries it set are set, the entries the call carried
  that it removed are removed, and the others the turn's record holds stay;

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner, the changes a call's result brings back: any other key set. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: - any other key set takes the value the handler wrote.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner, the changes a call's result brings back: two calls of one turn served at once adding entries to one mapping, a key a concurrent call wrote, a call served alone. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
So two calls of one turn served at once that each add entries to one mapping
keep both, a key a concurrent call wrote is never removed by a call that did
not carry it, and a call served alone leaves the record as a local handler
would.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner, the changes a call's result brings back: two calls each setting a key to a value other than a mapping. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Two calls that each set a key to a value other than a mapping leave the
value of the one answered last: a host that has concurrent calls contribute to
one fact writes each contribution under an entry of its own. The whole record
crosses with each call, and only what the handler changed comes back.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner: a call made outside the turn: a declared verb served between turns, and work the turn began once it ended. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call
made outside the turn carries no record: a declared verb the owner serves
between turns, and work the turn began once it ended, read the empty value
from `current_response_metadata()`, as a realtime tool call does, and what
they write reaches no message.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The turn's record on the owner: a call or an answer without the record fields. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call or an answer without these fields reads
as one that carries no record and changed nothing.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The in-memory backend's execution context: the execution context a turn's work and its stream run in, and the reentrancy guards that hold for the turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**The in-memory backend's execution context.** The in-memory backend runs in
the owner's process, where a host's tool holds the kit itself and may call it
from a turn. It therefore runs a turn's work in a copy of the execution
context of the owner task that submitted the turn, and advances the turn's
stream in a copy of the context of the task that first reads it, kept for the
stream's life: the reentrancy guards that task holds (its room's delivery
lane, a room lock, a kit-held run) hold for the turn as they hold in the
owner's own code, and a tool that waits on the delivery of the event it sent
gets its completion detached rather than wait on itself.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The in-memory backend's execution context: what the in-memory backend carries beside the messages. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
That context is the
only thing the in-memory backend carries beside the messages, and it is no
object of the turn.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The in-memory backend's execution context: a close called from a turn's code, and the depth of what it sends while its turns run. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn's code also knows the turns it runs under, so a
close called from one of them cuts them without cutting the call that awaits
it, nor waiting for it (§12.10.4), and what it sends into a room while they
run is at least as deep as the deepest of their responses (§8.3).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 The in-memory backend's execution context: an executor of another process. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor of another process has no such context: its turns reach a room
through `TurnHost`, whose verbs carry the depth.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Human input: where a tool waiting for a human runs, and the owner's answer_input and reject_input. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Human input.** A tool waiting for a human's answer runs on the executor, and
the answer may arrive on the owner, which keeps the open requests of its
rooms' turns and offers their answer (`answer_input(request_id, value)`) and
their rejection (`reject_input(request_id, reason)`).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Human input: the owner's read of an open request by its id, a request no longer open, and one of another organization's room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It also offers each open
request as `ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED` reads it, by its id (`input_request`): its
room, channel, tool call and the actor of its turn, which `input_request`
carries, so the host's door can tell who was asked before it answers, and
nothing for a request that is no longer open or, given an organization, whose
room is another organization's (§17.2).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Human input: how a request settles: once, first come first served, never retracted. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The request settles
where its tool waits, once, first come first served: an answer the
human-input handler the host gave the channel takes, a hook's block, its
bound, a release, or the owner's outcome, whichever comes first; a later one
never retracts it (§9.3).

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Human input: the order of input_request and ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED, and an answer for an id the owner does not know yet. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The executor MUST send `input_request` before it
fires `ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED`, and the owner MUST hold an answer for an id
it does not know yet until the request arrives or `input_hold_timeout`
(default 60 seconds) passes, so a request is answerable from its creation
(§9.3); an implementation bounds how many answers it holds.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Human input: the owner's outcome reaching the executor as input_answer, and input_taken. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner's
outcome reaches the executor as `input_answer`, which settles the request only
while it is still open: an answer the tool reads, or a rejection it reads as a
refusal (§9.3); the executor answers `input_taken`, and the owner's door
answers whether the waiting tool read its outcome.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Human input: a request settled on the executor other than by input_answer. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A request settled on the
executor otherwise sends `input_closed`, and the owner closes its record.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Human input: a request still open when its turn ends, and a detached one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
request belongs to the turn that opened it; one still open when its turn ends
is withdrawn on both sides, its waiter reading it released, but a detached
one (a request no tool waits on, which its creator alone releases): the
owner's record goes with the turn while the request stays open on the
executor, answerable there.

requirements.applies: §10.6.5 Human input: a request a task opens after its turn ended. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One a task opens after its
turn ended is the host's handler's alone.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, where a trigger fires: the triggers that fire on the executor hosting the channel, during a turn or between turns. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A trigger fires where the work it observes runs. These triggers fire on the
executor that hosts the channel, during a turn or between turns (a thinker's
thought, a human-input request's notification):

| Trigger | Fires on |
|---|---|
| `BEFORE_AI_CONTEXT_BUILD` (Planned) | Executor |
| `BEFORE_AI_GENERATION` | Executor |
| `ON_AI_THINKING` | Executor |
| `ON_AI_RESPONSE` | Executor |
| `BEFORE_TOOL_USE` | Executor |
| `AFTER_TOOL_ROUND` | Executor |
| `ON_TOOL_CALL` | Executor |
| `ON_USER_INPUT_REQUIRED` | Executor |
| `ON_SPEAK_DECISION` | Executor |
| `ON_THOUGHT` | Executor |
| `ON_PLAN_UPDATED` | Executor |
| Every other trigger of §9.2 | Owner |

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, where a trigger fires: the triggers that fire on the owner. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
On the owner fire, among others, `ON_ERROR` (from the turn's `error` frame,
§9.2), `ON_TASK_CREATED` (from the output's tasks), `BEFORE_BROADCAST` on each
stored segment (§9.5), `AFTER_BROADCAST`, and the triggers that owner-served
tools and discussions fire (`ON_HANDOFF`, `ON_TASK_DELEGATED`,
`ON_STATUS_POSTED`, `ON_SPEAK_QUEUE`, `ON_DISPATCH_DECISION`).

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, registration: a hook on an executor trigger. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Registration.** A hook on an executor trigger registers on the executor
that runs the turns it observes.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, registration: a hook on an executor trigger registered on the kit. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Registered on the kit, it is a registration
on the kit's own executor: it fires for the turns of the channels the kit
holds live, and for the calls outside any turn below.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, registration: a kit hook on an executor trigger that a channel held by declaration alone could fire, and such a channel's declaration while one is registered. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel the kit holds
by its declaration alone (§10.6.2) runs its turns on another executor, where
such a hook would never fire. An implementation MUST therefore refuse a hook
on an executor trigger registered on the kit that such a channel could fire
(its channel filter does not leave the channel out), and the declaration of
such a channel while such a hook is registered, naming the executor where the
hook registers instead.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, registration: a room hook on an executor trigger registered on the kit while the kit holds a channel by declaration alone. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A room hook on an executor trigger registered on the
kit is refused while the kit holds any channel by its declaration alone: the
room's channels are not known when it registers.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, registration: a host's setup of its turn hooks, which only the host keeps. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A host registers its turn
hooks with one function it runs on every executor, the kit's own included, so
its setup takes one path too.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, registration: the implementation's own hooks on executor triggers (a scorer, a console's view). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The implementation's own hooks on these triggers (a scorer of turns, a
console's view of tool calls) register on executors the same way, and one that
writes (a scorer recording an observation) writes through `TurnHost`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, registration: an executor trigger fired in the owner's process outside any turn (speech-to-speech, a conference). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A trigger of the table that fires in the owner's process outside any turn (a
speech-to-speech session's tool calls and its reasoning delegations, §12.4 and
§12.4.1; a conference's tool calls, §12.10) fires the hooks registered on the
kit's own executor: one registration covers both.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Room hooks: a room hook on an executor trigger the kit registers for a room, for its own executor. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Room hooks.** A room hook on an executor trigger the kit registers for a
room (above) is its own executor's hook for that room, and no request names
it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Room hooks: a room hook for a channel other executors run. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One for a channel other executors run (§9.1) is registered on the
executors under a name.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Room hooks: the names a room has, forgotten with the room, and the request's room_hooks. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner keeps which names a room has, as it keeps
the room's other hooks, forgetting them with the room (§9.1), and the request
carries them in `room_hooks`: the
executor runs the hooks registered under those names for that turn.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Room hooks: an executor that has not registered every name a request carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
executor that has not registered every name a request carries does not take
it (§10.6.7), so a turn never runs without one of its room's hooks.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Room hooks: a name on an executor, and a hook registered again under a name and trigger it carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
On an
executor a name carries at most one hook per trigger, and a hook registered
again under a name and a trigger it already carries replaces the first.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Room hooks: a name the room enables (§9.1). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
name the room enables joins the room's scope (§9.1).

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Room hooks: enabling a name already enabled for that room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Enabling a name already
enabled for that room MUST be a no-op: it creates no duplicate activation and
preserves its place in the activation order.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Room hooks: enabling a name another hook registration of the room holds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Enabling a name held by another
hook registration of the room MUST be refused, so that a room never holds
two different hooks of one name.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, context: the RoomContext a hook on the executor receives during a turn, and once its turn is over or a cut leaves the owner no longer answering. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Context.** A hook on the executor receives the `RoomContext` its room's
owner builds when the hook fires, asked as the `host_call` verb `room_context`,
as a hook on the owner does; once its turn is over, or when a cut leaves the
owner no longer answering it, the context the turn started with.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, context: a hook on the executor outside any turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Outside any
turn (an external agent's own activity between two prompts) it receives the
context of the last turn the executor ran in that room, and none when it ran
no turn there or once every channel whose turns it ran there was detached
from the room (a room created again under its id reads nothing of the
earlier one).

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, context: a context the owner fails to build. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A context the owner fails to build is one the hook does not
get, as on the owner.

requirements.applies: §10.6.6 Hooks, context: how a hook on the executor changes a room, during a turn and between turns. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook
changes a room only through `TurnHost` (§10.6.5); between turns, where
`TurnHost` is empty, it changes none.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: what an executor declares. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor declares the channels it can host, the organizations whose rooms
it serves, and the names of the room hooks it registered.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: which executor a backend delivers a request to, and one no executor accepts; the channels the owner holds live are RK-10.6.7-021's, and a backend that knows every executor fails a request none declares at once (RK-10.6.7-020). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The backend MUST
deliver a request only to an executor that declares the request's channel,
serves its room's organization and registered every name of its `room_hooks`;
a request no executor accepts within `accept_timeout` fails (§10.6.8).

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: an executor's channel entries: ids, prefixes, `*`, and an entry with a `*` elsewhere. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
executor declares its channels as ids and prefixes: an entry ending in `*`
declares every channel whose id starts with what precedes it (`acme-*`), and
`*` alone every channel; an entry with a `*` anywhere else is refused when the
executor is built.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: a distributed backend and the channel entries it tells other processes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A distributed backend tells these entries to the other
processes as they are.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: an executor given a predicate or no declaration. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor given a predicate, or given no
declaration at all (every channel), takes the turns of its own process only.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: a deployment's pool of executors building an organization's agents; only the deployment keeps it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A pool of executors that build an organization's agents from its
configuration declares the organization's prefix, so an agent created after
the pool started needs no executor told of it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: an executor's organization entries, an empty declaration and an entry holding a `*` with anything else. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor declares its
organizations (§17.2) as exact ids, and `*` alone for every organization; an
empty declaration, or an entry holding a `*` with anything else, is refused
when the executor is built.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: the rooms `*` and exact organization ids serve. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`*` serves the rooms of every organization and
the rooms without one; exact ids serve those organizations' rooms alone, not
the rooms without an organization.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: an executor that declares no organization. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One that declares none serves the rooms
without an organization alone, so an executor started without a declaration
never takes the turns of a room that has one.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: a room's turns, channel calls and committed events, and a room no executor serves. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A room's turns, channel calls and
committed events go only to an executor serving the room's organization, and
one none serves fails with `no_executor`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: work an executor receives for a room of an organization it does not serve, whatever placed it there. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor MUST refuse the work of
a room of an organization it does not serve, whatever placed it there: a
turn or a channel call fails with `no_executor`, and a `room_attached` or a
`committed_event` is dropped, nothing built for it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement, the owner's own executor: the organizations the kit's own executor serves, and an owner given an executor of the host's as its own. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The kit's own executor
serves every organization; an owner given an executor of the host's as its
own runs the channels it holds live only in the rooms that executor serves.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: what a declaration names. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A declaration names no room: the owner already
ties a room to the executor holding it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: the organizations executors declare, and who may reach the backend's transport to declare them, which the host controls. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Organizations keep apart the
executors that declare them honestly; a process that reaches the backend's
transport can declare any, so who may reach it is the host's to control
(§10.6.9).

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: a turn or channel call placed on an executor whose factory builds nothing for its channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn or channel call
placed on an executor whose factory builds nothing for its channel fails with
`no_executor`, and is not placed again (§10.6.2).

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: the room's next turns after one an executor's factory built nothing for. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
That executor still holds
the room for the channel, so the room's next turns go to it while it lives
and takes them: a host gives every executor a factory that builds every
channel its entries cover.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: how a turn crosses: in the owner's process, or over the backend's transport. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn placed on an executor of the owner's own process is carried in that
process, as the in-memory backend carries it; one placed elsewhere crosses
the backend's transport.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: a backend that knows every executor alive (the in-memory one, a distributed one with a registry), and a request none declares. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A backend that knows every executor alive (the
in-memory one; a distributed one keeping a registry of the executors alive and
what they declare) fails at once, with `no_executor`, a request none of them
declares.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement, the owner's own executor: the turns, channel calls and committed events of the channels the owner holds live, whatever else declares the channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner's own executor, the one that runs the channels the owner
holds live, takes their turns, channel calls and committed events: a backend
MUST place them on it and on no other executor, whatever else declares the
channel, and one it does not take (a room hook it does not define) fails with
`no_executor`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement, the owner's own executor: the work of the channels the owner holds live once its own executor closed, and their room_attached and room_detached. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Once the owner's own executor closed (a host closing it while
the owner runs), they fail with `no_executor` too: they are never placed on
another executor, whose copy of the channel would run without the live
channel's state. The channel's `room_attached` and `room_detached`
(§10.6.3) reach that executor alone, for the same reason.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: an agent a host runs on an executor of its own. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An agent a host
runs on an executor of its own is one the owner holds by its declaration
(§10.6.2).

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: how many executors a request reaches: a process that refuses it, one that does not answer within accept_timeout. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A request MUST reach one executor at
