most: a process that refuses it
(its executor closed) has it placed again; one that does not answer it within
`accept_timeout` loses the turn (`executor_lost`), which is never handed to
another.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: a room's turns of a channel and the executor that ran its previous one, while it lives and takes the turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
backend MUST place a room's turns of a channel on the executor that ran its
previous one while that executor lives and takes the turn, so its caches stay
warm and its session state stays, the session state the room needs among it
(an ACP session, a speak policy's listening state, §10.6.2): "the same
executor for the session's life" is the case where one executor holds the
room.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Placement: which executor holds a room's state for a channel; channel control is placed as §10.6.3 says. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The executor that holds a room's state for a channel is the one that
took its last turn or channel call, while it serves and declares the
channel. A channel control message is placed as §10.6.3 says.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: the executors a backend lists, the owner's own aside, what each entry carries, and a closed or silent executor. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Which agents can answer.** A backend lists the executors it carries turns
to, the owner's own aside: each one's id, process, declared entries,
organizations, room hook names, last beat, and whether it is online, that is not closed and beating
within `heartbeat_timeout` (§10.6.8); a closed executor is not listed, and a
silent one stays listed, offline, until its process's entry is forgotten.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: when an agent is online in a room, held by declaration or live. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An
agent is online in a room while an executor online covers it there, declaring
its channel, serving the room's organization and defining the room's enabled
hooks; an agent the owner holds
live, while the owner's own executor takes its turns there.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: the owner's answer of a room's agent presence. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner answers
a room's agent presence, each agent with the executors covering it, sorted by
channel id.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: when the owner publishes an agent's presence ephemerals in a room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It publishes an agent's presence in a room as the presence
ephemerals of §8.4 (`presence_online` / `presence_offline`, `user_id` the
agent's channel id): as the agent is attached there, and, for an agent it
holds by its declaration, in each active or paused room the agent is attached
to when the executors covering it change.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: when the owner looks at the executors, and an executor's silence. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It looks at the executors at each
heartbeat interval, and at once when an executor of its process other than its
own is served or closes, so an executor's silence turns its agents offline at
`heartbeat_timeout`, never at one late beat.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: the presence a backend keeps per agent and room, the owners that see one change, an owner restarting. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A backend keeps the presence last
published per agent and room, and each change is published by the owner that
records it there first: of the owners that see the same change, one alone
publishes it, and, where the backend keeps it beyond the owner's process (a
distributed backend), an owner restarting publishes nothing that did not
change.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: a publication or a claim that fails, and an owner closing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A publication, or a claim, that fails is tried again at a later look
of the owner that made it, while that owner runs; closing, it lets go of the
claims it could not publish, which the room's next change or attach, or an
owner that starts, then publishes.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: a detach and a room's close. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A detach, and a room's close, forget what
was published for the agent in the room.

requirements.applies: §10.6.7 Which agents can answer: a backend that cannot list its executors. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A backend that cannot list its
executors has the owner publish nothing for the agents it holds by
declaration, whose presence it cannot tell.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: the messages each side sends on a running turn's link, the in-memory backend included. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Liveness, both ways.** While a turn runs, each side MUST send a message on
its link at least every `heartbeat_interval` (default 2 seconds), a
`heartbeat` when it has nothing else to send, the in-memory backend included.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: the owner failing a turn: accepted not within accept_timeout, an executor silent for heartbeat_timeout; silence and the beat are counted as RK-10.6.8-009 and RK-10.6.8-011 say, and a backend that knows every executor fails a request none declares at once (RK-10.6.7-020). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- The owner MUST fail the turn when `accepted` does not come within
  `accept_timeout` (default 10 seconds), with `no_executor` when no executor
  that could take the request (§10.6.7) ran meanwhile and `executor_lost`
  otherwise, and when the executor stays silent for `heartbeat_timeout`
  (default 10 seconds), with `executor_lost`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: the executor cutting a turn whose owner stays silent; silence is counted as RK-10.6.8-009 says. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- The executor MUST cut the turn as `owner_lost` when the owner stays silent
  for `heartbeat_timeout`, and stop sending its frames: its tools stop acting
  for an owner that no longer reads them, and an ACP session's next prompt is
  not held behind a turn nobody reads (§6.4).

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: how silence is counted, and a busy turn in memory. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Silence is counted only while the side that counts it runs: a stall of its own
event loop is not the other side's silence. In memory, where the executor's
CPU is the owner's stall, a busy turn is therefore never lost.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: an executor in a process of its own and the context it beats from. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor in a process of its own MUST beat from a context the turn's work
cannot stall (a thread of its own), so a turn busy with its CPU, the case the
backend exists for, still beats.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: a beat that travels outside the turn's numbered messages, and what the owner counts before and after accepted. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
That beat MAY travel outside the turn's
numbered messages (a record of the executor alive that its thread refreshes,
on the transport's clock): once an executor took the turn, the owner counts
it as a message from that executor while that executor's process still runs
the turn, which it does until the turn's `end` is written (a turn whose work
ended without its `end` is then lost, not waited for); before, only `accepted` counts, so a turn no executor takes still fails
within `accept_timeout`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: an executor id restarted in another process. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor beats as one process's: the same id
restarted in another process beats for none of the first one's turns.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: a slow turn that keeps beating, and the framework's own timeout around on_event() (§13.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A slow
turn that keeps beating is never
failed by the owner: the framework sets no timeout of its own around
`on_event()` (§13.6), and the heartbeat tells a slow turn from a lost executor
without one.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: a turn that failed through its backend or its executor (no_executor, executor_lost, frame_lost, a drainage not complete, its executor closed under it), not one whose on_event() raised itself (§10.1 step 18): its target, ON_ERROR, the caller's error, a stream already read and its stored segments. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn that failed ends as an
`on_event()` that raised: its target is recorded failed in the delivery set,
`ON_ERROR` fires, and the caller reads the error (§10.1 step 18); a stream
already read ends as a stream that raised (§12.2 step 13s), its stored
segments kept.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: a turn whose executor the owner lost: its owner-served calls and the cancel sent. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The owner cancels the turn's owner-served calls and sends
`cancel` to the executor it lost, best effort.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Liveness: a turn that failed through its backend or its executor, as RK-10.6.8-014 reads it: the room's index and its lane. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The turn commits nothing by
itself, so its failure leaves no index unaccounted for, and the lane moves on.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: a reader that stops reading the turn's stream. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.

§10.6.8 Cancellation: a turn whose cascade is cancelled (§10.1 Explicit delivery cancellation, the kit's close): the cancel message and the executor's local cancellation. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- the turn's cascade is cancelled (§10.1, *Explicit delivery cancellation*;
  the kit's close, as it starts, with the reason `kit_closed`, §12.10.4):
  `cancel`, with the cascade's reason; the executor cancels
  the turn's work as its own process would cancel it locally, its running
  tool handlers included (§21.6).

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: a turn its cancelled cascade would start, and a submission the cancellation interrupts after its hand-over. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn its cascade would start once
  cancelled is never submitted, and a submission the cancellation interrupts
  after its hand-over gives the turn up: the backend releases it, and its
  executor cuts it as it would cut one whose owner was lost;

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: a steering Cancel (§21.3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: - a steering `Cancel` (§21.3): `steer`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: a close and a cancel reaching the executor, in either order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An executor cancels a turn's work once: a `close` and a `cancel` that reach it
in either order let the cleanup the first one started, the channel's
finalizers included, run to its end before `end`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: how a cut turn ends: its loop's end, its open calls, then end. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The turn then ends with what such an end produces locally (its loop's end with
reason `cancelled`, its open calls closed, §6.4 *A turn cut short*), then
`end`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: an end not received within cancel_timeout after cancel; a steering Cancel the owner waits for without it is RK-10.6.8-038's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An `end` that does not come within `cancel_timeout` (default 5 seconds)
after `cancel` is reported as incomplete drainage (§10.1): the turn ends
failed, the owner drops its later frames, and nothing reports its cleanup
done.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: the owner after close, and a call already running. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
After `close`, the owner waits for `end` while the executor keeps
beating: a call already running is let finish (§12.2 step 13s), within its
own bound (§21.6).

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: a turn still open when its owner itself closes (the kit's close once its grace is over): its end, its later frames, backend_closed, and the call the kit's close cut. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn still open when its owner itself closes (the kit's
close, once the grace it gives its running work is over, §12.10.4) is given
up and owes no `end`:
the owner waits for nothing more from its executor and drops its later
frames, and its reader fails it with `backend_closed`, a reason of its own (the
owner's backend closed; its executor is not lost, so never `executor_lost`),
which a host reads on the error a turn link raises; the call the kit's close
cut reads its cut (`kit_closed`), never that failure as its error.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: a turn its owner gave up as it closed: its release, its executor's cut, the turns the close runs under, the cascade that read it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
backend releases the turn, and its executor cuts it as it would
cut one whose owner was lost, at once when the release reaches it, else after
`heartbeat_timeout` of silence, except the turns the close runs under, those
of every `close()` the kit's shutdown answers (§10.6.5, §12.10.4); a cascade
that read it counts its cleanup done.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Cancellation: a turn already over when its owner closes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn already over
keeps what its end reported: one whose `end` is owed stays incomplete.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Closing an executor: TurnExecutor.close(): new turns, running turns, and the turns the closing call runs under. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Closing an executor.** `TurnExecutor.close()` refuses new turns, cancels
its running turns and waits for their end, except the turns the closing call
runs under.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Closing an executor: a later close from outside the turns an earlier close spared. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
That exemption applies to this call: a later close from outside
those turns cancels them too.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Closing an executor: a turn spared by its own close that its owner later cancels. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn spared by its own close can finish its
work if its owner later cancels it: the executor ends the owner's wait and
carries no further output on that turn's link.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Closing an executor: a later external close of the executor, after the owner cancelled a spared turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A later external executor close
still cancels that work.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Closing an executor: the channels an executor closes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The executor closes only channels it owns
(§10.6.3).

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Closing an executor: closing the kit's local executor: the kit, its backend, its registered channels and their later turns. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The kit's local executor borrows its registered channels; closing
it leaves the kit, its backend and its registered channels open, and their later
intelligence turns fail with `no_executor` (§10.6.7).

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Closing an executor: a separate room delivery, and a process_inbound called by a turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A separate room delivery
has its own turn scope; a `process_inbound` called by a turn does not make
that turn an ancestor in the new delivery's executor scope.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Steering: the owner's steer() call and what it answers. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Steering.** The owner offers the host an asynchronous `steer(room_id,
channel_id, directive, turn_id | null)` that answers the number of loops it
reached; across the backend a turn's id names its loop.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Steering: the room steer() names, and a turn id that narrows it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The room is always
named: a turn id narrows the steer to that turn of the room, and a turn of
another room is reached by nothing.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Steering: how steer() resolves its target turns and sums their steer_result. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It resolves the target turns from the
turns it submitted, in the order it started them, under the rules of §21.3 (a
room's most recent loop is the loop of its most recently started turn still
running), sends `steer` on each target's link, and
sums their `steer_result`.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Steering: a channel without steering, or one whose steering cannot reach the turn yet, given a Cancel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel without steering, or one whose steering
cannot reach the turn yet (it answers none), receives a `Cancel` as the
turn's `cancel`: the owner then waits for `end` as after `close`, without
`cancel_timeout`, and the turn counts as one loop reached.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Steering: an ACP agent channel given a Cancel, before and once the turn holds its room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An ACP agent
channel steers a `Cancel` alone, for the turn it names, as its own
cancellation (§6.4 item 7): it answers one once the turn holds its Room
(§6.4 item 7), its session being opened or its prompt out; before that it
answers none, and the owner cuts the turn.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Steering: a discussion that holds the room (§19.7.5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A discussion that holds the room cuts its turns this way
(§19.7.5).

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Steering: the turns a host can steer, with several owner processes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The turns a host can steer are those the process it
steers from submitted: with several owner processes, it steers from the one
running the room's delivery (§10.2), and another reaches none of them.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Errors: what an error record carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Errors.** An error record carries the error's kind (the implementation's
name of its class), its message, its arguments and the attributes JSON
carries (what classifies it: a provider's status code and whether it is
retryable, a cut turn's reason, an application's own code), the kinds of the
classes its class derives from, nearest first, and its causes, each a record
of its own, in order.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Errors: the side that reads an error record (the owner for a turn's error, the executor for an owner-served call's or a host verb's), and an error of a class it rebuilds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The side that reads a record (the owner for a turn's
error, the executor for what an owner-served call or a host verb raised)
rebuilds one error per record, its causes chained, so what reads it
(`ON_ERROR`'s `error_type`, a task's failure, §23.3, a reader that compares
the error it holds with the turn's, the host's own classification) reads it
as it reads a local one:

- an error of a class the side rebuilds comes back of that class, with its
  arguments and attributes.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Errors: the classes a side rebuilds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A side rebuilds the implementation's own classes,
  the language's built-in ones, and the classes its host declares, each with
  its subclasses, a class nested in another or defined in a function
  included.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Errors: what each side reads of what the other raised, and a host declaring its error classes to the owner and to each of its executors. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each side reads what the other raised, so a host declares its
  classes to the owner and to each of its executors, an executor in another
  process included.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Errors: an error of a class the side rebuilds that cannot be rebuilt so that it gives back its message. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
§10.6.8 Errors: an error of a class the side does not rebuild. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- any other comes back as a generic turn error that keeps the kind, the
  classes it derives from and the attributes, and that is also of the nearest
  of those classes the side rebuilds: a host's subclass of a provider error
  still reads as a provider error (its log line, §15.3; `ON_ERROR`);

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Errors: a generic turn error that crosses again. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- a generic turn error that crosses again crosses as the error it stands
  for, its kind and classes unchanged.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Errors: how a side resolves a kind or a class a record names. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A side MUST NOT import a module, nor run a module's code (an attribute hook,
a lazy loader), to resolve a kind or a class a record names: it looks the name up among the
classes already loaded, and one it does not find there is a class it does not
rebuild.

requirements.applies: §10.6.8 Errors: the message of an error record. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: The message is for logs and hooks, never for a model (§9.3).

requirements.applies: §10.6.9 Telemetry and prerequisites: the trace context a request carries, and the spans an executor records for the turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Telemetry.** The request carries the trace context of the broadcast span;
the spans the executor records for the turn (its generations, its tool calls,
its hooks) are its children, so a tracing backend shows one trace across the
processes.

requirements.applies: §10.6.9 Telemetry and prerequisites: an executor in another process and the store. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Prerequisites.** An executor in another process needs no store (§10.6.5):
the store is the room owner's, and several owner processes share theirs
(Section 14).

requirements.applies: §10.6.9 Telemetry and prerequisites: the lock manager several owner processes share, and an executor. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The distributed lock manager of §13.5 is what several owner processes need among themselves; an
executor takes no room lock.

requirements.applies: §10.6.9 Telemetry and prerequisites: the timeouts of every process of a backend; only the deployment keeps them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Every process of a backend keeps the same
timeouts (§10.6.8).

requirements.applies: §10.6.9 Telemetry and prerequisites: work a turn began that reaches the owner after the turn, with one or several owner processes. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Addressing and trust.** Work a turn began that reaches the owner after the
turn (§10.6.3) goes to the owner process that submitted the turn, which the
backend records as it carries the request, and is waited for while that
process lives; with several owner processes, the others do not see it.

requirements.applies: §10.6.9 Telemetry and prerequisites: a channel control a distributed backend carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
channel control a distributed backend carries is applied on the executor
before the owner goes on, as in memory.

requirements.applies: §10.6.9 Telemetry and prerequisites: a distributed backend's transport, who can write to or read it, and how it is restricted; only the deployment keeps it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A distributed backend's transport is its trust
boundary: the executor ids and owner addresses its messages carry are not
authenticated beyond it, so whoever can write to the transport can act as an
executor or an owner, as whoever can read it reads the rooms' turns. It is
restricted as the rooms are (credentials, encryption in transit).

requirements.applies: §10.6.9 Telemetry and prerequisites: what the owner keeps, read off the frames: ordering, reentry, chain depth, streamed segments, streaming targets, the turn record and the caller's turns. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**On the owner.** Ordering (per room, in index order), the reentry of response
events as commit passes, chain depth (§8.3), the persistence of streamed
segments and their hooks, the delivery to streaming targets, the turn record
(§6.4) and the caller's `turns` are the owner's, read off the frames.

requirements.applies: §11.1 IdentityResolver interface: its one call, with the inbound message and the room context, answering an IdentityResult. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
IdentityResolver (interface)
└── resolve(message: InboundMessage, context: RoomContext) → IdentityResult
```

requirements.applies: §11.1 IdentityResult: the fields a resolver answers with. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**IdentityResult:**

```
IdentityResult
├── status: IdentificationStatus            # IDENTIFIED, AMBIGUOUS, UNKNOWN, PENDING, CHALLENGE_SENT, REJECTED
├── identity: Identity | null               # Resolved identity (if IDENTIFIED)
├── candidates: list<Identity>              # Candidate identities (if AMBIGUOUS or PENDING)
├── address: string | null                  # The address resolved; the sender's if unset
├── channel_type: string | null             # Its channel type; the message's channel's if unset
├── challenge_type: string | null           # For CHALLENGE_SENT: its kind; not read
└── message: string | null                  # For CHALLENGE_SENT and REJECTED: the block's reason, unless empty
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 Resolution pipeline, for an inbound message with an address left to resolve (§11.6): the resolver's call with the message and the room context, and the IdentityResult it returns. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
Inbound arrives (channel_type, sender_address)
      │
      ▼
IdentityResolver.resolve(message, context)
      │
      ▼
Returns IdentityResult
      │
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 Resolution pipeline: a resolver's IDENTIFIED result (one match). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
      ├── IDENTIFIED (1 match)
      │   └── Create participant with identity_id set
      │
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 Resolution pipeline: a resolver's AMBIGUOUS result (several matches) or its PENDING, either of which fires ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
      ├── AMBIGUOUS (N matches), or the resolver's PENDING
      │   ├── Fire ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS hook
      │   └── Hook returns:
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: a hook's resolved(identity). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
      │       ├── resolved(identity) → use that identity
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: a hook's pending(), or a null from every hook. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
      │       ├── pending() or null → create pending participant
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: a hook's challenge(inject). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
      │       ├── challenge(inject) → commit the challenge (§9.4), block processing
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: a hook's reject(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
      │       └── reject() → reject the message
      │
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 Resolution pipeline: a resolver's CHALLENGE_SENT result, the challenge put by the resolver itself, which fires neither identity trigger. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
      ├── CHALLENGE_SENT (the resolver put the challenge itself)
      │   └── Block the message with the resolver's message, else
      │       identity_challenge_sent; neither identity trigger fires,
      │       nothing is committed
      │
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 Resolution pipeline: a resolver's UNKNOWN result (no match) or its REJECTED, which fires ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
      └── UNKNOWN (0 matches), or the resolver's REJECTED
          ├── Fire ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN hook
          └── Hook returns:
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN: a hook's resolved(identity). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
              ├── resolved(identity) → use that identity
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN: a hook's pending(candidates). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
              ├── pending(candidates) → create pending participant
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN: a hook's challenge(inject). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
              ├── challenge(inject) → commit the challenge (§9.4), block processing
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN: a hook's reject(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
              ├── reject() → reject the message
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN: a null from every hook, on a resolver's UNKNOWN and on its REJECTED. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
              └── null → UNKNOWN: process the message, its sender unresolved;
                         REJECTED: block it with the resolver's message,
                         else identity_rejected
```

requirements.applies: §11.2 Identity hooks of ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS and ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN: what each is handed, and their order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Identity hooks receive the event, the room context and the IdentityResult, and
run in registration order.

requirements.applies: §11.2 Identity hooks: the first result decides, and a hook that raises. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The first one that returns a result decides; one
that raises is logged and the next one runs.

requirements.applies: §11.2 Identity hooks: a result whose status the trigger does not act on. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A result whose status the trigger
does not act on is read as null.

requirements.applies: §11.2 ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS and ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN: a hook registered on them through HookRegistration (§9.1), an observer. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook registered on these two triggers
through HookRegistration (Section 9.1) runs after them as an observer and
cannot decide.

requirements.applies: §11.2 A pending participant an identity trigger creates: its candidates on each trigger, and the display_name of a hook's pending(). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The pending participant carries the resolver's candidates on
ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS, and on ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN the hook's, else the
resolver's; on either trigger, a hook's `pending()` gives the record it
creates its `display_name`.

requirements.applies: §11.2 A resolver's REJECTED: what the hooks of ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN read of it, what they may still decide, and the message when none decides. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A resolver's REJECTED is its refusal: the identity hooks of
ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN read it as REJECTED, with its message, and may still
name, pend, challenge or reject the sender, but when none of them decides,
the message is blocked with the resolver's message, else `identity_rejected`,
and nothing of it is stored.

requirements.applies: §11.2 A pending sender: the record their events are sent under, never one under the id the channel gave (the sentence after it gives the reason). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A pending sender is never given a record under the id the channel gave: the
event is sent under the room's record of that id when one was reached through
the channel (a member the host added), else under the sender's own record,
created for them: `pending-` and the first 16 hexadecimal digits of the
SHA-256 of the channel id, U+001F and the sender id, one per sender and
channel. A sender who chooses their id (on a WebSocket, in an HTTP body) could
otherwise take an identity's id: the pending record under it
would be completed when that identity is resolved on another channel, and
its impostor's next message would pass for an identified sender (§11.6).

requirements.applies: §11.2 A pending sender's own record: the sender's address names it on its channel, for an advisor's resolution and for routing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
sender's address names that record on its channel (§5.5): an advisor's
resolution of it spares the sender resolution (§11.6), and routing finds
their room by it (§10.4 step 1).

requirements.applies: §11.3 IdentityHookResult: the fields an identity hook answers with, and those the framework reads for each status. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
IdentityHookResult
├── status: IdentificationStatus            # The outcome (below)
├── identity: Identity | null               # For IDENTIFIED: the sender
├── display_name: string | null             # For PENDING: the new record's name
├── candidates: list<Identity> | null       # For PENDING, on UNKNOWN only
├── inject: InjectedEvent | null            # For CHALLENGE_SENT: the challenge
├── reason: string | null                   # For REJECTED: the block's reason
├── challenge_type: string | null           # Not read by the framework
└── message: string | null                  # Set by challenge(); not read
```

requirements.applies: §11.3: the helpers that build an IdentityHookResult, the status each sets, and reject()'s default reason. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`resolved(identity)`, `pending(display_name, candidates)`,
`challenge(inject, message)` and `reject(reason)` set `status` to IDENTIFIED,
PENDING, CHALLENGE_SENT and REJECTED; `reject` defaults its reason to
"Unknown sender".

requirements.applies: §11.3: what a hook's CHALLENGE_SENT result blocks and commits, and a REJECTED result with no reason, on each identity trigger. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A challenge blocks the message with the reason
`identity_challenge_sent`, and its `inject` is committed as an injected event
(§9.4), in a cascade of its own; a REJECTED result with no reason blocks it
with `identity_rejected` on ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS and `unknown_sender` on
ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN.

requirements.applies: §11.4 Channel type filtering: the channel types identity resolution runs for, configurable (the second sentence gives the reason). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Implementations SHOULD support configuring which channel types trigger identity
resolution. Not all channels carry meaningful identity information (e.g., an
internal WebSocket may not need identity resolution).

requirements.applies: §11.5 A resolution past the configured identity timeout: its result, read as UNKNOWN. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
If identity resolution exceeds the configured timeout, the implementation MUST:

1. Treat the result as UNKNOWN.

requirements.applies: §11.5 A resolution past the configured identity timeout: the identity_timeout framework event. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: 2. Emit an `identity_timeout` framework event.

requirements.applies: §11.5 A resolution past the configured identity timeout: the inbound message, processed on. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: 3. Continue processing the inbound message (do not block).

requirements.applies: §11.6 Senders with nothing to resolve, the list's rule and case 1: a channel that declares its inbound sender_id a room Participant.id, whose senders are not resolved (the opening sentence says what a resolver maps). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A resolver maps an **address** — a number, an email, a handle — to an Identity.
Three senders carry no such question, and an implementation MUST NOT run
resolution for them:

1. **The channel names its own senders.** A channel MAY declare that its
   inbound `sender_id` is a room `Participant.id` rather than an address.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 1, conference (media feature conference): a conference's utterances, under the identity their track was published under, not resolved (Section 12.10.2 rule 3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
   conference is the case this exists for (Section 12.10.4): its utterances
   carry the identity a track was published under, and resolving that is the
   "resolve on the opaque identity" Section 12.10.2 rule 3 rules out.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 2, under the list's rule: an event whose participant_id names, on the event's channel, an IDENTIFIED participant of the room, the sender's own record (§11.2) included, which is not resolved. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
2. **The room has already identified the sender.** Where the event's
   `participant_id` names, on the event's channel (Section 5.5), a Participant
   of the room whose `identification` is IDENTIFIED, the sender's own record
   (Section 11.2) included, the question has been answered and the answer is
   on the roster.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 2: an IDENTIFIED participant's id on a channel the participant was never reached through, which is resolved. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The same id on a channel the
   participant was never reached through answers nothing, and is resolved.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 3, under the list's rule: a message the framework writes into a room (a deliver(), an orchestration cue), not resolved and met by no identity hook. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
3. **The framework wrote the message itself.** A message the framework writes
   into a room (a `deliver()`, an orchestration cue: Section 10.4) names no
   correspondent. There is no address to resolve, and the kit's identity
   hooks would challenge the host's own delivery like a stranger's message
   and block it.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 3: the sender of the framework's own message, kept as system whatever record of the room that name would find. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It stays under the sender `system`, whatever record of the
   room that name would find: case 2 does not apply to it.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 3: how an implementation knows the framework's own message, and a caller's message under the sender system, which is resolved. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation
   knows such a message by where it comes from, never by the sender `system`
   it carries, which any caller can write: a message a caller sends under
   that name, in a room it names, is resolved like any other, an instruction
   included (Section 10.1.1).

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 3: how an application whose kit runs identity hooks sends its own instructions; only the application keeps it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An application whose kit runs identity hooks
   sends its own instructions with `deliver()`.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 1: a channel that reads its sender_id off the wire, which does not declare case 1. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Case 1 is not the conference alone. The test is where the `sender_id` comes
from. A channel that reads it off the wire carries whatever the remote network
put there, and is not this case.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 1: a channel the implementation itself names the sender of (an interactive terminal), which declares case 1. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel the implementation itself names the
sender of — an interactive terminal, whose sender is a Participant the
implementation chose rather than a party that reached it from outside — is the
same case as the conference, and declares it for the same reason.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 1: a channel whose sender_id the integrator supplies, which does not declare case 1, its resolution left to configuration (§11.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A channel
whose `sender_id` is supplied by the integrator is neither: it may carry an
address or it may not, which is why Section 11.4 leaves that one to
configuration rather than to the channel.

requirements.applies: §11.6 case 2: a PENDING or AMBIGUOUS participant, still resolved (the next paragraph says why skipping an identified one matters). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`PENDING` and `AMBIGUOUS` participants are deliberately not in case 2: a
participant the room *has* is not a participant the room has *identified*, a
resolver may still be what settles it, and the identity hooks of Section 11.2
may still want to challenge or refuse it.

This is not an optimisation. Re-resolving a sender the room has already
identified produces UNKNOWN — no resolver matches a framework identifier — so
`ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN` fires per message, and the refusal pattern Section 11.2
provides for (`reject`) then blocks every message from a participant the
implementation itself identified. Skipping it is what keeps that pattern
composable with channels that name their own participants.

requirements.applies: §11.6 A sender resolution skips: the event's participant_id, and no participant record created or modified. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When resolution is skipped, the event's `participant_id` MUST be left as the
channel set it, but in case 2 for an event the sender's own record (Section
11.2) names, which is sent under that record's id as their events were while
it was pending; and no
participant record is created or modified: the sender is either already a
participant, deliberately unattributed, or the framework itself.

requirements.applies: §11.7 Identity verification, where an implementation supports it: the senders it applies to, IDENTIFIED ones only (the paragraph's other sentences say what verification is, and what §11.7.1 to §11.7.7 give the implementation and leave to the integrator). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Identification says whose an address is; **verification** says the person
writing has proven it. A number that resolves to Alice says the phone is
Alice's, not that Alice is typing. A service that answers account questions
over a channel needs both. An implementation that supports verification
carries the state, its lifecycle, a label on every message and the hooks;
the integrator keeps the **method** (how a person proves who they are: a
page behind a link, a code, a login) and the **policy** (what a message from
an unverified sender may reach). Verification applies to an IDENTIFIED
sender only; an identification challenge (§11.2) is another matter.

requirements.applies: §11.7.1 Verification: its fields. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
Verification
├── identity_id: string
├── organization_id: string | null         # Its scope (§11.7.7)
├── status: VerificationStatus             # §5
├── method: string | null                  # The integrator's name for it ("link", "code", "sso")
├── verified_via: string | null            # Channel the completing request was opened on
├── verified_at: datetime | null
├── expires_at: datetime | null
├── ended_reason: string | null            # "expired", "revoked", "failed" once ended
├── request_id: string | null              # The request open for the identity
└── completed_request_id: string | null    # The request that completed it: its end is
                                           # announced in that request's room
```

requirements.applies: §11.7.1: a verification held by the identity, on every channel and in every room its addresses reach, and its verified_via. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A verification belongs to the **identity**: once verified, the person is
verified on every channel and in every room their addresses reach, and
`verified_via` tells where they proved it, for an integrator that requires a
channel of its own.

requirements.applies: §11.7.1: an identity with no verification record. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: An identity with no record is UNVERIFIED.

requirements.applies: §11.7.2 VerificationRequest: its fields. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
```
VerificationRequest
├── id: string                             # Public reference
├── identity_id, room_id, channel_id: string
├── organization_id: string | null         # The room's
├── method: string                         # "link", "code", or the integrator's
├── secret_hash: string                     # The secret is never stored in clear
├── window_start: datetime                 # Reception of the message that opened it
├── created_at: datetime
├── expires_at: datetime
├── attempts: int                          # Failed attempts so far
├── max_attempts: int                      # The policy's bound when it was opened
└── status: OPEN | COMPLETED | FAILED | EXPIRED | CANCELLED
```

requirements.applies: §11.7.2 request_verification: the request it opens, returned with its secret once, the secret's hash alone kept. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`request_verification(identity_id, room_id, channel_id, method, window_start)`
opens a request and returns it with its secret, once: the integrator puts the
secret in its link or sends it as a code, and the implementation keeps only
its hash.

requirements.applies: §11.7.2: a request's lifetime and attempts, from the configured policy. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Its lifetime and attempts come from the configured policy.

requirements.applies: §11.7.2: a request's organization, its room's, and a caller acting for another organization. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
request takes its room's organization, the scope whose messages it verifies;
a caller acting for another organization is refused as for the room itself
(§17.2).

requirements.applies: §11.7.2: the identity's verification status once a request is opened, unverified or already verified. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An identity that is not verified becomes PENDING; one already verified
stays VERIFIED meanwhile (asking again does not end a verification in force).

requirements.applies: §11.7.2: the identity's earlier open request, when a request is opened. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Opening a request cancels the identity's earlier open one.

requirements.applies: §11.7.2 complete_verification: the secret compared in constant time, and a request that is not OPEN or has expired. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
`complete_verification(request_id, secret,
method)` is called by the integrator once its own check passed (the page's
PIN, the login); it compares the secret in constant time and refuses a
request that is not OPEN or has expired.

requirements.applies: §11.7.2: a wrong secret and a failure of the integrator's own check (record_failed_attempt), each an attempt on the request's bound. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A mismatch counts as an attempt, and
so does a failure of the integrator's own check, which it reports with
`record_failed_attempt(request_id)` (a wrong PIN on its page): the bound is
the request's, so a PIN cannot be guessed through the integrator's page.

requirements.applies: §11.7.2: a request at the policy's bound on attempts, which fails, and the verification in force it ends. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
At
the policy's bound the request FAILS, and a request that fails while the
identity is VERIFIED ends that verification too: whoever could not prove it
is not let on as the person (fail closed).

requirements.applies: §11.7.2: a request that expires unanswered. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A request that expires unanswered
changes nothing.

requirements.applies: §11.7.2: a completion: the identity VERIFIED until now + ttl, verification_completed and ON_VERIFICATION_COMPLETED (ASYNC). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A completion makes the identity
VERIFIED until `now + ttl`, emits `verification_completed` and fires
ON_VERIFICATION_COMPLETED (ASYNC).

requirements.applies: §11.7.3, where verification is configured: source.verification, stamped on every event of an identified sender (§10.1 step 5b). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The inbound pipeline stamps `source.verification` on every event of an
identified sender (§10.1 step 5b), so a hook, a router, a user interface and
a context builder read one fact.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3: the identified sender a label is for, and an identity's id arriving through a channel it was never resolved on. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An identified sender is the identity the
pipeline resolved for the event, or the IDENTIFIED participant the event's id
names on its channel (Section 5.5): an identity's id arriving through a
channel it was never resolved on carries no verification.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3: ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED (SYNC), fired on every event of an identified sender who is not VERIFIED, its hooks deciding per message. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
While the
identity is not VERIFIED, every such event fires ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED
(SYNC), whose hooks decide per message:

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, hold, the default when no hook passes: the event stored and delivered marked held, its scope narrowed to the transport channels it reached, read by no intelligence channel. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **hold** (the default when no hook passes it): the event is stored and
  delivered marked held, its scope narrowed to the transport channels it
  reached — those both its own visibility and its source binding's include
  (§7.3) — so the room's people and transports (an advisor's console) see
  it and no intelligence channel reads it, in delivery or in context.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 hold: what a held message reached, never widened. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Holding never widens what a message reached.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 hold: the mark roomkit:verification_held and what it carries. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The mark is the event's
  metadata `roomkit:verification_held`: `{visibility, identity_id,
  organization_id}`, the scope it was committed with, which its release
  restores, and whose message it is;

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, pass: the event going on as the hooks left it, labelled. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **pass**: the event goes on as the hooks left it, labelled — where an
  integrator lets a general question through.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 pass: a hook that passes a message explicitly, and a hook that merely allows it or fails (past its timeout among them), whose message is held. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A hook passes a message
  explicitly, its result's metadata `roomkit:verification` set to `pass`
  (`HookResult.allow_unverified()`); a hook that merely allows it (as one
  that only watches does) does not, nor does a hook that fails, one past
  its timeout among them: the trigger fails open (§9.3), and the message
  is held;

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, block: the message refused before anything of it is stored. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- **block**: the message is refused with the hook's reason,
  `verification_required` when it gives none, before anything of it is
  stored: no record, no delivery.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 Where the policy holds: an edit or a deletion (§10.3) from an unverified sender. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Where the policy holds, an edit or a deletion (§10.3) from an unverified
sender is refused `verification_required` unless a hook passes it, nothing
of it stored: held, it would still change a message the agents read.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3: the ASYNC hooks of ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, which observe the message the chain let through. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
trigger's ASYNC hooks observe the message the chain let through, never a
blocked one.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3: labelling and holding where the integrator configured verification, and a configuration that labels without holding (the integrator's choice, which the implementation honours). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Labelling and holding apply where the integrator configured verification;
a configuration MAY label without holding.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3: opening a request and telling the sender, the hook's, and the method, the integrator's; only the integrator keeps it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Opening a request and telling
the sender (sending the link, the code) is the hook's: the method is the
integrator's.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 sender_verification(event, context): what it reads of the sender's verification, in the room's organization. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The hook reads the sender's verification with
`sender_verification(event, context)`: whose it is, in the room's
organization, and whether a request is open.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3 sender_verification on a sender's first message, before they are a participant of the room (the paragraph's last sentence is advice to a hook that opens requests). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It answers on the sender's
first message too, when the sender is not a participant of the room yet. A
hook that opens a request only when none is open leaves a sender who writes
again meanwhile in silence; reminding them means opening a new request, since
a secret is never kept to be sent again.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3: the hold mark, the runtime's: one a sender's message carries, removed by the inbound pipeline, and the events ever released. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The mark of a held event is the runtime's: the inbound pipeline removes one
that a sender's message carries, and only an event the pipeline held and
labelled not VERIFIED is ever released (§11.7.6).

requirements.applies: §11.7.3: a hold mark copied any other way than by the pipeline's hold. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A mark copied by any other
way releases nothing.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3, speech-to-speech (media feature realtime): a speech-to-speech session (§12.4), in which nothing is labelled or held. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Labelling and holding act on messages. In a speech-to-speech session
(§12.4) the model hears the person before any message exists, and their
transcript is recorded afterwards: nothing there is labelled or held, and
holding a transcript would not keep the words from the model.

requirements.applies: §11.7.3, speech-to-speech (media feature realtime): how an integrator that requires verification gates a session; only the integrator keeps it (the last sentence restates that the implementation holds nothing there). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An integrator
that requires verification gates the session itself: it starts the session,
or gives it the instructions and tools that reach an account, only once
`verification_of` reads VERIFIED for the identity in the room's
organization, and on ON_VERIFICATION_ENDED it ends or reconfigures the
session. The implementation does not claim to hold anything there.

requirements.applies: §11.7.4 The code method: a message from the request's identity, in its room, whose whole text has the code's form, attempted and consumed (the opening sentence says what a code is). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
With the method `code`, the secret is a short code the person replies with in
the conversation. A message from the request's identity, in its room, whose
whole text has the code's form (the policy's code length of characters
Unicode gives a digit value, the whitespace around them left out) is an
attempt and is consumed (§10.1 step 5b): the call is refused `verification_code`, its text is never stored nor
broadcast, no agent reads it, and the attempt is recorded by the framework
events alone.

requirements.applies: §11.7.4: a wrong code, an attempt consumed all the same. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A wrong code counts as an attempt and is consumed all the
same.

requirements.applies: §11.7.4: a code's attempt and what its completion runs (§11.7.6), free of the call's pre-commit deadline (§13.6), and a caller that stops waiting. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The attempt is a write: neither it nor what a completion runs (§11.7.6)
carries the call's pre-commit deadline (§13.6), which bounds step 5b's read
of the sender's verification and its hooks alone, and a caller that stops
waiting cuts neither.

requirements.applies: §11.7.4: any other message, digits with no code request open or a code sent in another room, an ordinary one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Any other message is an ordinary one: digits with no
code request open, or a code sent in another room.

requirements.applies: §11.7.4: a code request's time and attempts, bounded tightly. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A code is short, so its
request's time and attempts MUST be bounded tightly.

requirements.applies: §11.7.5: the ends of a verification, expired and revoked (revoke_verification), and the ends of a request. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A verification ends when its time runs out (EXPIRED) or when the integrator
revokes it (`revoke_verification(identity_id, reason)`, REVOKED); a request
ends when it fails, expires or is cancelled.

requirements.applies: §11.7.5: each end's verification_ended and ON_VERIFICATION_ENDED (ASYNC), with its reason and what ended, when it happens: a timer at expires_at, and check_verifications() when the implementation starts. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Each end emits
`verification_ended` and fires ON_VERIFICATION_ENDED (ASYNC) with the reason
and what ended (`ended`: `verification` when the verification in force ended —
expired, revoked, or a request that failed while it held — `request` when a
request alone did, the identity's verification as it was), **when it
happens**, not on the sender's next message: the implementation
arms a timer at `expires_at`, and when it starts it ends the verifications
whose time passed while nothing ran and re-arms the timers of the others,
from the store (`check_verifications()`).

requirements.applies: §11.7.5: after an end, a new request a policy opens at once (the integrator's choice, which the implementation honours), else ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED on the sender's next message. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A policy MAY open a new request at
once; otherwise the sender's next message meets ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: the messages a completed request releases to the room's intelligence channels, unless the policy says otherwise, within its bounds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When a request completes, the messages its sender wrote while it was open
are released to the room's intelligence channels, unless the policy says
otherwise: the held events of that room whose sender is the identity,
received from `window_start` to the completion, never released before and
not deleted since (a deleted message is no longer said, §10.3), within the
policy's bounds of number and age, the latest by index when more qualify.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: only a message the pipeline itself held, released; a mark a sender's message carries releases nothing. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Only a message the pipeline itself held is released: its hold mark is the
pipeline's own (§11.7.3), and a mark a sender's message carries releases
nothing.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a released event's visibility restored (update_event), the budget of its ON_EVENT_UPDATED hooks, and the answer the last released event alone solicits. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Releasing an event restores the visibility it had before it was held
(`update_event`), its ON_EVENT_UPDATED hooks running on the budget of the
work the release is made in (§9.5.1, §10.3), and the room's intelligence
channels act on it as on any inbound message of its author: nothing is
copied, and the last released event alone solicits an answer, the earlier
ones being its context.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a released event handed to the intelligence channels alone, never again to a transport. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The event is handed to the intelligence channels
alone, never again to a transport, and nothing of its first delivery runs
again.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a completion's release within its call, a code reply's before the reply returns, outside its pre-commit budget (§13.6). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A completion releases within its call: a code reply's (§11.7.4)
before the reply's call returns, outside its pre-commit budget, so the reply
returns `verification_code` once the answer is in, however long the answer
took (§13.6).

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a code reply made with defer_delivery, its attempt, release and answer the kit's own work. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A reply made with `defer_delivery` is the exception: its call
returns once the reply is known for one, and the attempt, the release and
the answer go on as the kit's own work, which its close ends as the rest of
it (§12.10.4), a failure of theirs logged, with no handle; the held message's
key still names the answer (§10.1, *Explicit delivery cancellation*).

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: the deferred work of a code reply, made apart from the call and never under a lock its caller holds. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
deferred work is made apart from the call, never under a lock its caller
holds: a deferred reply sent from a hook's locked section has its released
message answered after that hook's work is delivered.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a completion made under the room's lock, from a hook: the answer's place in the room's lane. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A completion made under
the room's lock, from a hook, places the answer in the room's lane at the
release, ahead of that work's own delivery, and the answer leaves its place
once that work is over, on the room as that work left it: a hook that
completes the request and lets its event through has the released message
answered first, and one that then closes the room has no agent answer it.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: the released event's answer, a regeneration (§13.6): process_timeout, a room closed or deleted while it waits in the lane, and a failed read of the room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The
answer is a regeneration of the released event (§13.6): `process_timeout`
bounds its wait for the room's lock (`process_timeout` with
`operation = regenerate`), and a room closed or deleted while it waited in the
lane refuses it before any agent runs (`room_refused_event`,
`operation = regenerate`, its `status` null for a room deleted, §8.2); a read
of the room that fails there runs no agent either, the failure recorded as the
regeneration's error.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a held message whose delivery was cancelled (§10.1, Explicit delivery cancellation), released with no answer. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A held message whose delivery was cancelled (§10.1, *Explicit delivery
cancellation*), before its commit, while it was delivered or while it waited
for its release, is released all the same and solicits no answer: when it is
the last released, no agent answers the release, and the earlier ones are
not answered in its place, since their answer would read the cancelled
message as context.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a held message's cancellation, recorded with the event and honoured by a release in any process, and a cancellation by key. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The cancellation is recorded with the held event, so a
release in any process honours it; a cancellation by key reaches the held
messages of the process that received them.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: how long a held message's key names it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The key names the held message
from its call's decision on, a message the room's own work adopted (a hook's
call into its room, §9.5.1) as any, so a release during the message's own
delivery set names its answer too; a message nothing will release, blocked after it
was held or held under a policy that releases nothing, is named no longer
than its call.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a completion handle (§10.1 step 18) and a held message. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A completion handle (§10.1, step 18) follows the delivery set
alone: it cancels a held message while that set runs, and past it the key is
what names the message.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: a released message, read by an agent as its author's own turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A released message MUST reach an agent as its **author's own turn**, never as
an instruction or anything else carrying the application's authority: a
message an unverified sender wrote, quoted or not, gains none by its author
proving who they are.

requirements.applies: §11.7.6: nothing outside the request's window released. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Nothing outside the window is released: what was
written before the request — before a verification was revoked, during a
request that failed — may not be the verified person's.

requirements.applies: §11.7.7 Security floor: the entropy of a secret carried in a link, and a code request's short life and few attempts. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A secret carried in a link has at least 128 bits of entropy; a code is
  short, so its request is short-lived and allows few attempts.

requirements.applies: §11.7.7: a secret stored only as its hash, compared in constant time, used once and never logged. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A secret is stored only as its hash, compared in constant time, used once,
  and never logged.

requirements.applies: §11.7.7: a completion after the request expired, failed, was cancelled or completed, and after the verification was revoked. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A completion is refused after the request expired, failed, was cancelled
  or completed, and after the verification was revoked.

requirements.applies: §11.7.7: each verification transition's framework event (§8). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: - Every transition emits its framework event (§8), the audit trail.

requirements.applies: §11.7.7: a method with no check of its own, which should guard nothing that matters; only the integrator, whose method it is, keeps it (the item's first sentence says a link is a bearer secret). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- A link is a bearer secret: forwarded, it verifies whoever opens it and
  passes the method's own check. That check (a PIN, a login) is the
  method's; a method with none SHOULD NOT guard anything that matters.

requirements.applies: §11.7.7: a request's bound on attempts, held under the lock key verification:<organization>:<identity> (§13.5): two attempts at its last one. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A request's bound on attempts holds within the reach of the lock manager the
implementation serializes an identity's transitions with (§13.5), under the
key `verification:<organization>:<identity>`: two attempts at a request's
last one count once.

requirements.applies: §11.7.7: a deployment of several processes on one store, which shares its lock manager; only the deployment keeps it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A deployment of several processes on one store shares
its lock manager, as it must for its rooms.

requirements.applies: §11.7.7: verification state, scoped to the organization (§17.2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: Verification state is scoped to the organization as identities are (§17.2).

requirements.applies: §11.7.7: the verification a message is labelled by, its room's organization's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A message is labelled by the verification of its **room's** organization:
one proven to an organization never verifies the person in another
organization's conversation, whatever the organization the resolver's
identity names.

requirements.applies: §12.1 Architecture Overview; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
RoomKit supports four real-time media architectures:

```
Architecture 1: STT/TTS Pipeline (VoiceChannel)
┌──────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────┐     ┌─────┐     ┌──────────┐
│ Client   │────→│Audio Pipeline│────→│   STT    │────→│Room │────→│   TTS    │────→ Client
│ (audio)  │     │(denoise/VAD/ │     │Provider  │     │Kit  │     │Provider  │
└──────────┘     │ diarization) │     └──────────┘     └─────┘     └──────────┘
                 └──────────────┘

Architecture 2: Speech-to-Speech (RealtimeVoiceChannel)
┌──────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────────┐     ┌──────────┐
│ Client   │────→│Audio Pipeline│────→│ Speech-to-Speech API     │────→│ Client   │
│ (audio)  │     │  (optional)  │     │ (OpenAI Realtime, etc.)  │     │ (audio)  │
└──────────┘     └──────────────┘     └────────────┬─────────────┘     └──────────┘
                  denoise, diarize                  │
                                              transcriptions
                                              tool calls
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                               ┌─────────┐
                                               │ RoomKit │
                                               │ (events)│
                                               └─────────┘
```

requirements.applies: §12.1 Architecture Overview; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
**Choosing between architectures:**

| Criterion | VoiceChannel (STT/TTS) | RealtimeVoiceChannel (Speech-to-Speech) | VoiceChannel (Bridge) | ConferenceChannel (SFU) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Latency** | Moderate (~500-800ms TTFA with streaming) | Lower — end-to-end streaming | Lowest — direct audio forwarding | Low — SFU forwards media directly between clients |
| **Control** | Full — choose STT, LLM, TTS | Limited — provider bundles all; with reasoning delegation (Section 12.4.1) the reasoning model is the integrator's | Full pipeline, no AI required | Control plane only — media plane is external |
| **Text access** | Always — utterances become RoomEvents | Optional — if transcription configured | Optional — if STT configured | Per-track STT, attributed per participant |
| **Multi-channel** | Native — text routes to any channel | Requires transcription | Requires STT for text routing | Native — transcripts are RoomEvents |
| **AI involvement** | Required (generates responses) | Required (speech-to-speech) | Optional (observer/monitor) | Optional (bot participant) |
| **Voice quality** | Depends on TTS provider | Native speech generation | Original voice preserved | Original voice preserved |
| **Pipeline control** | Full audio pipeline (all stages) | Pipeline optional | Full pipeline (all stages) | Per-track inbound lanes (no AEC/diarization) |
| **Use when** | AI voice agent with text in the loop | Lowest latency AI with native voice | Human-to-human calls, conferencing, call center | Multi-party video conferences, AI in meetings |

All four architectures MAY coexist in the same room. For example, a room could
have a VoiceChannel for a human participant (PSTN/SIP) and a RealtimeVoiceChannel
for the AI agent, with text events bridging them. Or two VoiceChannels in bridge
mode for a human-to-human call with optional AI observation.

```
Architecture 3: Audio Bridge (VoiceChannel with bridge=True)
┌──────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────┐
│ Client A │────→│Audio Pipeline│────→│ Audio Bridge  │────→│Audio Pipeline│────→│ Client B │
│ (audio)  │     │  (inbound)   │     │ (forward/mix) │     │  (outbound)  │     │ (audio)  │
└──────────┘     └──────────────┘     └───────┬───────┘     └──────────────┘     └──────────┘
                                              │
                                         (optional)
                                       STT transcription
                                              │
                                              ▼
                                         ┌─────────┐
                                         │ RoomKit │
                                         │ (events)│
                                         └─────────┘
```

```
Architecture 4: SFU Conference (ConferenceChannel — Section 12.10)
┌──────────┐           ┌─────────────────┐           ┌──────────┐
│ Client A │◄─────────►│                 │◄─────────►│ Client B │
│ (browser)│   media   │  External SFU   │   media   │ (browser)│
└──────────┘           │  (media plane)  │           └──────────┘
                       └────────┬────────┘
                                │ bot participant
```
