requirements.applies: §15.8 Audit System; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
RoomKit provides a two-tier auditing architecture for compliance, debugging,
and monitoring: **tool auditing** captures individual tool calls, and
**session auditing** captures the full conversation timeline.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): every tool call recorded with its input, output, timing and status, as a ToolAuditEntry with its members; the result's 500-character cut is the wrapper's step 4. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Tool auditing records every tool call with input, output, timing, and status.

**ToolAuditEntry:**

```
ToolAuditEntry
├── ts: string                              # RFC 3339 time, in UTC (§1.4)
├── agent_id: string                        # Which agent made the call
├── tool_name: string                       # Tool function name
├── arguments: map<string, any>             # Input arguments
├── result: string                          # Tool output (truncated to 500 chars)
├── status: string                          # "ok", "failed", "error" or "cancelled"
├── duration_ms: float                      # Execution time in milliseconds
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Optional extra data
```

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): status detection: "error" when the tool handler raises an exception; with the list's lead-in. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Status detection:**
- `"error"` — set when the tool handler raises an exception.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): "cancelled" when the call was cancelled before its handler answered: its turn or session ended, or the provider abandoned it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `"cancelled"` — set when the call was cancelled before its handler answered
  (its turn or session ended, the provider abandoned it).

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): a cancelled call is never recorded "ok", and its cancellation still reaches the caller. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A cancelled call
  MUST NOT be recorded as `"ok"`, and the cancellation still reaches the
  caller.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): a call the channel's per-call bound cut short (§21.6) reaches a wrapped handler as a cancellation and is recorded "cancelled", its duration the bound, while the channel reports it failed. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A call the channel's per-call bound cut short (Section 21.6)
  reaches a wrapped handler as a cancellation and is recorded `"cancelled"`
  as well, its duration the bound; the channel reports it as failed.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): "failed" stated structurally: a refusal (ToolRefusedError), a failure stated in the handler's words (ToolFailedError, an MCP isError result) or a call declined as not the handler's own (§21.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `"failed"`, structurally — set when the handler refused the call
  (`ToolRefusedError`), stated its failure in its own words
  (`ToolFailedError`, an MCP `isError` result: the structured form of the
  envelope below, which reads `"failed"` too) or declined it as not its own
  (Section 21.4).

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): "failed" read from the result body, inspected for every failure envelope the implementation itself emits: {"status": "failed"}, the {"error": ...} envelope of a refused call and of a wrapped MCP isError result, and {"success": false}. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `"failed"`, from the body — read from the result body, which MUST be inspected for every
  failure envelope the implementation itself emits, not for one convention
  only: `{"status": "failed"}`, the `{"error": ...}` envelope a refused call
  and a wrapped MCP `isError` result return, and the `{"success": false}`
  convention hosts commonly use. Recognising one shape and not the others
  records a denied tool — the outcome an audit exists for — as `"ok"`.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): "ok", the default, what a body outside every envelope reads as. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
- `"ok"` — the default, and a degradation rather than a contract: it is what a
  body outside every envelope reads as.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): a producer of a tool call's outcome that can state it structurally does so (§9.3) instead of relying on the body's reading. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A producer that can state its outcome
  structurally SHOULD do so (Section 9.3) instead of relying on this reading.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the ToolAuditor interface: record, entries, summary and print_summary. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ToolAuditor** (interface):

```
ToolAuditor (interface)
├── record(entry: ToolAuditEntry) → void    # Record a tool execution
├── entries: list<ToolAuditEntry> (property) # All recorded entries
├── summary() → string                     # Human-readable summary
└── print_summary() → void                 # Log summary via logger
```

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the built-in JSONL tool auditor, which appends one JSON line per call and keeps its entries in memory; with the table's lead-in and header. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Built-in implementations:**

| Implementation | Persistence | Description |
|---|---|---|
| JSONLToolAuditor | JSONL file | Appends one JSON line per call; maintains in-memory list |
|

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the built-in console tool auditor, which logs each entry as it is recorded (the text names Python's logging module). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: ConsoleToolAuditor | Logger | Real-time logging via Python logging module |

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): audit_tool_handler(handler, auditor, agent_id) wraps any tool handler to record its audit entries, measuring its execution time (step 1); with the wrapper's lead-in. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Handler wrapper:**

The `audit_tool_handler(handler, auditor, agent_id)` function wraps any tool
handler to automatically record audit entries. It:

1. Measures execution time.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the wrapper records a raised exception "error", a refusal, a stated failure or a declined call "failed" and a cancelled call "cancelled", then re-raises each, so that the channel reads the outcome it would read without it (step 2). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
2. Records a raised exception as `"error"`, a refusal, a stated failure
   (`ToolFailedError`) or a declined call as `"failed"` and a cancelled call
   as `"cancelled"`, then re-raises each, so
   the channel reads the outcome it would have read without the wrapper.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the wrapper otherwise detects "failed" from the response body (step 3). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: 3. Auto-detects `"failed"` from the response body otherwise.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the wrapper cuts the recorded result to 500 characters (step 4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: 4. Truncates the recorded result to 500 characters.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the wrapper returns the handler's result unchanged, the same object, so that content parts and structured values reach the channel as the handler gave them (step 5). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
5. Returns the original handler result unchanged: the same object, never a
   printed copy of it, so content parts and structured values reach the
   channel as the handler gave them.

requirements.applies: §15.8.1 Tool Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): an integrator may implement a ToolAuditor backend of its own by implementing the interface, the integrator's choice the wrapper honours (the text names two vendors as examples). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Integrators MAY implement custom `ToolAuditor` backends (e.g., Datadog,
Elasticsearch) by implementing the interface.

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the SessionAuditEntry and its members; with the sentence naming what session auditing captures, each kind a row of the type table. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Session auditing captures the full conversation timeline: speech turns, tool
calls, vision events, interruptions, and session lifecycle.

**SessionAuditEntry:**

```
SessionAuditEntry
├── ts: string                              # RFC 3339 time, in UTC (§1.4)
├── type: string                            # Event type (see below)
├── role: string | null                     # "user", "assistant", or "system"
├── content: string                         # Text, transcription, or description
├── duration_ms: float | null               # For timed events (tool calls)
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Extra data (tool_name, args, status, etc.)
```

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it), with voice (Level 3, §26.4): the speech entry, user or assistant, recorded on ON_TRANSCRIPTION, its content the transcribed speech; with the table's lead-in and header. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Session audit event types:**

| Type | Role | Trigger | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| speech | user/assistant | ON_TRANSCRIPTION hook | Transcribed speech text |
|

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the tool_call entry, assistant, recorded by record_tool, its content the tool's result. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
tool_call | assistant | Manual `record_tool()` | Tool result |
|

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it), with video (Level 3, §26.4): the vision entry, system, recorded on ON_VISION_RESULT, its content the frame's description. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
vision | system | ON_VISION_RESULT hook | Frame description |
|

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it), with voice (Level 3, §26.4): the barge_in entry, user, recorded on ON_BARGE_IN, its content "User interrupted". Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
barge_in | user | ON_BARGE_IN hook | "User interrupted" |
|

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the session entry, system, recorded on ON_SESSION_STARTED, its content "Session started". Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
session | system | ON_SESSION_STARTED hook | "Session started" |
|

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the error entry, system, which the application records, its content the error message. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: error | system | Application-specific | Error message |

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the SessionAuditor interface: record, entries, summary, print_summary, the record_tool and tool_auditor bridge to tool auditing, and attach. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**SessionAuditor** (interface):

```
SessionAuditor (interface)
├── record(entry: SessionAuditEntry) → void
├── entries: list<SessionAuditEntry> (property)
├── summary() → string
├── print_summary() → void
│
│   # ToolAuditor compatibility bridge:
├── record_tool(entry: ToolAuditEntry) → void  # Convert tool entry to session entry
├── tool_auditor: ToolAuditor (property)        # Bridge adapter
│
│   # Hook auto-registration:
└── attach(kit: RoomKit) → void                # Register hooks for automatic capture
```

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): attach(kit) registers hooks for ON_TRANSCRIPTION, ON_BARGE_IN, ON_SESSION_STARTED and ON_VISION_RESULT that capture the conversation's events; all but ON_SESSION_STARTED are voice and video triggers (Level 3, §26.4). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Hook auto-registration:** When `attach(kit)` is called, the session auditor
registers hooks for `ON_TRANSCRIPTION`, `ON_BARGE_IN`, `ON_SESSION_STARTED`,
and `ON_VISION_RESULT` to capture conversation events automatically.

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the tool_auditor property's bridge turns ToolAuditEntry records into SessionAuditEntry records, so that one SessionAuditor holds tool calls and conversation events in one timeline. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**ToolAuditor bridge:** The `tool_auditor` property returns a bridge adapter
that converts `ToolAuditEntry` records into `SessionAuditEntry` records. This
allows a single `SessionAuditor` to capture both tool calls and conversation
events in a unified timeline.

requirements.applies: §15.8.2 Session Auditing, where an implementation offers it (no level of §26 lists it): the built-in JSONL session auditor, which writes its entries to a JSONL file and keeps them in memory in chronological order. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Built-in implementation:** `JSONLSessionAuditor` — writes entries to a JSONL
file and maintains an in-memory chronological list.

requirements.applies: §15.8.3 Audit Data Format, where an implementation offers tool or session auditing: both auditors persist as JSONL, one independently parseable JSON object per line; with the example lines. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.

§15.8.3 Audit Data Format, where an implementation offers tool or session auditing: the JSONL files are append-only, an entry added after those already written. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: JSONL files are append-only.

requirements.applies: §15.8.3 Audit Data Format, where an implementation offers tool or session auditing: the auditor creates its file's parent directories. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Implementations MUST create parent directories
automatically.

requirements.applies: §15.8.3 Audit Data Format, where an implementation offers tool or session auditing: a write error is logged and never propagated to the caller as an exception. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Write errors MUST be logged but MUST NOT propagate exceptions
to the caller.

requirements.applies: §15.9 Feedback: an implementation may let a host record how a room, or one of its responses, was rated, through submit_feedback with this signature. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
An implementation MAY let a host record how a room, or one of its
responses, was rated:

```
submit_feedback(room_id, rating, event_id | null, channel_id | null,
                comment = "", dimension = "overall", metadata) → void
```

requirements.applies: §15.9 Feedback, where an implementation offers submit_feedback (§15.9 makes it a MAY): the rating is a number from 0.0 to 1.0, a value outside clamped. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text: The rating is a number from 0.0 to 1.0; a value outside is clamped.

requirements.applies: §15.9 Feedback, where an implementation offers submit_feedback (§15.9 makes it a MAY): the rating is recorded as an Observation of the room (§5.11): its channel_id the rated channel (empty when none is named), its category feedback:<dimension>, its confidence the rating, its content naming the dimension, the rating and the comment, and its metadata beside the caller's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It is
recorded as an Observation of the room (§5.11): its `channel_id` the rated
channel (empty when none is named), its `category` `feedback:<dimension>`,
its `confidence` the rating, its `content` a line naming the dimension, the
rating and the comment, and its metadata `type = "feedback"`, `dimension`,
`rating`, `comment` and `event_id`, beside the caller's `metadata`.

requirements.applies: §15.9 Feedback, where an implementation offers submit_feedback (§15.9 makes it a MAY): once the observation is stored, ON_FEEDBACK (ASYNC, §9.2) fires with it as its payload, and feedback is emitted (§8.2) with the room, the channel, the event, the dimension and the rating. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Once the
observation is stored, `ON_FEEDBACK` (ASYNC, §9.2) fires with it as its
payload, and `feedback` is emitted (§8.2) with the room, the channel, the
event, the dimension and the rating.

requirements.applies: §16 Integration Surfaces: the core depends on no specific web framework; the integration surfaces are thin wrappers that expose it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The RoomKit core MUST NOT depend on any specific web framework. Integration
surfaces are thin wrappers that expose core functionality.

requirements.applies: §16.1 REST API, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the room endpoints (create, get, update, delete, list by organization and status); with the lead-in: the host owns its HTTP surface, and an implementation that offers a REST API provides the endpoints below. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The framework is a library, and the host owns its HTTP surface. An
implementation that offers a REST API SHOULD provide the following endpoints:

**Rooms:**

```
POST   /rooms                                   # Create room
GET    /rooms/{id}                              # Get room
PATCH  /rooms/{id}                              # Update room
DELETE /rooms/{id}                              # Delete room
GET    /rooms?organization_id=X&status=active   # List rooms
```

requirements.applies: §16.1 REST API, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the channel endpoints (attach, detach, update a binding's access and visibility, mute, unmute, list a room's bindings, list the registered channels). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Channels:**

```
POST   /rooms/{id}/channels                     # Attach channel
DELETE /rooms/{id}/channels/{cid}               # Detach channel
PATCH  /rooms/{id}/channels/{cid}               # Update binding (access, visibility)
POST   /rooms/{id}/channels/{cid}/mute          # Mute channel
POST   /rooms/{id}/channels/{cid}/unmute        # Unmute channel
GET    /rooms/{id}/channels                     # List bindings
GET    /channels                                # List registered channels
```

requirements.applies: §16.1 REST API, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the event endpoints (inject an event, read the timeline with pagination and a visibility filter). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Events & Timeline:**

```
POST   /rooms/{id}/events                       # Inject event
GET    /rooms/{id}/timeline                     # Get timeline (supports pagination, visibility filter)
```

requirements.applies: §16.1 REST API, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the participant endpoints (add, remove, list, resolve a pending identity). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Participants:**

```
POST   /rooms/{id}/participants                 # Add participant
DELETE /rooms/{id}/participants/{pid}            # Remove participant
GET    /rooms/{id}/participants                 # List participants
POST   /rooms/{id}/participants/{pid}/resolve   # Resolve pending identity
```

requirements.applies: §16.1 REST API, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the task and observation endpoints (list a room's tasks, update a task's status, list a room's observations). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Tasks & Observations:**

```
GET    /rooms/{id}/tasks                        # List tasks for room
PATCH  /tasks/{id}                              # Update task status
GET    /rooms/{id}/observations                 # List observations for room
```

requirements.applies: §16.1 REST API, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the identity endpoints (create an identity, resolve one by channel and address, link a channel address to it). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Identity:**

```
POST   /identities                              # Create identity
GET    /identities/resolve?channel=sms&address=+1... # Resolve identity
POST   /identities/{id}/addresses               # Link a channel address to an identity
```

requirements.applies: §16.1 REST API, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the webhook endpoints (an inbound webhook and a delivery status webhook, by channel type and provider). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Webhooks:**

```
POST   /webhooks/{channel_type}/{provider}          # Inbound webhook
POST   /webhooks/{channel_type}/{provider}/status   # Delivery status webhook
```

requirements.applies: §16.1 REST API, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the WebSocket endpoint, a real-time room connection through the WebSocket channel (Appendix A.8). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**WebSocket:**

```
WS     /ws/{room_id}                            # Real-time room connection (WebSocket channel, Appendix A.8)
```

requirements.applies: §16.2 MCP Server, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the MCP tools, the table's eleven actions on rooms, tasks, observations, channels, room metadata and identities, and the escalation to a human; with the lead-in. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
For AI agents to interact with rooms natively via the Model Context Protocol:

**MCP Tools (actions):**

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| send_message | Send a message to a room |
| create_task | Create a task in a room |
| add_observation | Record an observation |
| attach_channel | Attach a channel to a room |
| detach_channel | Detach a channel |
| mute_channel | Mute a channel |
| unmute_channel | Unmute a channel |
| set_channel_visibility | Change visibility |
| update_room_metadata | Update room metadata |
| resolve_identity | Resolve an identity |
| escalate_to_human | Escalate to a human agent |

requirements.applies: §16.2 MCP Server, where an implementation offers one (OPTIONAL; Level 2, §26.3): the MCP resources, the table's six rows: a room's state, timeline, participants, channel bindings and tasks, and an identity's details. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**MCP Resources (data):**

| Resource | Description |
|---|---|
| room://{room_id} | Room state |
| room://{room_id}/timeline | Room timeline |
| room://{room_id}/participants | Room participants |
| room://{room_id}/channels | Room channel bindings |
| room://{room_id}/tasks | Room tasks |
| identity://{identity_id} | Identity details |

requirements.applies: §16.3 Surface Independence, where an implementation offers a REST API or an MCP server (§16.1, §16.2): both surfaces call the same core methods, and no business logic lives in them. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Both REST and MCP surfaces MUST call the same core methods. No business logic
should live in the integration surface layer.

requirements.applies: §17.1 Input Validation: every inbound payload validated before it is processed.
requirements.text: - All inbound payloads MUST be validated before processing.

requirements.applies: §17.1 Input Validation: a webhook's signature verified where its provider signs it.
requirements.text: - Webhook signatures SHOULD be verified when the provider supports them.

requirements.applies: §17.1 Input Validation: event content sanitized against injection.
requirements.text: - Event content SHOULD be sanitized to prevent injection attacks.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: room operations isolated per organization; with the item that scopes a room by its organization_id. The items below say how.
requirements.text:
- Rooms are scoped by `organization_id`.
- Implementations MUST ensure that room operations are isolated per organization.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: identity resolution scoped to the organization.
requirements.text: - Identity resolution MUST be scoped to the organization.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: a room the framework creates for another room's work (a delegation's child room, §23.3) belongs to that room's organization, or to none with it.
requirements.text:
- A room the framework creates for another room's work (a delegation's
  child room, Section 23.3) MUST belong to that room's organization.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers voice, realtime or conference (media): a door that admits a participant into a room's media (a framework join, a realtime session start, a conference mint_access()) reads the room with the caller's organization before any session exists or is bound and before any credential is minted; another organization's room is not found, joined, admitted to, or told of the session's tracks.
requirements.text:
- A door that admits a participant into a room's media (a framework join, a
  realtime channel's session start, a conference channel's `mint_access()`)
  MUST read the room with the organization the caller acts for, before any
  session exists or is bound and before any credential is minted: another
  organization's room is not found, no session joins it, no credential admits
  to it, and none of its recordings is told of the session's tracks.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers voice, realtime or conference (media): called without an organization, a framework join reads the room unscoped, and a session start or a mint reads none for the scope.
requirements.text:
Called
  without an organization, a framework join reads the room unscoped, and a
  session start or a mint reads none for the scope.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: a room's hooks, subscriptions and turns end with the room: the kit that creates a room under the id of a room the store deleted, for the same organization, another or none, forgets the deleted room's room hooks and enabled names and ends the subscriptions made through it to its ephemerals.
requirements.text:
- A room's hooks, its subscriptions and its turns end with the room
  (§8.4, §9.1, §10.6.2): the kit that creates a room under the id of a room
  the store deleted, for the same organization, another or none, forgets
  the room hooks registered for the deleted room and the names enabled for
  it, and ends the subscriptions made through it to the deleted room's
  ephemerals.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: nothing registered for one organization's room reads the events of the room another organization creates after it under its id.
requirements.text:
Nothing registered for one organization's room reads the
  events of the room another organization creates after it.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: hooks and subscriptions registered while no room held an id are the new room's.
requirements.text:
Hooks and
  subscriptions registered while no room held the id are the new room's.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: in every process, by the room's creation mark (created_at): a kit forgets for a later room the hooks and enabled names of an id (§9.1); a publication carries its room's mark and a subscription reads its own room's alone (§8.4); the owner keeps each turn record's mark, so a turn or a channel call in a room of another mark follows none of the earlier room's turns and an executor lets go of what it held (§10.6.2); a host verb made after a deleted room's turn is refused in the room created again (§10.6.5).
requirements.text:
So in every process: a kit keeps the creation mark (`created_at`) of the
  room its hooks and enabled names of an id are of, compares it with the
  room in hand when they fire, and forgets them for a later room (§9.1); a
  publication carries the mark of its room and a subscription reads its
  own room's alone (§8.4); the owner keeps the mark of the room each turn
  record is of, so that a turn or a channel call in a room of another mark
  follows none of the earlier room's turns and an executor lets go of what
  it held for the id (§10.6.2), and a host verb made after a deleted
  room's turn is refused in the room created again since (§10.6.5).

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: a call that names no organization (an inbound message, a direct injection) reads rooms unscoped, and a room it creates belongs to no organization.
requirements.text:
- A call that names no organization (an inbound message, a direct
  injection) reads rooms unscoped, and a room it creates belongs to no
  organization.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: a call acting for an organization reaches that organization's rooms only: a room of another organization, or of none, is not its own (§10.1 step 2), and a room it creates belongs to the organization.
requirements.text:
A call acting for an organization reaches that
  organization's rooms only: a room of another organization, or of none, is
  not its own (§10.1 step 2), and a room it creates belongs to the
  organization.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: every room operation names the organization it acts for, as a message does, among them the operations the item lists.
requirements.text:
- Every room operation names the organization it acts for, as a message does,
  among them a room's transitions (§5.1), a member's join, leave and rename
  and the reads of its roster (§5.5), a channel's attach, detach and binding
  changes (§7.5), an ephemeral's publication and a subscription to a room's
  ephemerals (§8.4), a room's read markers, marked and listed (§14.1), a
  room hook's registration, enabling, disabling and
  removal (§9.1, §10.6.6), an update or a delete of a stored event (§10.3), a
  direct injection and a record's commit (§10.5), a claim for a strategy
  (§19.7), a steer of a room's turns (§21.3), a delivery (§22), a delegation,
  a task the host starts and its cancel (§23.3, §23.4), a greeting, a
  regeneration of an answer and a feedback.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: against a room that is not the caller's, each room operation acts as on a room that does not exist: the listed calls fail as not found before any hook runs, anything is queued or drawn from a reentry budget, a turn starts or is steered, or a room is created; an update or a delete is a no-op that fires nothing; a task's cancel cancels nothing.
requirements.text:
Against a room that is not the
  caller's, each acts as it does on a room that does not exist: a transition,
  a membership change or read, an attach, a detach or a binding change, a
  publication or a subscription, a read marker marked or listed, a room
  hook's registration, enabling,
  disabling and removal, and a claim for a strategy, fail as not found, as
  do a message that names the room (§10.1 step 1), an injection, a record, a
  steer, a delivery, a delegation, a task, a greeting, a
  regeneration and a feedback, before any
  hook runs, anything is queued or drawn from a reentry budget, a turn starts
  or is steered, or a room is created; an update or a delete is a no-op that
  fires nothing, and a task's cancel cancels nothing.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: a call that takes the room lock checks the room's organization as the lock finds it, before its due timer transitions are applied, so it writes nothing in a room that is not the caller's, those transitions included; they fall due all the same, and the room's next own call or its timer check applies them at the instant each fell due (§5.1).
requirements.text:
A call that takes the
  room lock checks the room as the lock finds it, before its due timer
  transitions are applied, so nothing is written in it, those transitions
  included: they fall due all the same, and the room's next own call or the
  check of its timers applies them at the instant each fell due (§5.1).

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: a call that takes no lock (a delivery, a publication, a steer) checks the room's organization before its first effect, so it has none in a room that is not the caller's; a room's organization never changes while it exists, so that read holds.
requirements.text:
A call
  that takes no lock (a delivery, a publication, a steer) reads the room
  before its first effect; a room's organization never changes while it
  exists, so that read holds.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers a transport whose connection registry reads no room (the WebSocket channel, Appendix A.8): each connection held for the organization it was registered for, or for none.
requirements.text:
- A transport's connection registry that reads no room (a WebSocket channel's,
  Appendix A.8) holds each connection for the organization it was registered
  for, or for none.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers a transport whose connection registry reads no room (the WebSocket channel, Appendix A.8): a room of another organization, or of none, delivers nothing to a connection registered for one, whatever rooms it is subscribed to, streamed or not.
requirements.text:
A room of another organization, or of none, delivers
  nothing to a connection registered for one, whatever rooms it is subscribed
  to, streamed or not.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers a transport whose connection registry reads no room (the WebSocket channel, Appendix A.8): a stream under way sends only to the registrations present when it started, checked as each send starts: an id unregistered, evicted or registered again since gets nothing more of it, its end included.
requirements.text:
A stream under way sends only to the registrations
  present when it started, checked as each send starts: an id unregistered,
  evicted or registered again since, for any organization or the same one,
  gets nothing more of it, its end included, since a new registration never
  saw its start.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers a transport whose connection registry reads no room (the WebSocket channel, Appendix A.8): a call acting for an organization subscribes, unsubscribes, unregisters or registers again only a connection registered for that organization; one of another organization, one registered for none and one that does not exist are refused alike, nothing changed.
requirements.text:
A call acting for an organization subscribes, unsubscribes or
  unregisters only a connection registered for that organization, and
  registers again only such a connection: one of another organization, one
  registered for none and one that does not exist are refused alike, nothing
  changed.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers a transport whose connection registry reads no room (the WebSocket channel, Appendix A.8): a scoped registration of an id no connection holds succeeds; connection ids are one namespace across organizations, generated by the host, never chosen by a client.
requirements.text:
A scoped registration of an id no connection holds succeeds, which
  tells that the id is free: connection ids are one namespace across
  organizations, generated by the host and never chosen by a client.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers a transport whose connection registry reads no room (the WebSocket channel, Appendix A.8): a call that names no organization, the host's own, acts on any connection, and registering an id again without one registers it for none.
requirements.text:
A call
  that names no organization, the host's own, acts on any connection as
  before, and registering an id again without one registers it for none.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers a transport whose connection registry reads no room (the WebSocket channel, Appendix A.8): a registration that changes a known id's organization, to none included, drops the rooms the id followed; a connection evicted after repeated send failures is forgotten with its rooms and organization; a send failure of a registration gone counts against none.
requirements.text:
A
  registration that changes a known id's organization, to none included, drops
  the rooms the id followed, and a connection evicted after repeated send
  failures is forgotten with its rooms and its organization; a send failure of
  a registration gone counts against none.

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: by design, a call addressed by an identifier that works as a capability names no organization: answer_input() and reject_input() (a human-input request's id, §10.6.5) and unsubscribe_room() (a subscription's id, §8.4), holding the id being the authority; with the list's lead-in.
requirements.text:
- These calls name no organization, by design:
  - a call addressed by an identifier that works as a capability, issued to
    its holder: `answer_input()` and `reject_input()` (a human-input request's
    id, an unguessable random id, §10.6.5) and `unsubscribe_room()` (a
    subscription's id, §8.4): holding the id is the authority;

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: by design, a channel's own steering (AIChannel.steer()) and a turn client's (TurnClient.steer()) name no organization; given one, the turn client reaches only that organization's rooms' turns and answers 0 for the others; the kit's steer() is the door that reads a room.
requirements.text:
- a channel's own steering (`AIChannel.steer()`) and a turn client's
    (`TurnClient.steer()`): neither holds a store. Given an organization, the
    turn client reaches only the turns of that organization's rooms and
    answers 0 for the others: a turn it does not reach and one that does not
    run read alike. The kit's `steer()` is the door that reads a room;

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: by design, the trusted levels below the kit's calls hold no store, read no room and name no organization: a hook engine's add_room_hook(), remove_room_hook() and replace_room_hook(), a turn client's enable_room_hook() and disable_room_hook().
requirements.text:
- the trusted levels below the kit's calls, which hold no store and read no
    room: a hook engine's `add_room_hook()`, `remove_room_hook()` and
    `replace_room_hook()`, and a turn client's `enable_room_hook()` and
    `disable_room_hook()`;

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: by design, a strategy's install() called directly claims the room unscoped (claim_room_strategy()) and sets up its hooks with no organization; the kit's install_strategy() reads the room with the caller's organization first.
requirements.text:
- a strategy's `install()` called directly, which claims the room (through
    `claim_room_strategy()`, unscoped) and sets up its hooks with no
    organization: the kit's `install_strategy()` reads the room with the
    caller's organization first;

requirements.applies: §17.2 Multi-Tenant Isolation: where an implementation offers voice or video (media): by design, the deprecated connect_voice(), connect_video() and bind_voice_session() name no organization; join() replaces them with its organization.
requirements.text:
- the deprecated `connect_voice()`, `connect_video()` and
    `bind_voice_session()`, which `join()` replaces with its organization.

requirements.applies: §17.3 Sensitive Data: configurable redaction or encryption at rest of raw_payload; with the sentence that says it may hold sensitive data.
requirements.text:
- `raw_payload` MAY contain sensitive data. Implementations SHOULD support
  configurable redaction or encryption at rest.

requirements.applies: §17.3 Sensitive Data: hook-based scanning for personal data (e.g. SIN/SSN detection) so that it does not traverse channels; the integrator's hooks keep it.
requirements.text:
- Hook-based PII scanning (e.g., SIN/SSN detection) SHOULD be used to prevent
  sensitive data from traversing channels.

requirements.applies: §17.3 Sensitive Data: a blocked event stored for audit, its content handled according to the organization's data retention policy.
requirements.text:
- Blocked events are stored for audit but their content SHOULD be handled
  according to the organization's data retention policy.

requirements.applies: §17.4 Rate Limiting: per-organization rate limits; with the lead-in on per-channel rate limits, which §13.3 states.
requirements.text:
- Per-channel rate limits prevent abuse of external provider APIs.
- Implementations SHOULD support per-organization rate limits.

requirements.applies: §17.5 Chain Depth: the chain depth limit enforced, never allowed to be disabled, a discussion's own max_depth included (§19.7.5); with the lead-in on unbounded AI-to-AI loops.
requirements.text:
- The chain depth limit prevents resource exhaustion from unbounded AI ↔ AI loops.
- Implementations MUST enforce the limit and MUST NOT allow it to be disabled,
  a discussion's own `max_depth` included (Section 19.7.5).

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation supports audio recording (media: recording): a mechanism for recording consent management; with the paragraph's lead-in and its note on jurisdictions.
requirements.text:
**Recording consent and compliance:**

- Implementations that support audio recording MUST provide a mechanism for
  recording consent management. In many jurisdictions (TCPA, GDPR, PIPEDA),
  recording requires explicit consent from all parties.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation supports audio recording (media: recording): ON_RECORDING_STARTED fired before any audio is captured, so that integrators can notify participants.
requirements.text:
- The framework SHOULD fire ON_RECORDING_STARTED before any audio is captured,
  giving integrators the opportunity to notify participants.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation supports audio recording (media: recording): configurable consent modes SINGLE_PARTY, ALL_PARTY and NONE.
requirements.text:
- Implementations SHOULD support configurable consent modes: `SINGLE_PARTY`
  (one party consents), `ALL_PARTY` (all parties must consent), or `NONE`
  (integrator manages consent externally).

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation supports audio recording (media: recording): audio recordings encrypted at rest; with the paragraph's lead-in.
requirements.text:
**Audio data handling:**

- Audio recordings MUST be encrypted at rest.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation supports audio recording (media: recording): configurable encryption for stored recordings.
requirements.text:
Implementations MUST support
  configurable encryption for stored recordings.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation records audio or video (media: recording): every recording configuration carries the encryption settings (encryption, storage_encrypted_at_rest; Sections 12.3.7, 12.8.10, 12.10.8, 12.11).

§17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation records audio or video (media: recording): the audio recorder, the room media recorder and conference recording fail closed when neither encryption setting is set, a recording of video alone included; the session video recorder applies them when they are set.
requirements.text:
The audio recorder (Section
  12.3.7), the room media recorder (Section 12.11) and conference recording
  (Section 12.10.8) fail closed when neither is set, a recording of video
  alone included; the session video recorder (Section 12.8.10) applies them
  when they are set.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): audio streams in transit carried over an encrypted transport (TLS, SRTP, DTLS); shown by the transports an implementation offers and a deployment uses, not by a scenario.
requirements.text: - Audio streams in transit SHOULD use encrypted transport (TLS, SRTP, DTLS).

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): documentation of the providers that receive audio data, and the integrator's choice of provider configurable for data residency requirements; with the sentence that says STT and TTS calls send audio out.
requirements.text:
- STT and TTS provider calls transmit audio to external services.
  Implementations SHOULD document which providers receive audio data and
  SHOULD support configurable provider selection based on data residency
  requirements.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): voice session metadata (transcripts, recordings, DTMF digits) under the same data retention and redaction policies as other room events.
requirements.text:
- Voice session metadata (transcripts, recordings, DTMF digits) MUST follow
  the same data retention and redaction policies as other room events.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, TTS conversation context (Section 12.2.2), where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): context audio, a copy of the session's dialogue audio, kept in memory only: never written to the conversation store, the timeline, a recording, or a log; with the paragraph's lead-in.
requirements.text:
**TTS conversation context (Section 12.2.2):**

- Context audio is a copy of the session's dialogue audio (what the user said and
  what was synthesized), held so the TTS can hear it.
  It MUST be kept in memory only: never written to the conversation store, the
  timeline, a recording, or a log.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, TTS conversation context (Section 12.2.2), where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): context audio stays within max_turns and max_audio_seconds, and is dropped when the session is unbound or ends, with the call to release_context.
requirements.text:
- It MUST stay within `max_turns` and `max_audio_seconds`, and MUST be dropped
  when the session is unbound or ends, together with the call to
  `release_context`.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, TTS conversation context (Section 12.2.2), where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): keeping audio is opt-in (include_audio = false by default).
requirements.text: - Keeping audio MUST be opt-in (`include_audio = false` by default).

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, TTS conversation context (Section 12.2.2), where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): the context's text is the transcript already stored as room events, under the same policies.
requirements.text:
The text
  of the context is the transcript already stored as room events, and is under
  the same policies.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, TTS conversation context (Section 12.2.2), where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): a user turn whose transcript a hook modified keeps no audio.
requirements.text: - A user turn whose transcript a hook modified MUST NOT keep its audio.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, TTS conversation context (Section 12.2.2), where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): with DTMF redaction enabled, a user turn during which DTMF was detected keeps no audio.
requirements.text:
When
  DTMF redaction is enabled, a user turn during which DTMF was detected MUST
  NOT keep its audio either: in-band tones carry the digits.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, TTS conversation context (Section 12.2.2), where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): the documentation of the providers that receive audio says that one at level AUDIO run as an external service receives the user's voice on every call; with the sentence that says so.
requirements.text:
- A provider at level `AUDIO` that runs as an external service receives the
  user's voice on every call, not only the current sentence. Implementations
  SHOULD say so where they document which providers receive audio data.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, custom voices (Section 12.2.4), where an implementation offers them (media: voice): the recording of a voice made to replicate it and the recording of its consent are handed to the vendor for the call and kept nowhere: never written to the conversation store, the timeline, a recording, or a log; with the paragraph's lead-in and the sentence that calls them personal data.
requirements.text:
**Custom voices (Section 12.2.4):**

- A recording of a person's voice made to replicate it, and the recording of
  their consent, are personal data identifying that person. An implementation
  MUST hand them to the vendor for the call and keep nothing: never written to
  the conversation store, the timeline, a recording, or a log.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, custom voices (Section 12.2.4), where an implementation offers them (media: voice): what is kept is the integrator's evidence, as metadata: which voice was created, when, by whom, and whether the vendor verified the consent.
requirements.text:
What it keeps is
  the evidence the integrator needs, as metadata: which voice was created,
  when, by whom, and whether the vendor verified the consent.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, custom voices (Section 12.2.4), where an implementation offers them (media: voice): replicating a voice without the consent of the person it belongs to is not possible through the framework (Section 12.2.4).
requirements.text:
- Replicating a voice without the consent of the person it belongs to MUST NOT
  be possible through the framework (Section 12.2.4).

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, custom voices (Section 12.2.4), where an implementation offers them (media: voice): the integrator's responsibility for that consent and its withdrawal, a withdrawn consent meaning deleting the voice.
requirements.text:
The integrator remains
  responsible for that consent, and for its withdrawal: a withdrawn consent
  means deleting the voice.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, custom voices (Section 12.2.4), where an implementation offers them (media: voice): documentation of where a stored custom voice lives and for how long; with the sentence that says the vendor holds it under the integrator's account.
requirements.text:
- A stored custom voice is held by the vendor under the integrator's account.
  Implementations SHOULD document where it lives and for how long, as they do
  for the providers that receive audio.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, provenance of synthesized audio, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): a provenance mark received from the vendor (a C2PA manifest in the file, a watermark in the signal) is not removed: a file is passed on as produced, not rebuilt from its samples; with the paragraph's lead-in and the vendor's permission to mark.
requirements.text:
**Provenance of synthesized audio:**

- A vendor MAY mark the audio it synthesizes: a manifest in the file (C2PA)
  or a watermark in the signal. An implementation MUST NOT remove a mark it
  received: a file is passed on as the vendor produced it, not rebuilt from
  its samples.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, provenance of synthesized audio, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): documentation of where a stage that must decode the audio (resampling, mixing, encoding for a transport) loses a file-level manifest.

§17.6 Voice and Audio Security, DTMF sensitivity, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): configurable DTMF redaction, masking DTMF digits in stored events and logs; with the paragraph's lead-in and the sentence on sensitive digits.
requirements.text:
**DTMF sensitivity:**

- DTMF digits MAY contain sensitive data (credit card numbers, PINs, account
  numbers). Implementations MUST support configurable DTMF redaction — the
  ability to mask DTMF digits in stored events and logs (e.g., replacing
  "4111111111111111" with "4111********1111").

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, DTMF sensitivity, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): with DTMF redaction enabled, raw digits appear in no raw_payload, transcript or log output.
requirements.text:
- When DTMF redaction is enabled, raw digits MUST NOT appear in `raw_payload`,
  transcripts, or log output.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, voice model privacy, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): audio recordings and transcripts used for no model training without explicit integrator and end-user consent; the vendors' terms and the integrator's account keep it, the framework trains no model; with the paragraph's lead-in.
requirements.text:
**Voice model privacy:**

- Audio recordings and transcripts MUST NOT be used for model training without
  explicit integrator and end-user consent.

requirements.applies: §17.6 Voice and Audio Security, voice model privacy, where an implementation offers voice (media: voice): a configuration flag that disables any data sharing with STT, TTS and speech-to-speech providers beyond what the API call requires.
requirements.text:
- Implementations SHOULD provide a configuration flag to disable any data
  sharing with STT/TTS/speech-to-speech providers beyond what is required for
  the API call.

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): tokens minted per participant with least-privilege grants (hidden observers subscribe-only); with the lead-in that calls them credentials.
requirements.text:
ConferenceAccess tokens are credentials:

- Tokens SHOULD be minted per participant with least-privilege grants
  (e.g., hidden observers receive subscribe-only grants).

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): ConferenceGrants defaults to permissive values; narrowing them per participant is the integrator's call, RECOMMENDED to the integrator wherever a role does not publish.
requirements.text:
ConferenceGrants
  (Section 12.10.2) defaults to permissive values so that the common case
  works unconfigured; narrowing them for a given participant is the
  integrator's call, and is RECOMMENDED wherever a role does not need to
  publish.

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): tokens short-lived (expires_at, SHOULD) and never logged (MUST NOT).
requirements.text: - Tokens SHOULD be short-lived (`expires_at`) and MUST NOT be logged.

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): moderation operations (remove_participant, mute_track, unmute_track) reachable only through integrator-controlled code paths, never exposed unauthenticated; a review of the surfaces an implementation exposes.
requirements.text:
- Moderation operations (`remove_participant`, `mute_track`,
  `unmute_track`) MUST only be reachable through integrator-controlled code
  paths, never exposed unauthenticated.

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): the bot's presence, identity and hidden status observable to integrator code, as in force on the session, not as configured or admitted; with the paragraph that leaves disclosure to the jurisdiction.
requirements.text:
**Bot disclosure.** Whether a recording or transcribing bot must be
announced to human participants — and how — is set by the jurisdiction the
deployment operates in, and those rules differ by country and by sector.
This specification therefore mandates no disclosure behaviour and no
restriction on `hidden` observers (Section 12.10.6). It requires instead
that the framework give the integrator what it needs to comply with
whatever applies to it:

- The bot's presence, its `identity`, and its `hidden` status MUST be
  observable to integrator code — the status in force *on the session*,
  not the one it was configured or admitted with: grants can change
  while a session runs (Section 12.10.4), and a surface reporting the
  construction answers a different question than the one a disclosure
  obligation asks.

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): whether STT, vision or recording is active on a conference observable at any time, not only at configuration time.
requirements.text:
- Whether STT, vision, or recording is active on a conference MUST be
  observable at any time, not only at configuration time.

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): ON_CONFERENCE_PARTICIPANT_JOINED fired for every human participant the backend delivered.
requirements.text:
- `ON_CONFERENCE_PARTICIPANT_JOINED` MUST fire for every human participant
  the backend delivered, giving the integrator the point at which to
  announce an active bot, gate entry on consent, or record that disclosure
  was made.

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): across a reported discontinuity (Section 12.10.3), an integrator whose obligations require complete attendance treats the outage window as unaccounted, not as observed and empty; the integrator's to keep.
requirements.text:
Across a *reported discontinuity* (Section 12.10.3) that
  guarantee cannot reach the participants whose whole presence fell inside
  the outage window: the discontinuity is the signal that the window is
  unaccounted, and an integrator whose obligations require complete
  attendance MUST treat it so rather than as observed-and-empty.

requirements.applies: §17.7 Conference Access Security, where an implementation offers conference (media: conference): documentation of the integrator's disclosure responsibility rather than an assumed default; with the closing note on regulated sectors.
requirements.text:
Implementations SHOULD document this responsibility rather than assume a
default. Deployments in regulated sectors typically do need visible bot
identification; the specification's role is to make that implementable, not
to decide it.

requirements.applies: §17.8 Skill-Bundled Files: a skill file's resolution confined to the skill's own directory by resolving the path and checking containment, never by filtering the name alone (Section 24.6); with the item that makes every such read or execution an untrusted-input boundary.
requirements.text:
- A skill's references and scripts are addressed by a name the model chooses,
  which makes every such read or execution an untrusted-input boundary.
- Resolution MUST be confined to the skill's own directory by resolving the
  path and checking containment, never by filtering the name alone
  (Section 24.6).

requirements.applies: §17.8 Skill-Bundled Files: a file so checked read through the file its check opened, never by its name again, and a skill's SKILL.md resolving to a regular file inside the skill's directory (Section 24.6).
requirements.text:
- A file so checked MUST be read through the file its check opened, never by
  its name again, and a skill's `SKILL.md` MUST resolve to a regular file
  inside the skill's directory (Section 24.6).

requirements.applies: §17.8 Skill-Bundled Files: the same containment applied to script execution, including where execution policy is delegated to the integrator.
requirements.text:
- The same containment MUST apply to script execution, including where
  execution policy is delegated to the integrator.
