requirements.applies: §18 Design Principles; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
These principles define the conceptual architecture of RoomKit:

1. **The Room is the truth.** All state lives in the Room. The timeline records
   everything.

2. **Everything is a Channel.** SMS, browser, AI, observer — same interface.
   No special cases.

3. **Primitives, not opinions.** The framework provides access, mute, and
   visibility. Business logic decides when to use them.

4. **Two output paths.** Room events are subject to permissions. Side effects
   always flow. Muting silences the voice, not the brain.

5. **Providers are swappable.** Channel type ≠ provider. Twilio and Sinch both
   provide SMS. Anthropic and OpenAI both provide AI.

6. **Hooks intercept.** Sync hooks block and modify. Async hooks observe and
   react. Pipeline architecture.

7. **Channels are dynamic.** Attach, detach, mute, unmute, reconfigure at any
   time during a conversation.

8. **Channel awareness at generation.** AI knows target constraints and media
   types before generating — not after.

9. **Three layers of metadata.** Channel.info (instance), ChannelBinding.metadata
   (per-room), RoomEvent.channel_data (per-event). Never lose data.

10. **Direction declares capability.** Channels declare inbound/outbound/bidirectional.
    Permissions restrict per room.

11. **Two event levels.** Room events (per-room, stored) and framework events
    (global, for subscribers).

12. **Media types are first-class.** Text, audio, video — route to compatible
    channels. Ready for the future.

13. **Chain depth safety.** Event chains are bounded by a configurable depth
    limit. Uses existing blocked mechanism — no new concepts.

14. **Voice is a channel.** Real-time voice follows the same Room/Channel/Event
    model. STT/TTS are providers. No special "voice API."

15. **Sources complement webhooks.** Persistent connections (WhatsApp Personal,
    SSE) push events. Webhooks deliver per-message callbacks. Both feed the same
    inbound pipeline.

16. **Framework-agnostic core.** No web framework dependency. Integration surfaces
    are thin wrappers. Any language, any framework.

17. **Audio pipeline is transport-independent.** Resampler, AEC, AGC, denoiser,
    VAD, diarization, DTMF, turn detection, and recording run as a pluggable
    pipeline between transport and conversation engine. The transport delivers
    raw frames. The pipeline processes them. Stages are optional and composable.
    Same pattern as text hooks: preprocessing inbound, postprocessing outbound.

18. **Video pipeline mirrors audio.** Decoder, resizer, transforms, filters,
    overlays, vision, and recording run as a pluggable pipeline between the
    video transport and the conversation engine. Same stage pattern as audio:
    pluggable providers, optional stages, session-scoped state. Vision results
    feed back into AI channels and filter contexts.

19. **Agents are channels.** Multi-agent orchestration uses the same
    Room/Channel/Event model. Agents are intelligence channels with identity
    metadata. Routing, handoff, and coordination happen through existing
    primitives — no special agent API.

20. **Orchestration through primitives.** Multi-agent routing, handoff, and
    state management are built on existing Room/Channel/Event/Hook primitives.
    The router is a BEFORE_BROADCAST hook. State lives in room metadata.
    Handoffs are tool calls. No new core abstractions required.

21. **Memory is pluggable.** AI context construction is a swappable strategy,
    not a hardcoded sliding window. Implementations choose how to build
    conversation history: recent events, summarized history, vector retrieval,
    or token-budget-aware truncation.

22. **Audit is two-tiered.** Tool auditing captures every tool call (input,
    output, timing, status). Session auditing captures the full conversation
    timeline (speech, tools, vision, interruptions). Both use pluggable
    backends — same extensibility pattern as providers and stores.

23. **The conference media plane is external.** RoomKit orchestrates
    conferences — rooms, access, participant lifecycle, AI participation —
    but never forwards media between human participants. An external SFU
    owns packet routing; RoomKit joins it as one participant among many.
    Same boundary as storage: the framework defines the interface, the
    deployment provides the infrastructure.

requirements.applies: §19 Multi-Agent Orchestration; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
Multi-agent orchestration enables multiple AI agents to collaborate within a
single room. Agents are intelligence channels with identity metadata. Routing,
handoff, and state management use existing Room/Channel/Event primitives.

requirements.applies: An Agent is an AI intelligence channel with structured identity, including its role, description and scope.
requirements.text:
An **Agent** is an AIChannel subclass with structured identity:

```
Agent (extends AIChannel)
├── role: string | null                     # "Senior Engineer", "Triage Agent"
├── description: string | null              # Agent capabilities description
├── scope: string | null                    # "Backend systems", "Billing"
```

requirements.applies: Voice feature: an agent can specify a TTS voice identifier.
requirements.text:
```
├── voice: string | null                    # TTS voice identifier
```

requirements.applies: Greeting and language are optional agent identity fields.
requirements.text:
```
├── greeting: string | null                 # Auto-greeting text on session start
├── language: string | null                 # Preferred language
```

requirements.applies: The Agent's automatic session greeting is enabled by default.
requirements.text:
```
├── auto_greet: bool (default true)         # Greet on a session's start
```

requirements.applies: The agent renders its identity in prompts by default.
requirements.text:
```
├── identity_in_prompt: bool (default true) # false: the host renders identity itself
│
```

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the read-only configuration-only flag identifies an agent without an AI provider.
requirements.text:
```
├── is_config_only: bool (read-only)        # True when no AI provider (speech-to-speech mode)
```

requirements.applies: The agent exposes a language-aware identity block builder.
requirements.text:
```
└── build_identity_block(language) → string # Generate identity context for system prompt
```

requirements.applies: The identity block is appended to an agent's system prompt on its turns.
requirements.text:
The identity block is appended to the agent's system prompt wherever RoomKit
writes one: its turns,

requirements.applies: A handoff language change appends the identity block to the agent prompt.
requirements.text: a handoff's language change,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the pipeline session prompt includes the agent's identity block.
requirements.text:
a realtime pipeline's
sessions.

requirements.applies: Turning off identity rendering suppresses the block everywhere and preserves the agent's orchestration identity.
requirements.text:
An agent built with `identity_in_prompt` false writes it nowhere
(`build_identity_block` returns nothing), its fields kept for orchestration.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a configuration-only speech-to-speech agent accepts a null model provider and makes no generation calls.
requirements.text:
When `is_config_only` is true, the Agent has no AI provider and serves as a
configuration container for speech-to-speech channels (voice, greeting, language
metadata). A null provider MUST be accepted — no generation calls are made.

requirements.applies: Hosts may attach more than one agent to the same room.
requirements.text: Multiple Agents MAY be attached to a single room.

requirements.applies: Orchestration selects the agent for each event, subject to explicit addressing.
requirements.text:
The orchestration system
determines which Agent handles each event, unless the event names its
recipients itself (§19.3).

requirements.applies: The greeting API selects an identity-bearing agent by agent ID, then channel ID, then room binding order.
requirements.text:
**The greeting.** `send_greeting(room_id, channel_id?, agent_id?, greeting?,
organization_id?)` says an agent's greeting in a room. The agent is the one
`agent_id`, then `channel_id`, names when it is an intelligence channel with an
identity, else the first such channel the room binds;

requirements.applies: An explicit greeting takes precedence over the selected agent's configured words.
requirements.text:
the words are `greeting`,
else the agent's.

requirements.applies: A greeting with no agent or no words has no effect.
requirements.text: With no agent or no words nothing happens.

requirements.applies: A greeting scoped to an organization first checks the room and reports an inaccessible room as not found.
requirements.text:
With an
`organization_id`, the room is read first, and one it does not reach is not
found (§17.2).

requirements.applies: A text greeting is a delivered outbound AI message from the agent carrying auto_greeting metadata.
requirements.text:
With no voice or realtime session, the greeting is a MESSAGE from the agent,
OUTBOUND, of channel type AI, DELIVERED, its metadata `auto_greeting: true`.

requirements.applies: The text greeting is committed under the room lock after applying due room timers.
requirements.text:
It
is committed under the room lock, the room's due timers applied (§5.1);

requirements.applies: Missing rooms and rooms refusing events take no greeting and cause no failure on the ordinary commit path.
requirements.text:
a room
missing, or whose status refuses events, takes nothing and fails no one.

requirements.applies: A greeting bypasses the before-broadcast hook and the check of the source's right to write.
requirements.text:
It is
committed by a path of its own (§7.5 rule 2): no BEFORE_BROADCAST hook runs for
it and its source's right to write is not checked.

requirements.applies: The greeting inherits the agent binding's visibility restriction.
requirements.text:
Its visibility is narrowed
by its agent's binding (§7.3).

requirements.applies: Text greeting delivery uses the room lane, admits chained agent answers and runs the after-broadcast hook.
requirements.text:
It is delivered on the room's lane (§10.2), the
other agents' answers re-entering, and AFTER_BROADCAST observes it;

requirements.applies: A greeting from a bound agent that lacks write access is stored with no recipients.
requirements.text:
an agent
that cannot write has it stored and delivered to no one,

requirements.applies: An unbound agent's greeting is stored without a delivery set or after-broadcast observation.
requirements.text:
and one the room does
not bind has it stored with no delivery set and no AFTER_BROADCAST.

requirements.applies: A text greeting produces neither delivery reports nor an event_processed notification.
requirements.text:
Its
deliveries are not reported and no `event_processed` follows it (§8.2): it
entered neither through the inbound pipeline nor by direct injection.

requirements.applies: A stream answering a greeting follows chained-stream rules.
requirements.text:
A stream
that answers it is a chained stream (§8.3).

requirements.applies: A greeting waits for delivery outside the room lock and lane, returning at commit from the lock or lane.
requirements.text:
The call returns once its delivery
is over; made under the room's lock or from its lane, at its commit.

requirements.applies: A greeting from a hook or room delivery inherits its depth and shares the work's reentry budget with responses.
requirements.text:
Made in the room's own work, a hook's body or a delivery, a greeting is that
work's write, as a direct injection is (§9.5.1, §8.3): at the work's depth, and
drawing a pass, or a hook call from an ASYNC hook's body, on the work's budget,
which what answers it draws on too;

requirements.applies: A greeting beyond the work's budget is stored blocked with reentry_loop_cap and is not delivered.
requirements.text:
past the budget it is stored BLOCKED
`reentry_loop_cap`, with no delivery, so that a hook greeting on every answer,
or on its own greeting, stops at the limit.

requirements.applies: An external greeting starts at depth zero with its own budget.
requirements.text:
A call made outside the room's work
has a budget of its own, at depth 0.

requirements.applies: An agent with auto_greet and a greeting uses a named ON_SESSION_STARTED hook which the starting message waits for.
Unregistering an agent removes its automatic greeting hook.
requirements.text:
it goes
when the Agent is unregistered.

requirements.applies: The agent greets a bound room once and may greet at a later start if first encountered unbound.
requirements.text:
It greets a room once, and only one that binds
it: a room it was not bound to at a session's start may be greeted at the next.

requirements.applies: Implementations may bound the per-agent set of previously greeted rooms.
requirements.text: An implementation MAY bound what it remembers

requirements.applies: When the reference bound is used, an agent tracks 10,000 rooms and drops the oldest tenth on overflow.
requirements.text:
(the reference keeps 10 000 rooms
per Agent, dropping the oldest tenth when full).

requirements.applies: A text session does not gate on greeting delivery beyond the initiating message's process timeout.
requirements.text:
No greeting gate holds a text
session: another agent that reads the greeting and answers it delays the message
only within the message's `process_timeout`.

requirements.applies: Voice feature: the voice greeting gate delays agent deliveries until the greeting is said.
requirements.text:
A voice session's greeting is said
behind a gate the agents' deliveries wait for,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the session greeting is injected as the model's own turn.
requirements.text:
and a realtime session's is
injected as the model's own turn (§12.4).

requirements.applies: Room metadata can hold a ConversationState with phase, active agent, human hold, language and custom metadata.
requirements.text:
Each room MAY have a `ConversationState` stored in room metadata:

```
ConversationState
├── phase: string | null                    # Current conversation phase ("triage", "specialist")
├── active_agent_id: string | null          # Agent currently handling the conversation
├── human_hold: bool                        # Held for a human (Section 19.6)
├── language: string | null                 # Detected participant language
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Custom state (intent, escalation level, etc.)
```

requirements.applies: A transition of the room phase requires a handoff or an explicit programmatic update.
requirements.text: Phase transitions MUST be explicit — either via handoff or programmatic update.

requirements.applies: A state transition dispatches the ON_PHASE_TRANSITION hook.
requirements.text: The framework fires `ON_PHASE_TRANSITION` hooks on state changes.

requirements.applies: The host may set a room's active agent independently of a handoff.
requirements.text:
`active_agent_id` MAY be written by the host, not only by a handoff: a
console that switches which agent it is talking to is a legitimate writer of
this field.

requirements.applies: A supported public setter for a room's active agent is recommended.
requirements.text:
Implementations SHOULD expose a supported way to set it —
reaching into room metadata from application code is not one.

requirements.applies: An event sender may set addressed_to to a list of channel identifiers; null denotes an unaddressed event.
requirements.text:
Routing rules answer *which agent handles this kind of event*. Addressing
answers a different question, asked per message by whoever sends it:
**which agents are being asked to act, right now**. A room where a human
types `@reviewer check hello.py` needs the second question, and no rule
expresses it.

An event MAY carry an address:

```
RoomEvent
└── addressed_to: list<channel_id> | null    # null = unaddressed
```

requirements.applies: An explicit intelligence address never removes visibility that a channel otherwise has.
requirements.text:
**Addressing is not visibility.** Visibility (§7.3) is configured on a
binding, narrowed by an event's own, and answers who may *see* what a source
produces. Addressing is set on an event by its sender and answers who is
*asked to act*. The two are orthogonal: addressing one agent MUST NOT hide
the event from any channel visibility would have shown it to.

Normative rules:

requirements.applies: Addressing leaves deliveries to the room's transport channels unaffected.
requirements.text:
1. Addressing constrains **intelligence** channels only. Delivery to
   transport channels MUST NOT be affected — a message addressed to one
   agent still reaches the humans in the room.

requirements.applies: A non-null address solicits only the named intelligence channels.
requirements.text:
2. When `addressed_to` is non-null, the channels it names are the only
   intelligence channels solicited for that event.

requirements.applies: Unbound channel identifiers in an address are ignored, including when no bound intelligence recipient remains.
requirements.text:
Named ids not bound to
   the room are ignored; if none of them is bound, no intelligence channel
   is solicited.

requirements.applies: An empty address solicits no agent while preserving storage and transport delivery.
requirements.text:
3. An empty list addresses nobody: the event is stored and delivered, and no
   agent is asked to respond.

requirements.applies: The stored event retains the address that transcripts and replays use to reproduce solicitation.
requirements.text:
4. `addressed_to` is part of the stored event, so a transcript can show who
   was asked and a replay reproduces the same solicitation (in a discussion,
   the same queued turns, Section 19.7.5).

requirements.applies: An event injected by a hook solicits no intelligence channel and reaches only its transport targets irrespective of address.
requirements.text:
5. An event a hook injects (Section 9.4) solicits no intelligence channel,
   whatever its address: it is delivered to its transport targets only,

requirements.applies: A visible injected event is available to an agent reading its history on its next turn.
requirements.text:
and
   an agent its visibility names reads it in its history at its next turn.

requirements.applies: A router selects recipients for unaddressed events; absent a router every eligible intelligence channel is solicited.
requirements.text:
**Unaddressed events** (`addressed_to = null`) keep the behaviour of earlier
versions: the router decides (§19.4), and with no router installed every
eligible intelligence channel is solicited.

requirements.applies: An installed discussion determines the solicitation of unaddressed events.
requirements.text:
A discussion decides instead
(Section 19.7.5, rule 8).

requirements.applies: A discussion queues only the explicitly addressed agents and solicits each on its turn, one at a time.
requirements.text:
A discussion (Section 19.7.5) defers the solicitation an address asks for to
the addressed agent's turn: the channels the address names are still the only
ones asked to act, later, one at a time. It MUST NOT solicit a channel the
address does not name.

requirements.applies: Proactive text delivery preserves the intelligence address through publication.
requirements.text:
Proactive `RoomKit.deliver()` calls carry the same intelligence address through
the text publication pipeline (§22.1).

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: choosing a target transport session does not address an intelligence channel.
requirements.text:
A realtime session target is a separate
transport selection, not an intelligence address.

requirements.applies: At Level 0 every event has the addressing field and an explicit address must be honored; Level 2 adds router precedence and response policies.
requirements.text:
**Conformance.** Addressing itself is Level 0 — the field exists on every
event and MUST be honoured when set, which an implementation without
intelligence channels satisfies trivially. The router precedence (§19.4,
step 0) and the named policies below belong to Level 2 with the rest of this
section.

requirements.applies: By default an agent's output solicits the other eligible agents within the maximum chain depth.
requirements.text:
An agent's own output is an event like any other, and by default it solicits
the other agents in the room — the chaining Appendix B.4 describes, bounded
by `max_chain_depth`. That is a feature for a pipeline (analyst → writer)
and a hazard for a room of independent agents, where two agents answer each
other until the depth limit stops them.

requirements.applies: The room can select either of the two agent response policies.
requirements.text:
Implementations MUST provide both policies (`AgentResponsePolicy`), selectable
per room through the room's `agent_response_policy`:

| Policy | An agent's output solicits |
|---|---|
|

requirements.applies: Under AGENT_CHAIN an agent output solicits every eligible intelligence channel unless explicitly addressed.
requirements.text:
`AGENT_CHAIN` | every eligible intelligence channel — the behaviour of earlier versions |
|

requirements.applies: Under ADDRESSED_ONLY an agent output solicits only the intelligence channels it explicitly names.
requirements.text: `ADDRESSED_ONLY` | only the channels named in `addressed_to`, if any |

requirements.applies: AGENT_CHAIN is the default in a room without an explicit response policy.
requirements.text:
`AGENT_CHAIN` MUST remain the default, so a room written against an earlier
version behaves unchanged.

requirements.applies: Under both response policies an explicit agent address solicits the named agents alone.
requirements.text:
Under either policy an explicit address is
honoured: an agent MAY address another agent and be answered by it alone.

requirements.applies: A discussion translates written agent mentions in its agent's output into the event address.
requirements.text:
Section 19.7.5 is how: under a discussion, the `@` names an agent writes
become its event's address.

requirements.applies: The response policy is mutable on an existing room.
requirements.text:
Per room means *for the life of the room*, not at its creation only. A room
rarely knows when it is created how many agents it will end up holding: one
that opens with a single assistant and gains a second when a human asks for
it becomes a room of independent agents at that moment, and the policy it
needs changes with it. Implementations MUST therefore allow the policy to be
set on an existing room (`set_agent_response_policy(room_id, policy)`:

requirements.applies: The response-policy setter serializes its write under the room lock and returns the room.
requirements.text: written under the room lock and the room returned,

requirements.applies: The response-policy setter reports a missing room or another organization's room as not found.
requirements.text:
a missing room, or
another organization's, not found,

requirements.applies: Setting an already effective response policy leaves the room unchanged.
requirements.text:
a room holding the policy already left
as it is).

requirements.applies: A response-policy change acts on subsequent events without reopening a prior broadcast or its deferred discussion turn.
requirements.text:
A change applies to events processed after it; an
event already broadcast is not reconsidered, because solicitation was
decided when it was routed and reopening it would ask an agent to act on a
turn that has already closed. A discussion's deferred turn (Section 19.7.5)
reopens nothing: it carries out, later, a solicitation decided when the event
was routed.

requirements.applies: An unsolicited intelligence channel is neither delivered the event nor asked to respond.
requirements.text:
A channel that is not solicited MUST NOT be asked to produce a response, and
MUST NOT be delivered the event either — the implementation skips it. At
§10.2 step 3c the two are one decision, not two.

Skipping alone would not settle the question, because the cost is not the
same for every channel. An agent whose context is rebuilt from the room's
timeline on every turn loses nothing by being skipped. An agent that owns
conversational state outside RoomKit — an ACP coding agent holding a session
in its own process — permanently lacks whatever it was not delivered. Left
there, a room of such agents is not a shared conversation but a bundle of
private threads, and nothing in the transcript says so: asked what was said
earlier, an agent answers from the only history it has, in good faith, about
something else.

requirements.applies: The room timeline must be available to a solicited channel to rebuild missed context.
requirements.text:
The counterpart is therefore normative. An implementation MUST make the
room's timeline available to a channel at the moment it *is* solicited, so a
channel that keeps its own state can rebuild what it missed instead of
diverging from the room.

requirements.applies: The rebuilt timeline is filtered for the reader using the same visibility boundary as delivery.
requirements.text:
That rebuilt history is subject to §7.5 rule 8
without exception: it is filtered per reader, and a channel MUST NOT obtain
through it an event visibility withheld from it at delivery. Catching up is
not a second door into the room.

requirements.applies: Implementations may bound the context supplied to a solicited channel.
requirements.text:
The rebuild MAY be bounded — by a count of events, by a token budget, by
whatever the channel can carry.

requirements.applies: When a rebuilt timeline is bounded, the channel should learn it is partial and how much is missing.
requirements.text:
When it is, the channel SHOULD be told that
what it received is partial, and how much is missing. A bound the reader
cannot see reproduces the same silent divergence one layer down: an agent
that knows its history was truncated can say so, or ask for the rest; an
agent that believes it holds the whole room cannot.

Nothing here obliges a channel to read the timeline. An implementation whose
channels all rebuild their context from storage each turn satisfies this
section by construction — which is why the requirement is that the timeline
be *available*, not that it be consumed.

**Conformance.** Level 2, with the rest of §19.3.

requirements.applies: The conversation router selects event recipients via a synchronous before-broadcast hook.
requirements.text:
The `ConversationRouter` selects which Agent processes each event. It is
installed as a `BEFORE_BROADCAST` sync hook.

requirements.applies: The router accepts ordered rules, an optional default agent and optional supervisor.
requirements.text:
```
ConversationRouter
├── rules: list<RoutingRule>                # Ordered by priority
├── default_agent_id: string | null         # Fallback when no rule matches
└── supervisor_id: string | null            # Always receives events (if set)
```

requirements.applies: A routing rule has a target agent, conditions and an integer priority.
requirements.text:
**RoutingRule:**

```
RoutingRule
├── agent_id: string                        # Target agent
├── conditions: RoutingConditions           # When this rule applies
```

requirements.applies: A routing rule defaults to priority zero, with lower numbers evaluated first.
requirements.text:
```
└── priority: int (default 0)               # Lower = evaluated first
```

requirements.applies: A routing rule may match the room's current conversation phase.
requirements.text:
**RoutingConditions:**

```
RoutingConditions
├── phases: set<string> | null              # Match when ConversationState.phase is in set
```

requirements.applies: A routing rule may match the event's source channel type.
requirements.text:
```
├── channel_types: set<ChannelType> | null  # Match when source channel type is in set
```

requirements.applies: A routing rule may match the intent carried by the event.
requirements.text:
```
├── intents: set<string> | null             # Match on detected intent
```

requirements.applies: A routing rule may match particular source channel IDs.
requirements.text:
```
├── source_channel_ids: set<string> | null  # Match on specific source channels
```

requirements.applies: A custom routing rule may test the event, room context and conversation state.
requirements.text:
```
└── custom: function | null                 # Arbitrary predicate (event, context, state) → bool
```

requirements.applies: An explicit address takes precedence, bypassing sticky affinity, matching rules and the default.
requirements.text:
**Evaluation order:**

0. If the event is addressed (§19.3), the address decides. The router MUST
   NOT override it, and steps 1–3 are skipped.

requirements.applies: Without a phase transition a room's active agent takes precedence over routing rules.
requirements.text:
1. If `ConversationState.active_agent_id` is set and no phase transition
   occurred, route to the active agent (sticky affinity).

requirements.applies: Of the matching routing rules, the first in priority order wins.
requirements.text: 2. Evaluate rules in priority order. First matching rule wins.

requirements.applies: The default agent is selected when no rule matches.
requirements.text: 3. If no rule matches, use `default_agent_id`.

requirements.applies: A configured supervisor observes beside the selected agent or the addressed channels.
requirements.text:
4. If `supervisor_id` is set, the supervisor ALWAYS receives the event
   (in addition to the selected agent, or to the addressed channels).

requirements.applies: The supervisor may observe unaddressed agent traffic even under ADDRESSED_ONLY.
requirements.text:
This holds under every `AgentResponsePolicy`, `ADDRESSED_ONLY` included,
   because the two rules answer different questions. A policy decides who is
   **solicited to act**; the supervisor is not being asked to act, it is
   watching. Reading `ADDRESSED_ONLY` as excluding it would blind a supervisor
   to precisely the traffic it exists to oversee — every unaddressed
   agent-to-agent exchange — and the role would be worth nothing in the
   deployments that need it most. The policy table in Section 19.3.1 describes
   solicitation, and it is not narrowed by this step.

requirements.applies: While a room is held for a human, the supervisor gets no turn for unaddressed or transport-only traffic.
requirements.text:
One exception: while a room is held for a human (Section 19.6), an event with
   no address, a post naming nobody or an address naming only a transport gives
   the supervisor no turn, since no agent acts on it and its reply would reach
   the person who was promised a human.

requirements.applies: During a human hold the supervisor remains beside an expressly addressed agent.
requirements.text:
Beside an addressed agent, which still
   acts, it stays.

requirements.applies: The router stamps routing metadata and the event router skips non-targeted intelligence channels.
requirements.text:
Step 0 exists because sticky affinity would otherwise swallow every explicit
request. With the active agent consulted first, a rule written to honour an
address is unreachable for as long as any agent holds the conversation — the
two mechanisms could not coexist. An address is a direct instruction from
the sender and outranks both the affinity and the rules.

The router stamps routing metadata on the event. The Event Router skips
non-targeted intelligence channels during broadcast.

requirements.applies: Routing control metadata comes from framework hooks; equivalent sender-supplied keys are dropped.
requirements.text:
`_routed_to` and `_always_process`, the keys it stamps, are the framework's:
only a hook writes them, the router among hooks, and a sender's are dropped
(Section 10.1), so that a sender never chooses the agent that answers it.

requirements.applies: A routing rule reads intent as ordinary caller-supplied event data.
requirements.text:
`intent`, which a rule's `intents` reads from the event's metadata, is the
caller's data, not a framework key: whoever wrote it is read,

requirements.applies: A host that distrusts its transport's copied intent sets it in a before-broadcast hook ahead of the router.
requirements.text:
and a host that
does not trust what its channel copies from the wire sets it itself, in a
`BEFORE_BROADCAST` hook that runs before the router.

requirements.applies: A linear pipeline generates routing rules from its stages.
requirements.text:
A `ConversationPipeline` generates `RoutingRule` entries from a linear stage
definition:

requirements.applies: A pipeline has stages, an optional supervisor and a default phase that falls back to the first stage.
requirements.text:
```
ConversationPipeline
├── stages: list<PipelineStage>
├── default_phase: string | null            # Initial phase (first stage if null)
└── supervisor_id: string | null            # Supervisor for all stages
```

requirements.applies: Pipeline stages define their phase, agent, next phase, permitted returns and optional description.
requirements.text:
**PipelineStage:**

```
PipelineStage
├── phase: string                           # Phase name ("triage", "specialist", "closing")
├── agent_id: string                        # Agent handling this phase
├── next: string | null                     # Next phase on handoff (null = terminal)
├── can_return_to: set<string>              # Phases this stage can return to
└── description: string | null              # Human-readable stage description
```

requirements.applies: Each pipeline stage produces a routing rule matching that stage's phase.
requirements.text:
The pipeline generates one `RoutingRule` per stage with
`conditions.phases = {stage.phase}`.

requirements.applies: Construction refuses a forward or return transition to an unknown phase, treating an empty next as absent.
requirements.text:
A stage whose `next` or `can_return_to` names a phase no stage holds MUST be
refused when the pipeline is built; an empty `next` is none.

requirements.applies: The last stage for the default phase supplies the router's default agent, or none for an unknown default phase.
requirements.text:
The router's
default agent is that of the default phase's stage, the last of several, and
none when no stage holds that phase.

requirements.applies: The next and permitted-return stage fields determine a phase's legal transitions.
requirements.text:
A phase's allowed transitions are its
stage's `next` and `can_return_to`,

requirements.applies: A multi-stage agent takes the last stage it occupies as its phase.
requirements.text:
and an agent's phase is that of the last
stage it holds.

requirements.applies: Pipeline installation validates all agents before installing and a refused installation leaves no hook or tool.
requirements.text:
`ConversationPipeline.install` reads every agent before it installs anything:
one it refuses leaves no hook and no tool behind,

requirements.applies: Installation refuses existing handoff wiring in any or one room, duplicate agents and conflicts with the handoff tool name.
A router installation observes the same preflight and atomic refusal as a pipeline installation.
requirements.text: a router's `install` refuses the same way.

requirements.applies: Pipeline installation registers the global before-broadcast router at priority -100 or the supplied priority.
requirements.text:
It
registers the router's
hook on every room's `BEFORE_BROADCAST`, at priority -100 unless given another,

requirements.applies: The installed handoff handler receives the pipeline phase map and allowed transitions.
requirements.text: builds a `HandoffHandler` with those phases and transitions,

requirements.applies: The installed handoff tool lists the agent's reachable peers in stage order, excludes itself and uses agent or stage descriptions.
requirements.text:
and gives each
agent a handoff tool naming the agents its last stage reaches, itself excluded,
in the stages' order, each by its own description, else its stage's.

requirements.applies: An agent with no reachable stage or no stage receives the generic handoff tool.
requirements.text:
An agent
that reaches none, or holds no stage, takes the generic tool.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: an implementation may offer pipelines that drive speech-to-speech sessions.
requirements.text:
**On a realtime channel.** A pipeline MAY drive a speech-to-speech session
(Section 12.4) instead of routing events:

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a session in pipeline mode takes the active agent's configuration and handoff switches it to the next agent.
requirements.text:
the active agent is then the
session's configuration (its prompt, its voice, its tools), and a handoff
reconfigures the session to the next agent's.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: session start reads the room's agent and handoff changes only that room's sessions, leaving other rooms and channel defaults intact.
requirements.text:
The active agent is the room's:
a session that starts in a room starts with that room's active agent, a
handoff in one room reconfigures that room's sessions, and neither changes
another room's sessions nor the channel's configuration for future sessions
(Section 19.7).

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: without a prompt or identity, the active agent inherits the channel prompt at session start or handoff.
Realtime feature: a room language change preserves the session prompt when the agent supplies none.
requirements.text:
a language change of the room keeps the
session's prompt as it is.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a pipeline session includes the channel tools, the active agent's tools and handoff.
requirements.text:
The tools an agent's
configuration declares are the channel's own tools, the agent's tools and the
handoff tool; a pipeline MUST NOT drop the channel's tools, nor declare an
agent without its own.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: late channel tool changes are read at session start or handoff.
requirements.text:
The channel's tools are read as they are when a session
starts or a handoff lands: a channel configured after the install keeps them
under every agent.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: an agent tool uses its agent handler or falls back to the channel handler.
requirements.text:
A call to one of the active agent's tools is served by the
handler the agent was given; a tool the agent declares without one is served
by the channel's handler.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a conflicting tool retains the channel's definition and handler, is warned at install, and never reverts to the agent's copy.
requirements.text:
A name the channel's tools carry is the channel's
(Section 21.1): declared with the channel's schema and served by its handler,
and an agent's tool of that name is neither declared nor served, a warning
naming it at the install, nor declared once the channel drops its own:
nothing of the agent's serves it.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: channel reservations include host, human-input, search and skill tools even when hidden, without refusing the agent's other tools.
requirements.text:
The channel's tools here are its host
definitions, every name its human-input tools serve, declared or not, and the
tools it serves itself (Tool Search's and the skills', whether or not a session
declares them now); for a pipeline agent's own tool, this skip takes the place
of the refusal Section 21.1 gives a tool orchestration sets up over the
channel's, so the install goes through with the agent's other tools.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: both participant-resolved policies govern declaration, discovery, handler catalogue and execution of a session tool.
requirements.text:
The active agent's tool policy holds on its
session beside the channel's: a tool that either policy denies, each resolved for the
session's participant, is neither declared, nor listed by Tool Search, nor
among the names a handler reads, and the gate refuses it with the policy's
words.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: handoff applies the new agent policy per participant across the room before declaring its tools.
requirements.text:
A handoff applies the next agent's policy, read for each session's
participant, to every session of the room before any declares the next
agent's tools.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the serving room agent's policy governs calls despite stale session declarations.
requirements.text:
The gate MUST judge a call by the agent the room talks to when
the call reaches it, the one that serves the call, whatever a session still
declares.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: sessions use only the channel's skills, human input and MCP instructions and do not serve an agent planner, sandbox or external handler.
requirements.text:
A realtime session serves the channel's skills, human-input
tools and MCP servers' instructions (Section 21.2), never an agent's, and
serves no agent's planner, sandbox or external tool handler:

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: installation rejects unservable capabilities, including an empty agent skill registry, before partial installation and names each cause and available channel option.
requirements.text:
an agent that
carries one of these, a skill registry even empty (a skill added to it later
would open its gated tools with nothing to gate them), is refused at the
install, before anything is installed, each cause named, with the channel's
own option where the channel has one (its skills, its human-input handler,
its servers' instructions). Its gated tools would run without their skill,
and its other ones would be called by a model that was never told of them
or of how to use them.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a reasoning backend rejects the same unsupported agent capabilities and agent tools; its MCP instructions reach its own model.
requirements.text:
A reasoning backend's agent is refused for the same
causes by the same rule, its servers' instructions aside, which reach its own
model (Section 21.2), and for tools of its own besides (Section 12.4.1).

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: installation refuses declaration-only agents and intelligence channels without an Agent's prompt.
requirements.text:
An
agent the kit holds by its declaration alone, or an intelligence channel that
is not an agent, is refused at the install as well: a session runs the
agent's own prompt, which only the agent itself carries
(Section 10.6.2).

requirements.applies: A phase can hand off forward to its next stage or laterally/backward to a permitted return phase.
requirements.text:
**Allowed transitions:** An agent in phase P MAY hand off to:
- `stage.next` (forward progression)
- Any phase in `stage.can_return_to` (backward/lateral)

requirements.applies: Handoffs to other phases are refused.
requirements.text: - Transitions to other phases MUST be rejected.

requirements.applies: A HandoffRequest names the target, reason, summary and context for an agent's handoff tool call.
requirements.text:
Agents request handoffs by calling the `handoff_conversation` tool:

**HandoffRequest:**

```
HandoffRequest
├── target_agent_id: string                 # Agent to hand off to
├── reason: string                          # Why the handoff is happening
├── summary: string                         # Context summary for the target agent
├── context: map<string, any>               # Additional handoff context
```

requirements.applies: The handoff request carries an optional channel escalation, illustrated by same, voice, email and sms; this field names the requested switch.
requirements.text:
```
├── channel_escalation: string | null       # "same", "voice", "email", "sms" (channel switch)
```

requirements.applies: The handoff request's urgency flag defaults to false.
requirements.text:
```
└── urgent: bool (default false)            # Priority flag
```

requirements.applies: HandoffResult carries acceptance, new agent and phase, a readable message and the rejection reason where applicable.
requirements.text:
**HandoffResult:**

```
HandoffResult
├── accepted: bool                          # Whether the handoff was accepted
├── new_agent_id: string | null             # Active agent after handoff
├── new_phase: string | null                # Phase after handoff
├── message: string                         # Human-readable result
└── reason: string                          # Rejection reason (if not accepted)
```

requirements.applies: An agent initiates a handoff by calling handoff_conversation with a handoff request.
requirements.text:
**Handoff protocol:**

1. Agent calls `handoff_conversation` tool with `HandoffRequest`.
2. `HandoffHandler` validates:

requirements.applies: Target validation admits a bound intelligence channel, human or a known target and refuses a bound transport.
requirements.text:
- Target is an intelligence channel attached to the room, `human`, or a
     target the handler knows. A transport the room binds is not found: an
     active agent that is a transport leaves the room with no agent to answer.

requirements.applies: A handoff must satisfy configured pipeline transition rules.
requirements.text: - Phase transition is allowed (per pipeline rules, if applicable).

requirements.applies: With a phase map and allowed transitions, the target must own its mapped or routed phase.
requirements.text:
- With allowed transitions and a phase map, the target holds the phase: the
     one the map gives it, or one a rule of the router asks it in.

requirements.applies: Under a phase map, human and known targets pass the target phase check only when unmapped, while other unmapped targets have no phase.
requirements.text:
A `human` or
     known target the map does not name passes; one it names does not, and a
     target it does not name otherwise holds no phase. A model's `next_phase`
     decides no more than that: a tool's `enum` is not enforced at run time,
     and a model reads what a sender wrote.

requirements.applies: A caller must own the room's current phase; a stale agent cannot hand off.
requirements.text:
The caller holds the room's phase
     by the same rule: an agent the room moved past hands nothing on.

requirements.applies: An unmapped caller other than human or a known target passes only as the active agent or, with none active, the default.
requirements.text:
A caller
     the map does not name, neither `human` nor known, passes as the room's
     active agent, or its default agent while none is active.

requirements.applies: With no phase map neither target nor caller is bound to a phase.
requirements.text:
With no phase map,
     nothing ties an agent to a phase, and the target and the caller are free.

requirements.applies: An accepted handoff updates the room's phase and active agent.
requirements.text:
3. If valid:
   - Update `ConversationState.phase` and `active_agent_id`.

requirements.applies: An accepted handoff dispatches ON_HANDOFF.
requirements.text: - Fire `ON_HANDOFF` hook.

requirements.applies: An accepted handoff dispatches ON_PHASE_TRANSITION.
requirements.text: - Fire `ON_PHASE_TRANSITION` hook.

requirements.applies: A valid request returns an accepted handoff result.
requirements.text: - Return `HandoffResult(accepted=true)`.

requirements.applies: A rejected handoff fires ON_HANDOFF_REJECTED.
requirements.text:
4. If invalid:
   - Fire `ON_HANDOFF_REJECTED` hook.

requirements.applies: An invalid request returns an unaccepted handoff result with a reason.
requirements.text: - Return `HandoffResult(accepted=false, reason=...)`.

requirements.applies: The target gets the conversation summary framed and attributed to the sanitized previous agent ID.
requirements.text:
The handoff summary is injected into the target agent's context so it
has continuity, set apart as a summary of the conversation
(`<conversation_summary>`, Section 6.4) under the previous agent's id kept to
an identifier's characters.

requirements.applies: The handoff timeline record quotes the reason.
requirements.text:
The reason the room's timeline records for the
handoff is quoted.

requirements.applies: A handoff records a visible system event from the caller with the internal orchestration marker.
requirements.text:
The timeline's record of a handoff is a system event from the calling agent,
visible to all, carrying `_orchestration_internal` in its metadata:

requirements.applies: An internal orchestration event solicits no agent but still reaches the room's transports.
requirements.text:
an event
that carries it asks no agent, whatever its type, and still reaches the room's
transports.

requirements.applies: The inbound path discards a sender-supplied internal orchestration marker.
requirements.text:
The key is the runtime's alone: a sender's is dropped at the door
(Section 10.1), or a sender would silence the room's agents.

requirements.applies: Setting up a handoff installs a callable agent tool served by the supplied handler.
requirements.text:
`setup_handoff(agent, handler, tool, room_id)` wires the handoff tool into an
AI channel and serves its calls with the `HandoffHandler`.

requirements.applies: An explicitly supplied handoff definition replaces the default handoff_conversation tool.
requirements.text:
`tool` (default
null) replaces the default `handoff_conversation` definition;

requirements.applies: Setup may scope the tool to a single room; the default exposes it in every room the agent serves.
requirements.text:
`room_id`
(default null) declares it in that one room's turns, as a strategy installed
in the room does (Section 19.7), and null declares it in every room the agent
serves.

requirements.applies: Duplicate setup where the handoff tool is already declared is refused.
requirements.text: Setting it up again where it is already declared is refused.

requirements.applies: An accepted handoff to human sets human_hold.
requirements.text:
**A room held for a human (normative).** A handoff to `human` sets
`human_hold`.

requirements.applies: While a room is held for a human its ordinary traffic reaches transports without soliciting an agent and receives the no-route marker.
An explicitly addressed agent and its supervisor may act during a human hold.
requirements.text:
an address naming an agent asks it and the
supervisor beside it (Section 19.4, step 4).

requirements.applies: A human hold refuses an agent handoff through either the tool or handler and fires ON_HANDOFF_REJECTED.
A further handoff to human is accepted during a human hold.
requirements.text: a further handoff to `human` is taken.

requirements.applies: Only a host transition to an agent clears a human hold.
requirements.text:
Only the host's
transition to an agent takes the hold off, with no model's tool on its way.

requirements.applies: A human handoff emits ON_HANDOFF naming human for the host to audit.
requirements.text:
A
model can start a hold by itself, so `ON_HANDOFF`, naming the human, is the
signal a host audits it by.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: session handoffs use the room's active agent as caller; the human hold rule is not yet required there.
requirements.text:
A realtime session's call names no agent of its own:
its caller is the room's active agent, and this paragraph does not yet hold there.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: handoff changes room sessions to the target agent's prompt and a language change uses the active agent's prompt.
requirements.text:
**A realtime handoff needs its agents (normative).** A realtime pipeline
reconfigures the room's sessions with the next agent's prompt on a handoff
(Section 19.5), and a handler's language change reconfigures them with the
active agent's: the agent's own prompt, which a declaration does not carry
(Section 10.6.2).

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a handler with a registered realtime event channel rejects declaration-only agents and intelligence channels without an Agent.
Realtime feature: a language change refuses such an active agent before writing the room language.
requirements.text:
and a language
change on a realtime channel whose active agent is one MUST be refused before
the room's language is written, whoever put the agent among the handler's
agents.

requirements.applies: A handoff handler outside realtime accepts declared agents.
requirements.text: A handler with no realtime channel takes declared agents.

requirements.applies: A handoff acts on the room carried by the current tool call, irrespective of agent wiring or previous calls.
requirements.text:
**The room is the call's (normative).** A handoff acts on the room of the
call that requested it, read from the tool call context (Section 21.4). One
agent serves every room it is attached to, so a room captured when the tool
was wired, or left behind by a hook of another event, names whichever room
came first, not the one asking.

requirements.applies: A handoff tool invoked outside a tool call refuses to act without a room.
requirements.text:
A call made outside a tool call has no room
to act on, and the tool MUST refuse it rather than guess.

requirements.applies: Handler greeting uses the active agent's mapped line through the kit, irrespective of its own greeting and the room's language.
requirements.text:
**A handler's greeting (normative).** A handler's `send_greeting(room_id,
channel_id)` has the room's active agent say the line the handler's greeting
map gives it, through the kit's `send_greeting` (Section 19.1), whatever the
agent's own greeting and the room's language.

requirements.applies: The handler's greeting reports a missing room as not found.
requirements.text:
It reads the room first: a room
missing is not found.

requirements.applies: Without an active agent, a nonempty mapped line, or an explicit or configured event channel, greeting is a successful no-op.
requirements.text:
With no active agent, no line or an empty one, or no
channel named by the call or by the handler's event channel, it says nothing
and does not fail.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the addressed realtime channel delivers the handler's greeting to each of its sessions.
requirements.text:
The channel is read only for a realtime channel, whose
sessions each take the greeting (Section 12.4);

requirements.applies: Outside realtime, the handler's named event channel still greets the whole room.
requirements.text:
on any other, the greeting
reaches the whole room.

requirements.applies: Implementations should provide helpers for each of the common orchestration strategies.
requirements.text:
The following strategies are common patterns built on router and pipeline
primitives. Implementations SHOULD provide helpers for each.

requirements.applies: A strategy is installed per room while an agent object serves all rooms it is attached to.
requirements.text:
**A strategy in several rooms (normative).** A strategy is installed per room,
but its agents are shared: one agent object serves every room it is attached
to,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: one realtime channel serves its attached rooms.
requirements.text: and so does a realtime channel.

requirements.applies: A room's owner keeps its agent configuration and a strategy's additions reach only that room.
requirements.text:
What a strategy adds for a room is set up
for that room, kept by the room's owner for an agent (§10.6.1)

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a channel keeps a strategy's additions in the room's scope.
requirements.text:
and on the
realtime channel itself, and MUST reach that room only:

requirements.applies: Tools installed by a strategy are declared in that room's agent turns.
requirements.text:
- a tool it adds for a room (a supervisor's delegation tools, a delegation's
  result tool, a loop's tool, a handoff tool) is declared in that room's turns

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: room-installed tools are declared only in the room's realtime sessions.
requirements.text:
and in that room's realtime sessions, not in every room the agent or the
  channel serves,

requirements.applies: A call from another room to a room-installed tool is served as undeclared.
requirements.text:
and a call to it from another room is served as a call to
  an undeclared tool;

requirements.applies: A strategy tool uses the call room's configuration, preserving the first install when another room installs a different one.
requirements.text:
- the configuration that tool runs with (the workers, the reviewers, the
  strategy, the limits, the handoff's routing) is the one installed for the
  room of the call: a second room's install, with another configuration, runs
  its own, and changes nothing the first room runs;

requirements.applies: Replacement agent turns run only in rooms with the strategy. An attached agent serves other rooms as itself.
requirements.text:
- a turn the strategy runs in place of an agent's (a loop's produce and review,
  a supervisor's delegation passes) runs in the rooms it was installed in only,
  and an agent attached to a room with no such install answers there as
  itself;

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the active agent's configuration is the room's.
requirements.text:
- on a realtime channel, the active agent's configuration (Section 19.5) is the
  room's.

requirements.applies: Model inputs assembled from model outputs frame and label each worker separately, preserving boundaries and verdicts.
requirements.text:
**What a strategy hands a model (normative).** A strategy that composes a
model's input from other models' outputs (the workers' results a supervisor
reviews or presents, the team's work a next worker builds on, the content a
reviewer judges, a reviewer's feedback a producer revises with) sets each
output apart in a `<worker_output>` block of its own under its author's label:
one output cannot close its block, nor pass itself off as another worker's or
as a verdict.

requirements.applies: A user's task copied into a composed strategy input is framed as a task.
requirements.text:
The user's goal or task it copies into such an input is a
`<task>` block.

requirements.applies: A model's own task stays its input without a task block around it.
requirements.text:
The input a model acts on as its own (the task framed for a
worker, a worker's own task) stays that model's input and is not set apart.

requirements.applies: In a multiparty conversation a copied participant task names its actual asker using the conversation's label; one-to-one input retains its form.
requirements.text:
When several people speak in the room (the conversation's threshold, Section
6.4; a one-to-one conversation left as it is), the user's task such an input
holds as a `<task>` block is headed by who asked for it, by the label the
conversation gives the turn that led to it: `Alice asked:` before a
participant's own words,

requirements.applies: An agent-authored task in multiparty composed input identifies its requester and the delegating agent's authorship.
requirements.text:
`Requested by Alice (2, not Alice), in the delegating
agent's words:` before a task the delegating agent wrote.

requirements.applies: A runtime-authored prompt or worker's own task has no asker heading.
requirements.text:
The heading names the
asker of the task the block holds and nothing else: the runtime's own
prompts and the input a worker acts on as its own carry no asker.

requirements.applies: A supervised or Loop revision contains the original task and only the latest output and feedback.
requirements.text:
A revision a strategy asks for (a supervised step's rework, a Loop
producer's revision) starts from the original task, the step's or the
producer's, as a `<task>` block, with only the latest output and the latest
feedback: never from an earlier revision, whose text would nest one
revision inside the next, and never without the task.

requirements.applies: A room-specific strategy install or turn preserves the shared agent or channel's tools, handler, event handling and prompt.
requirements.text:
No install and no turn writes into the shared agent or channel on behalf of
one room: not its tools, its handler, its handling of events, its prompt,

requirements.applies: Voice feature: a room-specific strategy install or turn preserves the shared agent or channel's voice.
requirements.text:
its
voice,

requirements.applies: A room-specific strategy install or turn preserves a binding the agent or channel shares across rooms.
requirements.text:
nor a binding it shares. A write made for one room is read by every
other room the object serves, which would answer, or refuse, another room's
user with this room's configuration.

requirements.applies: Installing a strategy in a second room does not duplicate the tools declared in either room.
requirements.text:
Installing a strategy in a second room
MUST NOT declare a tool twice in a room.

The producer and the

An asynchronous loop ends with

requirements.applies: A text Discussion lets people and agents address one another without a fixed flow and gives one agent a turn at a time.
requirements.text:
Several agents and one or more people hold one conversation in a room. Any
agent may address any other, a person may address any agent, and no flow is
fixed in advance: who speaks next follows from who was addressed. One agent
speaks at a time.

```
Person ⇄ { Agent A ⇄ Agent B ⇄ Agent C }      one at a time, addressed by @name
```

Swarm (Section 19.7.2) passes the conversation from one agent to the next:
the active agent talks with the user and the others wait for a handoff. In a
discussion every agent stays in the conversation and speaks when it is
addressed, the way people in a group chat do. Neither replaces the other.

A room of several agents left to the default policy dogpiles: every agent
answers the same event at once, each reading the room as it was before the
others answered, and every answer solicits the others again (Section 19.3.1).
`ADDRESSED_ONLY` stops the dogpile by stopping the agents from answering each
other at all. A discussion keeps them talking and takes the turns itself.

requirements.applies: A text discussion supports AI channels, Agents and external ACP agent channels.
requirements.text:
This version covers text: AI channels (Section 6.4), Agents among them, and
external agents (ACP agent channels, Section 6.4), in rooms whose people
write. Its terms are those of Section 6.4, which speaks
for text and voice alike, so that voice can join it without renaming
anything (see "Left out").

requirements.applies: A Discussion is configured with its agents, optional derived or supplied handles and optional names of people.
requirements.text:
```
Discussion
├── agents: list<AIChannel | ACPChannel>      # The agents of the discussion: AI channels (Agents among them) and external agents
├── handles: map<channel_id, string> | null   # The name each agent is addressed by (rule 4; null or absent: derived)
├── people: set<string> | null                # Names agents address people by (null: the room's people, §6.4)
```

requirements.applies: A discussion defaults to allowing a person's unaddressed message to ask agents.
requirements.text:
```
├── addressed_only: bool (default false)      # A person's message asks only the agents it names (rule 8)
```

requirements.applies: The host may order the agents asked by default, with all agents used when the list is absent.
requirements.text:
```
├── everyone: list<channel_id> | null         # Asked, in this order, by a person's message that answers no one (null: all agents)
```

requirements.applies: The optional lifetime turn limit is separate from the depth limit and is unbounded when absent.
requirements.text:
```
├── max_turns: int | null                     # Turns given in the room's lifetime (null: no bound but max_depth)
```

requirements.applies: A discussion without an explicit depth limit uses the kit's maximum chain depth.
requirements.text:
```
├── max_depth: int | null                     # The depth limit of its turns (null: the kit's max_chain_depth)
```

requirements.applies: A host may supply a per-room completion predicate.
requirements.text:
```
├── done: function(room_id) → bool | null     # The discussion is over once it holds
```

requirements.applies: The default silence token is (silent).
requirements.text:
```
├── silent_token: string (default "(silent)") # The answer of an agent that stays silent
```

requirements.applies: The host may supply the discussion's rules for turn notes or use the default.
requirements.text:
```
├── rules: string | null                      # How the room works, as each turn's notes give it (rule 14; null: the default)
```

requirements.applies: A discussion accepts an optional policy for unaddressed messages.
requirements.text:
```
├── dispatch: DispatchPolicy | null           # Picks who takes a person's message that names no agent (rule 18)
```

requirements.applies: The configured deadline for a dispatch decision defaults to five seconds.
requirements.text:
```
└── dispatch_timeout: float (default 5 s)     # How long a decision may take (rule 18)

```

requirements.applies: A room's readable SpeakQueue identifies its current speaker, queue order, listeners, outstanding questions, waiting state and completion.
requirements.text:
```
SpeakQueue (one per room, readable by the host)
├── speaking: channel_id | null               # The agent whose turn runs now
├── queue: list<channel_id>                   # Agents owed a turn, in the order they get it
├── listening: set<channel_id>                # Agents that only listen (rule 12)
├── asked: list<(channel_id, person)>         # Agents that asked a person, and whom, waiting for the answer
├── waiting: bool                             # Whether the discussion waits for a person
└── over: bool                                # Whether the discussion is over (rule 15)
```

requirements.applies: Installing a discussion requires its agents to be the room's only intelligence channels.
requirements.text:
**Normative rules:**

1. **The room is the discussion's.** The intelligence channels the room binds
   are the discussion's `agents`, and no other: the install refuses a room
   that binds another intelligence channel,

requirements.applies: Voice feature: a text discussion refuses installation in a room already binding a conventional voice channel.
requirements.text: a voice

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a text discussion refuses installation in a room already binding a realtime channel.
requirements.text:
or realtime channel
   (Section 12),

requirements.applies: Discussion installation refuses a room containing an agent that thinks while listening.
requirements.text: an agent that thinks while it listens (Section 6.4),

requirements.applies: Discussion installation refuses a room with a router or another strategy.
requirements.text:
or that
   has a router or another strategy installed;

requirements.applies: While a discussion is installed, binding an incompatible voice channel, realtime channel or listening thinker to the room is refused.
requirements.text:
while the discussion is
   installed, binding such a channel to the room

requirements.applies: A room with an installed discussion refuses a router or another strategy.
requirements.text:
and installing a router or
   another strategy in it are refused. One rule decides who speaks, never two:
   the supervisor a router always solicits (Section 19.4 step 4) has no place
   in a discussion.

requirements.applies: The discussion supersedes the room's policy until uninstall, when the prior response policy applies immediately.
requirements.text:
The room's `agent_response_policy` plays no part while the
   discussion is installed; uninstalling it (Section 19.7, one strategy per
   room) gives the room back to its policy at once

requirements.applies: Uninstall forgets the queue and discussion state so a later installation starts fresh.
requirements.text:
and forgets the
   discussion (its queue, who only listens, what agents asked people, the
   turns given, whether it was over), so a discussion installed later starts
   fresh.

requirements.applies: Uninstall cuts the active turn in its serving process without recording an end in the forgotten queue; shutdown keeps the queue and records the end.
requirements.text:
The turn running when it is uninstalled is cut, as listening only
   cuts it (rule 12), in whichever process gives it (rule 16), and nothing of
   its end is recorded in the forgotten queue; a process that stops (rule 16)
   records it, its queue being kept.

requirements.applies: Reinstallation updates configuration while preserving queue state, turn counts, completion and a retained agent's running turn.
requirements.text:
Installing a discussion in a room that holds one, in any process (Section
   19.7), replaces its configuration and keeps the rest: the queue, who only
   listens, what agents asked people, the turns given, whether it is over,
   and the running turn of an agent it keeps.

requirements.applies: Replacing the configuration removes a dropped agent's queue entry, reports its dropped instruction and cancels its running turn.
requirements.text:
An agent it no longer holds
   leaves the queue (an instruction it was owed is reported dropped, rule 16),
   its running turn is cut as listening only cuts it (rule 12),

requirements.applies: A removed agent originally bound by the discussion is detached; a foreign pre-existing binding prevents replacement.
requirements.text:
and it is
   unbound when an install of the discussion bound it; an agent bound
   otherwise is an intelligence channel the room cannot keep, and the install
   is refused, as above.

requirements.applies: A non-bot, non-observer participant sending via a transport counts as a person, as does an unrecorded sender using a transport.
requirements.text:
2. **People.** A person is a participant of the room that is neither a bot
   nor an observer, the roles Section 6.4 leaves out of who takes part; a
   person's message is an event such a participant sent through a transport
   channel, or one a transport channel brought in with no participant record
   behind it (a room whose people the host never recorded still has people).

requirements.applies: A framework delivery through a transport is treated as another sender's event.
requirements.text:
A
   delivery (Section 22), which a transport brings in from the framework's
   own sender, is no person's message: it is an event from another sender
   (rule 8).

requirements.applies: Broadcast does not solicit agents; the strategy gives later turns to the agents the event asked for.
requirements.text:
3. **The strategy takes the turns.** No event solicits an agent at broadcast
   (Section 10.2, solicitation): the strategy queues the agents an event asks
   for and gives each its turn later (rule 7).

requirements.applies: Only the agents named in an explicit address are solicited and the committed event retains the address.
requirements.text:
The address keeps its meaning
   (Section 19.3): only the channels it names are asked to act, it is stored
   with the event, and what changes is *when* they act.

requirements.applies: Discussion preserves ordinary transport delivery.
requirements.text:
Transports receive
   every event as before (Section 19.3 rule 1).

requirements.applies: Broadcast skips agents, and their own turns read the room through the reader's visibility boundary.
requirements.text:
An agent is not delivered an
   event at broadcast, as no channel left unsolicited is (Section 19.3.2); a
   turn reads the room when it starts (rule 9), filtered by what visibility
   lets the agent see (Section 7.5 rule 8).

requirements.applies: On commit, the executor for each agent's room memory receives every visible and readable message except the agent's own, even when it took no turn.
requirements.text:
Its memory provider (Section 20)
   is still handed every message the agent may see (visibility and access,
   rule 4), the agent's own excepted, as the message is committed, as a room
   with no discussion hands it, through the turn backend to the executor that
   holds the agent's state for the room (`committed_event`, §10.6.3): a provider that learns as messages arrive (an
   index, a summary) learns the whole conversation, not only the messages
   that asked for the agent.

requirements.applies: Answering a committed message does not deliver it to the same agent's memory a second time.
requirements.text:
The turn that answers a message does not hand it
   again.

requirements.applies: Per-agent memory notifications run concurrently so the commit waits only for the slowest memory.
requirements.text:
Every agent's memory is handed it at once, so the commit waits for
   the slowest memory, not for the sum of them;

requirements.applies: A discussion's committed-message memory notification skips agents with no available executor.
requirements.text:
an agent offline (rule 7) is
   handed nothing, as no executor would take it.

requirements.applies: An agent's answer and a person's message address agents by their handles, with @all naming all agents.
requirements.text:
4. **Names.** An agent's answer and a person's message address agents by
   naming them: `@` followed by an agent's handle; `@all` names every
   agent.

requirements.applies: Parse mentions at the specified character boundary, using the longest identifier, excluding final dots and matching case-insensitively.
requirements.text:
A name starts the text or follows a character that is neither a
   letter, a digit, `_` nor `@`; it is the longest run of the characters an
   identifier holds (letters of any script, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`) that
   follows, a final `.` excepted, and it matches a handle ignoring case.

requirements.applies: Resolve a handle from the host mapping, then a valid channel ID, then the agent's identity name reduced to identifier characters.
requirements.text:
Each agent has one **handle**, the name the room addresses it by: the
   one `handles` gives it; else its channel id, when the channel id is a
   handle; else its `name` (an Agent's identity, Section 19.1, or an
   external agent's, Section 6.4) kept to a name's characters (`Research
   Desk` gives `ResearchDesk`), when that is a handle.

requirements.applies: A handle is a valid unchanged identifier of at most 32 characters, without a trailing dot, and cannot be all.
requirements.text:
A handle is a run of
   those characters, at most 32 of them, with no final `.`, that an
   identifier keeps as it is (the transcript labels the agent's turns with
   it, Section 6.4: `dev-` and `a--b` are none), and is not `all`. A channel id such as `agent:3f2a…` cannot be one (`@agent:3f2a`
   reads as `@agent`), and a 36-character identifier is no name for a model
   to copy or a person to read: an agent named `Analyst` is addressed as `@Analyst`.

requirements.applies: Reject missing, invalid or case-colliding handles and explicit handles for agents outside the discussion.
requirements.text:
The discussion is refused at construction when an agent has no handle,
   when `handles` gives one that is not a handle or names a channel that is
   not one of its agents, and when two agents' handles read alike ignoring
   case.

requirements.applies: A channel ID different from its handle cannot address the agent by name; stored addresses, queue entries and hooks use channel IDs.
requirements.text:
A channel id that is not its agent's handle is no name: the
   address a name sets, the queue and every hook keep channel ids.

requirements.applies: The host is responsible for avoiding a handle that collides with another channel's label in the room.
requirements.text:
A host
   names no handle after another channel of the room: a sender with no name
   on that channel would carry the same label (Section 6.4).

requirements.applies: Parse names from the text actually committed after before-broadcast hooks, excluding tool material, reasoning, fenced code and quoted lines.
requirements.text:
Names are read in
   the text the event commits with, once its `BEFORE_BROADCAST` hooks have
   run (Section 10.1): never in a tool's arguments or result, an agent's
   reasoning, a fenced code block or a quoted line.

requirements.applies: Combine parsed mentions and a supplied transport address in mention order, excluding the speaker and unknown names.
requirements.text:
They set the event's
   `addressed_to`, the speaker left out, in the order named, alongside an
   address a transport set; a name that is no agent of the room addresses
   nobody.

requirements.applies: A named agent is queued only when its access and the intersection of event and source-binding visibility let it read the event.
requirements.text:
A name queues an agent only when the event's visibility includes
   it and its access lets it read the event (Section 7.5): a name is no way
   around visibility; the visibility is the one the event carries, its own
   intersected with its source binding's at commit (Section 7.3).

requirements.applies: Mentioning a person records who was asked and does not solicit an intelligence channel.
requirements.text:
A person's
   name addresses no intelligence channel: it records that the agent asked
   that person (rule 10).

requirements.applies: Eligible person names derive from the transcript labels and optional host people list, using identifiers up to 32 characters without truncation.
requirements.text:
The names people are addressed by are those of the
   room's people as the transcript labels them (Section 6.4: a participant's
   name, a transport's stamp, else the channel of a sender with no name), only
   those `people` lists when it is set, kept to an identifier's characters and
   at most 32 of them: a longer name addresses nobody, never cut short, since
   a cut name could be another person's whole one.

requirements.applies: Record a unique transcript person label; ambiguous normalized names and ranked look-alike labels address no one.
requirements.text:
What is recorded is the
   person as the transcript labels them, and only when one person answers to
   the name: a name two people answer to (`Alice Martin`, `AliceMartin`)
   records no one, and a look-alike's ranked label (`Alice (2, not Alice)`,
   Section 6.4) is addressed by no name.

requirements.applies: When a person and an agent share a name, the agent's handle wins.
requirements.text:
Where a person's name and an agent's handle read
   alike, the name is the agent's. This is the mechanism Section 19.3.1 leaves
   open: an agent MAY address another agent.

requirements.applies: Each committed event retains its own mentions. The turn queues names only after it ends and only from delivered events.
requirements.text:
5. **A turn queues each agent once.** Each event a turn commits carries its
   own names when it is committed (Section 19.3 rule 4). The queue takes them
   when the turn has ended, from the turn's delivered events only: an event a
