   hook blocked, the depth limit stopped or the source's access withheld
   queues nobody,

requirements.applies: Multiple mentions of one agent across the turn's segments queue that agent once.
requirements.text:
and an agent named in three segments of one turn is queued
   once.

requirements.applies: A discussion turn ends after all its events commit, including a failed or cut-short turn.
requirements.text:
6. **A turn's end.** A turn has ended once every event it produced is
   committed. A turn that fails, or that a round cap, a deadline, a budget or
   a `Cancel` cuts short, has ended too:

requirements.applies: After a cut, committed events and their queued addressees remain, the agent is not retried for that turn and a failure follows ordinary reporting.
requirements.text:
the events it committed before the
   cut stay in the room and queue whom they name, the agent is not queued
   again for that turn, and a failure is reported as any turn's is (Section
   9.3).

requirements.applies: When the running turn ends, give the first queued agent a turn that its listening state and depth allow.
requirements.text:
7. **One turn at a time.** The strategy gives the next turn once the current
   one has ended. It goes to the first agent of the queue that can take it:
   one that does not only listen, or whose turn rule 12 lets it take while it
   listens, and whose turn stays within the depth limit (rule 11).

requirements.applies: A recently speaking agent cannot take the next turn while another queued agent can, even when a person put it first.
requirements.text:
The agent
   whose turn just ended does not take the next one while another agent of the
   queue can, a person's message that put it first included: an agent that
   asks a person at every turn would otherwise keep the turns from the agents
   it waits on.

requirements.applies: Every turn an agent takes in a discussion passes through its room queue.
requirements.text: Every turn an agent of the room takes goes through the queue.

requirements.applies: Queue a dedicated instruction turn at the front for each addressed agent, using the instruction as its input.
requirements.text:
An instruction addressed to agents (Section 10.1.1) queues each of them at
   the front for a turn of its own, which takes the instruction as its input
   (rule 16).

requirements.applies: Queue regenerated turns at the front for the original answerers or original requested agents when no answer remains, once per agent and event.
requirements.text:
A regenerated answer queues at the front, for a turn of its own,
   each agent that answered the event (each agent the event asked for, when
   no answer to it is left), once per agent and event.

requirements.applies: Dedicated instruction and regeneration turns run despite waiting, listening or the immediately preceding speaker.
requirements.text:
Such a turn is given
   even while the discussion waits for a person (rule 10), to an agent that
   only listens, and to the agent whose turn just ended.

requirements.applies: Dedicated turns inserted at the front run in request order.
requirements.text:
Requests that put
   agents at the front are served in the order they came.

requirements.applies: At its turn, an offline declared agent is dequeued and announced skipped, and its pending instruction is dropped.
requirements.text:
An agent offline when its turn comes, one held by its declaration that no
   executor online covers in the room (§10.6.7), is not given it, rather than
   given a turn that fails with `no_executor` at each message: its entry
   leaves the queue and the skip is announced (rule 17), then an instruction
   it was to take is dropped.

requirements.applies: Read executor coverage when the turn is due, allowing a newly online agent to take turns again.
requirements.text:
Whether it is offline is read as the turn
   comes, not from a list read earlier, which may miss an executor started
   since. Once an executor covers it, it takes its turns again.

requirements.applies: When the backend cannot list executors, still give the turn.
Posted task results proceed independently of the agent's executor presence.
requirements.text:
a task's result to post (rule 19) is posted whatever the agent's
   presence.

requirements.applies: Agent requests queue agents at the back or merge into an existing place so one pending turn answers multiple requests.
requirements.text:
8. **The queue.** An agent an agent names is queued at the back, or keeps its
   place when already queued: the request merges into its pending turn, one
   turn for every event that asked for it.

requirements.applies: A person's explicitly addressed agents go to the front in address order.
requirements.text:
A person's message puts the agents
   it addresses at the front of the queue, in the order addressed.

requirements.applies: An unaddressed personal reply goes to the agents that asked that person in question order, else to everyone in host order.
requirements.text:
A person's
   message with no address (`addressed_to` null, and no name read in it)
   answers the agents that asked that person (`asked`), and puts them at the
   front in the order they asked; when none asked, it puts `everyone` there,
   in their order;

requirements.applies: Automatic routing to outstanding askers and everyone still requires each agent's access and visibility.
requirements.text:
each only when the message's visibility includes it and its
   access lets it read the message (rule 4).

requirements.applies: Route a person's answer using outstanding questions before clearing them.
requirements.text:
The message is routed so before
   rule 10 clears what was asked.

requirements.applies: A dispatch policy replaces automatic asker and everyone selection for an unaddressed person's message.
requirements.text:
With a dispatch policy, such a message is
   left to the policy instead, whether agents asked that person or not
   (rule 18).

requirements.applies: An empty address or a message naming only people asks no agent.
requirements.text:
A message whose address is empty, or that
   names only people, asks no agent (Section 19.3 rule 3).

requirements.applies: Other senders queue explicitly addressed agents at the back and otherwise ask no agent.
requirements.text:
An event from any
   other sender (a bot, a webhook, a delivery, Section 22) queues the agents
   its address names, at the back; with no address it asks no agent.

requirements.applies: A hook-injected event solicits no discussion agent regardless of its address.
requirements.text:
An
   event a hook injects asks no agent, whatever its address (Section 9.4).

requirements.applies: A merged turn answers the latest personal request if present, otherwise the latest requesting event.
requirements.text:
A
   merged turn answers the latest person's message among the events that asked
   for it, else the latest of them.

requirements.applies: The everyone order is the host's and is not rotated by the discussion.
requirements.text:
The order of `everyone` is the host's, so
   the agent that should open (the one that looks at the facts before the
   others act) comes first; the discussion does not rotate it.

requirements.applies: In addressed-only mode a person's message solicits only its explicit agents, including when an outstanding asker would otherwise answer.
requirements.text:
With
   `addressed_only`, a person's message asks only the agents it addresses, as
   `ADDRESSED_ONLY` asks only the channels an event names (Section 19.3.1):
   one that names nobody asks no agent, the agents that asked a person
   included, which wait for a message that names them. People who talk among
   themselves in the room are then never cut into by an agent; a host that
   wants agents to judge for themselves whether an unaddressed message is for
   them leaves `addressed_only` off and gives them a speak policy (Section
   6.4), or gives the discussion a dispatch policy, which judges once for the
   room (rule 18).

requirements.applies: A message turn replays the answered event for one agent under the room lock and on the delivery lane, building the context at turn start.
requirements.text:
9. **A turn reads the room as it is.** A turn a message asked for is a rerun
   of the event it answers, planned for that one agent under the room lock and
   run in the room's delivery lane, as a regeneration re-broadcasts an event
   already committed (Section 13.6): its context is built when the turn
   starts, so what was said while the agent waited is in it.

requirements.applies: Use the answered event as current_event and keep it at its original position relative to later history.
requirements.text:
The event it
   answers is passed as the turn's `current_event` and keeps its place in the
   history, before what came after it (Section 20.1),

requirements.applies: The speaking policy's SpeakTurn.recent includes the visible conversation through turn start.
requirements.text:
and a speak policy reads
   the conversation up to the turn's start in `SpeakTurn.recent` (Section
   6.4).

requirements.applies: Turn notes identify the answered event by quoted words and author label, and name all speakers who requested the turn.
requirements.text:
The turn's notes say which event the turn answers (its author's label
   and a quote of it, Section 6.4) and every speaker that asked for it.

requirements.applies: An external agent receives the history it missed together with the answered event as its request.
requirements.text:
An
   external agent, whose session keeps its own history, is sent what it has
   not read yet and the event it answers as its request (Section 6.4).

requirements.applies: Giving a discussion turn publishes no synthetic request message or instruction into the room.
requirements.text:
A turn is never given by publishing a message or an
   instruction in the room for the agent to answer, which a model reads as a
   third party's words and may rightly refuse to obey.

requirements.applies: An agent's personal question records the agent and transcript label; a reply clears only that person's outstanding requests after routing.
requirements.text:
10. **Asking a person, waiting for one.** When an agent names a person, the
    discussion owes that person an answer (`asked` records the agent and the
    person as the transcript labels them, rule 4), and a person's message,
    once routed (rule 8), clears what was asked of them: of that label alone,
    so a sender who takes another's name (ranked apart, Section 6.4) answers
    for nobody else.

requirements.applies: Dispatch may choose whether a reply answers the askers, but the person's outstanding requests are still cleared.
requirements.text:
With a dispatch policy, the policy judges whether the
    message answers them (rule 18); what was asked is cleared all the same.

requirements.applies: In addressed-only mode only a message naming the asking agent clears that agent's question.
requirements.text:
With `addressed_only`, only a message that names the
    agent clears what it asked.

requirements.applies: No eligible turn plus a known person and an outstanding question, listening agent or depth stop sets waiting.
requirements.text:
When no agent of the queue can take a turn,
    the discussion waits for a person's message, its `waiting` reading true,
    if the room has a person to wait for (one of its participants is, or a
    person's message reached it) and it owes a person an answer, an agent of
    the queue only listens, or the depth limit stopped the next turn.

requirements.applies: Waiting suspends ordinary turns until a person writes or its cause clears, while dedicated instruction and regeneration turns can proceed.
requirements.text:
Until a
    person writes, whatever the message asks, or the cause of the wait is gone
    (the agent it waited on talks again), it gives no turn but those of rule 7
    (an instruction, a regenerated answer).

requirements.applies: With no person or no cause to wait, the discussion becomes idle and a later request can restart it.
requirements.text:
With no person in the room, or
    nothing to wait for, a discussion that can give no turn is idle, not over:
    the next event that asks for a turn opens it again.

requirements.applies: Discussion responses have the triggering event's depth plus one, and an ordinary person's message opens a chain at depth zero.
requirements.text:
11. **Depth.** A turn the strategy gives answers an event (rules 8 and 9) and
    carries its `chain_depth + 1` (Section 8.3). A person's message is at
    depth 0, so each one opens a chain.

requirements.applies: A discussion's configured maximum depth replaces the kit limit for turns and their events and cannot be disabled.
requirements.text:
`max_depth` takes the place of
    `max_chain_depth` for the turns the discussion gives and the events they
    produce, and cannot be disabled (Section 17.5).

requirements.applies: The depth limit bounds hops rather than the number of peers answering one trigger.
requirements.text:
It bounds how far a chain
    of agent turns reaches from a person's message (four hops with the default
    of 5), not how many turns follow it, since several agents a person's
    message asks for each answer at depth 1.

requirements.applies: Report a depth-blocked ordinary turn once, keep the agent pending and answer the next shallower request that reaches it.
requirements.text:
A turn the limit stops is not
    given and is recorded once as Section 8.3 says; its agent stays queued,
    and its turn answers the next event that asks for it within the limit: a
    person's message, which opens a new chain, or a request from a shallower
    one (rule 8).

requirements.applies: Each discussion turn, including regeneration, receives its own budget of ten times max_depth independent of the caller.
requirements.text:
Each turn has a reentry budget of its own, `10 × max_depth`
    passes (Section 8.3), whoever asked for it, a regeneration included: the
    budget of the work a call is made from does not follow it into the
    discussion's queue.

requirements.applies: Async hook requests and regenerations retain their inherited depth, including when another process gives the discussion turn.
requirements.text:
Its depth does: a message, a post or a regeneration
    an ASYNC hook's body makes stands at least one deeper than the event the
    hook runs for (Section 8.3), and the turn that answers it at that depth,
    so `max_depth` ends a hook that asks an agent again after each of its
    answers, in every process that gives the discussion's turns.

requirements.applies: A dedicated instruction over depth is dropped and announced without a stored event; a regenerated turn over depth is recorded once and dropped.
requirements.text:
A turn of
    its own (rule 7)
    past the limit does not wait: an instruction's is dropped and reported as
    dropped (rule 16), there being no stored event to record it against; a
    regenerated answer's is recorded once and dropped.

requirements.applies: The host of an autonomous discussion must choose a depth limit sufficient for its intended work.
requirements.text:
An autonomous
    discussion, with no person to open a new chain, needs a `max_depth` that
    lets its work through.

requirements.applies: Discussion provides the host operations listen_only and talk_again for a room and set of channel IDs.
requirements.text:
12. **Listening only.** An implementation that provides Discussion MUST
    provide `listen_only(room_id, channel_ids)` and `talk_again(room_id,
    channel_ids)` for the host, which binds them to what a person does (a
    console's "@sre hold on", "@sre you can carry on").

requirements.applies: A listening agent keeps its pending place and cannot take an ordinary agent-requested turn.
requirements.text:
The discussion keeps
    the state, and it means what the listening state of Section 6.4 means: an
    agent that only listens keeps its place in the queue and takes no turn an
    agent's message asks for;

requirements.applies: A person's direct address grants a listening agent one turn without resuming it; unaddressed automatic routing grants none.
The host resumes a listening agent with talk_again.
requirements.text: `talk_again` ends the state.

requirements.applies: A listening decision by either the discussion or the speaking policy silences the agent.
requirements.text:
An agent
    whose speak policy also listens (Section 6.4) is silenced by either.

requirements.applies: Starting listen-only during a turn cancels that agent's turn and preserves already committed work.
requirements.text:
Setting the state on the agent whose turn runs cuts that turn, as a
    `Cancel` steering directive does (Section 21.3), or, for an external
    agent, as its channel's cancellation does (Section 6.4): what the turn committed
    stays in the room;

requirements.applies: A turn allocated before listen-only but not started is abandoned before execution.
requirements.text:
a turn given but not running yet, which no `Cancel`
    reaches, is abandoned before it runs.

requirements.applies: A resumed agent's next turn reads the room's full available history.
requirements.text:
Talking again, its next turn reads
    the whole room (rule 9).

requirements.applies: A message-requested turn consults the agent's speaking policy; a dedicated instruction bypasses it.
requirements.text:
13. **Staying silent.** A turn a message asked for is submitted to the agent's
    speak policy, when it has one, as any event the agent would answer
    (Section 6.4); an instruction's turn is not, as Section 6.4 says.

requirements.applies: A silent speaking-policy decision ends the turn without calling generation.
requirements.text:
A
    `silent` decision runs no generation and ends the turn.

requirements.applies: Whole-row silence tokens are matched ignoring case, surrounding whitespace, a final period and optional token brackets; a turn of only silent rows is silent.
requirements.text:
Without a policy,
    or when the policy lets it speak, the model may stay silent itself: a text
    row of the turn whose only text is `silent_token`, ignoring case,
    surrounding whitespace, a final period and the brackets around the token
    if it has some, says nothing; a turn whose text rows all say nothing
    stayed silent.

requirements.applies: A silent token row is stored blocked as discussion_silent, produces no mentions and reaches no recipient.
requirements.text:
Its row is stored with `status = BLOCKED` and `blocked_by =
    "discussion_silent"`, read for no name and delivered nowhere:

requirements.applies: Buffer the start of streamed text until it cannot still be the silent token.
requirements.text:
the start of
    a streamed answer is held back until its text can no longer be the token,
    since a streamed segment once delivered is not taken back (Section 6.4).

requirements.applies: A generation ending with no text stores no row and stays silent.
requirements.text:
A
    turn that ends with no text produces no row and says nothing too.

requirements.applies: A silent discussion turn consumes one of the room's allotted turns.
requirements.text:
A silent
    turn counts as a turn (rules 7 and 15).

requirements.applies: Runtime notes name the agent and all peers by handle and give identity names, roles and descriptions where available.
requirements.text:
14. **What a turn knows.** Each turn's notes (Section 6.4) carry, as the
    runtime's own block and not a participant's words: the agent's own
    handle, the other agents of the room by their handles, with the `name`,
    `role` and `description` of those
    that carry an identity (Agents, Section 19.1, and external agents given
    one, Section 6.4);

requirements.applies: Runtime notes name the people the agent can address using the room's transcript labels.
requirements.text:
the people the agent may address, by the
    names rule 4 gives them;

requirements.applies: Runtime notes identify the answered event and requesting speakers, quoting the person's label and words.
requirements.text:
which event the turn answers and who asked for
    it, a person's label and their words quoted (Section 6.4); and how the
    room works.

requirements.applies: Host-supplied discussion rules substitute another agent's @handle and the configured silence token.
Default turn instructions explain who acts next, handle syntax, an unaddressed reply and the silence token.
requirements.text:
without them, it is the default, which tells the agent to end its
    message with the handle of the agent that must act next, says that a
    name without `@` reaches nobody and a message that names nobody wakes
    nobody, and gives the silence token for when it has nothing to add.

requirements.applies: Room context in the runtime notes stays under discussion control and the one-speaker statement uses the current agent's handle.
requirements.text:
The rest of the notes, what the turn knows of the room, is the
    discussion's alone. That one agent speaks at a time is stated with the
    agent's own handle.

requirements.applies: A discussion is over when done holds on the check before a turn is given.
requirements.text:
15. **The end.** The discussion is over once `done` holds, checked before each
    turn is given,

requirements.applies: A discussion reaches its turn limit from the moment its final allowed turn is given.
requirements.text:
or once `max_turns` turns were given in the room, from the
    moment the last of them is given.

requirements.applies: An ended discussion gives no more turns and drops its queue.
requirements.text:
It gives no further turn and drops its
    queue;

requirements.applies: Later instructions and regenerations are blocked with discussion_over.
A turn already running may finish normally; later room events still commit and reach recipients without soliciting agents.
requirements.text:
a turn running then ends as it would; the room's later
    events are stored and delivered with no agent asked. `done` is the host's:
    a mission's state, a person's word, a budget. A host that wants the agents
    to answer again uninstalls the discussion (rule 1).

requirements.applies: Installation persists the discussion's configuration and speak queue with the room.
requirements.text:
16. **Its state, across processes.** Installing a discussion stores it with the
    room, as `ConversationState` is (Section 19.2): its configuration (the
    agents' channel ids and their handles, `people`, `addressed_only`, `everyone`, `max_turns`,
    `max_depth`, `silent_token`, `rules`, whether it has a dispatch policy, and the
    agents its installs attached to the room) and its
    speak queue;

requirements.applies: Older configurations missing handles use the channel ID as each agent's handle.
requirements.text:
a configuration stored without handles addresses each
    agent by its channel id.

requirements.applies: All processes follow the stored discussion's queue and addressing rules and reload another process's configuration replacement.
requirements.text:
Every process that
    serves the room follows the stored discussion, whether or not its host
    installed it there: it asks no agent at broadcast (rule 3), and reads
    names and queues (rules 4, 5, 8, 10) by the stored configuration, read
    again once another process replaced it (rule 1).

requirements.applies: The room lock serializes queue changes; one queue and its lifetime turn count survive restart.
requirements.text:
Every
    change of the queue is read and written under the room lock (Section
    13.5), so the processes that serve one room keep one queue, and the queue
    and the count of turns given outlive a restart.

requirements.applies: A follower can uninstall globally, post held task results, then detach agents installed by the discussion.
requirements.text:
Uninstalling, in any
    process, one that only follows the discussion included, ends it in all of
    them, posts the task results the discussion took and has not committed
    (rule 19), then unbinds the agents its installs attached

requirements.applies: An older stored discussion lacking the list of attached agents detaches none on uninstall.
requirements.text:
(a configuration
    stored without them names none).

requirements.applies: A following or mismatched process immediately drops and reports instructions and posts task results instead of holding them.
requirements.text:
A process that gives no turn, because it only
    follows the discussion or its host installed another configuration, keeps
    no instruction and no task result for a turn: it reports the instruction
    dropped and posts the result at once.

requirements.applies: Only an installer matching the persisted configuration may give turns; a stale installer yields its lease until reconfigured.
requirements.text:
A process where the host installed the discussion may give its turns
    while the configuration its host installed is the stored one: a process
    whose host installed another (the stored one was replaced elsewhere) gives
    up the lease and only follows, until its host installs the stored one.

requirements.applies: The host can ask whether its installed discussion matches the stored configuration.
requirements.text:
`room_strategy_is_current(room_id, Discussion)` (Section 19.7) is how
    the host learns it.

requirements.applies: A host reinstalls a noncurrent discussion only while its own state still calls for that discussion.
requirements.text:
A host that finds it false installs the
    configuration it wants again while its own state still wants the
    discussion, so that a room no longer waits on a process that replaced it
    and stopped; it does not reinstall a discussion its own state no longer
    wants, which would bring back one another process uninstalled.

requirements.applies: A single process gives turns under a stored lease with expiration, defaulting to fifteen seconds.
requirements.text:
One
    process at a time gives the turns: the one that holds the room's
    **lease**, stored with
    the queue with the time it expires (15 s by default).

requirements.applies: The lease holder renews while active; another matching installer takes over after expiry and treats the stopped holder's running turn as ended.
requirements.text:
It gives the turns,
    renews the lease while it holds it, and another process that installed
    the discussion takes it once it has expired: a process that stopped gives
    up its turns that way, and its running turn has ended (rule 6).

requirements.applies: The holder rereads the shared queue at least once per second for another process's queued turn or change to its current turn.
requirements.text:
A process
    that queues a turn without holding the lease makes it known through the
    stored queue, which the holder reads again at least once a second; a
    change that concerns the running turn (its agent set to listen only, rule
    12) reaches the holder the same way.

requirements.applies: Persist the lease holder's active speaker with the lease.
requirements.text:
`speaking` is stored with the lease
    and names the holder's running turn.

requirements.applies: The lease holder evaluates the host's done predicate and dispatch policy.
requirements.text:
`done` is the host's and is checked
    by the process holding the lease, which asks its dispatch policy too
    (rule 18).

requirements.applies: Followers never give turns; messages remain queued when no live installer can serve them.
requirements.text:
A process that only follows the
    discussion never gives a turn: with no process that installed it alive,
    messages are queued and wait.

requirements.applies: Retain instructions only in the receiving process's memory and identify that process in the queue entry.
requirements.text:
A queued turn's instruction is kept in memory only, by the process that
    received it, as an instruction is stored nowhere (Section 10.1.1). Its
    entry names that process.

requirements.applies: Transfer the lease to the instruction's owner when needed; drop the instruction after one lease period without takeover.
requirements.text:
When the turn comes and the holder is another
    process, the holder hands the lease over; an instruction whose process
    does not take the lease within one lease period is dropped.

requirements.applies: Report a queued instruction dropped on completion, uninstall or owner shutdown through ON_SPEAK_QUEUE.
requirements.text:
An
    instruction the discussion drops (it is over, uninstalled, or its process
    stopped) is reported through `ON_SPEAK_QUEUE` as dropped.

requirements.applies: A posted result gets an owner-named queue entry and persists privately with its ID, agent, depth and message until commit, outside publicly readable room metadata.
requirements.text:
A task's result to post (rule 19) is queued as an instruction is, its
    entry naming its holder; unlike an instruction, it is also kept, from when
    the discussion takes it until it is committed, with the room's private
    state (Section 14.1): its id, agent, chain depth and the message it posts,
    apart from the room's metadata, which a reader of the room gets whether or
    not the posted message's visibility (Section 7.3), or a hook that blocks
    it, would show it to them.

requirements.applies: The host may read the room's SpeakQueue at any time.
requirements.text: 17. **Following the queue.** The host reads a room's `SpeakQueue` at any time,

requirements.applies: Every queue transition fires ON_SPEAK_QUEUE with the room, resulting queue, and the corresponding change kind.
requirements.text:
and each change of it fires `ON_SPEAK_QUEUE` (Section 9) with the room,
    the queue as it now is and what changed: an agent queued, a turn given or
    ended, a turn skipped as its agent is offline (rule 7), a queued
    instruction dropped, an agent listening only or talking
    again, the discussion waiting for a person or no longer waiting, the
    discussion over.

requirements.applies: Host discussion operations are scoped to the room's organization and report no discussion to a different organization.
requirements.text:
The host's calls take the organization a room belongs to
    (Section 17.2): a room of another organization holds no discussion for it.

requirements.applies: A host console follows the queue, reads agent identities and bindings, and displays and parses handles consistently with discussion addressing.
requirements.text:
A console
    that shows who speaks, who is next, who only listens and whether the
    discussion waits for a person follows it, and draws the room's agents from
    the room's intelligence bindings and the agents' identity (Section 19.1),
    each shown and named by its handle (rule 4): a command that names an
    agent reads the name as rule 4 does, and the queue's channel ids are
    shown as handles.

requirements.applies: A person's message returns after commit and broadcast without waiting for queued answers, which are absent from its immediate result.
requirements.text:
A person's message returns once committed and broadcast, with no agent's
    answer in its result (Section 10.1 step 18): the answers come in the turns
    that follow, as a regenerated answer the discussion queued does.

requirements.applies: Hosts may provide a dispatch policy that chooses which agents take an unaddressed person's message and their order, including none.
requirements.text:
18. **Who takes an unaddressed message.** A discussion MAY carry a dispatch
    policy, which decides, for a person's message with no address and no
    name (rule 8), which agents take it and in which order, or that none
    does.

requirements.applies: With no dispatch policy an unaddressed message goes to the person's outstanding askers, otherwise to everyone.
requirements.text:
Without one, rule 8 gives that message to the agents that asked
    that person, else to `everyone`: a room where every agent is asked every
    remark spends turns on agents with nothing to add (each says nothing,
    rule 13, but its turn runs), the agent that should answer may come
    third, and an agent that asked the person a question takes the person's
    next message even when it answers nothing of it (a request for another
    agent, a thanks).

requirements.applies: Explicit addresses, names of agents and names of people bypass dispatch.
requirements.text:
The policy is asked for that message only: a message
    with an address, or that names an agent or only people, is routed as
    rule 8 says,

requirements.applies: An addressed-only discussion refuses a dispatch policy.
requirements.text:
and a discussion with `addressed_only`, where a message that
    names nobody asks no agent, takes no dispatch policy.

requirements.applies: A dispatch decision cannot override a name explicitly given by the person.
requirements.text:
A name stays the
    person's word: no policy overrides it.

requirements.applies: The dispatch policy takes a DispatchTurn and returns a DispatchDecision.
requirements.text:
```
    DispatchPolicy (interface)
    └── decide(turn: DispatchTurn) → DispatchDecision

    ```

requirements.applies: A DispatchTurn carries the room, event, visible history, speakers, candidates and outstanding asks.
requirements.text:
```
    DispatchTurn
    ├── room_id: string
    ├── event: RoomEvent                    # The person's message
    ├── recent: list<RoomEvent>             # The conversation before it, oldest first: the room's messages a candidate may read
    ├── speakers: map<string, string>       # Who said `event` and each of `recent`, by event id: a person by their transcript label, an agent as `@handle`
    ├── candidates: list<DispatchCandidate> # The agents it may pick: those that asked the author first, then `everyone`'s order
    └── asked: list<channel_id>             # The candidates that asked the message's author and wait for the answer (rule 10)

    ```

requirements.applies: A DispatchCandidate carries channel ID, agent identity fields and the room's handle.
requirements.text:
```
    DispatchCandidate
    ├── channel_id: string
    ├── name: string | null                 # An Agent's identity (Section 19.1), as a turn's notes give it (rule 14)
    ├── role: string | null
    ├── description: string | null
    └── handle: string | null               # The name the room addresses it by (rule 4); null: its channel id

    ```

requirements.applies: A DispatchDecision carries ordered agent IDs with a reason and judgments that default to empty.
requirements.text:
```
    DispatchDecision
    ├── agents: list<channel_id>            # Who takes the message, in the order they answer; empty: no agent
    ├── reason: string = ""                 # Why, in a few words, for logs and hooks
    └── judgments: map<string, float> = {}  # What the policy weighed, by name
    ```

requirements.applies: Candidate order is the person's outstanding askers followed by everyone, excluding invisible, unreadable and listening agents.
requirements.text:
The candidates are the agents that asked that person, in the order they
    asked, then `everyone`, in its order, less the agents the message does
    not reach (its visibility and their access, rule 4) and those that only
    listen, which an unaddressed message gives no turn (rule 12).

requirements.applies: With no eligible candidate, neither the dispatch policy nor any agent is asked.
requirements.text:
With no
    candidate, the policy is not asked and no agent is.

requirements.applies: Dispatch queues selected agents at the front in decision order and excludes unknown, ineligible and duplicate IDs.
requirements.text:
The agents a decision
    names are put at the front of the queue in its order, as rule 8 puts
    `everyone`; one that is not a candidate, or named twice, is left out, so a
    policy is no way around visibility or the listening state.

requirements.applies: An empty dispatch decision preserves storage and transport delivery, queues no agent and leaves the discussion idle.
requirements.text:
An empty
    decision asks no agent: the message is stored and delivered, and the
    discussion goes idle (rule 10).

requirements.applies: History exposed to dispatch includes only events visible to at least one eligible candidate.
requirements.text:
The recent events a policy reads are
    those a candidate may read: a policy may hand them to a classifier
    outside, and an event no candidate may read MUST NOT reach it that way.

requirements.applies: The lease holder decides each waiting message once off the room lock, before giving the next turn.
requirements.text:
The decision is the room's, taken once per message, off the room lock, by
    the process holding the lease (rule 16): routing the message leaves it
    waiting for a decision in the stored queue, with the candidates it
    reaches, and the holder decides it before it gives another turn, so the
    agents a person's message asks for still come before the agents queued
    after it.

requirements.applies: Pending dispatch decisions are processed in message commit order.
requirements.text: Messages waiting are decided in the order they were committed;

requirements.applies: Ending a discussion discards messages still waiting for dispatch.
requirements.text: once the discussion is over, they are dropped with its queue (rule 15),

requirements.applies: A stopped decision maker leaves its pending message for the next holder.
requirements.text:
and a process that stops while it decides leaves the message waiting for
    the next holder.

requirements.applies: Bound the undecided queue to sixteen and route the oldest excess message with the no-policy fallback.
requirements.text:
At most 16 messages wait: past them, the oldest asks
    what it asks with no policy (below), undecided, so a room with no holder
    alive keeps a bounded queue.

requirements.applies: Apply dispatch_timeout to each decision, using five seconds by default.
requirements.text:
The discussion bounds
    the wait for a decision (`dispatch_timeout`, 5 s by default).

requirements.applies: On failure, timeout, unreadable decisions or an absent holder policy, route to the candidate askers or all candidates and report fallback.
requirements.text:
A policy
    that fails, does not decide in time or returns no readable decision does
    not silence the room: the message asks what it asks with no policy, the
    candidates that asked its author, else every candidate, and the decision
    reported names them with the reason `fallback`; so does a process
    holding the lease whose host gave it no policy, and any failure in
    deciding.

requirements.applies: Applied decisions fire ON_DISPATCH_DECISION with the room, event, eligible candidates, decision and elapsed time, capped to the deadline on timeout.
requirements.text:
Every decision applied fires `ON_DISPATCH_DECISION` with the room, the
    message, the candidates, the decision and how long the policy took (the
    bound, when it did not decide in time), so who took what, why and at
    what cost can be followed and measured without wrapping the policy.

requirements.applies: A competing stale decision is neither applied nor reported, so a committed message has one decision notification.
requirements.text:
A
    decision on a message another process decided first (it took the lease
    over meanwhile) is neither applied nor reported: each message is
    reported once.

requirements.applies: Dispatch leaves the original address null; regeneration with no answer uses everyone and does not redispatch.
requirements.text:
The decision is
    not stored with the message: its `addressed_to` stays null, and a
    regenerated answer to it with no answer left asks `everyone` (rule 7),
    not a new decision.

requirements.applies: A dispatched agent still passes through its own speaking policy.
requirements.text:
An agent picked still answers through its speak
    policy, when it has one (rule 13).

requirements.applies: The built-in classifier dispatch policy asks all candidate yes/no questions together with identities, speaker-labelled conversation and waiting-agent context.
requirements.text:
RoomKit provides a policy built on a classifier (Section 6.8). It asks one
    yes/no question per candidate, all in one call: whether that agent should
    take the message, given what each agent's identity says it does, over the
    message, its speaker and the recent conversation named by speaker; an
    agent that waits for the speaker's answer is marked as such, so that it
    is picked when the message answers it and not otherwise.

requirements.applies: The classifier policy selects qualifying candidates in probability order, using threshold 0.5 and a two-agent cap by default and nobody below threshold.
requirements.text:
The
    candidates whose probability reaches a threshold (0.5 by default) take it,
    likeliest first, at most a number of them (2 by default); with none
    reaching it, no agent takes it (thanks, small talk).

requirements.applies: The classifier policy includes each candidate's probability in the decision's judgments under its channel ID.
requirements.text:
Each candidate's
    probability is reported with the decision, under its channel id.

requirements.applies: The classifier policy presents candidates by handle and judges an agent with no identity by its handle alone.
requirements.text:
Each
    candidate is presented to the classifier by its handle, the name the
    conversation it reads uses for it; an agent with no identity is judged
    by its handle alone.

requirements.applies: An agent given the background tool can start its long work as a task off the discussion floor.
requirements.text:
19. **Talking and working.** A turn talks; long work runs as a task (Section
    23), off the floor. An agent given the background tool (Section 23.4)
    starts one

requirements.applies: A discussion agent starting background work acknowledges it in a single sentence and ends its turn.
requirements.text:
and says once, in a sentence, that the work is under way, and
    its turn ends there;

requirements.applies: The host can start a discussion task for an agent and can expose this operation to a person.
requirements.text:
the host starts one for an agent with `start_task`,
    and a person through what the host gives them.

requirements.applies: Tasks run alongside one another and discussion turns while the floor gives one turn at a time.
requirements.text:
Tasks run in parallel with
    the discussion's turns and with one another, and the floor stays one turn
    at a time: a question asked while a task runs is answered in its turn, not
    after the task.

requirements.applies: Relay results, including failure and cancellation, enter as dedicated instructions to the notified agents at the front in arrival order.
requirements.text:
A task's result comes back as its hand-back, an
    instruction addressed to the agent the task is for, which the discussion
    queues at the front for a turn of its own (rule 7), results served in the
    order they come; a task cancelled or failed says so the same way (Section
    23.3).

requirements.applies: A result in post mode takes the same queue position but publishes the agent's message without generation, interrupting a turn or soliciting mentions.
requirements.text:
A posted result (`hand_back = "post"`) takes the same place, and
    its turn posts it as the agent's message without running the agent's
    model: it never cuts a turn under way, and the names it carries ask no
    one, its worker having written it outside the room.

requirements.applies: A discussion turn exposes the room's tasks in its notes so the agent can answer progress questions.
An agent or the host can cancel an existing discussion task.
requirements.text:
and `cancel_task` or the host's `cancel_task(task_id)` stops
    one.

requirements.applies: Workers run in separate child rooms outside the discussion and may be hosted by an external agent.
requirements.text:
A worker runs in its own child room, outside the discussion, so an
    agent of the discussion may work through any intelligence channel, an
    external agent among them.

requirements.applies: Tasks outlive uninstall and completion; an ended discussion refuses a relayed instruction and preserves the result in its completion hook and StatusBus.
requirements.text:
A task outlives an uninstalled or ended
    discussion: a relayed hand-back is then an instruction like any other,
    refused once the discussion is over (rule 15), its result kept on
    `ON_TASK_COMPLETED` and the StatusBus;

requirements.applies: Pending posted results still publish once the floor is free after discussion completion or uninstall.
requirements.text:
a posted result, which asks no
    turn, is posted once no turn runs, one queued when the discussion ends or
    is uninstalled included.

requirements.applies: Before detaching agents an uninstaller posts every retained uncommitted result through that process's hooks, including results being committed elsewhere.
requirements.text:
Uninstalling, in any process, posts every result the discussion took and
    has not committed, whichever process holds it and whether it is queued,
    waits for the floor or is being committed, before it unbinds the agents
    its installs attached: a posted result is the agent's message, committed
    through its binding (Section 23.3) and through the hooks of the process
    that uninstalls,

requirements.applies: The host is responsible for registering consistent hooks in every process that serves the room.
requirements.text: so every process serving a room registers the same hooks.

requirements.applies: An uninstaller already holding the room lock posts the result without waiting for a competing commit.
requirements.text:
It waits for no commit under way: a host that uninstalls while it holds
    the room lock, which that commit needs, has the result posted by the
    uninstall itself.

requirements.applies: Use the retained result ID as the idempotency key so a later holder or in-flight commit replays without duplicating the message.
requirements.text:
A result's idempotency key is the id the discussion took
    it under, not the id of the message it commits (Section 13.4): the post
    that comes second, the holder's own once it learns of the uninstall (its
    agent detached by then included) or the commit under way once the lock is
    released, is a replay and stores nothing.

requirements.applies: Closing or failed posting keeps the result private until the next uninstall, which posts it after later room events.
requirements.text:
A result a closing process did
    not post, or whose post failed, stays kept, and nothing posts it before
    the next uninstall, not the process that gives the next turn nor a
    restarted process that installs the discussion again: it then comes after
    the room's later messages, and a discussion never uninstalled never posts
    it.

requirements.applies: If a retained previously committed result was permanently deleted, uninstall can post it again once its key has gone.
requirements.text:
One committed but still kept, whose message was deleted for good
    meanwhile (Section 10.3), is posted again, its key gone with it.

requirements.applies: Each room's speak queue and listening state are isolated even when it uses the same agents as another room.
requirements.text:
The rules of Section 19.7 for a strategy in several rooms hold: the speak
queue and who only listens are the room's, and the same agents may hold a
discussion in another room with a speak queue of its own.

requirements.applies: Discussion keeps external agents' tools local to the external agent; this version wires no room tools into them. Voice and realtime are outside this text discussion.
requirements.text:
**Left out of this version.** Voice: a turn would end when its playback
ends, which no event reports yet; a person speaking names no one with `@`;
an agent's written names would be spoken. Realtime channels, whose turns run
outside the room's queue, and agents that think while they listen, which
need every event without a turn. The room's tools for an external agent:
its tools are its own (its workspace, what its agent accepts), and this
version wires none of the room's into it.

requirements.applies: Tasks may run off the floor but the discussion never runs agents' turns in parallel.
requirements.text:
One turn at a time: work that does not need the
floor runs as tasks (rule 19), but turns themselves never run in parallel,
each reading a room the others' answers would have changed.

requirements.applies: Inter-round text reaches the room as messages while its mentions wait until turn end.
requirements.text:
The text an agent writes between tool rounds still
reaches the room as messages; only the names they carry wait for the turn's
end. An approval a person gives for one production change is a tool's
concern (Section 21), and a mission's shared state is the host's (`done`).

requirements.applies: An agent waiting for a person remains eligible for a new explicit request by another agent.
requirements.text:
An agent that asked a person may still be named by another agent before the
person answers.

requirements.applies: Dispatch does not solicit agents on an unaddressed agent-authored message.
requirements.text:
A dispatch policy decides for a person's message only: an
agent's message that names nobody still asks no agent.

requirements.applies: Answers retain their event thread but all threads currently share one room queue and give turns whole-room context.
requirements.text:
Threads (`parent_event_id`): an agent's answer already stays
in the thread of the event it answers, but this version keeps one queue for
the room and gives every turn the whole room; a later version makes each
thread a conversation of its own (its own queue and chains, a turn reading
its thread with the room before it as background, an agent taking one turn
at a time across the room).

**Conformance.** Level 2, with the rest of Section 19.

requirements.applies: A StatusBus exposes the inter-agent status operations and returns a status entry when publishing.
requirements.text:
The `StatusBus` enables inter-agent coordination through status messages:

```
StatusBus (interface)
├── post(agent_id, action, status, detail = "", metadata = null) → StatusEntry
│       # Publishes without waiting for the subscribers
```

requirements.applies: Asynchronous StatusBus posting waits for subscribers, unlike the synchronous post operation.
requirements.text:
```
├── post_async(agent_id, action, status, detail = "", metadata = null) → StatusEntry
│       # Waits for the subscribers
```

requirements.applies: A StatusBus subscriber receives each posted entry.
requirements.text:
```
├── subscribe(callback) → void              # callback(StatusEntry) on every post
```

requirements.applies: A subscriber can leave the StatusBus.
requirements.text:
```
├── unsubscribe(callback) → void
```

requirements.applies: Recent entries can be filtered by agent and status, defaulting to ten entries.
requirements.text:
```
├── recent(n = 10, agent_id = null, status = null) → list<StatusEntry>
│       # Most recent entries, optionally filtered
```

requirements.applies: Recent status can be obtained as context text, defaulting to ten entries.
requirements.text:
```
├── recent_text(n = 10) → string            # Recent entries as text, for an agent's context
```

requirements.applies: Completion lookup optionally filters by agent across the last 50 completed entries.
requirements.text:
```
├── has_completed(agent_id = null) → bool
│       # Whether a COMPLETED entry is among the last 50 completed ones
```

requirements.applies: The StatusBus interface supports closing the bus.
requirements.text:
```
└── close() → void

```

requirements.applies: StatusEntry contains its UTC RFC 3339 timestamp, agent, action, status, detail and metadata.
requirements.text:
```
StatusEntry
├── ts: string                              # RFC 3339 time of the post, in UTC (§1.4)
├── agent_id: string
├── action: string                          # What the agent is doing or did
├── status: StatusLevel                     # OK, FAILED, PENDING, INFO, COMPLETED
├── detail: string = ""
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # room_id here names the entry's room
```

requirements.applies: Status levels use the specified lowercase wire values.
requirements.text:
`StatusLevel` values are written `ok`, `failed`, `pending`, `info` and
`completed`.

requirements.applies: A framework shares one bus and an entry's optional room is named in its metadata.
requirements.text:
One bus serves the framework; an entry names its room, if any, in
`metadata.room_id`.

requirements.applies: Framework posts bound detail at a word boundary and mark truncation with an ellipsis.
requirements.text:
The framework's own posts bound `detail`, a summary for
whoever follows the bus: cut at a word, the cut ending in `…`, never in the
middle of a word or a number.

requirements.applies: A truncated completed entry retains its outcome separately in metadata.result, bounded to 4,000 characters on a marked word boundary.
requirements.text:
A `completed` entry whose detail was cut keeps the
whole outcome in `metadata.result`, bounded at 4,000 characters and its cut
marked the same way: an agent reads an outcome back from it (Section 23.4),
never from the summary, which once turned a 14.9 °C forecast into "1".

requirements.applies: Status hooks are delivered only to the named room, with no hook for an entry without a room.
requirements.text:
Status posts fire `ON_STATUS_POSTED` hooks in that room; an
entry that names no room reaches no room's hooks.

requirements.applies: The first room activity awaits bus subscription, so later posts reach the room's hooks.
requirements.text:
The framework follows its bus
from its first room activity on, which waits for the subscription when the
backend's does not end at once: an entry posted once that activity is over
reaches the room's hooks.

requirements.applies: Status hooks preserve the posting work's depth so feedback cannot evade the chain depth limit.
requirements.text:
The hooks fire at least as
deep as the work that posted, read as it posts (§8.3): what a hook sends into
the room is that deep, so a hook that tells the posting agent again ends at
the depth limit.

requirements.applies: Status hooks remain live during close until the framework seals its store.
requirements.text:
They fire during the framework's close too, until it seals
its store (Section 12.10.4): the end of a task the close cuts reaches them.

requirements.applies: The framework's status_posted event is roomless and its payload retains the entry's room identifier.
requirements.text:
Its framework event,
`status_posted` (§8.2), is the bus's and names no room, whichever room the
entry names: a reader finds that room in the entry's `metadata.room_id`.

requirements.applies: Agents can signal completion, progress or attention through the bus without publishing a room event.
requirements.text:
Agents MAY use the StatusBus to
signal completion, progress, or request attention without sending room events.

requirements.applies: Delegated tasks are posted on the framework's status bus.
requirements.text: The framework posts each delegated task on the bus (Section 23.3),

requirements.applies: The task_status tool reads the room's tasks and an agent is not directed to an unavailable tool.
requirements.text:
and an agent
reads its room's tasks through the `task_status` tool (Section 23.4); an agent is
never pointed at a tool it was not given.

requirements.applies: Implementations choosing a strategy for constructing AI conversation history.
requirements.text:
The Memory System provides pluggable AI context construction. Instead of
always using a fixed sliding window of recent events, implementations MAY
choose different strategies for building conversation history.

requirements.applies: MemoryProvider retrieval before AI generation, with the room, input, context and requesting channel.
requirements.text:
```
MemoryProvider (interface)
├── retrieve(room_id, current_event, context, channel_id) → MemoryResult
│       # Build conversation context for AI generation
│       # Called by AIChannel before each generation
│
```

requirements.applies: MemoryProvider compaction called by AIChannel after a tool round it ran.
requirements.text:
```
├── compact(room_id, history, usage, channel_id) → list<AIMessage> | null
│       # The history to send in place of `history` between two tool rounds
│       # Called by AIChannel after each tool round it ran; null by default
│
```

requirements.applies: Releasing a memory provider's resources.
requirements.text:
```
└── close() → void
        # Release resources
```

requirements.applies: The context the caller hands a memory, including a custom provider or summarizer, for one reader.
requirements.text:
A provider is handed history, it does not fetch it: the `context` it receives
MUST already be the requesting channel's view of the room (§7.5 rule 8). Making
each provider apply the visibility filter itself would put the rule in five
places and leave every third-party provider outside it; making the caller apply
it once puts it in one, and a provider that summarizes what it is given can then
never summarize something the channel was not allowed to read.

requirements.applies: The event the turn answers, including when a deferred turn reads later history or the memory omits its input.
requirements.text:
The `current_event` is the event the turn answers, and what the turn reads
MUST keep it whatever the provider's window or budget: when events follow it
in the `context` (a discussion's deferred turn, Section 19.7.5), it reads at
its place in the history, before them, and is never folded into a summary. A
provider returns it there, or leaves it out as it does a turn's input and the
channel places it there; either way a window cannot drop it, which would
leave the model answering an event it cannot read.

requirements.applies: Arguments passed to memory compaction between two tool rounds, including missing provider usage.
requirements.text:
`compact` is how a memory keeps a long tool turn within its window, which a
read at the turn's start cannot (Section 6.4, "The history compacted between
two rounds"): `history` is what the turn sends before its input, `usage` the
token counters of the round's generation, disjoint, as its provider reported
them (empty when it reported none).

requirements.applies: Between tool rounds when a memory does not implement compaction.
requirements.text:
A provider that does not define it answers
nothing, and the turn is left as it is.

requirements.applies: Between tool rounds when a wrapper delegates compaction to its inner memory.
requirements.text:
A provider that wraps another and
does not compact itself hands the call to the one it wraps.

requirements.applies: Fields of a memory result used to construct a model request.
requirements.text:
```
MemoryResult
├── messages: list<AIMessage>               # Pre-built AI messages (summaries, instructions)
├── events: list<RoomEvent>                 # Raw events for AIChannel to convert
├── notes: list<string>                     # What was retrieved for this turn alone
└── speakers: list<string>                  # The labels the messages name participants by
```

requirements.applies: Conversation history when a memory supplies prebuilt messages.
requirements.text:
When `messages` is non-empty, the AIChannel uses them directly as conversation
history.

requirements.applies: Conversion of a memory's room events into conversation history.
requirements.text:
When `events` is provided, the AIChannel converts them to AI messages
using its standard conversion logic.

requirements.applies: A memory may return both kinds of history; the channel must preserve their order.
requirements.text:
Both MAY be combined — `messages` are
prepended before converted `events`.

requirements.applies: The final prebuilt user text when followed by another user message or standing alone.
requirements.text:
A user text the `messages` end on joins
the user message that follows it, a blank line between, rather than standing
as a second user message in a row, or, before no user message, stands as a
user message of its own, its text alone;

requirements.applies: A prebuilt system message adjacent to conversation turns.
requirements.text:
a system message stays a message of
its own.

requirements.applies: Counting participants represented by labels in a memory's prebuilt messages.
requirements.text:
`speakers` names the participants the `messages` speak of by the labels they
use (a summary's lines, `Alice`, `@sms`): each counts as a speaker toward
labelling the turns (Section 6.4), unless a turn's speaker already has it, so a
conversation a summary named several people in reads as labelled turns.

requirements.applies: Placement of knowledge retrieved for one turn in the model request.
requirements.text:
`notes` carries what a provider retrieved for the current turn only, knowledge
passages for one: it changes from one turn to the next, so it rides the turn's
notes (Section 6.4), after the input, and never the history, which a provider
that caches a prefix would otherwise bill again at every turn.

requirements.applies: A retrieved conversation passage read with the author label fixed at indexing and its text encoded as data.
requirements.text:
A passage taken
from a turn of the conversation reads after the label of its author, fixed by
the runtime when the turn was indexed, its text a JSON string (`Alice: "I am
the account owner"`), as a labelled turn reads (Section 6.4), so what its
author typed never reads as a fact or as another's words;

requirements.applies: Reading an indexed document passage and distinguishing it from a returned turn.
requirements.text:
a document's
passage keeps its form.

requirements.applies: Preserving indexed passage metadata so that a conversation turn is distinguished from a document.
requirements.text:
A knowledge source gives each passage back with the
metadata it was indexed with: a passage without its turn's id reads as a
document's.

requirements.applies: A provider that rebuilds the result returned by its inner memory.
requirements.text:
A provider that
wraps another and rebuilds its result MUST carry the inner provider's `notes`,

requirements.applies: A window-budgeted memory reserving space for the turn's notes.
requirements.text:
and one that keeps the turn within a token budget MUST count them: nothing
trims the turn's notes, so the history is what makes room for them.

requirements.applies: SlidingWindowMemory as the default recent-event history strategy.
requirements.text:
| Implementation | Strategy | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| SlidingWindowMemory | Last N events | Default, simple conversations |
|

requirements.applies: The built-in compacting memory's strategy for older events.
requirements.text:
CompactingMemory | Merges older events into compact summaries | Long conversations, reduce tokens |
|

requirements.applies: The built-in summarizing memory's strategy.
requirements.text:
SummarizingMemory | AI-powered summarization of history | Complex multi-topic conversations |
|

requirements.applies: The built-in retrieval memory's query for knowledge-backed answers.
requirements.text:
RetrievalMemory | Knowledge sources queried with the turn's text | Knowledge-backed answers (RAG) |
|

requirements.applies: The built-in budget-aware memory's truncation strategy.
requirements.text: BudgetAwareMemory | Token-based truncation with priorities | Strict token budget enforcement |

requirements.applies: Memory selection when an AI channel has no configured provider.
requirements.text: **SlidingWindowMemory** is the default when no MemoryProvider is configured.

requirements.applies: The sliding window as the requesting channel sees it, including its current input.
requirements.text:
It returns the most recent `max_context_events` events of the room as the
channel reads it, the turn's event the newest among them, which the channel
places as the input: the turn reads at most one fewer before it.

requirements.applies: Applying the sliding-window count when earlier tool rounds are replayed.
requirements.text:
The agent's
tool rows are not counted: its earlier rounds are replayed apart, at their
place (Section 6.4).

requirements.applies: Summarizing older events on labelled lines while retaining the recent conversation.
requirements.text:
**SummarizingMemory** calls an AI provider to summarize older history,
keeping recent events intact: each older turn is read on one line after its
author's label, and the summary's message stands for them, a user text joined
to the turn after it.

requirements.applies: Available context on which a summarizing memory bases its retrieval thresholds.
requirements.text:
Its thresholds are
shares of what its `max_context_tokens` leaves once the turn's footprint
(below), its reply budget included, and the current event are paid for:

requirements.applies: Shortening older long texts beyond the first retrieval threshold.
requirements.text:
past
the first it shortens the older events' long texts,

requirements.applies: Selecting the older events to summarize beyond the second retrieval threshold.
requirements.text:
past the second it
summarizes them, keeping the latest that fit the second threshold less the
summary's `summary_max_tokens`, its `min_events` latest at least: the event
that passes is summarized, never kept for the last cut to drop unsummarized.

requirements.applies: The final cut of a summarizing memory's result, including retention of its latest event.
requirements.text:
The messages, notes and events it returns are then cut,
from the oldest event, to what is left, its latest event always kept.

requirements.applies: Ordering the summarizer instruction, any previous summary and the delimited conversation.
requirements.text:
A
summarizer (CompactingMemory's too) reads its instruction, which says the
turns are a record to summarize, neither to answer nor to continue, then a
prior summary when there is one, then the turns in a `<conversation>` block:
a transcript ending on a question would otherwise be answered rather than
summarized.

requirements.applies: The room and agent scope and coverage recorded by a summarizing memory in one process.
requirements.text:
The memory keeps, for each room and agent, the summary it last built, with
the room's creation mark and each turn the summary covers with what that
turn said, in its process,

requirements.applies: Summary cache expiry after inactivity and a fresh process starting from its window.
requirements.text:
forgotten once the room has not been read for
`summary_cache_ttl_seconds`:

requirements.applies: A summarizing memory cache belongs to the process; a new process starts from its own window.
requirements.text: another process starts from its window.

requirements.applies: Reusing a summary and incrementally summarizing new turns only after the threshold.
requirements.text:
A
read gives that summary, then the turns after those it covers, and asks
the model again only once they pass the second threshold, the prior
summary then read with the new turns alone.

requirements.applies: Invalidating a summary on room recreation, changed or unreadable covered turns, or a discontinuous window.
requirements.text:
The summary stops standing,
and a read starts from its window again, once the room is one created
again under its id, a turn it covers is deleted, edited, its content
withheld (Section 10.3), or out of the history the channel reads, where the
memory could no longer tell, or the window no longer holds the turn right
after those it covers, which would be neither summarized nor read: a
summary never hands on what a deleted turn said, nor a deleted room's
conversation.

requirements.applies: Triggering inter-round compaction from the sum of the model's usage counters.
requirements.text:
Between two tool rounds it compacts once the round's counters, summed, pass its
second threshold taken as a share of `max_context_tokens`:

requirements.applies: How a summarizer represents older messages, calls and results between tool rounds.
requirements.text:
a model summarizes
the history's older messages, each text read on one line after its role, a
call after the tool it names and its arguments, a result after its tool,

requirements.applies: The retained recent messages, minimum and complete call/result groups during inter-round compaction.
requirements.text:
and
the latest messages are kept whole, those that fit what the history must give
back to come under the threshold once the summary's tokens are paid for, its
`min_events` latest at least, a call's results never kept without their call.

requirements.applies: Reading a prior summary between rounds according to its provenance and placement.
requirements.text:
A summary the history still holds as a memory's message, its provenance kept,
is carried into the new one; a summary the channel placed in the turn, joined
to a user message or standing as a user message of its own, its text alone,
is read as one of the messages.

requirements.applies: Inapplicability of the first retrieval threshold during inter-round compaction.
requirements.text:
Its first threshold does not apply between
rounds,

requirements.applies: A summarizing memory implements its own inter-round compaction.
requirements.text: and the memory it wraps is not asked.

requirements.applies: Resources closed or left with their owner when a summarizing memory closes.
requirements.text:
Its close closes the memory it
wraps and leaves open the provider it summarizes with, its owner's (Section
6.4).

requirements.applies: RetrievalMemory's query, the inner history and the retrieved passages in turn notes.
requirements.text:
**RetrievalMemory** wraps another provider and queries its knowledge sources
(vector stores, search engines, document indexes) with the text of the current
turn; the passages it retrieves are the turn's `notes`, each set apart as
data, while the inner provider supplies the history.

requirements.applies: Indexing a retrieved turn's event and author label as fixed at commit.
requirements.text:
It indexes each ingested
event in its sources, with the label of its author the event's commit fixed
(`metadata.speaker`, Section 20.2).

requirements.applies: BudgetAwareMemory's latest-first retention within the remaining budget, with its minimum latest events.
requirements.text:
**BudgetAwareMemory** keeps the room's latest events that fit what its
`max_context_tokens` leaves once its safety margin, the turn's footprint
(below), the current event and the messages and notes of the memory it wraps
are paid for, dropping the oldest, its `min_events` latest always kept.

requirements.applies: CompactingMemory's allocation for retained events, the summary and its minimum recent events.
requirements.text:
**CompactingMemory** keeps the latest events that fit what its
`max_context_tokens` leaves once the same are paid for as by
BudgetAwareMemory, less the summary's share of the window, its `min_events`
latest always kept,

requirements.applies: Summarizing trimmed events and positioning the result between wrapped messages and retained events.
requirements.text:
and has a model summarize the events it trims; the
summary's message comes after the messages of the memory it wraps, before the
events it keeps.

requirements.applies: Ownership of the wrapped memory and summarizer when a compacting memory closes.
requirements.text:
Its close, as SummarizingMemory's, closes the memory it
wraps and leaves open the provider it summarizes with.

requirements.applies: The system prompt, tools, channel notes and reply budget a memory must reserve for the turn.
requirements.text:
**The turn's footprint.** What the history may take is what the window leaves
once the rest of the turn is in it: the system prompt, the tools declared, the
notes the channel itself adds to the turn's input (the room's plan, the
speaker attribution) and the reply budget.

requirements.applies: Charging each replayed tool round or instruction to its history turn when retaining or cutting events.
requirements.text:
The earlier rounds of tool calls
and the instructions its history replays (Sections 6.4 and 10.1.1) are
measured apart, each with its timeline index and its turn: a memory charges
each to the history event it reads with (its turn's first event after it,
else the last event before it), so that it keeps or cuts a turn whole,
rather than reserving them all for rounds whose turns it then cuts.

requirements.applies: The per-turn footprint measured by AIChannel before reading memory and made available to that memory.
requirements.text:
A
host cannot always name that rest, since the prompt is composed per turn
(skills, Tool Search, the agent's identity, a binding's tools). So an AI channel
MUST measure it, as it will send it, before it reads its memory, and make the
measure readable to the memory for that turn (`current_turn_footprint()`): the
input it measured, the reply budget the turn requests, zero when the
channel sets none and the provider applies its own, and each piece its history
replays as `(index, turn, tokens)`.

requirements.applies: Budgeted memories count labelled and unlabelled turns in the form the model receives, including the input.
requirements.text:
A memory that keeps the turn within a window (BudgetAwareMemory,
CompactingMemory and SummarizingMemory above) counts each turn as the
conversation sends it: where the conversation labels its turns (Section
6.4), a participant's turn, the current one included, costs its label and
the JSON string of each of its lines, a 14-line JSON paste 143 tokens where
its text alone is 96; a one-to-one conversation's turns cost what was typed.

requirements.applies: History is sized against the remaining model window after the footprint and current event.
requirements.text:
It sizes the history against what
the window, the model's, leaves once the turn's footprint and the current
event are in it, never against the whole window: a 32,000-token window with a
12,000-token system prompt, 8,000 tokens of tools and a 6,000-token reply
budget leaves the history under 6,000.

requirements.applies: The given input reserve as a floor on the measured input.
requirements.text:
It reserves the larger of the
reserve it was given and the measured input: the given reserve is a floor on
that same input, not an addition to it, so a host that measures its own system
prompt is not counted twice.

requirements.applies: The reply allocation when a budgeted memory has a safety margin.
requirements.text:
For the reply it reserves the larger of its
safety margin and the reply budget: the margin is the reply's headroom when
the reply budget is unknown or smaller, and the reply budget when it is
larger.

requirements.applies: A summarizing memory with no safety margin reserves the requested reply budget alone.
requirements.text:
A memory without a margin (SummarizingMemory) reserves the reply
budget alone: with none set, its last cut may fill the window, and only its
thresholds, below that cut, leave the reply room.

requirements.applies: Context added by a hook after the memory read is outside the measured footprint.
requirements.text:
What a hook adds to the
context after the memory read is not measured.

requirements.applies: The ToolPolicy configuration supplied to an AI agent, including allow patterns, deny patterns and per-role overrides.
requirements.text:
A `ToolPolicy` controls which tools an AI agent can invoke:

```
ToolPolicy
├── allow: list<string>                     # Glob patterns for allowed tools
├── deny: list<string>                      # Glob patterns for denied tools
└── role_overrides: map<string, RoleOverride>  # Per-role policy adjustments
```

requirements.applies: Applying a deny pattern even when the same tool is otherwise allowed.
requirements.text:
**Resolution rules:**

1. If `deny` matches the tool name, the tool is DENIED (deny always wins).

requirements.applies: A nonempty tool allow list restricts access to names matching at least one allow pattern.
requirements.text:
2. If `allow` is non-empty and the tool name does NOT match any allow pattern,
   the tool is DENIED (whitelist mode).

requirements.applies: Default access when no deny or nonmatching allow rule applies.
requirements.text: 3. Otherwise, the tool is ALLOWED.

requirements.applies: Star and question mark wildcards in configured tool patterns.
requirements.text: Glob patterns support `*` (any characters) and `?` (single character).

requirements.applies: Literal matching outside the supported glob wildcards.
requirements.text: Every other character stands for itself,

requirements.applies: Rejecting reserved brackets in a tool policy when patterns are configured.
requirements.text: and a pattern holding `[` or `]` MUST be refused where it is configured: a rule written as a character class (`rm_[a-z]*`) read as written would cover none of the names it was written for, and a deny rule or a skill's gate would open.

requirements.applies: Applying the pattern rules to skill tool gates and prerequisites.
requirements.text:
The same holds for a skill's `allowed_tools` and `requires` (Section 24.2).
Example: `allow: ["search_*", "get_*"]` permits all search and get tools.

requirements.applies: The channel applies tool policy to declarations and execution across tool origins.
requirements.text:
**Tools the channel provides.** A channel MUST apply its policy to every tool
it declares to the model or executes, the tools it injects itself included,

requirements.applies: The channel-owned read and discovery tools that remain callable irrespective of tool policy.
requirements.text:
with one exception: the tools that only read or unlock and never act —
`activate_skill` and `read_skill_reference` (Section 24), `read_stored_result`
(Section 21.5), `find_tools` and `list_tools` (Tool Search). Without them a
skill could not be activated nor a deferred tool found, so they stay declared
and callable whatever the policy says.

requirements.applies: An exemption requires exact channel ownership and the exact name; other origins and prefix matches remain governed.
requirements.text:
The exemption covers the tool the
channel serves itself under one of these exact names, and nothing else: it
MUST NOT extend to a name that merely shares a prefix, nor to a tool of the
host, of an MCP server, of orchestration or of a hook that carries one of
these names, which the policy governs like any other.

requirements.applies: Conference feature: a conference without channel-owned reader tools grants no exemption.
requirements.text:
A channel that serves
none of them (a conference) exempts nothing,

requirements.applies: Realtime voice feature: reasoning and spoken-recovery entry points that serve no channel-owned readers grant no exemptions.
requirements.text:
and neither does a door through
which the channel serves none of its own tools (a reasoning backend's calls,
a call recovered from speech): the exemption is read door by door, the same
for the policy and for skill gating.

requirements.applies: The policy governs acting tools injected by the channel, including sandbox, script and planning.
requirements.text:
Every other tool the
