channel injects — sandbox commands (`sandbox_*`), `run_skill_script`,
`plan_tasks` — is subject to the policy like a host tool: a host that wants
them allows them.

requirements.applies: The channel-owned reader exemption from skill gating uses the same exact names.
requirements.text:
The same names, and only them, are exempt from skill gating
(Section 24.2).

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a fixed-declaration tool-search transport is available in the handler catalogue while the named underlying tool is checked.
requirements.text:
A transport that only carries a call to another tool (the
`call_tool` of Tool Search on a provider whose declarations are fixed for the
session) is exempt the same way: it stays declared and is among the names a
handler reads (Section 21.4), and the policy applies to the tool it names, at
the gate, once the call is unwrapped.

requirements.applies: Nameless provider-native tools remain declared and outside tool search and policy matching.
requirements.text:
A provider's native tool, which has no
name (`{"google_search": {}}`), stays declared: a policy names the tools it
governs, and Tool Search neither hides nor lists a tool it cannot name.

requirements.applies: Applying policy and skill gates to both the called alias and the tool's underlying name.
requirements.text:
A
call under an alias a handler serves as another tool (an MCP tool called
`mcp__<server>__<tool>`, which the MCP handler runs as `<tool>`) is judged under
both names, by the policy and by skill gating: refused when either is, so no
tool runs under an alias that its own name is refused.

requirements.applies: When every MCP provider is labelled, the policy can admit or exclude a particular server's alias.
requirements.text:
A policy names a server
through its aliases, which run on the server they name when every provider of
the chain is labelled (Section 21.2): `deny: ["mcp__archive__*"]` keeps that
server out, and `allow: ["mcp__crm__*", "delete_records"]` admits one tool of
one server, both names passing.

requirements.applies: Routing a bare MCP name through labelled providers admitted by the call's policy.
requirements.text:
A call under a bare name names no server: a
labelled provider serves it unless the policy names its server to keep it out
(Section 21.2), so it runs on the first server of the chain the policy does
not keep out, and on none when the policy keeps out every server that has it;
a policy that names no server leaves it on the first server that has it.

requirements.applies: The declaration filter and execution guard apply the same policy rule.
requirements.text:
The
declaration filter and the execution guard MUST apply one rule, so a tool the
model is offered is a tool it may call.

requirements.applies: Consistent refusal precedence and messages in a text AI turn.
requirements.text:
**One refusal per cause.** A call is refused in the same order and with the
same text for the same cause on every door: an AI channel's turn,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a reasoning backend uses the common refusal order and messages.
requirements.text:
a reasoning
backend's (Section 12.4.1),

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: applying the shared refusal precedence and messages on a realtime session.
requirements.text: a realtime session,

requirements.applies: Conference feature: applying the shared refusal precedence and messages to a conference tool call.
requirements.text: a conference.

requirements.applies: Refusal precedence from interruption and withdrawal through declaration, access, arguments and the before-use hook.
requirements.text:
The order is: a
call cut short, a tool withdrawn for the turn, the declared check, the policy,
skill gating, the arguments, then BEFORE_TOOL_USE, so a tool refused for
access never has its arguments read.

requirements.applies: The first argument gate reports a required name absent from the call.
Primitive top-level type mismatches report the offending argument and its declared type.
requirements.text:
a top-level argument whose
property declares a primitive `type` (`string`, `boolean`, `integer`,
`number`, `object`, `array`, `null`) of another type reads `argument '<arg>'
must be of type <type>`;

requirements.applies: Unknown arguments on a closed schema report its sorted accepted names, including an empty set.
requirements.text:
and on a schema that closes itself
(`additionalProperties: false`) with `properties`, an argument it does not
declare reads `unknown argument '<arg>' (this tool accepts: <names>)`, the
declared names sorted and joined by `, ` (`none` when it declares none), so
the model can correct the call;

requirements.applies: The first argument gate allows undeclared properties on an open schema.
requirements.text: an open schema passes it.

requirements.applies: Combining all first-gate reasons for model or rewritten arguments, in the specified groups and order.
requirements.text:
The check names
in one text every argument that does not fit among those it reads, the
model's once repaired and a BEFORE_TOOL_USE hook's as it left them, its
reasons joined by `; `: the required names the call lacks, each once, in
the order `required` lists them, then the
arguments a closed schema does not declare, then each argument of another
type, both in the call's order.

requirements.applies: Grouping several missing or unknown argument names into a single reason of each kind.
requirements.text:
Several names the call lacks read as one
reason, `missing required arguments '<a>', '<b>'`, as several undeclared
arguments do, `unknown arguments '<a>', '<b>' (this tool accepts: <names>)`:
a model that renamed an argument reads the name it lacks beside its own.

requirements.applies: The first argument gate does not perform nested or general JSON Schema validation.
requirements.text:
Nothing deeper
(nested objects, `$ref`, `anyOf`, `format`, `pattern`) is checked.

requirements.applies: Prefix of an argument error for the model's original call.
Prefix of an argument error after a before-use hook edits or replaces arguments.
requirements.text:
arguments a
BEFORE_TOOL_USE hook left that do not fit it, whether it returned them or
edited them in place, read `Invalid rewritten arguments for '<name>': <why>`.

requirements.applies: The reason returned for a tool denied by policy.
requirements.text:
A tool the policy denies reads `Tool
'<name>' is not permitted by the agent's tool policy.`;

requirements.applies: The activation hint returned for a skill-gated tool on a channel that can activate the skill.
requirements.text:
a tool a skill keeps
closed reads `Tool '<name>' is gated by a skill. Activate the skill first using
activate_skill.`

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: wording of a reasoning backend's skill gate when it cannot activate a skill.
requirements.text:
(a reasoning backend, which cannot activate one, reads that
the conversation has not activated it);

requirements.applies: The undeclared-tool refusal outside Tool Search.
requirements.text:
a name the turn or session does not
carry reads `Tool '<name>' is not declared.`,

requirements.applies: Search hint for unknown tool names when Tool Search is enabled on text turns.
requirements.text:
and under Tool Search, on a text
turn

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: unknown names in a Tool Search session, including transport and inventory calls.
requirements.text:
as on a realtime session, its `call_tool` transport and its `list_tools`
included, that no tool by that name exists, with the hint to search.

requirements.applies: The policy reason prevails when the same tool is also gated by a skill.
requirements.text:
A tool
the policy denies and a skill gates reads the policy's text: activating the
skill would not let it through.

requirements.applies: A tool in the catalogue but omitted from declarations for access gets its actual refusal cause.
requirements.text:
A tool of the turn's
catalogue that a round did not declare because the policy denies it or a skill
keeps it closed is refused with that cause's text, not as undeclared: the
model learns to activate a skill rather than to give up.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the delegated reasoning model sees admitted tools and the channel supplies exclusion reasons.
requirements.text:
A reasoning backend's
model is offered only the session tools it may call; a call it makes to one
it was not offered reads the session's cause, which the channel hands the
backend with the catalogue (`unavailable`).

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: reading the current session role and room agent within the delegation's bound, with spoken fallback on failure.
requirements.text:
Both are read when the channel
hands the delegation to the backend, with the participant's role and the
room's agent as they stand then, as the gate reads them at each call, and
inside the delegation's bound: a read that fails is answered by the spoken
fallback.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a queued delegation keeps its handed-over snapshot while each call uses the role then current.
requirements.text:
A role changed during the session holds for the catalogue of the
delegations handed over after it; one a backend queues behind another keeps
what was read when it was handed over, its calls judged at the gate as the
role stands.

requirements.applies: One definition is declared and served for a tool's name within a room.
requirements.text:
**One tool per name.** A name is served by one tool in a room, and declared
with that tool's definition: a tool declared under a name with one schema and
served by another would have the model call the one's schema on the other's
server.

requirements.applies: A channel-owned tool retains its own declaration.
requirements.text:
A name the channel serves itself is declared with the channel's
definition only.

requirements.applies: Refusing a conflicting host tool at construction, with its name in the error.
requirements.text:
The channel MUST refuse, when it is given, a tool under a
name it already has for the same room, naming the tool: a host tool at
construction under a name the channel serves or under a name another host tool
already carries (two tool servers exposing the same name),

requirements.applies: Refusing a conflicting orchestration installation in the same room and isolating independent rooms.
requirements.text:
and a tool
orchestration sets up over the host's, over the channel's, or over another
setup's for the same room (a setup for one room does not collide with another
room's;

requirements.applies: Reinstalling a strategy in its room replaces its own installation.
requirements.text: the same strategy installed again for a room replaces its own).

requirements.applies: Late binding, configuration or hook tools that collide with reserved declarations are omitted and named in a warning.
requirements.text:
A tool
that arrives with the turn (a binding's or a config provider's tools, a
generation hook's) comes too late to be refused: under a name the channel or a
setup already serves it MUST NOT be declared, and a warning names it,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: accepting a setup's own late declarations in a per-agent pipeline session.
The later definition wins for duplicate names supplied by a turn.
requirements.text:
a name it gives
twice is declared once, with the later definition.

requirements.applies: Uniqueness of each tool name in a round's provider declarations.
requirements.text:
No name is
declared twice in one round: a provider rejects a duplicate name.

requirements.applies: Both discovery tools omit denied and skill-gated tool names.
requirements.text:
`find_tools` and `list_tools` MUST NOT name a tool the policy denies or a skill
gates: a name the model can never call is a false promise and discloses what
the policy hides.

requirements.applies: Inventory of callable declared and hidden tools, excluding its own discovery tools and including a declared result reader.
requirements.text:
`list_tools` is the inventory: it lists every other tool the
turn or the session can call, declared or hidden, its discovery tools aside,
the re-read of a stored result included once a round declares it, on every
path.

requirements.applies: Search and its related names include only tools hidden by Tool Search.
requirements.text:
`find_tools` names what Tool Search hides only, and its related
names (a match's family) exclude what it never returns.

requirements.applies: Orchestration tools stay declared when Tool Search hides a large catalogue.
requirements.text:
**Tools orchestration injects stay declared.** When Tool Search hides a large
catalogue behind its discovery tools, a tool that orchestration injects on an
agent or a channel (the handoff tool, a delegation tool, a delegation's result
tool, a strategy's tools; Sections 19 and 23) MUST stay declared as a pinned
tool does,

requirements.applies: Excluding orchestration tools from the catalogue size that enables hiding.
requirements.text:
and MUST NOT count toward the catalogue whose size decides whether
Tool Search hides it.

requirements.applies: Applying policy and skill gating to tools injected by orchestration.
requirements.text:
The tool policy and skill gating still apply to it; Tool
Search does not:

requirements.applies: Omitting already-declared orchestration tools from discovery.
requirements.text: `find_tools` does not name it, being declared already,

requirements.applies: The always declaration reason for orchestration tools.
requirements.text:
and
the declaration reports it as `always` (Section 6.4, `declared_tools`). The
agent is told to call these tools, often that it must: a tool it would first
have to find is a tool it does not call.

requirements.applies: RoleOverride's non-null allow and deny lists, empty defaults, and the supported override modes.
requirements.text:
**RoleOverride:**

```
RoleOverride
├── allow: list<string> = []                # Allow patterns (see mode); not nullable
├── deny: list<string> = []                 # Additional deny patterns; not nullable
└── mode: "restrict" | "replace"            # Narrow the base or replace it entirely
```

requirements.applies: Resolving the role of the waking sender on its source channel.
requirements.text:
The role an override is chosen by is the role of the participant the waking
event's sender is on its channel (Section 5.5);

requirements.applies: Using the base tool policy without a matching participant on the source channel.
requirements.text:
a sender who names no
participant there has no role, and the base rules apply.

requirements.applies: Restrict mode adds the override's deny patterns to those of the base.
requirements.text:
When `mode` is `"restrict"`, the override narrows the base policy: its deny
patterns are added to the base's,

requirements.applies: Restrict mode intersects the two nonempty allow lists and never grants additional access.
requirements.text:
and its allow patterns constrain alongside
the base's, so a tool must match both allow lists (each when non-empty). A
restricting override can take access away, never grant it.

requirements.applies: Replace mode substitutes the role's entire tool policy for the base.
requirements.text:
When `"replace"`,
the override completely replaces the base.

requirements.applies: Recommended support for loading tools through an MCP provider.
requirements.text:
Implementations SHOULD support loading tools from MCP (Model Context Protocol)
servers via an `MCPToolProvider`:

requirements.applies: The MCP provider interface for remote URLs or local subprocesses, its configuration, discovery, tools and host-facing operations.
requirements.text:
```
MCPToolProvider
├── server: one of
│   ├── url: string                         # a remote server (streamable HTTP or SSE)
│   └── command: string, args: list<string> # a local server started as a subprocess (stdio)
├── connect_timeout: seconds = 60           # handshake and listing, a command's start too
├── discover: bool = true                   # List the server's tools when connecting
├── label: string | null                    # The host's name for the server: the <server> of an MCP alias
├── tools() → list<ToolDefinition>          # Discover available tools
├── call(name, arguments) → string          # Execute a tool
├── server_extensions → map<string, object> # Extensions the server declared
├── instructions → string | null           # What the server published for the model
├── server_info → object                   # What the server said of itself
├── read_resource(uri) → contents           # Read one resource
└── request(method, params) → object        # A request the provider does not model
```

requirements.applies: Where stdio MCP is supported, starting on connection and stopping on disconnection.
requirements.text:
A server named by `command` is started when the provider connects and MUST be
stopped when it disconnects.

requirements.applies: Where stdio MCP is supported, passing command arguments as a list without a shell.
requirements.text:
Its arguments MUST be passed as a list, never
through a shell.

requirements.applies: Releasing resources opened during a partially established connection, including a local server.
requirements.text:
A connection that fails part-way MUST release what it had
opened, the server process included, before the error is reported.

requirements.applies: One connection deadline covers start, handshake and listing; expiry cleans up the local or remote connection.
requirements.text:
Connecting
to a server is bounded by `connect_timeout`, the handshake and the listing
together, and a command's start with them: past it a started server is
stopped, a remote one's connection closed and its session deleted, and the
connection fails with a timeout, so a server that never answers does not
hold its host.

requirements.applies: Stdio shutdown escalates after the grace following input closure.
requirements.text:
A started server's stop gives it a grace to exit once its
input is closed (2 seconds in the reference implementation), then terminates
it, then kills it.

requirements.applies: Rejecting invalid remote MCP URLs at provider construction.
requirements.text:
A provider given a `url` MUST be refused at construction when the URL is not
HTTP(S), names no host, or carries credentials (which every log and proxy of
the URL would see: a credential goes in a header) or a fragment,

requirements.applies: Rejecting transport-owned, invalid or excessive MCP request headers at construction.
requirements.text:
and when a
header it is given is one its transport writes itself (HTTP's framing, the
content it accepts and sends, MCP's `mcp-*` negotiation), is not a valid
header, or exceeds the bounds of the reference implementation (32 headers,
8192 bytes a value).

requirements.applies: Validating a host-assigned server label and keeping the provider's identity independent of handshake metadata.
requirements.text:
`label` is the host's name for the server, never the name the server gives
itself: an identifier (letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `-`, at most 64 characters)
that holds no `__` and does not end with `_`, either of which would make an
alias read another server; a provider given any other label MUST be refused at
construction.

requirements.applies: Serving a labelled MCP alias only on its named provider, with normal chain fallthrough.
requirements.text:
A labelled provider's tool handler serves an MCP alias
`mcp__<server>__<tool>` (Section 21.1) only when `<server>` is its label: an
alias naming another server is not served by it (Section 21.4), and the next
handler of a chain takes it.

requirements.applies: An unlabelled provider accepts an alias naming any server.
requirements.text:
A provider without a label serves an alias
whatever server it names, so an alias runs on the server it names whatever the
order of the chain only when every provider of the chain is labelled.

requirements.applies: Filtering bare-name dispatch by the labelled provider's alias under the call policy.
requirements.text:
A
labelled provider serves a tool called by its bare name unless the tool policy
of the call names its server to keep it out: a deny pattern covers its alias
`mcp__<label>__<tool>`, or the policy's allow patterns name aliases (one of
them starts with `mcp__`) and none covers it.

requirements.applies: Bare-name dispatch continues to the first provider its policy admits, or none when all are excluded.
requirements.text:
It then declines the call, so
that the next handler of the chain takes it: a bare name runs on the first
server of the chain the policy does not keep out, and on none when it keeps
out every server that has it.

requirements.applies: Bare-only allow patterns impose no server restriction.
requirements.text:
An allow list of bare names alone names no
server and keeps none out.

requirements.applies: A text AI turn supplies its effective call policy to the tool handlers.
requirements.text:
Each door that judges a call under a policy (an AI
channel's turn,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the voice session and its reasoning agent supply the effective policy to tool handlers.
requirements.text:
a realtime voice session and the agent a reasoning backend
drives for it,

requirements.applies: Conference feature: supplying the effective access policy to the handlers for each conference call.
requirements.text:
a conference) hands that judgement to the handlers the call
runs (Section 21.4).

requirements.applies: Recommended server labelling by a host that composes multiple providers.
requirements.text: A host that composes several servers SHOULD label each.

requirements.applies: Discovering tools once at connection and following every valid page cursor.
requirements.text:
A provider lists the server's tools once, when it connects, following the
listing's cursor across every page,

requirements.applies: Retaining the output schema from each tool's discovery entry.
requirements.text:
and keeps the output schema each tool was
listed with.

requirements.applies: Passing the server's declared name, description and parameters through provider declarations, outside the runtime prompt.
requirements.text:
A listed tool is its server's declaration: its name, its
description and its parameters reach the model as the server wrote them,
among the tools a request declares, which the model's API keeps apart from the
prompt, and not in a text of the runtime, so they are not framed (Section 6.4).

requirements.applies: Bounding the size and number of MCP tool declarations.
requirements.text:
A provider SHOULD bound them, so that a server cannot fill the model's request
with them:

requirements.applies: Reference discovery limits on name, description, parameter schema, and number of entries, with server warnings.
requirements.text:
the reference implementation cuts a description past 4,096
characters at a word, leaves out a tool whose name is past 128 characters or
whose parameters' schema, serialized, is past 32 KiB, and keeps 512 tools of a
listing at most, each with a warning naming the server.

requirements.applies: The first of duplicate discovered tool names wins and the others are reported.
requirements.text:
A name the listing
gives twice keeps its first definition, the others left out with a warning
(Section 21.1, One tool per name).

requirements.applies: Ending a stalled, repeated or over-bound page sequence with a server warning.
requirements.text:
A listing that pages on without bringing anything new (an empty
page that still carries a cursor, a cursor handed out twice) or past a bound
of pages ends there, with a warning naming the server: a server that pages
forever MUST NOT hold the connection open.

requirements.applies: Connecting without discovery leaves the tool list empty and skips per-call result validation.
requirements.text:
With `discover` false it connects
without listing: `tools()` is empty and no call is validated, for a host that
only reads the server's resources.

requirements.applies: Tool calls use the saved catalogue without relisting.
requirements.text:
A `call` MUST NOT list the server's tools
again.

requirements.applies: Validating successful structured output against its discovered schema and marking invalid or absent output as failure.
requirements.text:
A tool listed with an output schema has a successful result's
structured content validated against that schema, and a result that breaks it
(or carries none) fails the call: the tool ran, so the call is failed, not
refused (Section 9.3).

requirements.applies: Calling an unnamed tool without output-schema validation.
requirements.text:
A tool the listing did not name is called as it is,
without validation. Listing again on each call of an unnamed tool
costs the whole catalogue every time, and a gateway that serves tools per
caller never names them to the connection that calls them.

requirements.applies: The local tool policy also applies to tools supplied by MCP.
requirements.text: MCP tools are subject to the same `ToolPolicy` as local tools.

requirements.applies: Accepting optional server instructions published at handshake.
requirements.text:
**Server instructions.** A server MAY publish, when it connects, how a model
should use its tools (the `instructions` of its handshake result).

requirements.applies: Retaining instructions or null and server identity from the negotiated handshake or discovery response.
requirements.text:
A provider
keeps them (`instructions`, null when the server published none) with what the
server said of itself (`server_info`: its name, its version), from the handshake
the connection made: a client that negotiates the newer protocol's discovery
reads them from that result instead.

requirements.applies: Host-supplied MCP instructions for an AI channel's composed system prompt.
requirements.text:
A channel that composes a model's system
prompt (an AI channel,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: host-supplied MCP instructions on a reasoning agent or realtime tool-enabled channel.
requirements.text:
the agent a reasoning backend drives (Section
12.4.1), a realtime voice channel whose provider takes tools) SHOULD take,
from its host, the instructions of the servers whose tools it
serves,

requirements.applies: Refusing an invalid host label when configuring instructions for a channel.
requirements.text:
each under the host's label for the server: an identifier, never the
name the server gives itself, and a label that is not one fails the channel's
construction.

requirements.applies: Ordering MCP instructions after the effective system prompt and before skill preambles on every composed turn.
requirements.text:
The channel MUST add them to every system prompt it composes,
after its own prompt (or the one a binding or a turn's configuration sets for
the room) and before the skills' preambles (Section 24).

requirements.applies: Server instructions remain in the cached prefix across Tool Search, eviction and compaction.
requirements.text:
The same on every
turn, they stay in the prefix a provider caches (Section 6.4); they are not
tools, so Tool Search does not hide them; and no eviction or compaction reaches
them.

requirements.applies: Framing each server's instructions with the host label and the proper authority boundary.
requirements.text:
They are text from outside (Section 6.4): each server's sits in a
`<server_instructions>` block under a line naming its label, the whole under a
heading saying that they are their servers' content, which does not outrank the
system's or the user's instructions and grants no permission.

requirements.applies: Truncation of server instructions with a server-specific warning.
requirements.text:
A server's text
past 8192 characters is cut, with a warning naming the server.

requirements.applies: Omitting unnamed or empty server instructions.
requirements.text:
A server the
host does not name, or names with no text, adds nothing: that is how a host
keeps a server's instructions out of the prompt.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a pipeline uses its channel's instructions.
requirements.text:
A realtime pipeline serves
the channel's, never an agent's (Section 19.5).

requirements.applies: Conference feature: sending the host prompt unchanged without channel-added MCP instructions.
requirements.text:
A conference's realtime bot
sends the prompt its host wrote as it is (Section 12.10): the channel adds
nothing to it, the servers' instructions included.

requirements.applies: Exposing server extensions, including the empty default, for an MCP skill source.
requirements.text:
A provider also carries what the skills a server serves need (Section 24.7)
and no more: the extensions the server declared when it connected
(`server_extensions`, empty for a server that declared none),

requirements.applies: Reading an MCP resource and passing through an unmodelled request and response.
requirements.text:
`read_resource`,
and `request`, which sends a request the provider does not model and returns
its result as the server sent it.

requirements.applies: MCP-served skills obtain identity and verified content from the registry independently of transport session state.
requirements.text:
The skills rely on nothing else the
connection holds: a skill's identity, the entry it was loaded from and the
content verified are the registry's, so a transport without a session
serves them alike.

requirements.applies: Rendering direct MCP call results as text, resource text or a short binary/resource note.
requirements.text:
`call` returns a string whatever the server sent: a text as itself, a text
resource as its text, and what is not text (an image, audio, a blob
resource, a link to a resource) as the short note below, never its encoding
nor an object's printing.

requirements.applies: Passing decodable PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP from an MCP tool handler to an image-capable model.
requirements.text:
The tool handler a provider
hands to an AI channel SHOULD instead hand an image the server returns to the
model as an image, when it is in a format vision vendors accept (PNG, JPEG,
GIF, WebP) and its payload decodes.

requirements.applies: Substituting a short note for binary or rejected image payloads.
requirements.text:
Binary content the model cannot take (an
image in another format or with a corrupt payload, audio, a blob resource)
SHOULD reach it as a short note naming what was left out, never as its
encoding: base64 read as text is noise the model pays for, and a bad image
fails the whole request at the vendor.

requirements.applies: The reference omission note's sanitized, bounded media type, content kind and defaults.
requirements.text:
The reference implementation's note
names the content's kind and its media type (`[image content (image/png)
not shown to the model]`), the type kept to the characters a media type
has, at most 64, so that it carries no text of the server's; for a type the
server did not name, `image/png` for an image, `audio` for audio, `binary`
for a resource, `unknown` for a link and for a kind of content it does not
know (`[other content (unknown) not shown to the model]`).

requirements.applies: Bounding a model-visible MCP tool result that contains images.
requirements.text:
A result the model sees an image of SHOULD be bounded, so that a server
cannot fill the model's request with it.

requirements.applies: Reference text truncation and omission notes in a model-visible result with images.
requirements.text:
The reference implementation holds
its texts within 100,000 characters in all, the text past the bound cut,
with a note saying how long it was when the note fits, and the texts after
it left out,

requirements.applies: Reference image count and aggregate data URL budget, with an omission note charged as text.
requirements.text:
and shows the model at most four of its images within 5 MiB of
data URL in all; each image past either reaches the model as its note,
which counts as a text.

requirements.applies: A Cancel directive aborts the current generation immediately as the table specifies.
requirements.text:
Steering directives allow dynamic mid-conversation control of AI behavior.
They are injected into the AI generation context:

| Directive | Effect |
|---|---|
| Cancel | Abort the current generation immediately |
|

requirements.applies: UpdateSystemPrompt appends the supplied instructions to the system prompt.
requirements.text:
UpdateSystemPrompt | Append additional instructions to the system prompt |
|

requirements.applies: An injected user or assistant message enters history with copied runtime marks replaced.
requirements.text: InjectMessage | Add a synthetic user or assistant message to the conversation history, a copy of the turn's notes' header or of another runtime mark it holds replaced (Section 6.4) |

requirements.applies: Cancelling at the tool announcement boundary prevents any announced handler from running.
requirements.text:
A Cancel ends the turn at the first point the loop reaches, and a round's
tools are one such point: a Cancel that arrives after the model's last event
of a round, while its calls are announced but before they run, MUST stop them.

requirements.applies: Closing every announced tool row as failed on a boundary cancellation, for every provider.
requirements.text:
None of them runs, and each announced call ends with `status = failed`, so no
start row stays pending. The loop honours the same points for every provider.

requirements.applies: Reading directives before a round and again when the model has answered.
requirements.text:
**The answer is a stop too.** A loop reads its directives before each round
and once the model has answered.

requirements.applies: A message arriving during an answer causes another round in the same turn after that answer.
requirements.text:
An `InjectMessage` that came while the model
wrote its answer MUST be read: the same turn asks the model again, the answer
then the message in its conversation, one round more.

requirements.applies: Closing reachability after the last directive read, subject to cancellation ending the loop first.
requirements.text:
Once the loop has read
its directives for the last time it MUST NOT be reached any more, so a
directive the host is told reached a loop is one that loop reads, unless a
`Cancel` ends the loop first: what it had not read then stays unread
(Section 6.4, *A message for the running turn*).

requirements.applies: Direct channel steering requires exactly one selector, before any loop is reached.
requirements.text:
**Which loop a directive reaches.** One AI channel object serves every room it
is bound to, so its running tool loops can belong to several rooms' turns at
once. A host steering the channel itself names exactly one of the loop, the
room or the turn a directive is for: one that names none, or several, MUST be
refused before any loop is reached, since the channel's most recent loop may
be another person's turn in another room.

requirements.applies: Room- or turn-directed cancellation reaches all the addressed loops.
requirements.text:
A `Cancel` addressed to a room or a
turn MUST reach every loop of it,

requirements.applies: Other room- or turn-directed steering reaches the most recent addressed loop.
requirements.text:
any other directive addressed to a room or
a turn MUST reach its most recent loop,

requirements.applies: Room steering cannot affect a different room.
requirements.text:
and a directive addressed to a room
MUST NOT reach a loop of another room.

requirements.applies: Reachability starts with the turn; callers are told the number of reached loops.
requirements.text:
A loop is reachable once its turn has
started; a directive that comes before reaches nothing, and the host is told
how many loops it reached.

requirements.applies: Cancelling one message's delivery by handle or key isolates that message's started and pending turns.
requirements.text:
To stop the turns one message starts, whether they have started or
not, a host cancels that message's delivery (§10.1, *Explicit delivery
cancellation*), by its handle or its `delivery_key`, rather than steering its
room: the room's other turns go on.

requirements.applies: The room owner steers the turns it started via the backend and returns the sum reached.
requirements.text:
The loops of a room's turns run on turn executors (Section 10.6): the host
steers them through the room's owner, which always takes the room and, to reach
one turn, that turn of the room. The owner resolves the turns a directive reaches
under the rules above, from the turns it started, sends it to each as the
backend's `steer` message, and tells the host the sum of what they reached
(§10.6.8).

Steering directives are typically issued by orchestration logic (e.g.,
supervisor injecting context for a worker agent) or by hooks reacting to
events.

requirements.applies: Tool handlers can return text and content parts, including typed mappings.
requirements.text:
**What a handler returns (normative).** A tool handler answers with text or
with a list of content parts (text and images, Section 21.5), which it MAY give
as mappings naming their type.

requirements.applies: A mapping is a content part only when it has the exact part shape.
requirements.text:
A mapping counts as a part only when it has
exactly a part's shape (a text part's type and text, an image part's type and
image fields): one that carries a `type` key among other data is a value, and
reading it as a part would drop the rest.

requirements.applies: JSON serialization of ordinary handler values, preserving mapping order.
requirements.text:
Any other value it returns (a
mapping, a list of values, a number, a null) MUST reach the model as its JSON
serialization, a mapping's members in the order the handler gave them, the
same on every channel,

requirements.applies: Applying the same result conversion to replacements provided by synchronous ON_TOOL_CALL hooks.
requirements.text:
and a result a SYNC ON_TOOL_CALL hook supplies in its
place (Section 9.3) is read the same way.

requirements.applies: Handling a value outside the result contract without failing the turn or printing a language object.
requirements.text:
A value outside the contract MUST NOT
fail the turn, nor reach the model as a language's own printing of it.

requirements.applies: How an application handler is advised to express a refusal rather than returning an ordinary body.
requirements.text:
A
handler that declines a call SHOULD say so as a refusal,

requirements.applies: A refusal returned by a tool handler carries the failure marker delivered to the model.
requirements.text:
which carries the
failure marker (Section 9.3);

requirements.applies: A handler returning an ordinary body has that body classified by the tool result convention in §15.8.1.
requirements.text:
a body it returns instead is read by its own
convention (Section 15.8.1).

requirements.applies: Fallthrough of a composition on the unserved signal, including the single legacy text-envelope adapter.
requirements.text:
A handler says a tool is not its to serve by
raising the implementation's unserved signal (`UnservedToolCallError`), so
that a composition of handlers passes the call on and the channel reads the
call as served by nothing; the text envelope an earlier convention returned
(`{"error": "Unknown tool: …"}`) is still read as that signal, from a
handler's answer only, by one adapter.

requirements.applies: Outcomes of a text call that no handler serves.
requirements.text:
A call whose handlers all decline it
was served by nothing (Section 9.3), on every channel and every entry of one:

requirements.applies: Conference feature: interpreting unserved conference calls as on the function-calling path.
requirements.text: a conference's calls

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: interpreting unserved tool calls recovered from speech as on the function-calling path.
requirements.text:
and the calls a speech-to-speech channel recovers from
speech read it as the function-calling path does.

requirements.applies: Tool-handler invocation takes only the name and arguments.
requirements.text:
A tool handler is called with the tool's name and arguments and nothing else.
One AI channel object serves every room and every speaker it is bound to, so
whatever a handler captured when it was built describes whoever attached the
channel, not the turn now running.

requirements.applies: A per-call turn context follows the async call chain and can be read without changing handler signatures.
requirements.text:
An implementation MUST therefore expose the
turn to the handler through a per-call context that follows the async call
chain (a contextvar, in Python), readable at any depth without a signature
change,

requirements.applies: The per-call accessors outside a tool call return their empty values.
requirements.text:
and MUST answer with the empty value outside a tool call so a host
keeps its own fallback there (a direct call);

requirements.applies: The running turn host is also available within an executor-fired hook.
requirements.text:
`current_turn_host()` alone also
answers inside a hook a turn executor fires while a turn runs (§10.6.5).

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: binding tool context to the session room and participant around a call.
requirements.text:
A realtime channel
serving a tool call (§12) MUST install the same context around the handler,
with the session's room and participant as the turn's room and actor, so one
handler answers the same questions on both paths. The context carries at
least:

requirements.applies: The current_tool_room_id accessor names the turn's room.
requirements.text:
| Accessor | Answers |
|---|---|
| `current_tool_room_id()` | The id of the room the turn belongs to |
|

requirements.applies: The handler reads the Room object shared with its turn's hooks, memory and configuration.
requirements.text: `current_tool_room()` | The `Room` of the turn itself: the object the store loaded when the turn began, the same one the turn's `RoomContext.room` holds for its hooks, memory provider and config provider;

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the current tool room accessor returns the room loaded for a call without a turn.
requirements.text:
on a realtime tool call, which runs no turn, the room as loaded for that call |
|

requirements.applies: Resolving the waking sender to the channel's participant ID or the sender ID.
requirements.text: `current_tool_actor_id()` | The participant id of the event that woke the channel this round: the id identity resolution gave its sender when it gave one (Section 11), else the id the message came under,

requirements.applies: The actor of a framework message or a sender named system in a host-named room.
requirements.text: which is `system`, the framework's own sender (Section 10.4), for a message the framework writes under that sender (a `deliver()`) as for one under that name in a room its host names;

requirements.applies: The empty actor when no participant is named or when a participant is known only on a different channel.
requirements.text:
empty when the event names no participant (one the host commits itself without naming one, another agent's answer, a task's brief to its worker), and when the sender's id is a participant's the room reached through other channels only (Section 5.5), whom it would otherwise name. An empty actor does not single out the host, since a sender's message can read so too: a gate compares the value with the id it expects |
|

requirements.applies: A text turn's live tool names include resolved and newly declared tools, exclude withdrawals and policy denials, and retain skill-gated tools.
requirements.text: `current_tool_allowed_names()` | Every tool name the turn resolved, and every tool a round declared beyond it (the re-read of a stored result), nothing withdrawn, that its tool policy admits for its actor, so a call is validated against the live toolset rather than an attach-time snapshot: a tool the policy denies is left out on every door, since the gate refuses it before any handler, while a tool a skill keeps closed stays in;

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the session's admitted catalogue, including an empty name set without a catalogue.
requirements.text:
on a realtime door, every tool the session declares (its catalogue, what orchestration set up, the channel's own) that its policy admits, and none when the session declares no catalogue: it names no list, and its gate, policy included, still judges each call |
|

requirements.applies: The waking author's conversation label, with its empty cases for one-to-one, instructions, authorless events and outside a turn.
requirements.text:
`current_tool_requester()` | Who asked: the label the conversation gives the author of the event the turn answers when it labels its speakers (Section 6.4: several speak, or two people or more take part), the label a task the turn delegates is headed with (§19.7); empty in a one-to-one conversation, for an instruction or a turn with no author, and outside a turn. It names a speaker; it authenticates no one |
|

requirements.applies: The active tool-call ID, channel and structured-result reverse channel.
requirements.text:
`current_tool_call()` | The per-call record: the call's id, its channel, and the structured-result reverse channel |
|

requirements.applies: The current turn's shared response-metadata record.
requirements.text: `current_response_metadata()` | The turn's one response-metadata record (§6.7);

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: absence of response metadata where no turn will merge it.
requirements.text:
empty where no turn will merge it (a realtime tool call) |
|

requirements.applies: Access to the current room-bound turn host from tools and executor-fired hooks with the documented outside-turn boundary.
requirements.text: `current_turn_host()` | The turn's `TurnHost` (§10.6.5), the only way a host tool or a hook an executor fires writes to a room; inside a hook a turn fires it is bound to the turn's room; between turns it is empty while the implementation carries no host call outside a turn's link; empty anywhere else |

requirements.applies: A text call's chain depth is the depth of the turn's response.
requirements.text:
The context also carries the turn's chain depth: the depth of the response
the turn produces (§8.3),

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a tool call's depth is the assistant answer's depth.
requirements.text:
on a realtime tool call the depth of the assistant's
answer (§12.4).

requirements.applies: Carrying a turn's actor and chain depth into later work, including the empty outside-turn default.
requirements.text:
A result delivered later on the turn's behalf reads it there
(Section 23.3); outside a turn it is 0. It is readable as
`current_tool_chain_depth()`, the turn over or not: a host that hands the
turn's work to another context (a task outside the turn, another process)
reads it there with the actor, and runs that work under both, so what the work
sends continues the turn's chain (§8.3) as it would have from the turn's own
context.

requirements.applies: Actor, room and toolset identify the turn without authenticating the actor or authorizing an organization.
requirements.text:
Two rules bind the values that name the turn (the room and its id, the actor,
the toolset); the response-metadata record and the per-call record are the
turn's write channels, described in §6.7 and above. **They name the turn; they
do not authenticate it.** The actor is the id the waking event carries, a room
`Participant.id` where the room holds one for it, and reads back
the same whether the sender is identified, pending or unknown, and the room's
organization is a fact of the room, not a grant:

requirements.applies: A host handler resolves the participant and applies its own access rule to person or tenant data.
requirements.text:
a handler that reaches a
person's or a tenant's data resolves the participant (§11) and applies the
host's own rule before acting.

requirements.applies: The room snapshot shared within a turn on one side of the backend; owner and executor have separate copies.
requirements.text:
**The `Room` is the room as the store loaded it
when the turn began**, shared by reference with `RoomContext.room` and so with
every hook, provider and channel of the turn on its side of the turn backend
(Section 10.6): the owner and the executor each hold their own copy.

requirements.applies: A store patch during a turn is absent from that turn's original snapshot.
requirements.text:
A patch written to the store
during the turn is not in it:

requirements.applies: Host handlers depending on their writes re-read the room.
requirements.text:
a handler whose decision depends on the turn's
own writes re-reads the room.

requirements.applies: Host handlers must leave the shared Room object unmodified and use store operations for changes.
requirements.text:
A handler MUST NOT mutate the object: a room
changes through the store, and a write on the shared object would be read by
the rest of the turn (the agent-response policy, the delivery plan) as if the
room had changed.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: loading a room once for a call, sharing with a gate context only when one exists.
requirements.text:
On a path that runs no turn, a realtime tool call, the
`Room` is the one the store loaded for that call: shared with the
pre-execution gate's context when a hook made the channel build one, read once
for the call otherwise, and shared with nothing else, since no turn's
`RoomContext` exists there;

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the response metadata accessor is empty on a path without a turn.
requirements.text:
`current_response_metadata()` MUST answer the
empty value on that path, because no MESSAGE event will carry the record.

requirements.applies: Successive rounds inherit the same room and actor from their turn.
requirements.text:
A
tool loop the implementation starts under a turn MUST
inherit the turn's context, so a handler called on any round of the loop reads
the same room and actor as on the first.

requirements.applies: When a large-result bound is offered, it covers all model-visible outcomes on every round, including errors, refusals and overrides.
requirements.text:
An implementation that bounds large tool results (stores the full text and
gives the model a bounded preview with a way to read the rest back) MUST
apply the bound to every outcome the model reads: a handler's result, a
result override from ON_TOOL_CALL, a refusal, and an error. A bound that
covers the success path only leaves the others unbounded, and an error page
or a rewritten result costs the same as the result it stands for, on every
round of the tool loop that carries it.

requirements.applies: Bounding a preview by characters, including a result consisting of one long line.
requirements.text:
- The preview MUST be bounded in characters, not only in lines: one long line
  would otherwise carry the whole result.

requirements.applies: Bounding text in content parts while retaining their images.
requirements.text:
- A result made of content parts has its text bounded and its images kept in
  place.

requirements.applies: Fallback text for a model without image support and the corresponding view exposed to ON_TOOL_CALL.
requirements.text:
- A model that cannot take images MUST be given the text of a content-part
  result, its parts one per line, each image an `[image]` mark; its
  ON_TOOL_CALL hooks read that text, as the model does.

requirements.applies: Reading the whole handler result in ON_TOOL_CALL before storing and bounding the rewritten model copy.
requirements.text:
- The bound applies to the model's copy, and it runs after ON_TOOL_CALL: the
  hook receives the handler's whole result (as text for a model that cannot
  take images), and what it returns (the result,
  or its override) is what is bounded and stored. Everything the model can
  read back has then passed through the hook, so a hook that redacts covers
  the full text; bounding first would let the model page the raw text back
  from the store.

requirements.applies: A refusal observer receives the unmodified refusal message.
requirements.text: A refusal observer receives the raw message.

requirements.applies: Exemption of active skill instructions from large-result eviction.
requirements.text: - An active skill's instructions are exempt (Section 24.4).

requirements.applies: Optional text-search interface for reading back a stored result.
requirements.text: - The read-back MAY search a stored result:

requirements.applies: Where stored-result search is offered, case-insensitive matching on numbered lines with bounded surrounding context.
requirements.text:
given a text on one line, it
  returns the lines of the result as stored that contain it, case aside, with
  the lines around them and their numbers, bounded as a page is, a line longer
  than its share of the page cut around the match.

requirements.applies: Where stored-result search is offered, searching whole lines, reporting absence and identifying truncated matches.
requirements.text:
A search reads every line
  whole, so one that finds nothing says the text is absent from the result,
  which a page read never can; its answer says when it holds only part of the
  matches.

requirements.applies: Where stored-result search is offered, treating a model-provided query as literal text.
requirements.text:
The text is matched as it is, never as a pattern the implementation
  would run: a model-supplied pattern could stall the process.

requirements.applies: Continued readability of stored model results while their room is active.
requirements.text: - What the model can read back SHOULD stay readable while its room works.

requirements.applies: Per-room result capacity and preferential global eviction from the room holding the most.
Accessing a stored result counts as use.
requirements.text:
a result read back
  counts as in use.

requirements.applies: A referenced result ID cannot be reassigned to a later result, including reuse of a call ID.
requirements.text:
A stored result's id MUST NOT be given to another result
  while a context can still name it, so a call id reused in a later turn, or
  an id whose result left the store, reads nothing it did not store.

requirements.applies: Persisted history cannot offer read-back IDs that the store no longer holds after restart.
requirements.text:
A
  summary rebuilt from persisted history (after a restart) MUST NOT offer an
  id the store no longer holds.

requirements.applies: Persisting, broadcasting and routing tool-end events through hooks.
requirements.text:
The event that records a tool call's outcome (`TOOL_CALL_END`) is persisted,
broadcast and handed to the event pipeline's hooks.

requirements.applies: Bounding images in all representations of a tool-end event, identifying omitted images.
requirements.text:
It SHOULD NOT carry a
result's images without bound, whatever shape the result takes (content
parts, or JSON such as an ACP agent's output) and in its structured copy as
much as in the result: an implementation keeps them up to a size and states
each one it leaves out.

requirements.applies: Event-specific image bounds leave the model copy intact.
requirements.text:
The bound is on the event only; the model's
copy keeps every image.

requirements.applies: Applying a common handler-wait bound in the text AI tool loop.
requirements.text:
A handler that never answers holds its turn for good: the model waits on the
call, and nothing else in the room's turn can proceed. An implementation MUST
therefore bound every wait on a tool handler's answer, on every path a call
takes (the tool loop of an AI channel,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: applying the same tool timeout to every speech-to-speech entry.
requirements.text:
every entry of a speech-to-speech
channel,

requirements.applies: Conference feature: applying the same tool timeout to conference handlers.
requirements.text: a conference's calls), through one rule:

requirements.applies: Configuring a channel default and a per-name override, either of which may be unbounded.
requirements.text:
- A channel has a default bound per call, and a bound per tool name that
  overrides it; either MAY be absent, meaning no bound.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a short default tool timeout is recommended where a person waits in silence.
requirements.text:
The default SHOULD be
  short where a person waits in silence (speech-to-speech,

requirements.applies: Conference feature: a short default tool timeout is recommended where a person waits in silence.
requirements.text: conference)

requirements.applies: A text channel may use a longer default timeout.
requirements.text:
and MAY
  be longer for text.

requirements.applies: Per-turn configured tool bounds override the channel's for that turn alone.
requirements.text:
- A turn whose tools come from the channel's per-turn configuration (Appendix
  A.9) MAY be given bounds per tool name with them, which override the
  channel's for that turn alone: a tool the turn declares may be one the
  channel was never built with, and its bound travels with it and its handler.

requirements.applies: Subsequent turns revert to their own configuration or the channel's defaults.
requirements.text:
The next turn reads the channel's bounds unless its own configuration gives
  others.

requirements.applies: Refusing nonpositive per-turn tool bounds before model invocation.
requirements.text:
A bound that is not positive fails the turn before its model is
  asked.

requirements.applies: Tools with their own timeout or intentional waiting boundary are exempt from the channel default.
requirements.text:
- A tool that keeps a bound of its own is not subject to the channel's default:
  one that waits on another agent or on a person by design (a delegation, an
  orchestration strategy's tool, a human-input tool), or a command run under
  its own timeout (a sandbox command).

requirements.applies: A named override still applies to tools exempt from the channel default.
requirements.text: A bound set for its name still applies.

requirements.applies: A host tool installed for an agent by orchestration is bound like other host tools.
requirements.text:
A tool an orchestration strategy installs for an agent to serve (a pipeline
  agent's own tool) is the host's and is bounded like any other.

requirements.applies: Cancelling the handler on timeout and reporting a failed call to the model and observers.
requirements.text:
- When the bound expires, the handler MUST be cancelled, and the call fails as a
  call whose handler raised (Section 9.3): the model reads the failure and the
  error's class, the observers the detail.

requirements.applies: A timeout raised by a handler is reported as that handler's own failure.
requirements.text:
A timeout the handler raises itself is
  that handler's failure, not an expired bound.

requirements.applies: Independence of handler-call timeouts and the turn deadline between rounds.
requirements.text:
The bound is per call, not per turn: a turn's own deadline still applies
between rounds.

requirements.applies: §22 Delivery Strategies; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
Delivery strategies control how proactive content (background task results,
delegated agent output, scheduled messages) is delivered into a conversation.

requirements.applies: Signature and permitted return types of a proactive delivery strategy.
requirements.text:
```
DeliveryStrategy (interface)
└── deliver(context: DeliveryContext) → DeliveryOutcome | void
```

requirements.applies: The context given to a proactive delivery strategy.
requirements.text:
**DeliveryContext:**

```
DeliveryContext
├── kit: RoomKit                            # Framework instance
├── room_id: string                         # Target room
├── content: EventContent                   # Content to deliver
├── channel_id: string | null               # Transport/source channel
├── addressed_to: list<string> | null       # Intelligence solicitation (§19.3)
├── idempotency_key: string | null          # Publication/injection identity
├── session_id: string | null               # Exact realtime model session
├── instruction: bool                       # The application's direction (§10.1.1)
└── metadata: map<string, any>              # Delivery metadata
```

requirements.applies: The outcome returned by the public delivery call.
requirements.text: `RoomKit.deliver()` MUST return an observable outcome.

requirements.applies: Built-in delivery strategies distinguish queue acceptance from publication into the room.
requirements.text:
Built-in strategies
MUST distinguish `queued` (accepted by the delivery backend), `sent`
(published into the room

requirements.applies: Voice feature: a built-in strategy reports sent on provider acceptance.
requirements.text: or accepted by the voice provider),

requirements.applies: Built-in delivery strategies distinguish refusal, unavailability and failure.
requirements.text:
`blocked`
(explicit refusal), `unavailable` (destination cannot be reached), and
`failed` (execution error).

requirements.applies: The reason a strategy reports for an unsuccessful delivery.
requirements.text: Each unsuccessful outcome MUST carry a reason.

requirements.applies: An implementation may continue to accept custom strategies returning no outcome.
requirements.text: Custom strategies returning no outcome MAY remain usable,

requirements.applies: Reporting a custom strategy that gives no outcome.
requirements.text:
but their outcome
MUST be reported as `unknown`, never inferred as successful.

requirements.applies: The queue and event identifiers, duplicate flag and unavailable targets exposed where applicable in a delivery outcome.
requirements.text:
The outcome SHOULD expose the queue item id, committed event id, duplicate
indicator, unavailable target ids,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: preferred exposure of the injected sessions in a delivery outcome.
requirements.text: injected session ids

requirements.applies: Preferred exposure of applicable structured errors in a delivery outcome.
requirements.text:
and structured error
where applicable.

requirements.applies: Distinguishing transmission from completion of the agent's turn.
requirements.text: `sent` MUST NOT imply that the agent completed its turn.

requirements.applies: Optional exposure of the inbound result and delivery handle to observe completion.
requirements.text:
An implementation MAY expose the existing inbound result and delivery handle
to observe turn completion;

requirements.applies: Replaying a committed publication and observing whether its original turn completed.
requirements.text:
replaying a committed event does not establish
that its original turn completed.

requirements.applies: Preserving explicit addressing through synthetic text publication and storage.
requirements.text:
For synthetic text inbound, `addressed_to` MUST pass unchanged into the
existing publication pipeline and stored event, with all of §19.3's rules.

requirements.applies: Routing a synthetic text delivery whose intelligence address is null.
requirements.text: `null` retains routing,

requirements.applies: Broadcasting and storing a text delivery with an empty intelligence address.
requirements.text:
`[]` stores and broadcasts without soliciting an
intelligence channel,

requirements.applies: Resolving unknown explicitly addressed intelligence channels in synthetic text delivery.
requirements.text: and unknown targets MUST NOT select a substitute.

requirements.applies: Reporting an unreachable explicitly addressed channel after publication.
requirements.text:
An unavailable explicit target MUST be observable even if publication itself
succeeded.

requirements.applies: The permissions and visibility applying to addressed proactive text.
requirements.text: Addressing MUST NOT change visibility or bypass permissions.

requirements.applies: Selection of the transport for proactive delivery.
requirements.text: `channel_id` selects a transport;

requirements.applies: Optional transport-selection alias when channel_id names an intelligence channel.
requirements.text:
naming an intelligence channel there MAY
remain an alias for selecting the room's transport,

requirements.applies: Preserving the explicit intelligence address when the transport alias is offered.
requirements.text:
but MUST NOT silently
replace explicit `addressed_to`.

requirements.applies: How an application selects intelligence recipients in a delivery request.
requirements.text:
Applications select intelligence channels
with `addressed_to`,

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: how an application selects a particular provider session.
requirements.text:
and realtime provider sessions with `channel_id` and
`session_id`; the latter are not intelligence channel ids (§19.3).

requirements.applies: System authorship, origin and deferred inbound publication of a proactive text message.
requirements.text:
**The publication.** A text delivery enters its room as a message the
framework's own sender, `system`, writes on the transport that carries it,
through the inbound pipeline (§10.1), its delivery deferred:

requirements.applies: Solicitation and delivery to the correspondent without echoing the proactive text to its own transport.
requirements.text:
the room's agents
read it and answer, the transport is not delivered its own message (§7.5), and
the correspondent receives the agents' answer, never the content itself.

requirements.applies: Voice or realtime feature: preferring the room's voice transport when no channel is named.
requirements.text:
A
delivery naming no channel takes the room's voice transport (a channel of type
`voice`, `realtime_voice` or `realtime_audio_video`, or one hosting a realtime
model),

requirements.applies: Transport selection when no channel is named and there is no voice transport; intelligence channels do not qualify.
requirements.text:
else the first other transport bound to the room; an intelligence
channel attached with the transport category is none.

requirements.applies: The turn completion reported by a delivery that waits for the turn it requested.
requirements.text:
The call waits for the
turn its publication asks for, and `turn_complete` says the turn is over only
when it waited for it:

requirements.applies: When a batch is published by Queued on behalf of waiting callers.
requirements.text:
a strategy that delivers a batch for others (`Queued`)
reports `sent` at the publication.

requirements.applies: No transport is available to carry a proactive publication.
requirements.text:
Among the reasons its unsuccessful outcomes
carry: `no_transport` (no transport to carry it),

requirements.applies: Naming an unregistered or unbound channel in a proactive delivery.
requirements.text:
`channel_unavailable` (a
channel named that is not registered or the room does not bind, among
`unavailable_targets`),

requirements.applies: Publishing to an unavailable explicit intelligence target, including retryability.
requirements.text:
`addressed_targets_unavailable` (published, an
addressed target unreachable, the error not retryable),

requirements.applies: Naming a session on a channel with no realtime model.
requirements.text:
`session_requires_realtime` (a session named on a channel hosting no realtime
model),

requirements.applies: Reporting an invalid combination of session, channel and intelligence address.
requirements.text:
`invalid_session_target` (a session with no channel, or with an
address),

requirements.applies: Reporting the reason for a blank publication key.
requirements.text: `empty_idempotency_key`,

requirements.applies: Reporting an unaddressed proactive instruction.
requirements.text: `instruction_unaddressed`,

requirements.applies: Inbound rate limiting of a proactive publication.
requirements.text:
`rate_limited`
(the kit's inbound rate limit, §10.1 step 1),

requirements.applies: Reporting the room's or a hook's refusal of a publication.
requirements.text:
and the refusal of the room or
a hook (`source_unbound`, a hook's reason);

requirements.applies: Reporting a sent duplicate publication.
requirements.text:
a replay that is
`sent` carries `duplicate_publication`.

requirements.applies: Rejecting the reserved publication namespace on application event-write APIs.
requirements.text:
The doors that store a caller's event
as given, `send_event()`, `post()` and `commit_event()`, refuse a key in the
publication namespace as an invalid argument.

requirements.applies: Delivering an application direction through the text pipeline as an instruction.
requirements.text:
**Instruction delivery.** `instruction = true` delivers the content as the
application's direction to an agent rather than as something a participant
said. Through the text pipeline it is an `INSTRUCTION` event (§10.1.1), with
that section's rules:

requirements.applies: Validating the instruction's address and lack of a key before writing.
requirements.text:
it needs a non-empty `addressed_to` and no
`idempotency_key`, and is otherwise refused with `blocked` before anything is
written.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: injecting an instruction with system intent.
requirements.text:
Injected into a realtime session it takes the `system` intent
(§12.4).

requirements.applies: Applying the normal strategy, hooks and delivery backend to an instruction.
requirements.text:
The strategy, the delivery hooks and the delivery backend apply to
it unchanged.

requirements.applies: How an application should send content intended for an agent.
requirements.text:
Content an application produces for an agent (a background
task's result, a scheduled nudge) SHOULD be delivered this way, so it is
never stored, shown or read as a participant's words.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: the scope of injection with an explicit destination.
requirements.text: An explicit realtime destination MUST NOT expand to all sessions.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: unambiguous active-session selection when the ID is omitted.
requirements.text:
Without
`session_id`, an explicitly selected realtime channel requires one active
session; multiple sessions are ambiguous.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: pinning and rechecking the selected session around an idle wait.
requirements.text:
Strategies waiting for idle MUST
pin the selected session before waiting and verify it is still active before
injecting.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: refusal without text fallback when a pinned session or model disappears.
requirements.text:
A pinned delivery stays an injection: a session or a model gone by
the time it goes out refuses it, and it MUST NOT be published to the room
instead.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: reporting unsuccessful injection or a missing or replaced session.
requirements.text:
Missing or replaced sessions and injection errors MUST NOT report
success.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: optional room-wide injection when no explicit destination is selected.
requirements.text:
Unaddressed calls without explicit destinations MAY retain room-wide
realtime injection.

requirements.applies: A non-null intelligence address selects the text pipeline even when a realtime destination exists.
requirements.text:
A non-null intelligence address uses the text pipeline,
not a direct realtime injection;

requirements.applies: Combining an intelligence address with an explicit realtime session ID.
requirements.text: combining it with `session_id` is invalid.

requirements.applies: Refusing a blank idempotency key before any publication.
requirements.text:
**Idempotency boundary.** A blank key, empty or whitespace only, names no
publication: `deliver()` refuses it with `blocked`, reason
`empty_idempotency_key`, before anything is written.

requirements.applies: Identifying an existing publication in its room before resolving or changing the transport.
requirements.text:
A keyed text delivery's
key names one publication in its room, whatever transport carries it: it is
checked within the room, before a transport is resolved, and a match returns
the original outcome without publishing again. A retry that would resolve
another transport (one plugged in or detached since the first attempt) is
still that publication.

requirements.applies: The proactive publication key namespace excludes unrelated provider or sender keys.
requirements.text:
The key is the
application's, so the collision of two providers' keys that scopes an inbound
key by its channel (§13.4) does not arise, and only an event a proactive
delivery published counts as an earlier copy of it: the publication is stored
under `roomkit:publication:<key>`, a namespace no other door writes (§5.2),
and the lookup within the room reads that stored key only, so neither a
provider's message id nor a sender's message keyed alike blocks the
publication or stands in for it.

requirements.applies: The key exposed to delivery hooks.
requirements.text:
The delivery hooks are given the
application's key (§22.3).

requirements.applies: The room-scoped stored-key lookup under the publication lock across transport channels.
requirements.text:
Publication uses the ConversationStore's locked
publication (§13.4), the stored key looked up under the room lock within the
room, whatever channel committed it (`get_event_by_idempotency_key` with no
channel, §14.1; §14.3).

requirements.applies: Atomically looking up, selecting a transport and committing when a publication races a replay.
requirements.text:
The lookup, the transport's resolution and the
publication's commit run in one section under the room lock, so a concurrent
replay waits for the first and finds its key.

requirements.applies: Off-lock callers enter in order and callers already holding the room lock reuse their section.
requirements.text:
Every caller takes that section,
whatever work of the room it runs in: an off-lock hook's body or a parse
(§9.5.1) waits for the lock as any caller does, behind the calls queued for it
before; a caller that holds the lock already (a locked hook) runs it within
its own section.

requirements.applies: Outcome and storage on expiry of the publication's process_timeout while awaiting the lock.
requirements.text:
The wait for the lock is bounded by `process_timeout`
(§13.6): past it the delivery is `blocked`, reason `process_timeout`, and
nothing is written.

requirements.applies: Rechecking a detached transport under the lock and later retrying with the same key.
requirements.text:
A transport detached while the delivery waits for the
lock is seen by the section's check: the delivery is `unavailable`, reason
`channel_unavailable`, and nothing is stored under its key, so a retry once
the transport is back is a first publication.

requirements.applies: Publishing without an admission ticket under the room lock.
requirements.text:
The publication's call is code
under the section's lock (§9.5.1, Reentrance): it takes no admission ticket,
so it never waits behind an arrival whose off-lock check holds one,

requirements.applies: Pre-commit parse and hooks, including reentrant room changes or nested publications.
requirements.text:
and what
it runs before its commit, its transport's parse and its hooks, the off-lock
ones among them, runs under that lock, where a change of the room they make
takes the lock again at once and a call they make into the room commits
within the section, ahead of the publication.

requirements.applies: Later cascade passes reacquire the room lock after publication releases it.
requirements.text:
Its cascade's later passes, an
agent's answer among them, take the lock as any section does once the section
has released it.

requirements.applies: At most one trigger event per retained publication key.
requirements.text:
Replays, including concurrent
ones, MUST NOT create a second trigger event while the key is retained.

requirements.applies: Replaying a publication after its body or address changes.
requirements.text:
The
same key identifies the same publication regardless of subsequent body or
address changes.

requirements.applies: Publication-key retention by an in-memory or durable store until the event or key is removed.
requirements.text:
Retention follows the store: memory does not survive
restart; durable stores retain committed keys until the corresponding
event/key is removed.

requirements.applies: A distributed deployment's selection of a shared store and corresponding lock manager.
requirements.text:
Distributed use requires a shared store and a lock
manager appropriate to that store.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: reserving a keyed attempt atomically before provider submission.
requirements.text:
**Realtime injection identity.** A keyed proactive voice injection MUST reserve
its attempt atomically in the ConversationStore before calling the provider.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: room, channel, session and application key identify an independent destination.
requirements.text:
Its identity is the tuple `(room_id, channel_id, session_id, idempotency_key)`;
different sessions are independent destinations.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: reusing a recorded outcome unless non-submission and retryability are established.
requirements.text:
A repeated identity MUST reuse
its recorded outcome without reinjection, unless the previous attempt explicitly
established that nothing was submitted and that retry is allowed.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: refusing the same identity for different effective text.
requirements.text:
Reusing a voice
identity for different effective text MUST be refused as an idempotency conflict.
This does not change the text publication replay semantics above.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: persistence of the reservation, unique attempt token and outcome.
requirements.text: The store MUST persist the reservation, a unique attempt token and its outcome.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: conditional claim and completion writes, including stale owners.
requirements.text:
Claiming a retry and completing an attempt MUST use atomic conditional writes;
an old owner MUST NOT overwrite another attempt.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: reservation retention beyond queue acknowledgement.
requirements.text:
The reservation MUST outlive
queue acknowledgement.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: retention by process-local and durable stores including room deletion.
requirements.text:
A process-local store provides process-local retention;
durable stores MUST preserve reservations across restart until the room is deleted.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: refusing a keyed send on a store without reservation support.
requirements.text: A store without this capability MUST refuse keyed voice injection before sending.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: an uncertain attempt remains protected across expiry or recovery.
requirements.text: No expiry or abandoned-claim recovery may authorize an uncertain injection again.

requirements.applies: Realtime voice injection: a caller may wait for the unresolved attempt's owner through the lock manager.
requirements.text:
A reservation without a final outcome is an unresolved attempt. A concurrent
