anything is built.

requirements.applies: Exceeding a frontmatter bound prevents parsing a local skill and verification of served content.
requirements.text:
Past a bound, the skill cannot be parsed (Section 24.5),
and a served skill's content fails its check (Section 24.7).

requirements.applies: An implementation may read local non-YAML frontmatter or local skills without a YAML reader line by line.
requirements.text:
A host's own skill whose frontmatter is not YAML, or is read without a YAML
reader, MAY be read line by line,

requirements.applies: A line-oriented reader recognizes top-level fields and excludes nested fields as top-level keys.
requirements.text:
each `key: value` line at the top level a
field; a line indented under a key is not one.

requirements.applies: A line-oriented reader must support block-item and single-line flow lists.
requirements.text:
That reading MUST keep both
YAML list forms: a key alone on its line followed by `- item` lines, as in the
example, and `[a, b]` whole on the key's line.

requirements.applies: For valid YAML the alternate reading must preserve all tool gates and prerequisites.
requirements.text:
Of a frontmatter that is also
YAML, it MUST NOT gate or require less than the YAML reading does.

requirements.applies: Both readers reject non-text gate or prerequisite values, lists containing non-text items and incomplete line-oriented parses.
requirements.text:
Whichever
reader, an `allowed_tools` or `requires` that is neither a text nor a list of
texts, or that a line-by-line reading cannot read whole (a list spread over
several lines, a block scalar, a line under the key that is not a `- item`),
means the skill cannot be parsed: a skill read without what it gates hands
the model, before any activation, the tools it was meant to keep closed.

requirements.applies: In-memory registration accepts skills supplied by the host.
requirements.text:
A host that builds its skills elsewhere (a store, a marketplace) registers them
with `add`,

requirements.applies: A narrowed copy resolves included skills, including discovered but not yet loaded skills, and preserves marks unless asked otherwise.
requirements.text:
and one that narrows a registry for an agent copies it with
`copy`: a copy finds every skill the source finds, a skill discovered but not
yet loaded included, and keeps the source's marks unless asked not to.

requirements.applies: A channel retains its original registry and accepts a per-turn registry through per-turn configuration.
requirements.text:
A channel's registry is the one it was built with. A host whose skills depend
on the person a turn is for (their own skills beside the agent's) gives each
turn a registry of its own through the channel's per-turn configuration
(Appendix A.9, per-turn settings).

requirements.applies: The per-turn registry controls the manifest, activation, reference and script tools and skill gating.
A per-turn registry is isolated from the channel and other turns, including concurrent rooms.
requirements.text:
it MUST NOT be installed on the channel nor read by another turn,
so a channel that serves one agent in several rooms serves each person their
own skills, concurrent turns included.

requirements.applies: A turn without a registry override uses the channel's registry.
requirements.text:
A turn whose configuration gives none
reads the channel's.

requirements.applies: The override requires a registry at channel construction, including an empty one; a channel without one declares no skill tools and warns when ignoring an override.
requirements.text:
A turn's registry is read only on a channel built with
one, an empty one included: a channel built without skills declares no skill
tools, and ignores a turn's registry with a warning.

requirements.applies: An active skill absent from a turn's registry leaves room activation and a later activation delivers the body again.
requirements.text:
Activation stays the
conversation's (Section 24.4): a skill active in the room that the turn's
registry does not hold leaves the room's active skills, as one its registry no
longer serves does, since its instructions cannot be in front of the model; its
next activation delivers its body again.

requirements.applies: The system prompt includes the XML skills manifest.
requirements.text:
Skills are injected into the AI agent's system prompt via `to_prompt_xml()`.
The agent can then select and apply skills based on the user's request. A

requirements.text:
skill a host marks unavailable is listed there with its reason, and a registry
whose every skill is unavailable still has something to tell: the prompt
carries the reasons and the activation tools are declared, on every path, so
the model says why instead of guessing.

requirements.applies: Each text activation checks prerequisites, including reactivation.
requirements.text:
A skill's `requires` is checked by
every activation, on a text turn

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: each realtime activation checks prerequisites against the conversation's tool catalogue.
requirements.text: as on a realtime session, with one rule:

requirements.applies: Activation checks declared tools, including channel and orchestration tools, after policy and before applying the candidate's skill gate.
requirements.text:
against every tool the conversation declares, the channel's own and what
orchestration set up included, once its tool policy is applied and skill
gating aside (the skill opens what it gates).

requirements.applies: Prerequisites use exact tool names unless the host supplies its matcher.
requirements.text:
A `requires` name is an exact
tool name unless the registry's host says how its names are served
(`requires_match`: a hub served by any tool named `<hub>_*`, say),

requirements.applies: A successful activation hands over the schemas of the tools serving the prerequisites.
requirements.text:
and an
activation hands over the schemas of the tools that serve it.

requirements.text:
A tool the
policy denies is no tool the skill can use: the activation is refused
(`Required tools not available: <names>`) and never hands over that tool's
schema, to the model or to a hook.

requirements.applies: An unavailable skill cannot be activated and marking it keeps its gates closed.
requirements.text:
A skill marked unavailable can never be
activated, so the tools it gates stay closed (marked while the registry holds
it): marking it does not open them,

requirements.applies: A required tool held only by an unavailable gate is missing and a direct call explains the restriction.
requirements.text:
a required tool only such a gate holds is
missing, and a call to it reads that a skill not available here gates it.

requirements.applies: An activated skill opens its pattern even when an unavailable skill gates that same pattern.
requirements.text:

skill gating the same pattern does not hold it closed (`closed_tool_names`).

requirements.applies: The same skill gating determines access at both tool doors.
requirements.text: `gated_tool_names` is the one reading of skill gating both doors use.

requirements.applies: Loading a skill activates it for the conversation across multiple turns.
requirements.text:
Loading a skill's body is an **activation**, and an activation is scoped to the
**conversation**, not to the turn that made it. A model working across several
turns on the same task is following the same rules throughout; a skill that
silently stops applying between two turns is a skill the model cannot rely on.

requirements.applies: The model retains an active skill's instructions for the duration of activation and activation reporting reflects their presence.
requirements.text:
An implementation MUST keep an active skill's instructions reachable by the
model for as long as the skill is active. It MUST NOT report a skill as active
while its instructions are absent from the model's context.

requirements.applies: An implementation may deliver instructions through the system prompt.
requirements.text:
The instructions MAY travel through the system prompt rather than through the
activation tool's result.

requirements.applies: On turns rebuilt from stored events, the system prompt is the recommended carrier of instructions.
requirements.text:
This is RECOMMENDED where the context is rebuilt per
turn from stored events: tool results that do not survive that rebuild force the
model to re-activate — and re-pay the full body — on every turn, whereas the
system prompt is composed fresh each turn and can carry the body once.

requirements.applies: When the prompt carries the body, repeat activation should answer with a short acknowledgement.
requirements.text:
Where the
body is carried this way, the activation tool SHOULD answer subsequent calls with
a short acknowledgement instead of the body,

requirements.applies: A repeated activation acknowledgement must say the instructions are already in force.
requirements.text:
and that acknowledgement MUST state
that the instructions are already in force.

requirements.applies: Large-result and context-compression mechanisms must preserve active instructions whole.
requirements.text:
An active skill's instructions MUST NOT be truncated, evicted, or summarized by
a large-result or context-compression mechanism. Such mechanisms exist for
*data*, which can be paginated or condensed without changing what it means;
binding rules reduced to a preview are no longer binding rules. Skill

requirements.applies: Skill reference data remains subject to ordinary large-result and context-compression mechanisms.
requirements.text: *references* are data and remain subject to those mechanisms.

requirements.applies: Activation is isolated by conversation scope even when a channel serves several conversations.
requirements.text:
Activation state is per (implementation-defined) conversation scope — a room, a
session — and is never global to a channel serving several conversations. An

requirements.applies: An implementation may limit simultaneous active skills.
requirements.text: implementation MAY bound the number of simultaneously active skills;

requirements.applies: Where active skills are bounded, retiring a skill makes its next activation deliver the body again.
requirements.text:
when it
does, retiring a skill MUST be equivalent to it never having been activated, so
that a later activation delivers the body again.

requirements.applies: A lost local activation record requires delivery of the body again.
requirements.text:
An implementation whose activation record is lost (process restart, a channel
object replaced) MUST fall back to delivering the body: losing the record and
losing the prompt block are the same event, and the model is never left holding
an acknowledgement without rules.

requirements.applies: A standalone turn omits active instructions and activating in it always returns the body.
requirements.text:
A turn that stands alone (Section 10.1.1) carries no active skill in its prompt,
so an activation in it MUST deliver the body, the skill active or not.

requirements.applies: Standalone activation reads stored activations first and persists its activation for the next room-aware turn.
requirements.text:
What it
activates counts for the conversation all the same, with what the room's stored
rows show activated, which the turn reads first, none of it reaching its prompt:
the next turn that reads the room carries the instructions.

requirements.applies: Restoration uses the TOOL_CALL_END arguments actually served, including a before-tool-use rewrite.
requirements.text:
A stored row shows
the skill its call ran with, its `TOOL_CALL_END`'s arguments, a `BEFORE_TOOL_USE`
rewrite included: those are the rules the model received.

requirements.applies: Activated tools stay open in the same conversation while the skill is active.
requirements.text:
Tool gating (Section 21) follows the same scope: tools revealed by activating a
skill stay revealed while the skill is active.

requirements.applies: A served skill's instructions stay separate from the binding rules of local skills.
requirements.text:
A skill an MCP server serves follows this lifecycle with what Section 24.7
adds: its instructions are data set apart as that server's, never among the
binding rules of the host's own skills,

requirements.applies: Lost served activation is never restored from stored history.
requirements.text:
and a lost record of its activation
is not restored from the stored history.

requirements.applies: Unknown skill activation names the missing skill and hints at matching callable tools.
requirements.text:
An activation that finds no skill under its name, when that name matches tools
the turn may call (a model that took the `spotify_play` tool for a "spotify"
skill), answers with the skill's absence and names those tools,

requirements.applies: Once served, the missing-skill hint replaces the reveal window, omitting already declared tools, for the rest of the session.
requirements.text:
and reveals
them as `find_tools` reveals its matches (the window swapped, what is declared
anyway left out), for the rest of the session, once the call is served:

requirements.applies: A hook-blocked missing-skill activation reveals no tools.
requirements.text:
an
`ON_TOOL_CALL` block reveals nothing.

requirements.applies: Realtime feature: a missing-skill activation returns the same answer and reveals tools as on text channels.
requirements.text:
The same answer and the same reveal on
every door, text or realtime;

requirements.applies: Where matching tools are reached through call_tool, including a realtime provider with fixed tools, the hint identifies that gateway.
requirements.text:
where the tools are reached through `call_tool`,
the answer says so.

requirements.applies: The missing-skill hint matches the current turn's tools and excludes channel-served tools.
requirements.text:
Only the turn's own catalogue is matched, never the tools
the channel serves itself.

requirements.applies: An unavailable skill returns its reason without a matching-tool hint.
requirements.text:
A skill that exists but is unavailable answers with
its reason and no such hint.

requirements.applies: Invalid or unparseable deployed skills are deployment failures.
requirements.text:
A skill that cannot be parsed, or whose metadata does not validate, is a
deployment error rather than a runtime condition. The two have opposite
remedies. A skill that exists but cannot be used in the present context is a
fact the model can be told and can work around; a malformed `SKILL.md` is a
mistake in what someone deployed, and nothing the model does at runtime will
repair it.

requirements.applies: Loading failures cannot silently omit a skill.
requirements.text:
An implementation MUST NOT silently omit a skill it failed to load. Omission is
the worst outcome available: the catalogue simply does not list the capability,
the model is never told it was meant to exist, and the agent answers as though
nothing were missing. Nobody reading the conversation sees a gap either. The
error surfaces much later, as an agent that inexplicably cannot do the thing it
was configured to do, by which point the frontmatter typo that caused it is far
out of view.

requirements.applies: Default discovery stops at the first unparseable skill.
requirements.text: Discovery MUST therefore fail by default on the first skill it cannot load, and

requirements.applies: Default discovery identifies the failed skill and gives the reason.
requirements.text: MUST report which skill failed and why.

requirements.applies: An unscannable directory is reported as a discovery failure.
requirements.text:
A directory that cannot be scanned is
the same class of failure and MUST be reported the same way: returning an empty
count for a path that does not exist is, to the caller, indistinguishable from a
directory that is genuinely empty.

requirements.applies: An implementation may offer a discovery mode that logs failures and continues.
requirements.text:
An implementation MAY offer a mode that logs each failure and continues. It is
the right behaviour where skills come from a source the deployment does not
control and a partial catalogue beats no service at all.

requirements.applies: Lenient discovery requires an explicit caller opt-in.
requirements.text:
That mode MUST be
requested explicitly by the caller and MUST NOT be the default,

requirements.applies: Lenient discovery logs the reason for every skipped skill.
requirements.text:
and every
skipped skill MUST be logged with the reason it was skipped.

requirements.applies: Discovery commits the entire discovered set or preserves the preceding registry.
requirements.text:
Discovery MUST NOT leave the registry partially populated. Whatever the outcome,
the registry a caller observes afterwards MUST be either the state that preceded
the call or the state with every discovered skill present. A half-filled
catalogue reproduces exactly the silent gap this section exists to prevent, and
does so at the moment the caller has most reason to believe the opposite.

requirements.applies: The fully rendered XML manifest, including escaping, wrappers, reasons and served origins, permits exactly 65,536 Unicode characters and no more.
requirements.text:
The registry's manifest, which every system prompt carries (§24.3), MUST NOT
pass 65,536 Unicode characters in its final rendered XML, after escaping,
including unavailable reasons, wrappers and served origins. Exactly 65,536
characters is permitted.

requirements.applies: Every addition, replacement and registry-producing operation checks the prospective manifest before committing or returning, with a manifest-size error for excess.
requirements.text:
Operations that add or replace manifest content, or
return a new registry, MUST validate the complete prospective manifest and fail
with the manifest-size error before committing or returning an oversized result:
discovery, registration, in-memory addition, an unavailable mark, a copy that
removes unlisted marks, and registration or fetching of served entries included. A

requirements.applies: A failed copy preserves the source registry.
requirements.text: failed copy leaves its source unchanged;

requirements.text:
replacement is checked after removing
the replaced name's old marks, not with both versions temporarily present.

requirements.applies: Rejection of a served listing or fetch preserves the shared catalogue.
requirements.text:
For served skills, a rejected listing or fetch MUST NOT change the shared
catalog either.

requirements.applies: A local refusal reason that would overflow leaves the local record unchanged and forbids serving stale cached content.
requirements.text:
Following a catalog update already accepted by another registry
is a local operation: if recording its refusal reason exceeds this registry's
bound, the read fails before changing its local record and MUST NOT serve its
old cached skill or file.

requirements.applies: A failed local follow does not undo a previously accepted shared update or verification retirement.
requirements.text:
It does not undo the earlier shared update or a
verification retirement (§24.7).

requirements.applies: When callers share mutable metadata, oversized rendering fails without modifying caller objects.
requirements.text:
An implementation exposing mutable metadata shared with its caller MUST also
reject an oversized manifest at rendering, without changing the caller's
objects. Direct writes through such aliases are not registry transactions.

requirements.applies: Removing or hiding entries may partially repair oversized state introduced by callers.
requirements.text:
Operations that only remove or hide entries MAY reduce an oversized state
introduced through external aliases in several steps; they need not reject a
partial repair,

requirements.applies: A partially repaired manifest still fails to render while oversized.
requirements.text: but rendering MUST still reject any oversized result.

requirements.applies: Replacing the offending entry or returning a fitting subset can succeed without repairing the source registry.
requirements.text:
A caller
can also replace an offending entry or return a fitting subset copy without
repairing its source. A manifest without a bound grows each prompt, and every
turn's cost, with each skill a deployment adds.

requirements.applies: Resolution of every bundled reference and script is confined to its skill directory.
requirements.text:
A skill's references and scripts are addressed by name, and the name is chosen
by the model. Resolution MUST be confined to the skill's own directory.

requirements.applies: A name filter alone does not establish containment; resolution follows links and verifies the destination remains inside the directory.
requirements.text:
Filtering the name does not achieve that, and an implementation MUST NOT rely on
name filtering alone. A name containing no traversal sequence, no separator and
no drive letter still leaves the directory when a symbolic link bearing that
name sits inside it. An implementation MUST resolve the candidate path, with
links followed, and MUST verify that the result is still inside the skill
directory, rejecting it otherwise. Containment is a property of where a path
ends up, not of how it is spelled.

requirements.applies: File reads verify the opened regular file corresponds to the checked path within the skill directory.
requirements.text:
The file an implementation reads MUST be the one whose path it checked. It
opens the resolved path and verifies the open file before reading it: a
regular file, which the path resolved again still names, inside the
directory.

requirements.applies: Where system-provided open-file paths are inspected, the path must be readable and inside the directory.
requirements.text:
Where the implementation reads the path the system gives an open
file, that path MUST be inside the directory, and a file whose path cannot be
read there is refused.

requirements.applies: The implementation reads the checked open file without reopening it by name.
requirements.text:
It MUST NOT read the checked path again by its name,
so that a file swapped for a link out of the directory between the check and
the read is refused, not read.

requirements.applies: SKILL.md must itself resolve to a regular file inside the skill directory and be read via the verified open file.
requirements.text:
A skill's `SKILL.md` is held to the same rules:
once its links are followed, it MUST be a regular file inside the skill's
directory, read through the file its check opened.

requirements.applies: Path normalization precedes validation.
requirements.text:
Names MUST be normalized before they are inspected, so that a character which is
not the ASCII separator but normalizes onto it cannot pass a check performed on
the raw string.

requirements.applies: All absolute path spellings recognized by the host are rejected.
requirements.text:
Absolute paths MUST be rejected, in every spelling the host
platform recognises.

requirements.applies: A delegated script is verified and rejected on boundary failure before the host executor is invoked.
requirements.text:
The requirement does not lapse where execution policy — sandboxing, timeouts,
permitted interpreters — is delegated to the integrator. *What* runs is part of
the skill boundary; *how* it runs is not. An implementation that delegates
execution MUST resolve the script name under these same rules and MUST reject a
name that fails them before any integrator-supplied executor is invoked, and

requirements.applies: Where execution is delegated, the executor should receive the resolved script path.
requirements.text:
SHOULD make the resolved path available to that executor. A check every
integrator is expected to rediscover is a check some integrator will omit.

requirements.applies: An MCP server may implement the Skills extension by listing skills, fetching entries by URI and serving individual files as resources.
requirements.text:
An MCP server MAY serve skills beside its tools under the MCP Skills
extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`, SEP-2640): it lists them with
`skills/list`, answers `skills/get` for one by the URI of its `SKILL.md`, and
serves each file of a skill as a resource read with `resources/read`.

skill format is the one Section 24.1 reads. This section is what a registry,
and every channel serving its skills, adds for such a skill; a skill the host
deploys itself is unchanged.

requirements.applies: §25 Image Generation; the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
An agent that can describe a picture cannot draw one. Image synthesis is a
capability a small number of models hold, and the model holding a conversation
is rarely one of them — so it is specified here as its own provider surface,
the way speech-to-text and text-to-speech already are, and not as an extension
of the conversational response.

requirements.applies: Image generation has a provider interface distinct from the conversational AI provider.
requirements.text:
An implementation MUST expose image generation through a provider interface
distinct from the AI provider interface,

requirements.applies: The two providers can use independent vendors, credentials and objects.
requirements.text:
and MUST NOT require that the two be
served by the same vendor, credential, or object.

requirements.applies: An agent using one conversational provider can generate images through another.
requirements.text:
An agent conversing through
one provider MUST be able to draw through another, exactly as it transcribes
through a third.

This is a normative requirement rather than an implementation preference. Image
generation reached as a mode of the conversational response inherits that
response's provider: the capability then exists only for the subset of
conversations already held by a model that draws, and acquiring it means
migrating the conversation. The decoupled form is what makes the capability
available to every conversation, and it is the property this section protects.

requirements.applies: The conversational response type retains its content contract when image generation is available.
requirements.text:
An implementation MUST NOT widen the conversational response type to carry
generated images. `AIResponse.content` is read by every consumer of the
framework; turning it into a union imposes a migration on all of them for a
capability that two providers offer.

requirements.applies: Generation returns exactly the requested number of results or raises.
requirements.text:
`generate` MUST return exactly `n` results or raise. Returning fewer without
error leaves the caller to discover the shortfall by indexing, which it will do
in production and not in testing.

requirements.text: `size` is a `"WIDTHxHEIGHT"` string, or null for the provider's default.

requirements.applies: The provider translates portable pixel sizes to its native geometry and hides native geometry conventions from the caller.
requirements.text:
A
provider whose API expresses geometry differently — an aspect ratio and a
resolution tier, say — MUST translate, and MUST NOT require the caller to know
which form its vendor speaks.

requirements.applies: The provider raises when it cannot honour the requested size.
requirements.text:
A provider that cannot honour a requested size
MUST raise rather than silently substitute another: an image of the wrong
geometry is a failure the caller can neither see nor correct.

requirements.applies: A request for more than one image produces distinct results.
requirements.text: `n` greater than one MUST produce `n` distinct results.

requirements.applies: A provider without a native batch parameter handles the requested count with concurrent calls.
requirements.text:
A provider whose API
has no batch parameter satisfies this with concurrent calls: the alternative —
honouring `n` on some providers and refusing it on others — leaves a parameter
in the interface that a caller cannot use without first knowing which provider
is behind it, which is the coupling this section exists to remove.

Omitted options inherit
provider defaults;

options MUST remain valid.

requirements.applies: A transport failure is retryable only when the request never left because the connection could not be made.
A timeout or connection lost after sending leaves a final ambiguous outcome.
requirements.text:
a timeout or a connection lost once the request went out is ambiguous,
and final.

requirements.applies: An image delivered in a form the provider cannot return has a final billed failure.
requirements.text:
An image the vendor delivered in a form the provider cannot return
was generated and billed: that failure is final too.

requirements.applies: Independent concurrent generation calls should settle so that their outcomes can be collected.
requirements.text:
Independent concurrent calls SHOULD settle so their outcomes can
be collected.

requirements.applies: Cancelling generation propagates cancellation as cancellation.
requirements.text: Cancellation MUST remain cancellation,

requirements.applies: Generation makes already received outcomes accessible through an optional asynchronous progress callback when cancelled.
requirements.text:
with already received
outcomes accessible through an optional asynchronous progress callback.

requirements.applies: ImageResult exposes encoded image data and its media type.
requirements.text:
```
ImageResult
├── data: string                              # data:<mime_type>;base64,<payload>
├── mime_type: string                         # Media type of the payload
```

requirements.applies: ImageResult exposes an optional revised prompt.
requirements.text:
```
├── revised_prompt: string | null             # Prompt as the model rewrote it, if reported
```

requirements.applies: ImageResult exposes a usage map for generation counters.
requirements.text:
```
└── usage: map<string, any>                   # Token counters (Section 25.5)
```

requirements.applies: Generated image data is always a data URI.
requirements.text: `data` MUST be a data URI, always,

requirements.applies: The generated data URI media type equals the result's mime_type.
requirements.text:
and its media type MUST equal `mime_type`.
The alternative — a field documented as "a data URI or bare base64" — forces
every consumer to sniff the value before it can use it, and one consumer will
sniff it wrong.

requirements.applies: Ordinary image message content and image message parts accept a data URI, so generated image data can enter a room without conversion.
requirements.text:
The invariant also makes the result directly usable: a data URI
is what image message content and image message parts already accept, so a
generated image enters a room,

requirements.applies: A generated data URI can be used directly as an image reference in a subsequent edit.
requirements.text:
or returns as a reference for a subsequent
edit, without conversion.

requirements.applies: The provider fetches any returned URL and encodes the image bytes in the result.
requirements.text:
A provider whose API returns a fetchable URL rather than bytes MUST retrieve
the bytes and encode them. Such URLs expire, and a result that decays into a
dead link some time after it was returned is not a result.

requirements.applies: An unreported revised prompt is null.
requirements.text: `revised_prompt` is null where the vendor reports none.

requirements.applies: The provider does not substitute the original prompt for an unreported revised prompt.
requirements.text:
An implementation MUST
NOT substitute the original prompt for it: the field exists to show the caller
what the model actually drew from, and echoing the input back conceals exactly
the divergence it exists to reveal.

requirements.applies: A result may expose original vendor identifiers and usage, effective parameters, actual dimensions and grounding attribution.
requirements.text:
Results MAY carry a vendor request or interaction identifier, the vendor's
original usage report, effective parameters, actual dimensions where reported,
and grounding attribution.

requirements.applies: Shared batch usage appears once with explicit scope.
requirements.text:
Usage shared by a batch MUST be represented once,
with its scope explicit;

requirements.applies: Shared batch usage is not divided into invented per-image measurements.
requirements.text:
it MUST NOT be divided into invented per-image
measurements.

requirements.applies: Original image metadata excludes inline image payloads.
requirements.text: Original metadata MUST omit inline image payloads

requirements.applies: Original image metadata excludes secrets.
requirements.text: and secrets.

requirements.applies: A generation progress callback may receive individual call outcomes or preview images.
requirements.text: A progress callback MAY receive individual call outcomes or preview images.

requirements.applies: A provider offering image previews identifies them separately from final results.
requirements.text: Previews MUST be distinguished from final results.

requirements.applies: Delivering image progress does not establish vendor cancellation or a refund.
requirements.text:
Callback delivery does not
imply vendor cancellation or a refund,

requirements.applies: Failure to deliver a progress outcome does not trigger another generation.
requirements.text:
and failure to deliver an outcome MUST
NOT trigger another generation.

requirements.applies: A caller edits through reference_images on generate rather than a separate public edit method.
requirements.text:
Editing — an image and a prompt in, an image out — is expressed through
`reference_images` on `generate`, not through a second method.

requirements.applies: The provider hides its vendor's distinction between editing with references and prompt-only generation endpoints.
requirements.text:
The distinction is the vendor's, not the caller's: one API takes reference
images as ordinary content on the same endpoint, another routes them to a
separate one. A provider MUST absorb that difference.

requirements.applies: Providers that cannot edit report supports_editing as false.
requirements.text:
A provider that cannot
edit MUST report `supports_editing` as false

requirements.applies: Providers that cannot edit reject nonempty references instead of ignoring them.
requirements.text:
and MUST raise when
`reference_images` is non-empty, rather than generating from the prompt alone —
a caller that asked for an edit and silently received a fresh image has no
signal that the reference was dropped.

requirements.applies: A provider may expose continuity through an earlier interaction identifier.
requirements.text: A provider MAY support continuity through a previous interaction identifier.

requirements.applies: The caller authorizes access to an earlier interaction used for continuity.
requirements.text: The caller remains responsible for authorizing access to that interaction.

requirements.applies: A stateful provider exposes an explicit choice that lets the caller disable remote history storage.
requirements.text:
A stateful provider MUST expose an explicit storage choice so applications can
disable remote history retention.

requirements.applies: A stateful provider may retain its default storage behaviour when the caller omits the choice.
requirements.text:
Omitting this choice MAY preserve the
provider default;

requirements.applies: Applications cannot assume that omitting the storage choice makes generation stateless.
requirements.text: applications MUST NOT assume that omitted means stateless.

requirements.applies: An implementation honours requests for external-search grounding only on models that support it.
requirements.text: Grounding with external search MAY be requested only on compatible models;

requirements.applies: Where external-search grounding is supported, available citations and search-suggestion metadata are retained for the caller to display under provider requirements.
requirements.text:
available citations and search-suggestion metadata MUST be retained for the
caller to display according to the provider's requirements.

requirements.applies: A generation reports the text and image consumption its vendor meters separately.
requirements.text:
A generation reports what it consumed. An image and the text around it are
metered separately by the vendors that meter them at all, so the counters stay
apart rather than collapsing into one number:

requirements.applies: The image generation usage model has separate integer input and output fields for text and image tokens.
requirements.text:
```
usage
├── input_tokens: int                         # Text input tokens
├── input_image_tokens: int                   # Reference-image input tokens
├── output_tokens: int                        # Text output tokens, where the model emits any
└── output_image_tokens: int                  # Generated-image tokens
```

requirements.applies: A reported generation token belongs to exactly one counter.
requirements.text: The counters MUST be disjoint: a token appears under exactly one of them.

requirements.applies: When image tokens are included in a total, subtract them to report the text count.
requirements.text:
Where a vendor reports image tokens as a subset of a total, an implementation
MUST subtract them before reporting the text counter, so a consumer summing
the counters counts each token once. Without that guarantee the counters cannot
be combined at all, and the breakdown is worth less than the single total it
replaced.

requirements.applies: Unreported token counters are absent, preserving the distinction from a reported zero.
requirements.text:
Counters a vendor does not report are absent, not zero: a reported zero and an
unreported quantity are different claims, and only one of them is safe to add
up.

Usage is a report, not a price. What a generation costs depends on how its
vendor meters it — per token in some lineups, a flat amount per image in
others, varying by resolution or quality — and on commercial terms no
specification can observe.

requirements.applies: An implementation may expose a price list for image generation.
requirements.text: An implementation MAY carry a price list

requirements.applies: An implementation may derive a cost from image-generation counters, subject to the turn-budget rule in section 6.4.
requirements.text:
and MAY
derive a cost from these counters; neither the shape of such a list nor the
arithmetic over it is specified here, beyond what a turn's cost budget counts
(Section 6.4). What is specified is that the counters
mean what they say, so that whatever does price them has something unambiguous
to price.

requirements.applies: The offline image and conversation catalogues have disjoint sets of model identifiers.
requirements.text:
An image catalogue is a set disjoint from the conversational one: a model that
draws is not a model that converses, and neither list contains an id belonging
to the other.

requirements.applies: A single catalogue enumeration does not merge image and conversational models.
requirements.text:
An implementation MUST NOT merge the two into the response of a single
enumeration. Merging saves no maintenance — the entries are written once
either way — while obliging every consumer of the conversational catalogue,
including those populating a model field for a conversational agent, to filter
a class of models it can never use.

requirements.applies: Image catalogue entries should include a capability tag identifying image generation.
requirements.text:
Entries SHOULD nevertheless carry a
capability tag identifying them as image-generating, so a consumer that
deliberately combines the lists can still tell them apart.

requirements.applies: An image catalogue entry may expose structured capabilities for its model.
requirements.text:
Catalogue entries MAY carry structured image capabilities, including accepted
controls and values, geometry constraints, reference limits, continuity,
masking, search, and retirement dates.

requirements.applies: Unknown image-model capabilities stay unknown rather than being inferred from another model.
requirements.text:
Unknown capabilities MUST remain unknown
rather than being inferred from another model in the same vendor's lineup.

requirements.applies: Image generation is not a stage of the inbound or broadcast pipeline.
requirements.text: Image generation is not a pipeline stage

requirements.applies: Image generation introduces no hook trigger.
requirements.text: and defines no hook triggers.

requirements.applies: A caller such as a tool handler or application invokes the generation service.
requirements.text:
It is
invoked by a caller — a tool handler, an application —

requirements.applies: Generated image content enters a room as ordinary message content subject to the existing inbound and broadcast rules.
requirements.text:
and its result enters a
room as ordinary message content, which the inbound and broadcast pipelines
(Section 10) already govern. Introducing a parallel path for images would
duplicate ordering, permission, and visibility rules that Section 7 and
Section 10 state once.

Video generation, image *understanding* (already covered by multimodal message
parts) and avatar synthesis (Section 12) are outside this section.

requirements.applies: §26.1: what a Level 0 implementation supports, the features listed (each owned by its section) and the hook triggers and framework events the table names for each step or operation; a feature of a higher level, or one no level lists, owes its own section's, only where an implementation provides it. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A conforming implementation MUST support:

- Room model with lifecycle (ACTIVE, PAUSED, CLOSED, ARCHIVED), including
  refusing new events at every entry point once the status says so (Section 5.1)
- Room timers (auto-pause, auto-close, resume on activity; Section 5.1)
- RoomEvent with all EventType values and all EventContent types
- Sequential event indexing
- Channel interface (handle_inbound, deliver, on_event, capabilities)
- ChannelBinding with access, mute, and visibility
- Permission enforcement (Section 7.5)
- Hook engine with SYNC and ASYNC execution
- BEFORE_BROADCAST and AFTER_BROADCAST hooks with HookResult
- InjectedEvent delivery, whatever the hook's action
- Event chain depth tracking and limiting
- Inbound processing pipeline (Section 10.1); its identity steps belong to
  higher levels, identity resolution (step 5) to Level 1 and identity
  verification (step 5b) to Level 2, and an implementation skips the step of
  a feature it does not provide
- Broadcast pipeline (Section 10.2)
- Reentry passes (response events re-enter the pipeline as commit passes)
- Inbound room routing (pluggable)
- Room-level locking
- ConversationStore interface with in-memory implementation
- Content transcoding (at least text fallback)
- The hook triggers and the framework events (Section 8.2) of the steps and
  operations below
- Structured logging
- Idempotency checking
- Event addressing: `RoomEvent.addressed_to`, honoured when set (Section 19.3)
- Turn backend with its in-memory implementation and the kit's own executor:
  every turn through its serialized messages (Section 10.6)

**Triggers and framework events.** A Level 0 implementation MUST fire each
hook trigger, and emit each framework event, that the table below names for a
step or an operation, whenever that step or operation runs. The table is
Level 0's conformance list; the Status column of Section 9.2 tells what one
implementation emits, not what conformance requires. A feature of a higher level, or one no level
lists, owes the triggers and the framework events its own section names, and
only an implementation that provides it owes them: identity resolution
(Level 1) owes ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS and ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN at §10.1 step 5,
identity verification (Level 2) ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED at step 5b and the
other triggers of Section 11.7, and an AI channel (Level 1) the triggers of
its turn (Section 6.4). Section 8.2 says which level or feature owes each
framework event.

requirements.applies: §26.2 Level 1: Transport (RECOMMENDED); the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
A Level 1 implementation SHOULD additionally support:

- At least one SMS provider
- At least one Email provider
- WebSocket channel
- HTTP/Webhook channel
- AI channel with at least one AI provider
- Agent class (AIChannel subclass with identity metadata)
- Provider abstraction (swappable per channel type)
- Identity resolution pipeline (Section 10.1 step 5, Sections 11.1–11.6)
- Identity hooks (ON_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS, ON_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN)
- Participant model with identification status
- Memory system with at least SlidingWindowMemory (Section 20)
- Circuit breaker
- Retry policy
- Rate limiting
- Telemetry provider abstraction (Section 15.7)

requirements.applies: §26.3 Level 2: Rich (OPTIONAL); the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
A Level 2 implementation MAY additionally support:

- Transport channels to messaging platforms, with their rich content: rich
  text, media, buttons, reactions, edits and deletes as each platform carries
  them (e.g., WhatsApp Business or Personal, Messenger, Teams, Telegram)
- RCS channel with SMS fallback
- Template content support
- Source providers (persistent connections)
- REST API (Section 16.1)
- MCP Server (Section 16.2)
- ACP agent channel (Section 6.4)
- Realtime/ephemeral events backend
- Per-room hooks
- Multi-agent orchestration (Section 19):
  - ConversationRouter with routing rules, addresses taking precedence
    (Section 19.4, step 0)
  - Both agent-response policies, selectable per room (Section 19.3.1)
  - ConversationPipeline with stages
  - HandoffHandler with tool-based handoff protocol
  - At least Pipeline and Swarm strategies; Discussion MAY be provided
    (Section 19.7.5)
- Tool access control with ToolPolicy (Section 21)
- Task delegation with child rooms (Section 23)
- Delivery strategies: Immediate, WaitForIdle, Queued (Section 22)
- Skills framework with SkillRegistry (Section 24)
- Image generation through an ImageProvider decoupled from the AI provider
  (Section 25)
- Response schemas: an AI provider constraining its answer to a portable
  JSON Schema (Section 6.7)
- Identity verification: requests, labels, holding and release, the three
  verification triggers (Section 10.1 step 5b, Section 11.7)
- AI steering directives (Section 21.3)
- Advanced memory providers: Summarizing, Retrieval (Section 20)
- A turn backend whose executors run in other processes (Section 10.6)

requirements.applies: §26.4 Level 3: Real-Time Media (OPTIONAL); the source unit and enclosing sections retain their capability conditions, defaults, exceptions and planned status. Conformance levels are declared in §26.
requirements.text:
A Level 3 implementation MAY additionally support audio and/or video real-time media:

#### Audio (Voice)

- Audio Processing Pipeline with:
  - AudioFrame and AudioFormat data models
  - AudioPipelineConfig with pipeline format contract
  - ResamplerConfig (RECOMMENDED)
  - VADProvider interface with at least one implementation (e.g., Silero) — REQUIRED for VoiceChannel, OPTIONAL for RealtimeVoiceChannel
  - DenoiserProvider interface (OPTIONAL, e.g., sherpa-onnx)
  - AECProvider interface (OPTIONAL, RECOMMENDED for non-WebRTC transports)
  - AGCProvider interface (OPTIONAL, built-in implementation REQUIRED)
  - DTMFDetector interface (OPTIONAL, RECOMMENDED for SIP/PSTN)
  - DiarizationProvider interface (OPTIONAL)
  - TurnDetector interface (OPTIONAL)
  - BackchannelDetector interface (OPTIONAL)
  - AudioRecorder interface (OPTIONAL, RECOMMENDED for regulated industries)
  - AudioPostProcessor interface (OPTIONAL)
  - InterruptionConfig
- Voice channel (STT/TTS pipeline)
- VoiceBackend interface with at least one implementation
- AudioCaptureSource interface (OPTIONAL, REQUIRED for capture that outlives a session — Section 12.12)
- Packet loss concealment for lossy transports (OPTIONAL, RECOMMENDED for RTP backends — Section 12.2.1)
- TTS conversation context — TTSContextLevel, TTSContext, `release_context` (OPTIONAL — Section 12.2.2)
- STTProvider interface with at least one implementation
- TTSProvider interface with at least one implementation
- Voice catalog — `VoiceInfo`, `available_voices`, `list_voices` (OPTIONAL — Section 12.2)
- Dialogue synthesis — `synthesize_dialogue`, `DialogueTurn` (OPTIONAL — Section 12.2)
- VoiceLibrary interface — custom voices, designed or replicated with consent (OPTIONAL — Section 12.2.4)
- Voice hooks (ON_SPEECH_START through ON_RECORDING_STOPPED)
- Barge-in and interruption handling (InterruptionStrategy)
- Audio bridging — AudioBridge (OPTIONAL — Section 12.7)
- Realtime Voice channel (speech-to-speech)
- RealtimeVoiceProvider interface
- Full-duplex providers and reasoning delegation (OPTIONAL — Section 12.4.1)
- RealtimeAudioTransport interface
- Realtime voice hooks (ON_TOOL_CALL, ON_REALTIME_TEXT_INJECTED, ON_PROTOCOL_TRACE)
- Protocol trace infrastructure (ProtocolTrace, emit_trace, on_trace, pre-room buffering)

#### Video

- Video data models:
  - VideoFrame — inbound frame container (encoded NAL units or raw pixels)
  - VideoChunk — outbound encoded frame container
  - VideoSession — active video connection state
  - VideoCapability flags (SIMULCAST, SVC, SCREEN_SHARE, RECORDING, BANDWIDTH_ESTIMATION)
- VideoBackend interface — transport abstraction (connect, disconnect, send_video, callbacks)
- VideoChannel — session-based channel orchestrator:
  - Session lifecycle with dual-signal ready mechanism (matching VoiceChannel pattern)
  - Hook triggers: ON_VIDEO_SESSION_STARTED, ON_VIDEO_SESSION_ENDED, ON_VISION_RESULT, ON_VIDEO_DETECTION, BEFORE_BRIDGE_VIDEO (ON_VIDEO_TRACK_ADDED and ON_VIDEO_TRACK_REMOVED are Planned, Section 9.2)
  - Optional VisionProvider integration with configurable analysis interval
  - Vision results emitted as framework events (video_vision_result)
- VisionProvider interface — frame analysis abstraction:
  - analyze_frame(frame, prompt, response_schema) → VisionResult (description, labels, confidence, faces, OCR text)
  - analyze_stream(frames, interval_ms, assumed_fps) for streaming analysis (Section 12.8.7)
- VideoRecorder interface (OPTIONAL — Section 12.8.10)
- AI integration: vision results reach the AI channels' turns as a `<vision>` block (Section 12.8.7); `setup_video_vision()` is deprecated and wires nothing
- Video and voice channels operate independently in the same room, enabling combined audio+video sessions where the AI can both hear (via STT) and see (via VisionProvider)

#### Room media recording

- MediaRecorder interface (OPTIONAL — Section 12.11); REQUIRED for an
  implementation that records conferences in framework mode (Section 12.10.8)

#### Conference (SFU)

- Conference data models (ConferenceTrack, TrackKind, ConferenceParticipant,
  ConferenceGrants, ConferenceAccess, BotSession, ConferenceCapability)
- ConferenceBackend interface with MockConferenceBackend (Section 12.10.3)
- ConferenceChannel with per-track STT lanes and bot TTS publication
  (Section 12.10.4)
- Conference hooks (ON_CONFERENCE_PARTICIPANT_JOINED/LEFT,
  ON_CONFERENCE_TRACK_PUBLISHED/UNPUBLISHED, ON_CONFERENCE_TRACK_MUTED/UNMUTED,
  ON_ACTIVE_SPEAKER_CHANGED, ON_CONNECTION_QUALITY_CHANGED, and
  ON_SCREEN_SHARE_STARTED/STOPPED for screen-share tracks)
- Explicit track subscription, participant identity correlation, and bot
  self-exclusion (Sections 12.10.2–12.10.4)
- Multi-party interruption policy (ConferenceInterruptionConfig)
- Participant lifecycle integration (conference events create/update
  Participant records)

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: each per-turn setting resolves from the binding metadata, then the channel's per-turn configuration, then the channel default. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Per-turn settings.** Each per-turn setting (`system_prompt`, `temperature`,
`max_tokens`, `thinking_budget`, `enable_thinking`, `reasoning_effort`,
`response_schema`, `turn_budget_tokens`, `turn_budget_usd`) resolves from the
binding metadata, then the channel's per-turn configuration, then the channel
default.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: a level that does not set a setting, its key absent or null, defers to the next; null never clears a setting at either level. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A level that does not set it, its key absent or `null`, defers to the
next: `null` never clears a setting, at either level, so an integrator that
serializes an empty form field as `null` keeps the next level's value.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: a setting is lifted for one room only by an explicit value that states off (thinking_budget 0, enable_thinking false, reasoning_effort "none", system_prompt ""). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
setting is lifted for one room only by an explicit value that states off
(`thinking_budget: 0`, `enable_thinking: false`, `reasoning_effort: "none"`,
`system_prompt: ""`).

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: the reasoning switch read across enable_thinking and thinking_budget (Section 6.7): an enable_thinking false at a level turns reasoning off over a less specific level's budget, a budget at the same or a more specific level still states the switch. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The reasoning switch is read across two keys (Section
6.7): an `enable_thinking: false` set at a level turns reasoning off whatever
`thinking_budget` a less specific level set, while a budget set at the same or
a more specific level still states the switch.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: a setting with no value that states off (temperature, max_tokens, response_schema, the turn budgets of Section 6.4) cannot be lifted for a room once a less specific level sets it, only replaced. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A setting with no value that
states off (`temperature`, `max_tokens`, `response_schema`, and the turn
budgets of Section 6.4) cannot be lifted for a room once a less specific level
sets it, only replaced.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: the binding's tools are a toolset of their own, and a null there declares none, like an absent key. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The binding's `tools` is a toolset of its own, and a
`null` there declares none, like an absent key.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: the per-turn configuration's tools, when it gives them, replace the binding's for that turn. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The per-turn configuration's
`tools`, when it gives them, replace the binding's for that turn.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: either toolset is declared before the tools the channel was built with, and none of its tools under the name of one of those, of a tool the channel provides or of one the room's setup serves it (Section 21.1) is declared: that tool stands. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
Either
toolset is declared before the tools the channel was built with, and none of
its tools under the name of one of those, of a tool the channel provides or of
one the room's setup serves it (Section 21.1) is declared: that tool stands.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: a binding's value read as its setting's type reads one of another kind (a number written as a text, a whole float or a whole number's text for an integer, a boolean for a number). Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A
binding's value is read as its setting's type reads one of another kind: a
number written as a text, a whole float or a whole number's text for an integer, a boolean for a number
(`"0.3"` reads 0.3, `64.0` and `"100"` read 64 and 100).

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn settings: a binding value that does not read so fails the turn before its model is asked, its error naming every setting refused, and so does a turn_budget_tokens that is not a positive integer or a turn_budget_usd that is not a positive number, the budgets read strictly. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
One that does not read
so (a `temperature` of `"hot"`, a `max_tokens` of `1.5`, a `system_prompt` that
is no text) fails the turn before its model is asked, its error naming every
setting refused, and so does a `turn_budget_tokens` that is not a positive
integer or a `turn_budget_usd` that is not a positive number, the budgets read
strictly (a text or a boolean refused): a binding written wrong shows at its
first turn, never replaced by the next level's value.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn configuration: a skill registry of the turn's own (Section 24.3), no binding setting, replaces the channel's registry for that turn alone; a turn that gives none reads the channel's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
The per-turn configuration may also give the turn a skill registry of its own
(Section 24.3). It is not a binding setting: it replaces the channel's registry
for that turn alone, and a turn that gives none reads the channel's.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn configuration: a tool handler of the turn's own serves the host's tools for that turn in place of the channel's handler, the channel's self-serving tools included; a turn that gives none, the next one included, reads the channel's. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It may give the turn a tool handler of its own the same way: it serves the
host's tools for that turn in place of the channel's handler, the tools the
channel was built with that serve themselves included, and a turn that gives
none, the next one included, reads the channel's.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), per-turn configuration: the bounds of the turn's tool calls (Section 21.6), above the channel's own bounds per tool name, for that turn alone. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
It may give the bounds of the turn's tool calls the same way (Section 21.6):
above the channel's own bounds per tool name, for that turn alone.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), constrained turn: a turn's response_schema resolves like the other per-turn settings. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
**Constrained turn.** A turn's `response_schema` resolves like the other
per-turn settings.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), constrained turn: with a response_schema set, none of the answer's text is delivered or stored before the provider's check has passed (Section 6.7): a streamed answer is held until the done event, and a failed check fails the turn with its ResponseSchemaError, leaving nothing in the room. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
When it is set, the channel MUST NOT
deliver or store any of the answer's text before the provider's check has
passed (Section 6.7): a streamed answer is held until the done event, and a
failed check fails the turn with its `ResponseSchemaError`, leaving nothing in
the room.

requirements.applies: §A.9 AI Channel (Level 1, §26.2), constrained turn: a turn whose tool loop stops before a final answer (its round cap, its deadline, its spending budget, a stop, or the provider interrupting it after a round) fails with truncated. Enclosing capability conditions and §26 levels still apply.
requirements.text:
A turn whose tool loop stops before a final answer, on its round cap,
its deadline or its spending budget, because it was stopped, or because the provider interrupted it
after a round, has no document to deliver and fails with `truncated`.

requirements.text:
